title: Testing reset: run-everything crash test plus a short promise list; delete the rest
description: Peter ruling 2026-10-22: testing goal is "nothing you open crashes, freezes or loses your work". Keep two kinds of test: (1) run everything: every preset, effect, generator and starter scene runs headless a few hundred frames, failing on crash, hang, NaN or black frame, no goldens or exact numbers; (2) a short promise list a crash test cannot see: undo exact, save/load round trip, MIDI map survives rename, clock lands on the beat, no command dropped, knob/MIDI/OSC change reaches the effect next frame. One version of each test, no small duplicates of nightly runs. Landing runs the promises plus run-everything for what the change touched; nightly runs everything plus a two-hour show run that fails on climbing memory; a nightly red is the first fix next morning. Delete shape tests, digests, half-built-feature tests, UI flows; audio detector accuracy moves to the training lab (one tiny export parity check stays). Add a lint banning unwrap/expect on the show path (about 2,500 sites). Evidence: side-session-notes testing_strategy_report.md and testing_paradigm_review.md (folder local_fdcd1661...).

title: Heavy water plus RT frames are killed by the macOS GPU watchdog (Impacting Interactivity); export stops on the first one because the hang retry never fires
description:
Symptom: Downloads/scene testing.manifold (GPU FLIP water plus RT shadow, AO+GI and reflection) fails export at 1080x1920 60 fps at frame 27, 46 and 84 across three runs on 2026-10-22; reproduces after a reboot, so not the stale-driver hang. The same kill hit live playback at preview size 396x704 once the water surface mesh grew to 3.6M vertices, so it is a stage risk too. Error: Command buffer "Generators" code 1, 0000000e kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorImpactingInteractivity. RT shadow always completes; the faulted encoder moves between AO+GI and reflection from run to run, a timeout signature, not a bad access.

Root cause, known part: classify_fault in crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/gpu_fault.rs matches ErrorHang but not ErrorImpactingInteractivity, so this kill falls to FaultKind::Other, is_recoverable_hang is false, and content_export.rs stops at attempt 0. The existing hang retry with conservative RT tiles never runs for it.
Root cause, unknown part: why one Generators submission runs long enough to hit the OS limit despite the adaptive RT tiles (trace_planner.rs, raytrace/trace_timing.rs). Suspects: RT trace cost against a multi-million-triangle water mesh (whether its acceleration structure is rebuilt or refit per frame is unknown; the mesh changes topology every frame), 7.4x the preview pixels at export, and the pressure solve running far past its normal round count (see the solver bead), all landing in one submission.

Fix shape: classify ImpactingInteractivity as a watchdog kill so retry and conservative tiles apply. Then the root fix: offline export bounds every submission so no single command buffer can reach the OS limit whatever the scene weighs (split heavy work across buffers, tile ray passes at export size). A slow export frame must mean slow, never failed. Retry caveat already noted in the code: simulation layers advance twice on a retry, and a kill mid water step can leave the sim half advanced, so a retry needs the step to be repeatable. Oracle: per-encoder GPU timing for one heavy export frame. Related: BUG-qh04 (Corrosion heavy-export Generators hangs), BUG-j8clo (pressed-lid pressure solves hit the iteration cap unconverged).

title: Box3D tree query assertion: stackCount < B3_TREE_STACK_SIZE - 1 (dynamic_tree.c:1142)
description: Symptom: during live use, Box3D asserts in b3DynamicTree_Query because the AABB tree traversal passed 1024 levels. A balanced tree for 100k proxies is about 20 deep, so the tree is degenerate. Root cause: unknown. Suspects: NaN or infinite AABBs from a non-finite transform, a zero or NaN scale, a degenerate mesh producing bad hulls, or an exploding body; all of these break tree balancing. Fix shape: the scene redesign CollisionShape service and the physics install validate every transform, scale and hull as finite and non-degenerate before Box3D sees it, and refuse with a reason. Also check whether a Box3D assert can abort the app in the show build, and make it never do so. Repro steps from Peter pending.

title: Direct level-set rendering: draw the water surface from the signed-distance grid, no mesh in the live path
description:
Direction doc D2. Peter: why have the mesh at all if we can do this? The solver already keeps a signed-distance grid every step. One full-screen pass walks each pixel's ray through that grid (sphere tracing: read the distance, jump that far, stop at zero) and writes depth, normal and position. The existing lighting, shadows, fog, transmissive layer and material system read those exactly as they read a mesh hit. Refraction and absorption are the same walk continued inside the water. The ray tracer gets a custom intersection on the water's tiles doing the same walk, so the no-partial-ray-tracing rule holds by construction. Marching cubes, the smoothing passes, the normals pass, the welded mesh and the mesh's ray-tracing structure leave the live path; marching cubes stays as an offline export tool only.

This is a render architecture change, not an optimisation. Consequences: water shading moves out of the mesh material into the march; shadows cast by the surface, edge anti-aliasing and motion vectors need their own handling; the engine-default look was tuned on the smoothed mesh and needs a look pass against the FLIP Fluids reference exports, with a grid-side blur replacing the mesh smoothing; the march costs per pixel, so 4K live needs a half-resolution search with a full-resolution refine (one or two exact steps per pixel from the coarse hit, the picture stays full-res). Rejected: fixing the five mesh copies and keeping the mesh, because the per-frame rebuild, the ray-tracing structure and the display ring would all still scale with the mesh. BUG-kipwz (mesh held as five copies) stays only as the stopgap that unblocks exports before this lands.

Design spec before build: write it to the design doc standard first (direction doc section 7).
notes: Priority 1 build, starts without the measurement (D2, D10). The field exists (shape_particle_blobs, particle_volume, redistance_lattice); the new work is the march pass in the scene renderer and a custom hit in the ray tracer. Runs inside the sealed Scene node and writes colour, depth, normals, the item-id buffer and exact motion vectors from the sim velocity. Light through thin water comes from the distance marched inside it. Modifiers: Scene Loop, Scene Mirror and copies apply by moving or reflecting the sample point, smooth deformers through the inverse deform with shorter steps; Shatter, Surface Peel and Ordered Recon do not apply to water. Spec first: docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md section 7 (Next session).

title: GPU FLIP live timing and display: water on the beat, display ring holds grids not meshes
description:
Sub-epic 3 of the GPU FLIP end game (docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md section 3).

The path from the sim tick to the pixel: the shared physics clock, display history and cursor, publication, and the CPU waits around them. Physics is never tied to display fps (decision log 2026-10-21). Today live water trails the music by 75 to 110 ms. Once direct level-set rendering lands in the Surface sub-epic, the display ring holds sparse grids and particles instead of meshes. The next sim tick overlaps this frame's render so the GPU never idles.

End state on stage: water reacts within a frame of the beat at 24, 30 or 60 fps, never stutters below 60 fps display, and the display ring holds grids, not meshes.

title: GPU FLIP simulation: correct, then cheap at 128, then unbounded, with bodies that rest and APIC transfers
description:
Sub-epic 1 of the GPU FLIP end game (docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md section 3).

The solver step (node.gpu_flip_step) and its pressure solve, transfers, sparse tiles, substeps and two-way body coupling. Order: correctness first, because those break the show (Solve Level above 0 jitters, density agreement, the solids gate). Coupling physics next, because light boxes that never settle break the show too. Then step cost at 64 and 128, re-ranked against the fresh measurement. Then structure and scale: coarse projection, narrow band, the 128 at 60 fps gate. Last, reference completeness: APIC, per-solid sheeting, and the deferred viscosity and surface tension (they wait for macro shots, D6).

Nests BUG-mi4qf (GPU FLIP coupled bodies) and BUG-xyqfq (GPU FLIP water with no air). Memory work lives in the Memory sub-epic, not here.

Free performance in this sub-epic: dispatch to live counts, fused smoother levels, warm start, solve tolerance tied to what is visible.

End state on stage: the sim at 128 costs what 64 costs today, never jitters, holds volume like the engine, floating bodies settle, and FLIP transfers like MPM.

title: GPU FLIP measurement and tooling: fresh 64 and 128 numbers, GPU busy percent, a full memory ledger
description:
Sub-epic 0 of the GPU FLIP end game (docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md section 3).

Every speed bead in this programme carries numbers from 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-06. Since then sparse phases 2a to 2c, the Sim Rate blend (979b6e895), idle-slot gating (17745d37a) and replace-oldest whitewater landed, and nothing was re-measured. No speed lane starts before a fresh 64 and 128 frame split and a GPU memory ledger on main (D10). After that, keep the proofs fast and honest so speed lanes land quickly, and report GPU busy percent so idle gaps show.

Order: the fresh frame split, then the memory ledger, then the unlanded-branch review, then the stamp and stall noise that hides real wins, then proof speed and tooling.

End state on stage: every speed and memory claim is a fresh number at 64 and 128, GPU busy percent is reported, and the water's memory is fully accounted. The lead knows, per landing, what the 128 frame and its memory cost, and where.

title: Typed identity for scene and physics: no slot numbers, positions or shared names in saved data
description: Peter 2026-10-21: fix identity at the class level. Saved scene and physics data refers to things by slot number (body_N ports, copies_N, BodySlots remaps on enable, duplicate, paste, copy groups) and by non-unique string ids (import model_file shared by every merged object). Each renumbering path is a bug source: BUG-2bulf (force makes every object load the cliff file), BUG-qiuhh (paste loses per-body forces), BUG-ic82j (adding a body rebuilds the world), BUG-agahe (fixed body moves only after reset). Design pass first (read-only inventory of every index, position or shared-name identity across scene, physics, bindings, forces, copy groups, swarms, water sources, gizmo targets and undo commands), then lanes. CG2 waits for this design.

title: Hook pre-approves persistent git config writes and strips GIT_* env prefixes, so auto mode can set core.hooksPath or core.pager unseen
description: Symptom: in auto mode preToolUseBash.py returns allow for git config core.hooksPath /tmp/x, git config core.pager cat, GIT_PAGER=x git log and GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS=... git log; env git ... and bash -c "git ..." get no decision; git restore . is allowed. A persistent git config write lands in the shared git dir every slot reads. Root cause: is_preapproved_command treats git config writes as normal workflow, and _strip_leading_keywords drops VAR= prefixes before matching. Found by the overnight 2026-10-19 lane 10 review (commit f2812315f). So the goldens recorded before it pin the retired drop-on-full behaviour for overflow ticks; a re-record of only those cases would cite this line.

title: Box3D world resets on every audio-fired scene impulse during export
description: Symptom: in export, each kick/snare-fired scene force snaps the Box3D world back to its start grid 1-2 frames after the hit and drops the impulse; live is fine. Evidence: Mirage Physics Test export, 21 resets correlated with kick/snare onsets. Root cause (static + video correlation): offline_audio_mod.rs:381-408 stamps hops at window end, so trigger times sit after frame k transport; content_pipeline.rs:2405 applies them pre-render; physics_sampling.rs:363-403 observe_physics_at_source clamps only the lower bound and runs a sample-only frame at the future time (physics.rs:860 sets last time); frame k at T_k then reads as a backward seek (physics.rs:813) and rebuilds the world. Fix shape: host passes frame transport into fire_scene_impulse; observation clamps trigger time into [prev frame, current frame]. Separate question: export audio analysis runs one frame ahead of live. Unverified: no runtime repro; GPU liquid/MPM anchors unchecked.

title: Effect chains: effects depend on neighbours, silent fallbacks kill params
description: Symptom: on Murmur 04 Triptogram breakdown, deleting or editing effects in the inspector leaves effects dead, wrongly shown, or working only when other chain effects are on. Class-level, not one effect. Root cause unknown; suspects: (a) segment fusion: neighbour enabled state changes the fused segment; groups.rs:162-176 + core.rs:920 fall back to canonical graph but keep fused bindings (all card params dead); freeze/install.rs:544 fused cache key ignores bindings; fusion untested in tests (install.rs:1020 stays Pending). (b) inspector cards target chain position not EffectId (manifold-ui panels/mod.rs:122, ui_bridge/mod.rs:616). Other silent fallbacks: chain_dispatch.rs:340 failed build stays bypassed through value edits; core.rs build failures eprintln + raw input; core.rs:1090-1101/713-733 unresolved bindings dropped; core.rs:1526; param_binding.rs:581-602; bound_graph.rs:559-576; core.rs:1740 + layer_compositor.rs:2375. Decisive test: launch with MANIFOLD_CHAIN_FUSION=0 MANIFOLD_LOG_REBUILD_REASON=1. Fix shape: fused == unfused by construction (per-pair proof), chain builds fully or fails loud on the card, cards carry EffectId, cache keys cover bindings. Crates: node-engine, ui, app.
notes: STOPGAP landed in 308ccd421: a merged segment that cannot wire every param is refused and cards build unfused (logged [chain-segment-refused], not shown on card). Root fix owed: (1) find why merges produce unresolvable bindings - run Murmur 04 and read [chain-segment-refused] lines, they name the failing merge and reason; (2) merge compiler (compile_segment_view / fused_view_for) proves at compile time every member param maps through, so a bad merge is never produced; (3) fused==unfused proof per shipped effect pair, running the production segment path in tests (install.rs ~1020 stays Pending in tests today); (4) chain build errors show on the card; (5) inspector cards target EffectId not chain position (manifold-ui panels/mod.rs:122, ui_bridge/mod.rs:616); (6) per-card unresolved bindings still dropped silently (core.rs ~1090). notes: Lane 1, 2026-10-19 (25af1c932 + lane commits): run-to-run nondeterminism inside the test itself, not suite order or neighbour state. Nightlies: failed 10-15, passed 10-16, failed 10-17..19. Tonight: passed by exact name (gpu_queue cargo test --exact, with two other tests after it); then failed with gpu_queue cargo test -p manifold-nodes --features gpu-proofs --test main -- --test-threads=1 code_terminal::gpu:: , where it also ran first in the process. title: Water setup you can see and trust: out-of-domain feedback, visible hidden things, gizmos for every setup shape
description:
Peter 2026-10-13: moving things in a water scene (fill level, start water column size and position, bodies, etc.) breaks the sim with no feedback when something leaves the domain. Very hard to work with creatively. Also no way to see domain size, hidden things (closed faces, colliders, sources, drains) or forces in the viewport.

Root cause: setup is accepted silently. Nothing checks scene shapes against the domain, and each solver handles out-of-domain input its own way (or not at all).

Fix shape, four parts:
1. One setup check, shared by FLIP and MPM through the liquid seam: reads every setup shape against the domain each edit and returns a list of problems (column outside, fill above top, body outside or straddling a wall, source in a wall, grid budget hit). Same list drives a red outline on the bad thing in the viewport and a warning line on its card.
2. Defined behavior for each problem instead of a broken sim: clip the column to the domain, ignore bodies fully outside, cap fill at the top. The warning says what was clipped. No silent clamps (see BUG-de4i, silent pipeline clamps).
3. A physics overlay in the viewport, on whenever a water layer is selected: domain box with open/closed faces, fill plane, column box, colliders, sources, drains, force arrows and radius.
4. Gizmos for the setup shapes that only have sliders today: column, fill plane, forces (BUG-uuso, force gizmo and Add menu). Domain gizmo exists (fluid_domain_edit.rs).

title: UI flow batch rebuilds the scene fixture for every flow
description: Symptom (feat/water-physics-view gate, 2026-10-13): 28 flows took 356s. 20 of them run on the gltfscene fixture at 7.5-12s each, even one-click flows like scene-setup-close-button (8.9s), while a timeline flow takes 0.5s. Root cause (from code, unmeasured): ui-snap batch (crates/manifold-app/src/ui_snapshot/script.rs run_batch) shares only the GpuDevice; every flow calls fixtures::build(scene) again, so the glTF scene is imported once per flow. Fix shape: group flows by scene in run_ui_flows.py, build each fixture once per batch and give every flow a fresh copy of the built project (clone, or a serialized snapshot restored per flow) so isolation holds. Measure first: time fixtures::build(gltfscene) alone. Expected: the gltfscene group drops from ~200s to well under a minute. ui_flows_batch_proof.py is the oracle that batched results still match solo runs.

No fixed waits in the scripts. water-family-preset (93 actions, 64s) and water-family-controls (70 actions, 23s) cost per action, not per fixture; caching will not help them.

title: Small landings in minutes: cut wall time from branch-ready to pushed
description: Peter, 2026-10-13: landing still takes hours for small changes; it is blocking feature work. Gate log since 2026-10-12: most gate runs take under 3 min, so the hours live in the loop around the gate (reds, re-merge when main moves, re-gate, GPU lock waits, rebuilds per leg), which nothing measures. Order: (1) measure end-to-end landing wall time, (2) one gate at a time against a fixed main, (3) build once, share across legs, (4) GPU lock only for GPU work, then the GPU-budget and red-classification children.

title: MIDI note shorter than one frame loses its NoteOff and the clip sticks until the next hit
description: Symptom: short-gate notes from Ableton hold until the same note is hit again; in record mode, committed durations become inter-onset gaps. Root cause: midir events carry absolute_tick -1 so compare_native_clock_events ties on tick and NoteOff-before-NoteOn reorders the whole frame batch, processing Off (untracked, ignored) before On (lead-verified). The 5 ms guards compare the same per-frame realtime_now, and the callback discards _timestamp_us, so the effective guard is one frame, not 5 ms. Fix: tick ordering only when a real tick exists, else arrival order; stamp each event with the midir timestamp and guard on it.

title: Drift correction disabled after Stop or any backward jump: last_sync_time never reset
description: Symptom: play to 5:00, Stop, Play: no drift correction (re-seek, stalled-player restart, out-point enforcement) for 5 minutes. An Ableton loop shorter than its jump-back plus 2 s never gets drift correction again. Root cause: engine.rs tick gates on current_time - last_sync_time >= video_sync_interval; last_sync_time is reset only on project initialize (lead-verified). Fix: run the cadence on realtime, not timeline time, so no transport jump can starve it.

title: Playback pre-Fable code audit pilot: findings
description: Read-only review of manifold-playback code written before 2026-06-10. Signal: about one real defect per 150-250 old lines on the timing path. Defects cluster where the Unity port changed architecture (no real clock ticks, async readiness, two threads) and the old assumption silently stopped holding. Stubs are synchronous and fakes carry no tempo map, so tests miss them. Wider audit should target ported-assumption seams, folded into the decomposition epics cleanup passes.

title: Detector Lab speed: A/Bs in minutes, not hours
description: Problem: a simple kick A/B takes ~2.5 h (2026-10-12): baselines retrain after any lab edit, swap stalls double fold times (484 s -> 897 s), gain copies 4x data. Sequence: (0) pull per-stage timing breakdown of a full kick A/B from meta.json - decides what dominates; (1) per-stage cache keys BUG-4x7jh (lab cache keys) + memory/mmap BUG-xd15a (lab training swaps the Mac) together; (2) trees/stage-only fast loop reusing cached net predictions (falls out of 1); (3) parallel seeds BUG-9ngk8.8 (two seeds on the GPU), only after memory fix; (4) bf16 training as its own A/B; (5) only if still slow: screening on a fixed stratified song subset, confirm winners on the full exam. Rule: releases and final verdicts always run full; screening never ships. Already on 4 folds. Target: a typical one-sided A/B under ~40 min.
notes: Gain-variant branch (feat/detector-gain-variants) landed. The net is gain-blind (both input channels are dB differences), so the next cost cut is applying gain augmentation per draw on the measures and stage instead of 4x net training.

title: Detectors are not level-invariant: snare scores swing with input gain
description: Symptom: same Corrosion T2 master through the shipped snare (snare-2026-10-12-b5ccd28c9) at -12/-6/0/+6 dB: fires 280/266/331/192; at -6 dB half the intro snares drop under the 0.53 cutoff, at +6 dB the main-section snares fall from 0.93-0.97 to 0.12-0.17. Live send level therefore changes what fires. Root cause: absolute-level inputs (note13 levels, cdom4 raw strength, stage level column, likely net spectrum dB) and training only at each song's own level. Fix shape: random gain augmentation per training draw (about +-12 dB) in the lab, A/B vs shipped kick and snare, and a gain-sweep release check. Scratch probe: shipped_on_file.py with GAIN_DB.
notes: Gain-variant branch (feat/detector-gain-variants) landed. The net is gain-blind (both input channels are dB differences), so the next cost cut is applying gain augmentation per draw on the measures and stage instead of 4x net training. Kept open until a release ships with it.

title: Live GPU water shows forces and hits 75-110 ms late at any grid size
description: Symptom (Peter, 2026-10-11): scene forces on GPU FLIP water do not land in real time or on the beat, even when the water meets its frame budget at low grid sizes. Root cause (read, not yet observed in the app): a fixed latency stack between transport and the water on screen. (1) The clock display time is one Sim Rate interval behind transport (manifold-physics clock.rs advance, display_from = transport - interval): 33 ms at 30 Hz, 67 ms at 15 Hz. (2) Live uncoupled water then presents at the display cursor (manifold-water-liquid display_cursor.rs), which lags the requested time by the max GPU retirement deficit over the last 2 s plus a quarter publication gap: 42 ms at 60 fps with a 3-frame GPU delay, 75 ms at 30 fps (latency table test cursor_equilibrium_matches_the_latency_table). The deficit comes from the content thread running up to SURFACE_COUNT=3 frames ahead of the GPU, so it does not shrink at low grid sizes. (3) A continuous force is sampled at its tick start, adding up to one more interval. Total roughly 75-110 ms behind every other layer and the audio, more after any hiccup (2 s max-hold). Fix shape (needs Peter): first log transport minus presented water time per frame in the live app to confirm the number; then cut the stack at the root, e.g. pick the presented snapshot GPU-side in the same command buffer so presentation need not wait for CPU-visible retirement, and revisit the one-interval display delay. Related: GPU_FLIP_DISPLAY_HISTORY_DESIGN.md (BUG-ckvpp), LIVE_SIM_CLOCK_DESIGN.md.
notes: Read 2026-10-13: the retire-delay part is the deferred row in GPU_FLIP_DISPLAY_HISTORY_DESIGN.md section 7 (GPU-resident count and acceptance). The CPU waits because each published frame particle count and accept/reject flag only exist on the GPU, and every downstream consumer (interpolation, mesher, whitewater, render) is launched with CPU-known counts. Fix = move count and acceptance onto the GPU: consumers read counts from a buffer, interpolation search needs a sentinel, fused kernels gain two gathers, rejected ticks need a GPU-side repeat per field. Gain about 42 ms at 60 fps. Revive trigger in the doc: P3 stage look lag too high. Re-test feel after BUG-k2whz (dropped late audio hits) before starting.

title: trace_subsurface faults the GPU on its own in about 5 percent of runs
description: Symptom: render_scene_subsurface::closed_curved_sphere_has_no_invalid_transport_pixels_in_either_mode failed in two landing gates in a row on 2026-10-10 (lane/rt-hang-diagnosis 21:50 and lane/rt-texture-usage 23:20) with kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorInnocentVictim; in the second the trace_subsurface encoder itself is MTLCommandEncoderErrorState(4), Faulted, so it is the guilty work, not a bystander. Passes alone in 3.6 s and under a serial debug-layer run. Earlier CDM Kill timeout reports (gpuEvent-gpu_proofs-91184, 16:13) fit the same watchdog kill. On stage: a subsurface material on a dense curved mesh can stall the GPU. Suspected root cause: work per pixel in trace_subsurface (crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/subsurface.msl) is bounded but multiplies: up to 64 samples (line 258) x SSS_MAX_EVENTS 256 (line 277) x boundary queries, and sss_boundary (line 25) forces non_opaque so each query visits every candidate triangle along the ray and filters by instance in software. On a finely tessellated sphere one dispatch can take seconds; under parallel GPU load it exceeds the watchdog. Fix shape: measure the dispatch GPU time first; then make the boundary query return the nearest same-instance hit without visiting every candidate (an instance mask or intersection function instead of non_opaque visit-all), and bound per-dispatch work (tile the dispatch or cap total events per frame) so no single command buffer can approach the watchdog. Likely also the guilty party behind BUG-zu7pc (RT history proof) and the InnocentVictim failures in BUG-hkbdp.6.16.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Measured 2026-10-10 (lane/subsurface-watchdog): the watchdog theory is wrong. The trace is already tiled (plan_trace_regions caps 2^24 query units per command buffer, tracer.rs about 1367); slowest command buffer in the whole subsurface module is 27.4 ms, closed sphere 12.2 ms random walk, 8.4 ms diffusion. The gate log state MTLCommandEncoderErrorState(4) is Faulted, Metal reporting for a faulting encoder, so the likelier cause is a GPU memory fault (residency, a stale acceleration structure, or an out-of-bounds read) that only appears with parallel test threads; serial runs pass. Next oracle: one parallel whole-binary run with MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 and MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1. Separate cost finding: random walk at 64 samples at 1920x1080 is about 25 s per frame (about 2000 command buffers of 12 ms each), shipped default Diffusion 8 samples about 0.3 s per frame at full coverage; filed as its own bead.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Shader validation 2026-10-10 23:00 (lane/subsurface-watchdog): no out-of-bounds, residency or encoder fault in any production kernel; all 13 render_scene_subsurface tests that ran passed under MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 plus MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1 with parallel threads, closed sphere included. Not covered: MetalFX paths (Apple validation segfaults instrumenting a MetalFX kernel via MPSGraph, crash report gpu_proofs-75ea1f1f82b96981-2026-10-10-231244.ips), so subsurface plus temporal upscale is unvalidated. Cause still unknown; candidates are the MetalFX paths or a timing-dependent fault that validation slowdown hides. Probe loop stopped by the lead: evidence now accumulates passively from landing and nightly runs (gate logs record every encoder state at a reset; the FLAKY records count recurrences). Reopen the hunt when there are three recurrences, starting from the faulted encoder each one names. Side finding filed: BUG-8ia5c (normal-fetch debug proof residency).

comments.text: Log analysis 2026-10-11 (read-only): the concurrency premise is wrong. gpu_proofs_gate.py:253 always runs --test-threads=1 and the run holds the machine-wide GPU lock, so no other test overlaps. The guilty work is this test own trace_subsurface random-walk regions: Faulted (state 4) in the 21:50 and 23:20 runs, Affected only at 02:00; the fault lands at a different region each time (about 0, 6, 8 of about 18 back-to-back region command buffers, tracer.rs 1377-1396 commit_and_continue). It is the heaviest subsurface proof (128x128, 64 samples, 4032-triangle sphere, up to 256 events). Suspects: unchecked raw-address vertex and index reads (sss_boundary_normal subsurface.msl 41-46, fetch_interpolated_normal shadow_rays.msl 848 via vertex_base_addr), or a driver fault in forced non-opaque visit-all queries on a dense mesh. Evidence gap: the faulted buffer error code goes through log::error! at encoder.rs 2809-2815, which the proof binary drops (no logger); route it through emit_diagnostic (gpu_fault.rs 35-43) so the next recurrence names page fault versus timeout. Oracle running: the sphere test alone, 40 times, under gpu_queue.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: REPRODUCED ALONE 2026-10-11: the sphere test run by itself 40 times under gpu_queue (prebuilt binary from c58c3ed31, --exact, --test-threads=1, nothing else on the GPU) failed 2 of 40 (runs 27 and 37), InnocentVictim, one with trace_subsurface Faulted (state 4). comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Fix lane step 1 (ca6482828 on lane/subsurface-fault, the faulted buffer error code now reaches stderr): 3 failures in 40 alone; every guilty buffer is code 2 kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang, no page faults; the hang fires about 0.6 s in, slowest normal buffer 12 ms. Index-read theory ruled out (a bad address would page-fault). Removing force_opacity(non_opaque) in sss_boundary still failed 3 of 60. Inputs and ray intervals finite and non-empty (not the BUG-ny4v degenerate-ray class). Deterministic seeds, about 5 percent hang rate: timing-dependent. comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE 2026-10-11 (lane/subsurface-fault): consecutive trace_subsurface region command buffers ran at the same time on the GPU; nothing ordered them on the GPU timeline (commit_and_continue, tracer.rs about 1392), and Metal hazard tracking does not cover the raw-address and useResource reads. Experiment A (CPU wait between regions): 0 of 60. Experiment B (wait for the acceleration-structure build): 2 of 60, ruled out. A shared event between regions: 80 of 80 clean. Same pattern in the main RT region loop (tracer.rs about 2254), the likely cause of BUG-hkbdp.6.16 (multibounce Hang). The encoder-level ordering fix (commit_and_continue signals an encoder-owned event, the next buffer waits) failed 5 of 80 right after a landing gate released the GPU, then passed 60 of 60 on the same binary with the GPU quiet. The hang rate follows prior GPU activity, so the earlier 0 of 60 and 0 of 80 results may be quiet-GPU runs. comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Interleaved oracle 2026-10-11 (120 runs, arms rotated each run, one gpu_queue session): baseline ca6482828 39/1, tracer-event 40/0, encoder-event 36/4. Ordering between region command buffers is not the cause; the encoder-event change is dropped. 4 of 5 failures ran about 8.5 s with every logged buffer InnocentVictim (7 to 25 victims) and no guilty buffer in our process; only one named render-scene-subsurface with Hang. comments.text: Parked 2026-10-11. Every GpuEncoder commit path carries register_fault_handler, acceleration-structure builds included; the unlogged raw buffers (tracer.rs debug helpers 1506 1662 1774 1902, empty retire_on_queue pins at device.rs 2379-2402, metalfx_m4.rs 383, fft.rs 162 MPS child buffers) are proof-only, carry no GPU work, or are off the sphere path. title: Snare + clap detector
description: Next detector after kick: snares and claps are usually the second most prominent hits in a mix and are trigger events. Reuses the kick infrastructure; needs its own candidate finder, measurements and labels (project snare/clap MIDI and stems).
notes:
Peter, 2026-10-10: snare and clap are one detector (the main off-beat backbeat in electronic music); snare rolls count; rimshots do not. Survey of the 30 kick songs (scratch snare_survey.py): about 2,300 snare/clap hits. MIDI: Flight 252 snare + 252 clap, 48 Hours ~460 on QFF Drums snare/clap pads, Back to You 240, Midnight Patience 134, Pattern 255, Lowkey 115 (recall-only timing), Corrosion SNARE TRIGGER 153 (muted trigger track). One-shot audio clips: Murmur 358, Default Haze 45, Late Night CLAP (frozen). Stems only: Gerrit (2 snare stems), Cold (snare), Business (claps), Worship (claps). title: Trained audio detectors
description: Realtime trained detectors that drive audio triggers and modulation, one group per sound: kick, snare and clap, hats and percussion, synths and bass. All share the same pieces: project-confirmed labels, tools/audio_analysis/kick_release.py-style training and export, the model container, detectors::EventDetector on the DetectorWorker thread, and golden parity tests (docs/KICK_REALTIME_DESIGN.md). comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: OVERNIGHT PLAN 2026-10-10/11 (Peter approved; no review overnight). Goals: (1) best kick + snare at today's delay, held-out proven; snare ported on a branch with a launch command, kick as a candidate (no swap without Peter); (2) shared detector toolkit so new families are labels + candidate finder + measurements; (3) bass and synth family feasibility with numbers. Phases: A foundations (snare research scratch -> repo tools/audio_analysis/eval; shared toolkit; kick rebuilds bit for bit); B snare Rust port on a branch (golden-clip parity, CPU under kick); C kick candidate (13 new WIP songs, 4 time segments, noisiness) + snare zero-delay sweep and precision operating point (P >= .75); D edge cases (kick high-passed build-up rolls BUG-qy8q7, snare fast breaks BUG-9ngk8.2.1) via simulated data; E surveys (2026 folder snare/hats/perc) + bass and synth families (labels, family candidate finders and measurements, baselines); F morning report (optimal detectors, learnings, what awaits Peter, beads). Guard rails: Ableton folders read-only via als_extract; no public data; nothing that changes the show lands; research tools/toolkit land via land_branch --skip-gpu; causal, no grid cues, no long song memory; held-out songs with cutoffs from other songs; frozen kick fusion files untouched; one GPU training job at a time; agents only for the port (one per slot), Fable review at medium.

comments.text: Overnight 2026-10-11. Optimal detectors: kick unchanged (no candidate beat it). Snare = rise candidates in 1-8 kHz + one CNN (190 ms slice, shape/new/noisiness channels), held-out F1 .678 over 3 seeds; ported to Rust on feat/snare-port with exact parity, 18 ms CPU per audio second; live test pending (BUG-nss46 snare ship decision). Bass and synth: candidates find 98% of prominent notes, but nets reach only F1 ~.25 at P ~.16 (BUG-ymy4z). Hats are plentiful in the projects (BUG-9ngk8.3).

title: Trained kick detector misses drop kicks after a high-passed build-up roll
description:
Symptom (Peter, live test 2026-10-10, branch feat/kick-realtime): in build-ups with a high-passed kick roll, the thin top-only kicks are missed at first; after a few seconds the detector starts firing on them. At the drop the kick returns to full spectrum and is missed again, because it no longer resembles the build-up rolls.

Root cause (suspected, unverified): the 8 s song-relative stage (tools/audio_analysis/eval/kick_goal_selfsim.py; crates/manifold-audio/src/kick/stage.rs). Its sim, lvl_rel and lp_rel inputs compare each candidate to the p**8-weighted recent confident kicks. The filtered roll becomes the template, so a full kick at the drop scores as dissimilar and is suppressed. Secondary suspect: few high-passed kicks in the training data, which explains the early misses.

Fix shape: (1) reproduce on a recording of a build plus drop; compare stage_p with base blend_p per candidate (kick_release.py reference on the clip). (2) If the stage is to blame: train with kick-swap and filter-sweep augmentation (high-pass rolls into full drops) so the stage learns that template changes are normal, and/or never let the stage pull a confident base blend below the cutoff. (3) Add high-passed kick rolls to training (augment existing kick stems with high-pass sweeps). Re-gate with run_kick_goal_fast.py and ship via kick_release.py.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Simulation 2026-10-11 (tools/audio_analysis/eval/kick_buildup_sim.py, released final model, Pattern kick one-shots over Pattern NO KICK bed, 174 bpm, 6 shots): (1) every roll hit and drop kick gets a candidate; (2) the drop is NOT missed: 6/6 in its first 2 s and 26/26 after, after a 150 Hz-2.5 kHz high-passed build and after a gentle 100-600 Hz one; (3) the high-passed roll is missed and the trees+net blend already misses it (bars 3-4 at ~150-250 Hz high-pass: 0-2/8 caught, blend 0-1), so the stage is not the cause here; the stage even rescues some (bars 1-2: 4/8 shipped vs 1/8 blend); (4) sixteenth rolls (86 ms apart) are missed even unfiltered (2-15/32; blend 0-2). Peter's live drop miss does not reproduce on this material. Revised root cause: training data has no high-passed kicks or fast rolls, so the base models score them low. Fix shape: high-pass and roll augmentation for trees and net (fix (3) of the description), scored held out with run_kick_goal_fast.py; the stage change is not indicated. Caveat: the model saw Pattern in training; only filtering and arrangement are new.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Augmentation trial 2026-10-11 (kick_goal_buildup clips, KICK_GOAL_NN_BUILDUP=train, shipped recipe, seeds 0-2): held-out roll-hit recall at net p>=.5 rises from 6-8% to 47-52%; other kicks in the clips 82-83% -> 87-89%. Main set (30 songs, blend+stage pooled F1, kick_fast_compare): plain .8955/.8666/.8835 mean .8819, build-up .8572/.8937/.8945 mean .8818 (flat). Seed 0 collapsed cold_remix (355/674 vs 564-619 plain) and facade lost 7 points on average; seeds 1-2 are fine. Seeds 3-4 running to see if the collapse is typical.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Seeds 3-4 in. Five seeds, main set blend+stage pooled F1: plain mean .8862, build-up trained .8788 (-0.75, inside the 1-point edge-case budget). Roll-hit recall 7% -> 47% (45-52% per seed). cold_remix loses 8.6 recall points on average (seed 0: 355/674; seeds 3-4: 555-562 vs 588-613 plain), so not shippable as is. Next try: a lighter dose (2 donors per song instead of 4, or the clips at half weight), five seeds, same compare (kick_fast_compare.py over _s0.._s4). Shipping needs Peter yes either way.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Half dose (KICK_GOAL_NN_BUILDUP_DOSE=2, 2 clips per target instead of 4), five seeds: roll-hit recall 40-45%, main-set F1 mean .8659 vs plain .8862 (-2.03, worse than the full dose -0.75); apricots -25.7, eat_sleep -11.4, cold_remix -8.1, got_it -5.3 recall. Two tries, both cost the main set more than they should; the direction (mixing roll clips into the one net training) is closed for now. The net can learn rolls (7% -> ~47%), so the next shape is one that keeps the main net untouched: a separate roll path gated by its own candidates, or fine-tuning only the head on clips. Not shipped; kick unchanged.

title: Flaky tests: record failures so the gate names flakes, ban wall-clock assertions in landing tests, clear the ten open flake beads
description:
Flaky tests stop costing landings: detect them mechanically, fix the class, clear the backlog. Peter, 2026-10-10: as part of the post-T2 cleanup, remove or improve flaky tests so landings never get stuck in rerun loops again.

FINDINGS (2026-10-10)
- The gate cannot see flakes. Gate-pass records under the git common dir's gate-passes-v1 store passing legs only (27,643 per-test timings, every one status ok), so "failed then passed on identical content" is invisible; each flake costs a full re-gate and a human read.
- Ten open flake beads share one class, wall-clock or contention-sensitive assertions inside landing tests: BUG-zu7pc (RT history proof), BUG-xesy (gpu-proofs under load), BUG-m0c9 (RT never_stalls_past_20ms), BUG-56d (OSC timecode under CPU load), BUG-jgsf and BUG-2vrk (RT kernel toggle), BUG-nwwtz (skinned glTF 20.1 ms vs 20 ms), BUG-yhe1 (tracer reconstruction beside other gpu tests), BUG-ovnb (perf budgets under gate load), BUG-ffis (straggler GLB warmup).
- New today: scene_modifier_file_authoring::consolidated_peel_loads_attaches_and_routes_two_stage_event_path panicked once in a full manifold-nodes run (gpu_encoder called with no encoder bound), passed 12 of 12 alone and 508 of 508 on rerun; a diagnosis lane owns it (suspect: randomly seeded hash iteration order).
- .config/nextest.toml has a ci profile with retries=1; landing does not use it, correctly: retries hide flakes.

FIX SHAPE (existing infrastructure only)
1. Record failures: the gate writes failing per-test statuses beside passes in the same records, keyed the same way; a test that fails and passes on one content key is flagged FLAKY in the gate summary and trunk_health.py files or updates one bead per test. No retries in landing.
2. Class rule, written into docs/ADDING_PRIMITIVES.md and the test cut rules (BUG-hkbdp.6.11): landing tests never assert wall-clock time or contention-sensitive budgets; they assert work done (counts, dispatches, frames waited). Timing budgets are measurements and run nightly under the GPU lock (gpu_queue.py) through the gpu_scope.py nightly filter.
3. Clear the backlog: for each bead above, fix by determinism or seed control, convert the timing assertion to a work assertion or a nightly measurement, or delete the test with its contract covered elsewhere. Close each bead with the call made.
4. Nondeterminism class: grep for iteration over randomly seeded hash maps feeding evaluation order or node choice in engine and node crates; ordered maps or explicit tie-breaks where order decides behaviour.

DONE: the gate reports flakes by name; zero open flake beads; the class rule is in the docs and the test cut follows it.

title: Water subsystem boundaries the compiler enforces: cut the liquid-hub cycles, then leaf crates
description:
Make the water subsystems compiler-enforced boundaries, so a change in one runs only its own tests plus the contract tests of what it exposes. Peter, 2026-10-10: a water change must not need unrelated tests, so boundaries and interfaces must be rock solid and the compiler must stop small changes rippling into unexpected areas.

FINDINGS (main at ff4c4b8bd, scratch census over crate:: paths in manifold-nodes-water/src, areas by path keyword, so approximate)
- Liquid is the hub: matter -> liquid 55 refs, gpu_flip -> liquid 40, whitewater -> liquid 32. That direction is right; liquid is the shared solver contract.
- The hub reaches back into its leaves: liquid -> matter 15, liquid -> gpu_flip 10, liquid -> whitewater 6. Leaves reach each other: gpu_flip <-> matter 6/3, matter -> whitewater 3. These cycles are why any water edit must rerun everything.
- 67 files are shared or unclassified (runtime/, wire_values, node.rs, vector_field, testkit).

TARGET SHAPE
- Layers: shared water types and the liquid contract at the bottom; gpu_flip, matter (MPM), whitewater and rigid physics as leaves that depend only on the bottom layer's public interface, never on each other; manifold-nodes-water as the thin registration layer on top.
- Stage 1 (module level, rides BUG-hkbdp.6.7 god-file split): cut every upward and sideways edge; leaf internals pub(crate) or narrower; one interface module per subsystem; a crate_layering-style test pins zero upward/sideways edges.
- Stage 2 (decision for Peter after stage 1 shows the cut count): leaves become crates. The Cargo graph then does the enforcing, and the landing gate's existing crate-to-test mapping scopes water landings for free: a leaf edit runs that leaf's tests; the liquid contract suite runs only when the bottom layer changes.
- Limit stated plainly: the compiler stops interface changes rippling; a behaviour change behind an unchanged interface is caught only by the contract tests at that interface, so each interface needs one contract suite that always runs when its owner changes.

LINKS: BUG-bkfv2 (gate scope split) consumes these boundaries for water selection; BUG-hkbdp.6.11 (water test cut) places each surviving test with the subsystem that owns its contract.
notes: Peter, 2026-10-10: crate split approved (stage 2 decided: each water subsystem becomes its own crate). Fable designs the interfaces and the answers to the cons (interface shape, shared test helpers, per-crate gpu-proofs wiring, move timing versus open branches, hot-path inlining); Opus lead executes from that design.

title: Split the water god-files along stage boundaries; inline tests to sibling files
description:
Split the water god-files along their stage boundaries and move inline tests into sibling test files.

FINDINGS (main at 7f732cb0f; re-measure after the CPU FLIP cut)
- physics.rs 4793 lines: production through line 2611, then 2.2k lines of inline tests, with a separate coupling_tests.rs already beside it. The production half holds RigidBody, RigidSimulation (impl from line 590 to about 2600), HeldClock, four scope guards and the serialization glue.
- primitives/gpu_flip_step.rs 3148 lines with about 2.1k lines of inline tests, and gpu_flip_step_tests.rs (3136 lines) already exists beside it: split-brain test placement.
- primitives/gpu_flip_clock.rs 2046 (about 1.3k inline tests), primitives/fluid_surface.rs 1694 (goes with CPU FLIP), fluid_cache.rs (goes with CPU FLIP), primitives/whitewater_step.rs 1958, primitives/gpu_flip_pressure.rs 1702, liquid/bodies.rs 1390, primitives/physics_world.rs 1432.
- 33 sibling `_tests.rs` files exist already, so the sibling pattern is the crate's convention; the inline `mod tests` blocks are the drift.

FIX SHAPE
- Tests first: move every inline `mod tests` in a production file over 1k lines into the existing or a new sibling `<file>_tests.rs`, keeping test names so gpu_scope.py filters and gpu_test_times.json keys stay valid. Pure moves, one commit.
- Then split production files over 1.5k lines along the stage boundaries their design docs already name: gpu_flip_step.rs by the stages in GPU_FLIP_PRESSURE_SOLVE.md section 1.1 (stage design) and GPU_FLIP_SPARSE_BLOCKS_DESIGN.md (tile classify, rings, extend, pockets, solid velocity, body passes); physics.rs into body model, simulation step, history/input and serialization; gpu_flip_clock.rs into interval acceptance and slot gating; whitewater_step.rs per lifecycle stage. Each split is a module directory beside the file, matching how extent.rs submodules already sit under primitives/<name>/.
- DECOMPOSING_GENERATORS.md section 1.2 (Engine internals are stage nodes) applies: a split that would need a new node is not a file split, stop and say so.

PROOF: water nextest and the mapped contract filters; GPU proofs scoped by gpu_proofs_gate.py for the kernels whose files moved; byte-identical bundled preset stills.
NO NEW FRAMEWORK: no new traits to make the split compile; a function that needs a trait to move was cut in the wrong place.

title: Post-T2 water cleanup: engine seams, water crate internals, docs map, test cut
description:
Post-T2 cleanup of the water seam, run the same way as the post-T1 cleanup (BUG-hkbdp.3, BUG-hkbdp.4, BUG-hkbdp.5: one audited finding per bead, concrete fix shape, existing infrastructure only, landed one at a time). Audit by Fable on 2026-10-10 at 7f732cb0f; this epic is the brief for the Opus 5.5 lead. Peter's goals: fewer and faster water tests and landings, slop and over-engineering out, seam bugs fixed at the root, a water crate that can be changed in an afternoon and trusted on stage.

GOALS (acceptance for the epic)
1. The engine knows node pairs, substep regions, typed CPU wires, instantiation hooks and migration stages. It never knows fluid, liquid, rigid physics or whitewater. Oracle: `rg -c -i 'fluid|liquid|physics|whitewater' crates/manifold-node-engine/src` outside atomic/fluid_sim_2d, param_tooltips and trigger_shadow_lint (FluidSim2D/3D are image atoms) reaches zero, and the crate_layering test pins it.
2. The water crate carries no half-compiled reference engine: CPU FLIP is either deleted from the product or lives under one cfg at a module root (decision bead). No per-item `#[cfg(feature = "gpu-proofs")]` in production files.
3. No production file in manifold-nodes-water over 1.5k lines; tests live in sibling `_tests.rs` files, never inline beside kernels.
4. A water-touching landing gate runs under 15 minutes end to end, and the water GPU proof minutes drop by at least half, with a before/after map of contract to test that shows no public contract lost coverage.
5. One authoritative water map doc; every other water design doc is a cited contract or archived.

BASELINE (2026-10-10, main at 7f732cb0f; re-measure the same way before and after)
- Engine files still naming water concepts: 74 (`rg -l -i 'fluid|liquid|physics|whitewater' crates/manifold-node-engine/src`).
- Water crate: 297 files, about 78k production lines and 28k test lines; eight files over 1.9k lines (physics.rs 4793, fluid.rs 3474, gpu_flip_step.rs 3148, gpu_flip_step_tests.rs 3136, gpu_flip_pressure_tests.rs 2503, liquid_surface_tests.rs 2059, gpu_flip_clock.rs 2046, whitewater_step.rs 1958).
- Tests: 897 `#[test]` in the water crate (834 run in about 1 minute, keep), 81 in manifold-nodes/tests/contracts/water, 192 in manifold-nodes/tests/gpu_proofs (14 water files), 54 in manifold-app renderer_contracts/gpu_proofs (liquid_conformance.rs alone: 30 tests, 2632 lines), 95 water-ish in manifold-app catalog_tests, 142 in manifold-physics, 122 in manifold-fluids.
- GPU proof time (scripts/gpu_test_times.json merged with the learned cache in the git common dir, scratch script `times.py`): water-related tests account for 113 of 158 recorded minutes; 30 water tests over 60 s, 125 over 10 s. Slowest: liquid_coupled_live_frame_rate 277 s, liquid_live_flip_force_and_coupling_match_accepted_progress 226 s, gpu_flip_density_projection_settled_column_depth_and_density 207 s, matter_collider_penetration_bounded 310 s, matter_fill_skips_colliders 261 s, matter_body_reaction_counts_field_velocity 249 s.
- Landing gate time for the last two water landings (gate-passes records summed per commit): 53 min (7b9fba333, 57 legs) and 62 min (d6c8149ab, 57 legs).
- Bundled water presets render byte-identical to main across five stills each (WaterDamBreakGpuFlip, WaterDamBreakMatter via `target/debug/examples/fluid_capture` through scripts/gpu_queue.py); that stays the render oracle for every landing here.

ORDER
1. The CPU FLIP decision bead first; it removes the most code and the most proof minutes, and every later cut gets smaller.
2. Engine seam moves (A beads) can run in parallel with it; they touch different files.
3. Water internals (B beads) after the CPU FLIP cut lands.
4. Docs map and lifecycle sweep after A and B.
5. The test cut (D bead, with BUG-hkbdp.1) last, so no test pinned to a seam about to move is cut twice.

RULES FOR THE LEAD
- One lane per bead, one commit per lane, lead reviews and lands with scripts/land_branch.py. Lanes never land.
- Fix at the root; no shims, no new framework, no new shared state, no new feature flags.
- Every bead's close reason states the before/after numbers for its goal line.
- Peter reviews the test cut list before any deletion (BUG-hkbdp.1 rule).
- Unverified claims are reported as unverified.

title: GPU FLIP surface: one level set, drawn directly, mesh only on export
description:
Sub-epic 4 of the GPU FLIP end game (docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md D2 and section 3). Reused from the old surface qualification epic.

Build one high-quality signed-distance level set from the particles, once, and feed both the solver and the renderer. Draw the water straight from it (sphere tracing, D2). No mesh in the live path: marching cubes, the smoothing passes, the normals pass, the welded mesh and the mesh's ray-tracing structure all leave it. Marching cubes stays as an offline export tool only.

Until direct rendering lands the mesh path still ships. So the mesh cost, overflow and look beads below stay open as export-path and interim items, and each carries a note saying so. BUG-kipwz (mesh held as five copies) is the stopgap that unblocks exports before then and lives in the Memory sub-epic.

The look: engine defaults are the look (particle scale 3.0, subdivision 1, smoothing 0.5 x 2). The engine-default look was tuned on the smoothed mesh, so direct rendering needs a look pass against the FLIP Fluids reference exports, with a grid-side blur replacing the mesh smoothing.

Original scope, kept: liquid level set, surface extraction, smoothing, mesh and index generation, render surface look and surface-local cost. Whitewater belongs to BUG-imy3 (GPU whitewater); pressure and coupling belong to the Simulation sub-epic.

End state on stage: one high-quality level set built once from the particles and drawn directly in raster and ray tracer. The mesh exists only on export.

title: Physics scenes can lose all bodies after returning from an export (offline-to-live history moves backward)
description: Symptom (static trace, unverified at runtime): after an export, returning to the saved position can make a physics scene reject its input history ("physics input history cannot move backward within an epoch"), which renders zero bodies. Root cause (Astra, static): at unchanged resolution content_pipeline.rs:3679 keeps runtimes and generator_renderer.rs:1821 keeps generator state across stop; export restoration (content_export.rs:494) seeks back without resetting generators. If the saved position is more than two intervals past the last exported frame, physics_sampling.rs:381 samples with the clock's old offline policy, then physics.rs:1112 advances live, caps and reanchors, and records an earlier timestamp that input.rs:122 rejects. Fix shape: set the current execution policy before historical sampling and use the same policy for clock advancement, so accepted history is never rewritten. Add transition tests for export return, both mode directions, and seeks. Found while fixing BUG-3zx1n (physics_boxes proof switches offline to live mid-run). Paths are pre-crate-split (manifold-renderer).
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — evidence. Remaining: Reproduce export-to-live seek on a physics project and capture the first history rejection before changing generator reset policy. Evidence in record: source-only (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-10-07T15:48:06Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. title: GPU FLIP coupled bodies: light and floating boxes never come to rest
description: One family, likely one root: the water push on a coupled box is noisy tick to tick, and light boxes amplify it. FLIP Fluids has no two-way rigid coupling, so this layer is ours (MANIFOLD-owned rigid coupling in the CPU engine, GPU FLIP matched to it only on short reaction scenes). No proof covers a light box settling over a long run. First step: a GPU FLIP light-body settling proof (energy and rest speed over 30 s at densities 20, 100, 500), then the root. title: Box3D hull cook traps the app on a photoscan Collision Proxy
description: Symptom: fluid_role_source with Geometry Collision Proxy on coastal_cliff_02 (Poly Haven), fragment_count 8 / fragment_index 3, any collider_parts (64, 48, 40), kills the process with SIGTRAP and no message, at preset load. Crash stack: b3InternalAssert <- b3HullBuilder_NewFace <- b3CreateHull <- manifold_box3d_cook_hull <- manifold_physics::cook_hull <- physics_mesh::prepare_colliders <- fluid_role_source::geometry::prepare_geometry. Root cause: B3_ASSERT(b->faceCount < b->faceCapacity) in crates/manifold-physics/native/box3d/src/hull.c b3HullBuilder_NewFace: quickhull on the near-coplanar shell points prepare_colliders makes (each scan triangle offset +-0.05% of the extent) creates more interim faces than the pool holds. Asserts are compiled in, so release traps too. Fix shape: size the face/edge pools from the input point count (or grow them) and return a NULL hull instead of asserting, so cook_hull reports PhysicsError and the role falls back or errors by name; add a CPU test that cooks piece 3 of the scan. Stopgap in OceanCliff.json: the right gully wall uses pieces 5 and 4 instead of 3.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Size or grow hull face/edge pools for the scan, return a NULL hull as PhysicsError instead of asserting, and add the piece-3 CPU regression. title: GPU FLIP pushes a light box tilted into a corner down instead of up (lost wet gap)
description: Symptom: liquid_lift_off on GPU FLIP. A density-0.3 box, 0.4 m, tilted 0.3 rad with one bottom edge on the floor and one side edge on the -x wall, under 1 m of water (48 cells, dx 0.05). From the first tick the reaction points down and into the wall (tick 1: J = (-8.7, -2.6, 0.1) N*s at 30 Hz, L_z = +1.5; fully wetted hydrostatic reference is about (0, +20.9, 0)). The box is slammed flat into the corner within about 20 ticks and stays pinned with J about (-52, -48, 0) per tick: pressure on its top and +x faces, none on its bottom and -x faces. MPM lifts the same box by tick 21. Failing before the body handoff work too (P13 red run: 39% water lost; now 0.08%, 49307 refused push-outs summed over ticks). Root cause unknown. Leading suspect (Astra consult 2026-10-06): the thin wet gap under and beside the box is lost on the grid: liquid_fill seeding, phi_into_solids only extends wetness near existing particles, open_fractions corner sampling, or closest_body giving gap faces to the wall instead of the body. Decisive check: capture the first pressure solve on the wedge cells and their faces before any motion (particle count, phi/water, open volume, face fraction, owner, pressure, signed face_impulse) and sum by body side. A dry wedge confirms the wet-mask cause; wet cells with collapsed geometry or wall ownership point elsewhere. Reference for unresolved thin gaps: Qiu, Yu, Fedkiw 2015. Also blocks the tilted fixture in liquid_handover_agreement. Conformance exemptions to remove when fixed: GPU FLIP LiftOff and HandoverAgreement in liquid/conformance.rs.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — evidence. comments.text: Measured 2026-10-06, still 1 m pool, density 100, median body speed (|v|+|w|r above g*dt) over 30-60 s: Sim Rate 60 0.138 m/s, 30 0.228, 15 0.537; res 64 at 30 Hz 0.206 (resolution-independent). title: GPU FLIP velocity extrapolation runs 12 full-grid layers three times a substep (largest step cost group at res 64)
description: gpu_flip_step.rs extend() dispatches extend_faces over every face record for each of step.band layers (12 at CFL 5, engine parity) at three call sites per substep (extend_old, extend_new, extend_spread; plus the narrow-band extend_old). Each layer reads a 32-byte record and six neighbours for every invalid face and writes every record (ping-pong). Complete per-dispatch split on main 77a67783d, waterFunv3 res 64 calm (ratios): extend_old 6.5, extend_new 4.3, extend_spread 4.1 = 14.9 ms, level with the pressure smoother (13.7). Faces farther than L layers from the initially valid set cannot change at layer L. Fix shape: band-limited or tile-culled layers (indirect dispatch over tiles near valid faces, with the far region made consistent once), or shared-memory multi-layer blocking, or in-place layers with a layer stamp; output byte-identical at every call site.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text:
Peter requested a broader correctness/cost audit on 2026-10-05, explicitly beyond fragmentation, and questioned the shipped density correction. Source review at 18a3e41df: the recorded off result is volume gain (21.5% excessive settled column depth, interior 6.6/8), not proof of mass loss. gpu_flip_scene_tests::column_depth is a highest-marker-per-column estimate plus 0.25h, not measured liquid mesh volume or retained particle mass. The exact cause of particle dilution remains unisolated; do not state that pressure projection alone guarantees particle packing or that CPU FLIP holds volume exactly. Older GPU_FLIP_PRESSURE_SOLVE measurements report native volume gain too, under different fixtures.

Density correction executes every substep, re-prepares the pressure hierarchy on the plain mask, solves again and extends the spread velocity for 12 layers. Its displacement is not included in stored particle velocity or body reaction. It can change potential energy and future transfers; the source comment saying it cannot add speed is not proof of dynamically neutral motion (see BUG-5oxx). The density solve ignores the separating-contact mask, so audit the two together. Need a bounded, same-input/current-tip on/off comparison of motion, energy, retained count, volume and cost, including wall/collider contact. Do not disable the production default solely from this audit or attribute reported appearance to it without reproduction. No app code or new runtime measurements in this audit.

With separation off, density off GPU median2.795ms/encode3.468ms; density on4.261ms/5.236ms. Separation on changes results modestly here. Native wall median9.122ms. Probe test passed34.59s. No renderer/mesh or64^3 performance/visual claim. Investigate wall/grid/transport before default removal.

title: Freeze region capacity probe admits an output that follows slot 0 as MinInputs
description: Symptom: a buffer atom whose Array output capacity follows ONE input (slot 0) but which declares the default FusedOutputCapacity::MinInputs is admitted into a fused buffer region, and the fused output is then sized to the min over ALL array externals. If another external is smaller, the fused dst is too small. Found on feat/liquid-seam-build with node.clamp_liquid_to_solids (levelset coincident, coarse solid lattice gathered): fused into Smooth Z, the fused dst took the solid lattice size (71^3) instead of the level set (211^3); count_surface_triangles and volume_surface_mesh refused it by name, so nothing was corrupted. A consumer that does not check its extent would read or write out of bounds on the GPU, the machine-lock class. Root cause: the honesty probe in crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/freeze/region.rs (BufferGather output-capacity admission, around line 1895, slot_synthetics) gives each external slot one DISTINCT ASCENDING synthetic capacity (1009 + 1000*e). An output that follows slot 0 equals min(...) under that single ordering, so the black-box array_output_capacity agrees with the composed Min and the declaration passes. Fix shape: probe a second, descending ordering (or probe each slot alone at a larger value) and require agreement under every ordering, so a follows-one-input atom declared MinInputs is refused (renders unfused) until it declares FromInput. Add a region test with a two-input atom whose capacity follows slot 0 declared MinInputs, asserting the region is refused. The clamp now declares FromInput { input: levelset }, which is its true shape.
notes:
Fixed at the root on feat/fft-water in c708d7ff8 (the capacity probe also runs descending, so an output that follows one input is refused as MinInputs). Found independently by the SWASH worker via collar_source (32,769 of 262,144 cells at 64). Regression test owed on that branch. Closes when feat/fft-water lands.
Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Add the middle-slot MinInputs probe and a regression covering its missing-input path. title: GPU FLIP end game: the fastest real-time water on consumer hardware
description:
The goal is fast, low-memory, real-time GPU FLIP water: the fastest and most efficient GPU FLIP simulation there is, on consumer hardware, live on stage. The live path keeps no mesh. Export to other apps is out of scope. Bakes are low priority. Benchmarks come last, if at all.

The governing insight: the simulation is small. At resolution 128 the solver's own state is about 100 MB. Everything that made water expensive on this machine sits beside the solver: a surface mesh held as five copies, a ray-tracing structure rebuilt from it every frame, a display ring that copies the mesh per slot, and dense passes over a box that is mostly air. Remove those and the only cost left is wet cells plus particles, which is what a state-of-the-art sparse solver pays and no more.

Where we stand (measured 2026-10-03, five speed landings since, none re-measured): resolution 64 costs 64 ms a frame. Resolution 128 costs 461 ms. Forces and hits land 75 to 110 ms behind the beat. Exports at 128 Surface Detail 1 and at 192 die on GPU memory. The first job is the fresh number; no speed lane starts before it.

Assumed headline target, Peter's call: 128 at 60 fps display with the sim at 30 steps a second on the M4 Max, plus a 512 overnight export.

Sub-epics, in attack order:
0. BUG-l2h3.26 (Measurement and tooling): every speed and memory claim is a fresh number at 64 and 128, GPU busy percent is reported, the water's memory is fully accounted.
1. BUG-l2h3.27 (Simulation): the sim at 128 costs what 64 costs today, never jitters, holds volume like the engine, floating bodies settle, and FLIP transfers like MPM (APIC).
2. BUG-l2h3.28 (Memory): memory follows the water; budgets of 128 live under 2 GB, 256 solver state under 1 GB, 512 export inside 36 GB, reported per landing.
3. BUG-l2h3.29 (Live timing and display): water reacts within a frame of the beat at 24, 30 or 60 fps; the display ring holds grids, not meshes.
4. BUG-651ho (Surface): one high-quality level set built once from the particles and drawn directly in raster and ray tracer; the mesh exists only on export.
5. BUG-l2h3.30 (Rendering): the same water under raster and ray tracer; refraction and caustics that read as water; spray as spheres; particle velocity in the motion blur; foam as a field on the surface.
6. BUG-imy3 (Whitewater simulation): spray, foam and bubbles always refilling, matched to the engine, feeling wind and solids.
7. BUG-l2h3.31 (Instrument and authoring): driven bodies, audio-shaped waves, wave tanks that do not resonate, the ocean feeding the tank, action areas inside a height-field sea.

title: MPM solver budget (6 or 12 ms): Peter decides at P4 from P1b numbers and the side-by-side
description: GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md P1 kill check (Water kernel, look gates and the cost probe). Probe: crates/manifold-renderer/tests/gpu_proofs/matter_cost_probe.rs on feat/gpu-mpm-build-b (3a579a2ff), M4 Max, no other GPU work. 64 cubed cells, 4 m, Stiffness 1, 34 substeps. At 524,288 points: production GPU 54.5 ms per frame. Profiled per frame: P2G 45.0 ms, G2P 7.5, clear 1.4, grid update 1.0, stats 0.55. Projection 2.94 ns per point-substep x 500,000 x 34 + lattice 2.3 + stats 0.55 = 53 ms. Cause: P2G is atomic-bound (108 global atomic adds per point, about 43e9 adds/s, same-address conflicts from 8 points per cell in fill order). G2P already runs at about 420 GB/s of the 546 GB/s roofline. Floor if lever L1 (cell-sorted block P2G) removed every atomic: G2P + clear + grid + stats + P2G point reads = about 12.6 ms; with L2 and L3 at their section 8 estimates, about 10 to 11 ms. The P4 6 ms gate is out of reach at 500k points x 34 substeps on this machine. Options: (a) run P1b anyway and measure L1 to L5 against a budget near 10 to 13 ms; (b) Peter-only levers from section 8 (resolution 48 about 0.4x, Stiffness 0.5 about 0.6x, budget 6 to 12 ms); (c) stop MPM. L1 sort can reuse the surface branch PrefixScan and counting-sort pattern. Rest of P1 (look gates A1 to A6, presets, momentum test) waits on this call.
notes:
Decided 2026-09-30 by the lead: option (a). Run P1b as designed (L1 cell-sorted block P2G, L2 shared-memory G2P tiles, L3 half-precision affine only if every P1 gate holds, L5 dispatch trimming); no dial, threshold or numerics changes. Re-probe at 125k, 250k and 500k points for Stiffness 1 and 0.5. The 6 ms or 12 ms budget is Peter, decided at P4 on real numbers plus the side-by-side.
