title: Material fidelity follow-through: SSS qualification and hybrid RT boundaries
description:
MANIFOLD has a substantial real-time PBR implementation, but it does **not** currently support all materials faithfully or provide consistently physically correct rendering. The core metallic/roughness, lighting, texture and material-editing infrastructure is real; several advanced features are approximations, and some ordinary glTF material inputs are ignored.

This review covers Rust source at `7328598c1b576b0cbb66c529b50df61906d6c7eb`, including material atoms, glTF import, texture conversion, the material inspector, scene and standalone mesh rendering, native Metal ray tracing, and existing proof coverage. Main advanced to `38e706d5d` during the review through unrelated waveform changes; a diff check confirmed the reviewed material, shader and proof paths were unchanged. Other worktrees and their unlanded features were not audited. “Supported” below means traced through the implementation, not independently certified across every asset. No application code was changed. Rigid-body physics is outside this review; physically based shading is the subject.

| Material feature | Current support | Practical limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Metallic/roughness PBR | Implemented, incomplete | GGX, Fresnel and split-sum IBL exist, but an MR texture replaces rather than multiplies the factors. |
| Base colour and emission | Implemented | Factor × texture is present in raster rendering; secondary RT hits lose some base-colour information. |
| Normal mapping and AO | Partial | Tangent-space normals and occlusion maps exist; normal scale and AO strength are ignored. |
| Subsurface scattering | **No full SSS model found** | No scattering radius/profile, diffusion or random-walk surface transport. Skin, wax and marble cannot be represented faithfully. |
| Thin translucency | Approximation | Wrap-diffuse backlighting and tinted shadow-ray transmission exist; diffuse-transmission textures and independent colour are not applied. |
| Anisotropy | Implemented, incorrect glTF parameter mapping | Tangent-oriented GGX and a bent-normal environment approximation exist; RT rays remain isotropic. |
| Clearcoat | Implemented with correctness defects | Coat response gets Fresnel twice and inherits the base normal map when no coat normal is supplied. |
| Sheen / velvet | Approximation | Charlie distribution with Ashikhmin visibility; GGX environment lookup reused and no base-layer energy compensation. |
| Iridescence / thin film | Implemented, needs correction/qualification | Thin-film evaluation exists, but its angle-dependent result is treated as F0 and passed through Schlick again. |
| Glass / refraction | Screen-space approximation | Refraction, roughness blur, absorption and dispersion exist. Only the opaque scene snapshot is sampled; nested transparent objects and off-screen transport are not generally represented. |
| Volume | Absorption only in this material path | Beer–Lambert attenuation is not volumetric multiple scattering or SSS. Separate scene fog/shafts do not supply a surface scattering model. |
| Specular / IOR | Partial | Dielectric F0 is configurable; specular weight is not respected at grazing angles. |
| Legacy specular/glossiness | Lossy conversion | Converted to metal/rough; textured specular colour is discarded. |
| Unlit, Phong and Cel | Implemented | Intentional alternative shading models, with renderer and import limitations; they are not all physically based models. |
| Arbitrary DCC materials | No general interpreter | Blender-assisted imports convert to glTF; this does not preserve arbitrary Blender shader networks or every Principled BSDF feature. |

The most consequential findings, in priority order:

1. **P1 — Metallic/roughness factors are ignored when a texture is connected.** `resolve_mr()` returns sampled G/B directly. The loader retains the scalar factors, and the texture conversion shader does not bake them, so this is a real missing operation. For example, a texture with G=0.8 and roughnessFactor=0.25 produces roughness 0.8 rather than 0.2. This affects ordinary imported assets, not only exotic extensions. The inspector even blocks some look changes because the map owns these values; that protects against ineffective edits but does not repair import fidelity. Multiply texture channels by factors consistently in raster and RT, then revisit those ownership restrictions. [Shader](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:1028>), [texture conversion](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/gltf_texture_blit.wgsl:36>), [edit restriction](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-editing/src/commands/material.rs:225>). The multiplication rule is explicit in the [glTF material specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/main/specification/2.0/Specification.adoc).

2. **P2 — Transmission samples an already exposed image, then applies exposure again.** The opaque pass writes its final exposed colour; that result is copied into `opaque_scene_color`. The glass shader samples it into `base_rgb`, and subsequently multiplies by the same camera exposure. The transmitted part therefore acquires two exposure multipliers. This is a source-backed finding; the attempted runtime probe did not reach rendering, as recorded below. Preserve scene-linear, unexposed radiance across the transmission seam or explicitly undo/reapply exposure at the correct boundary. [Opaque snapshot](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/render_scene.rs:4542>), [sample](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:1249>), [final exposure](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:2008>).

3. **P2 — Anisotropy does not implement the imported extension's roughness semantics.** Current code uses `at = a*(1+s)` and `ab = a*(1-s)`. glTF specifies `at = mix(a, 1, s*s)` with `ab = a`. With roughness=0.5 and strength=0.8, MANIFOLD uses approximately `(0.45, 0.05)` instead of `(0.73, 0.25)`. That changes highlight width and shape substantially. In addition, RT samples an isotropic GGX lobe, then substitutes it into the anisotropic raster material. [Raster mapping](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:1633>), [RT sampling](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/shadow_rays.msl:1369>), [Khronos definition](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/main/extensions/2.0/Khronos/KHR_materials_anisotropy/README.md). Correct the parameter mapping and explicitly qualify or implement anisotropic RT.

4. **P2 — Clearcoat applies Fresnel twice and uses the wrong default normal.** The direct coat BRDF already includes `F_coat`, and the coat IBL already includes its Fresnel-weighted split sum; final composition multiplies both by another `clearcoat * Fresnel`. At normal incidence the direct layer receives approximately 0.04² instead of one 0.04 factor. Separately, the fallback coat normal is the already normal-mapped base normal; glTF requires an unmapped coat when no coat normal texture is supplied. [Coat BRDF](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:1761>), [composition](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:2004>), [normal fallback](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:1150>), [Khronos layering and normals](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/main/extensions/2.0/Khronos/KHR_materials_clearcoat/README.md).

5. **P2 — Specular weight does not disable the complete reflection lobe.** The implementation scales F0 but always approaches white at grazing angles; the IBL bias also remains unweighted. Thus `specularFactor=0` still produces grazing reflection. The source acknowledges this limitation. Coloured specular also uses componentwise diffuse reduction rather than the extension's scalar maximum-component reduction. [F0 and limitation](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:1575>), [direct Fresnel](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:1701>), [Khronos specular weighting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/main/extensions/2.0/Khronos/KHR_materials_specular/README.md).

6. **P2 — Texture support is not complete end to end.** Only UV0 is imported. The five core texture families carry transforms/samplers, while extension maps sample raw UVs and reuse core samplers. Normal scale and AO strength are reported as unsupported, not applied. Varying vertex colours are dropped; specular/glossiness texture RGB is discarded. Unlit imports have an existing transform/sampler issue, `BUG-dwv1`. These limits affect layered paint, patterned fabric, authored normal detail and secondary UV workflows. [Extension sampling](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:1066>), [UV limitations](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/gltf_load.rs:3774>), [normal/AO/vertex-colour report](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/gltf_import/object_group.rs:146>), [spec-gloss repack](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/gltf_texture_blit.wgsl:42>).

7. **P2 — Ray-traced secondary hits do not evaluate the same material as the raster view.** RT's compact material table does not carry the shading-model discriminator or advanced PBR lobes. At a reflection hit, a sampled base-colour texture replaces the factor, metallic/roughness use flat values, dielectric F0 is fixed at 0.04, and diffuse environment energy is added without the metal/Fresnel suppression used by raster PBR. Secondary-hit normal mapping and most per-map transforms/samplers are also absent. Glass and blend draws are excluded from the acceleration input. Consequently, a surface and its reflection need not agree, and enabling RT cannot make all material families physically correct. [Material table](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/raytrace/params.rs:233>), [secondary-hit shading](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/shadow_rays.msl:2234>), [transparent exclusion](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/render_scene.rs:2759>). Existing `BUG-yrca` and `BUG-k16z` cover related parity/proof debt; the full discrepancy is wider.

8. **P2 — The same Material wire has different capabilities in different renderers.** `render_scene` has the advanced path. `render_mesh` and `render_copies` upload only the older subset, treat Blend as opaque coverage, use a single environment mip with heuristic roughness attenuation, and interpret normal maps differently. Advanced PBR fields can therefore be accepted but unused. Consolidate material evaluation or make unsupported capabilities explicit at the connection. [Standalone mesh uniforms](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/render_3d_mesh.rs:248>), [legacy IBL](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_3d_mesh.wgsl:278>), [copies uniforms](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/render_instanced_3d_mesh.rs:216>).

9. **P2 — Advanced scattering and layering need an honest capability boundary.** The current translucency term adds wrapped backlighting without reducing the front diffuse lobe; it is a useful leaf/petal effect, not full SSS. Diffuse-transmission colour and textures are explicitly discarded. Sheen uses a GGX lookup approximation and adds energy without compensating the underlying layer. Iridescence is evaluated once at N·V and then reused as F0 for another Fresnel evaluation, including direct lights; it should be audited against the intended angular Fresnel model. [Translucency](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:1779>), [ignored inputs](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/gltf_load.rs:3687>), [sheen IBL](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:1889>), [additive layering](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:1951>), [iridescence](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:1605>). Compare the [sheen model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/main/extensions/2.0/Khronos/KHR_materials_sheen/README.md), [diffuse transmission model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/main/extensions/2.0/Khronos/KHR_materials_diffuse_transmission/README.md), and [iridescence model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/main/extensions/2.0/Khronos/KHR_materials_iridescence/README.md).

10. **P2 — Lighting and geometry transforms limit physical fidelity too.** Point lights use `1/(1+d²/range²)` rather than physical inverse-square attenuation and glTF range semantics. Imported spots become omnidirectional points. Raster normals use the model matrix directly, which is wrong under nonuniform scale; RT documents a matching approximation. Correct materials cannot compensate for incorrect incoming light or surface normals. [Falloff](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:288>), [spot/range conversion](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/gltf_import/scene.rs:425>), [normal transform](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl:848>), [Khronos punctual lights](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/main/extensions/2.0/Khronos/KHR_lights_punctual/README.md).

Several foundations are sound in shape: the raster path distinguishes sRGB colour maps from linear data maps, performs lighting in floating-point targets, includes split-sum environment lighting, supports alpha cutouts and sorted blending, carries authored tangents, and routes material edits through validated undoable commands. Base-colour/emissive multiplication is present. These are implementation observations, not a claim that every combination has been visually certified.

Peter additionally reports glass producing strange cuts and grid-like blocky lines. That exact symptom has **not yet been reproduced** against a named project/object. There are three concrete implementation risks to check against it: (a) the screen-space transmission texture uses the environment sampler with horizontal `Repeat`, so off-screen refraction wraps to the opposite screen edge; (b) transparent sorting uses object-origin depth, not per-triangle or per-pixel ordering, and glass depth writes are disabled; (c) refraction samples a fixed opaque-colour snapshot without a refracted-depth intersection test, and roughness blur uses ordinary image mips. These can explain seams, incorrect overlaps or coarse blur in particular scenes, but matching the user's grid requires an observed reproduction. [Transmission sampler binding](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/render_scene.rs:4224>), [horizontal Repeat](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/render_scene.rs:6443>), [object sorting](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/render_scene.rs:4364>), [depth writes disabled](</Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/render_scene.rs:2275>).

Validation is narrower than the feature inventory. I ran `cargo test --manifest-path '/Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/Cargo.toml' -p manifold-renderer --features gpu-proofs --test gpu_proofs render_scene_ibl::roughness -- --nocapture --test-threads=1`. The sandbox attempt could not obtain a Metal device. The same focused test outside the sandbox passed: low-roughness peak spread **0.1001**, high-roughness **0.4948**, meeting its ≥3× criterion. This proves the named roughness response, not full BRDF correctness. The source findings above have not all been independently reproduced on GPU.

I prepared two 96×96 neutral-glass/exposure scenes but did not obtain rendered images. Building the existing `render-import` tool first failed because the sandbox denied sccache access. The permitted build outside the sandbox then failed with E0599 at `clip_content_gpu.rs:365`, calling `content_fingerprint()` on `Arc<WaveformRenderer>`, while the unrelated waveform commits above landed. The method exists in the final source; this review does not establish a persistent waveform defect or the exact build-race mechanism. I stopped the visual probe instead of using an unverified old binary or widening the review into build repair. The prepared graphs are [EV0](glass-ev0.json) and [EV1](glass-ev1.json); they are unexecuted reproduction inputs, not passing tests.

The checked-in Khronos manifest contains **148 entries: 135 expect_pass and 13 xfail**. These are classifications, not fresh results from this review. Four xfails are diffuse-transmission/scattering assets, including ScatteringSkull. Most checks establish nonblank output or similarity to MANIFOLD's own goldens; they cannot independently validate material equations. The suite called `render_scene_glass` primarily tests alpha blending, ordering and shadows, not the complete refractive material. There are useful map, RT and white-furnace proofs, but no comprehensive independent energy/reciprocity/material-extension matrix was established here. I did not run a broad conformance sweep.

The recommended order is to fix factor multiplication and transmission/exposure first, then clearcoat/specular/anisotropy and texture-coordinate fidelity, then explicitly reconcile raster versus RT and legacy renderer capabilities. Full SSS should be a separately specified feature with a chosen real-time quality/performance target. Acceptance should include analytic numeric tests, controlled paired renders and independent reference comparisons for each supported family, especially feature combinations; updating our own goldens alone is insufficient.
acceptance_criteria: Resolve or explicitly scope each source-backed finding with focused numeric/reference evidence. Preserve undo and saved-project compatibility. Prove MR factor multiplication, exposure through glass, clearcoat/specular/anisotropy semantics, map transforms and sampler ownership, and raster/RT capability boundaries. Do not close based solely on own-golden rebaselines. Provide diffusion and volumetric random-walk SSS with shared controls and honest qualification limits. The withdrawn grid/cuts report is excluded from investigation and acceptance.
notes:
2026-09-26 user correction: there is no grid-like artifact and no search for one is wanted. Drop the hypothetical grid/cuts reproduction from acceptance. Continue only source-backed material corrections and their focused tests. Both SSS modes are implemented in slot-6; landing is still pending.

SSS small-fixture captures were inspected; no production-size frame-rate or universal material certification claim. One new RT proof initially uploaded f32 data into an rgba16 texture; corrected the fixture to rgba32 with a format assertion, then all seven passed. Full d6 landing gate caught missed 80B MeshVertex consumers, unlit identity-UV defaults, integer material-reset validation, stale light enum labels, and obsolete reference assumptions. Fixed causes; focused native Metal mesh/cutout/math-view/lighting/glass checks now pass. Integrated full gate at 00ad92744 passed CPU/clippy, 2693 renderer lib tests, the glTF corpus with no golden drift, and all GPU integration proofs except two authored custom-writer fixtures still naming UV1 as padding. Both are corrected in 2bbb240d6; all three dynamic-catalog GPU proofs now pass. comments.text:
2026-10-09 full materials source review at a9286a95d. New source-backed findings filed as .2-.9: GGX/coat singularities; whole-document image decode per texture source; gray-alpha conversion; anisotropic denominator clamp; WebP texture dimensions; instanced authored glass thickness; Cel emissive-skin activation; SSS history reset by temporal-upscaling jitter. Concrete RT clearcoat-frame mismatch added to BUG-yrca. CPU arithmetic/control-flow counterexamples checked; no Cargo suite, production GPU render, live UI or fresh performance benchmark was run, and no app source was changed.

Additional optimization work: render_scene.wgsl evaluates eval_iridescence per light (:1834) and for IBL (:1974), coat direct/IBL and sheen terms even with zero feature weights. Values are runtime uniforms, so the shader cannot generally statically remove this. Guard inactive lobes using derivative-safe structure or specialize supported feature combinations; profile before assigning a frame-time saving. render_scene.rs still allocates draw/binding/light/transparent arrays per frame (:2135, :4843-4851, :6007, :9446), despite retained RT scratch. Reuse capacity through existing scratch patterns after establishing allocation counts.

Validation gaps: current anisotropy GPU proof uses roughness/strength .5; clearcoat proof uses roughness .25 and constant maps, missing the new edge cases. Khronos manifest still classifies four diffuse-transmission/scattering assets as deferred despite landed support; counts are 135 expect_pass and 13 xfail, not fresh results. Reconcile each asset against its actual remaining unsupported features rather than blanket-promoting it. Existing BUG-5l4o.1 retains production/reference SSS qualification.

Capability boundaries confirmed: imported Unlit becomes lit PBR by Peter's explicit existing policy, with Baked Look opt-in; no doubleSided/cull selection by existing design; full material inspector is PBR-only, generic Cel/Unlit controls remain; arbitrary material texture rewiring is graph-editor-only. KTX2/BasisU has no transcoder (required extension rejects; optional extension-only runtime source lookup can fail instead of displaying reported magenta dummy); external-URI WebP explicitly unsupported; decoded 16-bit PNG formats rejected by load_gltf_texture. These are missing capabilities or disclosed approximations, not newly reproduced crashes. Report supplied in chat.

title: MacBook brightness changes cause reported stutter after HDR presentation rework
description: Peter reports stutters when changing MacBook screen brightness after the HDR rework. Read-only diagnosis 2026-09-26: Sep22 commit 2ad52bf0d changed native capability selection from primarily potential headroom to current headroom and app-side dedup from a 0.01 threshold to exact DisplayCapabilities equality. app.rs update_edr_headroom sends every distinct update; content_commands.rs UpdateDisplayCapabilities logs and marks the compositor dirty. session_log.rs synchronously writes file and stderr. Latest retained session-1790383739397-32397.log records 60 workspace headroom updates during 00:49:00Z, but this is the startup ramp, NOT a reproduction of the reported brightness-adjustment stutter. retarget_if_needed returns false when display ID is unchanged, so ordinary headroom changes do not statically restart the display link. No observed frame-time correlation or proven root cause; no app changes or new GPU runs. Next: establish whether visual playback, UI, or both hitch; use one bounded brightness adjustment with frame timing and event/log attribution, then fix the demonstrated cause. Preserve current-headroom correctness, independent destination state and display-independent export. Related native display acceptance remains BUG-qdn7.
acceptance_criteria: Brightness changes update presentation without avoidable playback or UI stalls, demonstrated by a bounded before/after observation. No change to project data, creative effects, export pixels, or transport timing from monitor brightness changes.
notes:
2026-09-26 bounded baseline: isolated unmodified commit7328598c1 app built with ui-automation,profiling. Launcher permit-store mismatch resolved; first actual child exited because another app held single-instance lock. When that app exited naturally, test launch succeeded. Empty UI steady baseline approx120Hz with ~1.5ms UI CPU; loading HeadGlitchV2 then hit pre-existing glyph_atlas retained-output debug assertion during warmup, before playback. No brightness adjustment occurred and no stutter cause established; native probe stopped after this inconclusive result. Separate colour control work BUG-zpb3 does not claim to fix stutter.
GPU reproduction 2026-09-26: production PresentationPipeline maps input [1.0, 0.9, 0.5, 0.75] to [0.9526367, 0.89208984, 0.5, 0.75] at current headroom 1.001, while headroom 1.0 preserves SDR white. The old knee at 0.8 * headroom enters the SDR range, causing a visible discontinuity. Focused real Metal test failed as expected; log /private/tmp/hdr-white-baseline-proof.log. Repair in codex/hdr-colour-repair holds the knee at or above white and caps highlights; validation pending. This supports the reported headroom-pumping hypothesis but does not establish dropped-frame timing; native playback observation remains outstanding.
Repair verification: the focused Metal gate passed all 16 presentation/policy tests, including constant SDR white across headrooms 1.0, 1.001, 1.01, 1.1, 1.25 and 2.0, and bounded monotonic HDR highlights across 1.0 through 4.0. Log /private/tmp/hdr-colour-gpu-proof.log. Physical brightness-adjustment playback remains unverified; keep this issue open for that observation.
The independently proven SDR-white headroom discontinuity repair (4c69f6c99) is now landed/pushed in main 1d3e4d484. Final presentation GPU checks and full GPU suite passed. This establishes stable white and bounded highlights across headroom changes, not a physical dropped-frame/stutter fix. Physical brightness-adjustment playback acceptance remains open.
Backlog review 2026-10-09 — evidence. Remaining: Reproduce the reported brightness-change stutter with current HDR presentation and correlate it with capability/headroom changes; the retained startup log is not that reproduction. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-09-26T04:36:46Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. Original scope and acceptance remain authoritative.

title: Physics: qualify automatic fast contacts and large copied-body cost
description: Landed 386b2a35b: runtime selects Box3D bullet mode for Dynamic bodies predicted to move more than half their smallest scale in a fixed tick; fast Animated motion gets up to eight outer steps. No user CCD setting. Remaining: measure Physics CPU and lag at representative 256 and 4000 copy counts, test high-speed Dynamic versus Dynamic and extreme Animated sweeps, and refine policy if cost or missed contacts require it.
acceptance_criteria: Representative Physics CPU/lag measurements are recorded for 256 and 4000 copies; focused fast-contact matrix covers Dynamic versus Animated, Dynamic versus Dynamic, and extreme Animated sweeps; limits and policy are documented without requiring user configuration.
notes:

title: Hidden raster/RT shadow limits change scene appearance
description:
A scene with eight shadow-enabled lights silently changes shadow coverage when switching between raster and ray tracing. All eight lights can still illuminate the scene, but raster allocates four shadow maps while RT supports eight shadow-caster slots. Lights beyond a backend's budget contribute unshadowed light. The light's castShadows setting does not communicate this difference, so users cannot readily understand why the same scene changes appearance.

Peter explicitly reported this as hidden and confusing on 2026-09-22. Treat it as a user-facing correctness and authoring consistency issue, not just an internal documentation task.

The related light-caster-contract fix restores RT's intended eight slots and corrects shared Point-light shading, but intentionally retains raster's four-map budget. It does not resolve this issue. Four and eight are historical software budgets, not hardware limits. Simply changing a constant is insufficient: raster bindings, caster tables, shader bounds, allocation and per-light draw costs must agree.

Relevant code: crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/render_scene.rs (MAX_RASTER_SHADOW_CASTERS and caster collection), crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/raytrace/params.rs (MAX_RT_CASTERS), render_scene.wgsl and shaft_march.wgsl shadow lookup. Existing contracts: docs/RAYTRACING_DESIGN.md section 15.2 and docs/RENDER_SCENE_UNBOUNDED_LIGHTS_DESIGN.md. Confirm exact current code paths before implementation.

Acceptance:
- Define and implement a coherent user-facing shadow policy for raster and RT. Prefer consistent light participation across modes; if a capability difference is necessary, make it explicit and understandable while authoring and switching modes.
- Do not silently discard a requested shadow merely because a light exceeds an undisclosed budget. Make selection and any limit predictable.
- Verify eight shadow-enabled lights, mixtures of Sun and Point lights, reordered/sparse caster selection, overflow and live renderer switching. Verify all lights still contribute illumination as intended.
- Distinguish expected raster/RT technique differences from missing light participation. Cover surfaces and volumetric consumers where the chosen policy applies.
- Evaluate resource and draw cost using existing infrastructure. Do not assume four or eight must remain the final limit, and do not introduce speculative rendering infrastructure.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Read-only finding, 2026-09-07: render_scene.rs:3933 warmup_pending checks only an existing rt_accel ready flag; it does not include rt_accel_pending_key or rt_accel_content_pending_key. evaluate schedules topology/content rebuilds through a one-frame defer (around 5805-5839). generator_renderer.rs:1478 ends prewarm on !generator.warmup_pending after GPU completion. Consequently a deferred rebuild can be omitted from readiness when no other node remains pending; this is a static readiness-contract gap, not a reproduced failure or proven cause of Corrosion hangs. Add a focused deferred-topology/content readiness regression before fixing; distinguish pending deferred work from intentionally continuously changing geometry. Related inspection: trace gate at render_scene.rs:5914 checks topology but not content version. Same topology preserves vertex buffer identity and triangle count, so this mismatch alone does not establish an out-of-bounds access; may be stale geometry/shading. Initial build completion and completion resource pins exist. Warmup is sequential per layer with a GPU wait per rendered frame; uncontrolled simultaneous submission of all layers is not established. No code changes, builds or runtime tests performed. Next bounded audit: shared/mapped RT material and instance buffer writes versus outstanding GPU readers, then accumulation/retirement of resources across warmed layers.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Bounded read-only follow-up: GeneratorRenderer::prewarm_layer allocates a fresh RenderTarget scratch at generator_renderer.rs:1405 each call and pushes it into available_rts at :1498. start_clip consumes at most one pooled target (:509) and stop_clip returns the active target (:1517), so successful repeated warmups accumulate an additional pooled scratch target per call instead of reusing one. No available_rts clear/truncate/retain/drain found in this file. Layer generator state intentionally persists after stop_clip, retaining scene resources until release_all or replacement (:1522-1540); total memory can therefore grow across sequential warmup layers. Image warmup activates all image clips (:438), while outer cleanup stops only first clip (content_commands.rs:302), confirming retained extra image resources. Mapped RT normal/material writes exist but generator and chain warmup wait for each rendered frame; no overlap demonstrated in this bounded warmup audit. RtAccel Drop normally pins resources through retirement completion. Additional failure-path concern: device.rs:1975 retire_on_queue drops pins inline if commandBuffer returns None, assuming GPU stopped without checking completion; no evidence this branch was hit in Corrosion. These are static findings, not proof of root cause; no edits/builds/runtime tests.

comments.text: Concrete memory explanation, read-only: gltf_mesh_source retains per-instance cached_verts Vec plus shared GPU staging plus graph output buffer; for the verified flower geometry each is ~151.7 MB, ~455 MB combined per source before downstream geometry/AS/textures. cached_load_gltf_mesh returns owned Vec via disk cache, not shared resident mesh storage. render_scene::ensure_rt_irradiance (:2627) allocates 39 textures: 32 full-resolution RGBA16F, 2 full-resolution R32F, 2 full-resolution RGBA32F and 3 trace-resolution RGBA16F. This explains a substantial retained working set, not proof of memory exhaustion. No code changes or runtime tests.

comments.text: Additional quantified allocation finding: ensure_rt_masks allocates six full-resolution and three trace-resolution RGBA16F textures (~102.64 MB at crash dimensions). comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Concrete unsafe mechanism found in read-only audit: manifold-renderer/src/uniform_arena.rs push_bytes increases capacity bookkeeping when required size exceeds capacity, but does NOT allocate a larger buffer then. It silently skips the write if aligned+len exceeds buffer.size and still returns the out-of-range offset. flush only allocates afterward. Generator warmup calls uniform_arena.flush AFTER try_commit_and_wait_completed (generator_renderer.rs:1473-1477), so an overflowed frame can submit bindings against the undersized old buffer before growth. This is an actual potential missing/OOB uniform-data path, unlike the memory-pressure hypothesis. Need inspect push consumers and diagnostic log for whether Corrosion exercised it. Not yet established as incident cause; no changes/tests.

Therefore the hypothesized GPU out-of-bounds path is NOT established in current native production and should not be treated as the Corrosion cause. The helper growth behavior is latent, but dead/unused data must not distract this investigation.

comments.text: Static audit finding: dispatch_compute_with_accel declares every bound GpuBinding resource with MTLResourceUsage::Read, including RT-A3a output textures out_sv/out_sv2/out_svt/out_irr/out_n/out_refl that the kernel writes. This is a concrete Metal hazard-tracking/coherency defect candidate under heavy warmup; it can produce GPU faults/timing-sensitive hangs. Not yet proven as the root cause because bypass/pre-ray variants share the dispatch path.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Implemented targeted RT hazard fix in slot-6 crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/encoder.rs: dispatch_compute_with_accel now declares bound textures with MTLTextureUsage::ShaderWrite as MTLResourceUsage::Read|Write; input-only textures remain Read. This covers RT-A3a outputs while leaving regular dispatch behavior unchanged. test_guard.py passed; cargo check was blocked by exhausted execution budget.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Verification result: after changing dispatch_compute_with_accel to declare SHADER_WRITE textures as MTLResourceUsage::Read|Write, Peter ran the normal RT path with Metal validation and GPU diagnostics; no crash occurred. This is strong evidence the prior Read-only hazard declaration caused or materially contributed to the warmup GPU hang. One successful verification is recorded; broader stress testing is intentionally deferred.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Post-fix normal-mode run still crashed. Saved report crash-1788775635.log identifies warmup command buffer hang during INTRO FLOWERS frame 14; RT-A3a encoder[2] is state=2 (affected), not state=4 faulted, so it confirms the command buffer still hangs but does not prove RT-A3a is the originating instruction. Frame/Present encoders are innocent victims. Resource usage fix is insufficient alone; retain it as a real synchronization correction.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Post-fix diagnostic reproduction still confirms RT-A3a as the faulted encoder: diag#3070 warmup encoder[2] state=MTLCommandEncoderErrorState(4), while later upsample/atrous/Frame/Panel buffers are victims. Failure layer d205b27e clip 65af0261 frame 22 at 1080x1920. The Read|Write hazard fix remains valid but does not remove the underlying RT-A3a GPU hang.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Deep audit finding (instancing path): encode_descriptor_build binds descriptor_buffer (GPU-private output) and obj_params but only declares wired source instance buffers via useResource(Read). It never declares descriptor_buffer as Read|Write on the compute encoder. The following TLAS encoder reads that same buffer. This is a concrete missing write-usage declaration and can corrupt TLAS descriptors under instanced scenes. Latest failing run's faulting accel was non-instanced, so this is a related class defect, not the direct cause of that specific frame.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Deep audit finding (cross-frame lifetime): render_scene rewrites CPU-mapped rt_gi_materials, rt_normal_sources, rt_obj_motion, and ShadowRayParams buffers in place every RT frame. GPU trace command buffers are committed asynchronously; these buffers are single shared allocations, not frame-ringed or fenced. This can let a later frame overwrite data while an earlier RT-A3a command still reads it, especially under heavy warmup/playback. Warmup waits per layer, so this is more directly relevant to normal playback overlap, but it is a concrete class-level race to fix/audit.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Follow-up audit: GeneratorRenderer::prewarm_layer commits each warmup encoder with try_commit_and_wait_completed before reusing RT buffers, so the single-buffer CPU rewrite race is unlikely to explain this exact per-layer warmup crash (though it remains a normal-playback bug). The failed run's AS builds completed before tracing. This rules out simple warmup command overlap and keeps the remaining direct suspects in RT-A3a's shader/resource binding or completed-AS contents.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static audit finding (2026-09-07): RT-A3a's only potentially unbounded shader work is the candidate traversal in walk_with_alpha_test() and walk_with_transmission(): while (q.next()) has no iteration cap. Any-hit/alpha/transmission rays can be delivered many candidates on dense foliage, and closest-hit paths intentionally walk every candidate. The failing Corrosion frame is a single 789,958-triangle flat mesh at 270x480, spp=1; prior warmup frames complete ~9.6 ms then frame 23 trips the watchdog (~512 ms), so a frame-specific traversal explosion is plausible even with valid finite rays. This is a concrete class-level risk; the log does not prove alpha mode or candidate count for the failing frame, so treat as leading candidate, not exact proof.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static audit finding (2026-09-07): world_pos_from_depth() rejects NaN/Inf and cleared depth but does not reject near-zero clip w or bound finite world-position magnitude. A tiny finite wh.w can yield enormous finite wp, texel_scale, and ray max distances; rt_validate_ray accepts any finite magnitude. This can create a valid-looking but pathological intersector workload and would explain frame-specific warmup/export hangs. Diagnostic state=0 only proves no NaN/Inf/inverted interval was recorded; it does not test extreme finite values.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static audit of export seam (2026-09-07): export_one_frame() drives the same ContentPipeline::render_content() / node.render_scene RT-A3a dispatch, then waits on the same native completion event before encoding. Warmup uses generator_renderer::render() and try_commit_and_wait_completed() per frame. Thus warmup and export share the RT shader/AS/resource path; export is not a separate encoder bug. Export's wait_for_export_complete only detects GPU fault count/event timeout, so a RT-A3a hang is expected to surface as an export failure too.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static audit finding (2026-09-07): render_scene derives RT triangle_count as ((GpuBuffer.size / sizeof(MeshVertex))/3)*3. ObjectDraw carries no logical vertex count, so an Array buffer's capacity is treated as initialized geometry. Sources such as gltf_mesh_source allocate a max_capacity buffer and upload only cached_verts.len(); the destination retains a larger capacity. If capacity > live data, BLAS/RT can include zero/stale/uninitialized tail vertices, and raw normal/UV fetches can shade them. This is a concrete AS-input validity hole and a plausible shared warmup/export crash class. The failing log's 789,958 triangles exactly match the bound buffer size, but the log does not prove that all those vertices were initialized; add logical-count logging/validation before calling this the exact frame-23 cause.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static audit 2026-09-07: RT-A3a is the first fault during warmup (encoder state Faulted, frame 23, 270x480, 1 spp); later UI/postprocess buffers are victims. Corrosion Azalea source geometry is finite/nondegenerate and its AS buffer matches the declared 2,369,874 vertices, so malformed GLB or simple capacity overclaim is not established for this frame. The shader still performs primary + shadow + AO + GI (2 bounces) + reflection traversal in one monolithic dispatch over a ~790k-triangle BLAS; logs show normal ~9.6ms frames followed by a >0.5s watchdog hang, supporting a variable pathological traversal/workload or resource-pressure class. Warmup and export share render_content/render_scene RT-A3a, so export can share the class. Separate finding: dispatch_compute_with_accel declares every direct buffer Read, including the diagnostics buffer that atomically writes; fix diagnostics usage separately, but it cannot explain diagnostics-off crashes.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Targeted mitigation added in slot-6 (uncommitted): world_pos_from_depth now rejects non-finite/near-zero homogeneous W and finite coordinates beyond 1e6, falling back to raster void handling; RT-A3a diagnostics binding 7 is declared Read|Write in dispatch_compute_with_accel. This is hardening, not proof of the root trigger. cargo check could not run: sccache failed with Operation not permitted, and the prescribed RUSTC_WRAPPER= retry was stopped by the execution-budget guard; git diff --check passes.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Run 2026-09-07 small-hardening: crash persists during INTRO FLOWERS warmup frame 33 (RT frame 33), 270x480, 1 spp. Allocation stayed flat at ~2.13 GB; AS/geometry handle and 151,671,936-byte geometry buffer stayed stable with no rebuild; prior frames were ~6.7–8.2 ms. Warmup command buffer status=5 (GPU hang, ~104.6 ms), but RT-A3a encoder is state=2 Affected, RT-D3/atrous/accumulate are Pending, and UI/Present are InnocentVictim; no encoder state=4 Faulted. RT diagnostics reported no invalid record through frame 32 and validation unavailable on frame 33, so the world-position guard did not fire but also cannot prove inputs valid. This weakens VRAM exhaustion and a confirmed arithmetic fault; current leading class is a frame-specific RT resource/query or synchronization/pathological traversal hazard. Run still loaded/saved pipeline archive, so it is not a clean archive-free validation result.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static audit 2026-09-08 — the suspected RT-table CPU/GPU race is not established for normal app warmup. UI and content each create separate GpuDevice/MTLCommandQueue; RT buffers belong to the content-side GeneratorRenderer and are not passed to UI. Content warmup creates one command buffer per frame and calls try_commit_and_wait_completed before rewriting the next frame, so same-queue frame-to-frame rewrites are fenced. Generators/Compositor are also serialized on the content queue. Keep cross-queue/lifetime checks in scope for teardown/export, but do not treat the UI Frame queue as evidence that it is reading rt_gi_materials/rt_normal_sources/rt_obj_motion.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static audit 2026-09-08: concrete readiness defect. render_scene captures rt_ready from rt_accel_built before the accel rebuild/refit block. A rebuild then replaces self.rt_accel and sets rt_accel_built=false, but the same evaluate call continues with the stale local rt_ready=true. Because rt_accel_topo_key is immediately updated to the new key, the later guard can dispatch RT-A3a against the newly enqueued, not-yet-ready RtAccel. The documented topo-key mismatch guard does not actually block this path. This is a class-level GPU hang candidate for any post-initial topology or content rebuild; the crash logs reviewed here do not prove that a rebuild happened on the failing frame.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static plus log audit 2026-09-08: the primary-ray probe was a real specialized PSO. compile_pipeline_with_constants calls newFunctionWithName_constantValues_error and newComputePipelineStateWithFunction_error directly; it does not use binary archives. The MSL stage 1 branch returns before intersection_query and all secondary-ray loops, while writing deterministic values to every RT output. /Users/peterkiemann/Desktop/manifold-rt-primary-ray-20260907-192906.log shows archives disabled and the same RT-A3a encoder still reached a GPU hang at trace frame 18, with encoder state Faulted. Therefore ray traversal or secondary-ray arithmetic is not necessary for the hang. The remaining target is the RT-A3a dispatch ABI/resource set or frame-to-frame state; the probe does not prove the shader is innocent because it still binds the AS and reads depth/writes outputs.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static audit 2026-09-08: slot-6 diagnostic PSO setup passes a one-byte u8 pointer to MTLDataType::UInt at function-constant index 102 (RT_A3A_STAGE) in raytrace.rs. Metal copies a four-byte uint, so the normal binary RT pipeline has an unsafe size mismatch and an undefined stage value. Probe/translucent builders use u32 correctly. This can explain inconsistent diagnostic runs and contaminates normal-vs-probe comparisons in this worktree; it is not by itself proof of the production RT hang.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static audit 2026-09-08: mesh upload and RT acceleration have a real same-frame handoff hazard. gltf_mesh_source and gltf_skinned_mesh_source encode staging-to-destination vertex copies on the current frame command buffer. render_scene detects vertex generations, but the RT trace gate requires only rt_ready and matching topology; it does not require the accel content key to match the current content key. On a same-topology mesh update, the frame can therefore trace an old TLAS against newly copied vertex bytes, while build_accel is deferred to a later frame. This can expose stale acceleration nodes to new positions and raw normal/UV fetches, and the path is shared by warmup and export. The latest Corrosion crash did not log a content change on its failing frame, so this is a concrete class-level candidate, not the proven frame trigger.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Log audit 2026-09-08: the small-hardening crash uses Apple MTLCommandEncoderErrorState values where 1=Completed, 2=Affected, 3=Pending, 4=Faulted. In manifold-small-hardening-20260907-212906.log, RT-A3a encoder 2 is Affected, while upsample and atrous encoders are Pending; earlier clears/depth are Completed. Therefore RT-A3a is the first incomplete labeled pass and remains the strongest boundary, but the log does not identify an instruction or prove A3a itself caused the hang. The earlier primary-ray run with encoder state Faulted remains stronger isolation evidence; both should be kept distinct.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static audit 2026-09-08: strongest warmup/loading candidate. While gltf_mesh_source or gltf_skinned_mesh_source is still parsing, run() returns early with no logical vertex count and does not call mark_outputs_unchanged(), so Executor bumps the mesh slot generation every warmup frame. render_scene nevertheless derives triangle_count from the full preallocated buffer capacity via vcount(d.vertices), even when no parsed vertices have been copied yet. Its one-frame topo/content defer can therefore build an AS over empty, stale, or not-yet-loaded buffer contents; when the GLB arrives, the source copies new vertices into that same buffer while the old AS remains resident until the deferred content rebuild. RT can then traverse stale AS nodes against new vertex data during the loading window. This is a concrete shared warmup/export ordering and live-count hole, and it directly matches crashes that occur while a heavy scene is still warming. The current crash log does not prove the failing frame was the parse-arrival frame, so the next diagnostic should log parse state, logical vertex count, slot generation, topo/content keys, and RT dispatch eligibility per frame.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Qualification against docs/WARMUP_DESIGN and BUG-326: the permanent empty-BVH bug was already addressed by the content-settle rebuild. The residual seam found here is narrower: render_scene blocks topology changes but still permits RT while rt_accel_content_key differs from the current vertices_generation key. The deferred rebuild repairs the AS later, but the transition frame can still run RT against the old or empty structure. Treat this as a residual transient-state bug, not a re-opening of BUG-326’s original permanent-frozen-BVH diagnosis.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static audit 2026-09-08: warmup quiescence coverage is incomplete. warmup_pending() exists for gltf_mesh_source, gltf_texture_source, hdri_source, render_scene, and DNN nodes, but the async gltf_skinned_mesh_source and gltf_morph_deltas_source primitives have pending_load channels and no warmup_pending override. The animation loaders gltf_skeleton_pose, gltf_morph_weights, and gltf_animation_source likewise own pending async loads without a warmup_pending override. A project containing these nodes can report warmup complete before its geometry/deformation data is resident, then first-touch during playback/export. This is a separate warmup contract hole and can combine with the RT stale-content transition above.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Static audit 2026-09-08: warmup completion has a precise race with the content-settle fix. render_scene::warmup_pending() returns true only while rt_accel.ready is false; it does not report pending content reconciliation when rt_accel_content_key differs from the current vertices_generation key or when rt_accel_content_pending_key is waiting for its second stable frame. PresetRuntime stops when every node reports false. After a GLB parse lands, gltf_mesh_source clears pending_load immediately while its staging copy is only encoded for the current frame; an old or empty accel may already be ready, so both nodes can report warmup complete before render_scene performs the deferred content rebuild. The project then opens with stale AS/new vertex state, and the first later RT frame can hit the same loading-window failure. This is the strongest static explanation found so far and is shared by warmup and any export started before the content-settle rebuild.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Log boundary 2026-09-08: manifold-small-hardening-20260907-212906.log shows one RT accel build (before trace frame 3), then no later RT accel rebuild or content-change record through the frame-33 hang. The failing frame therefore had a stable resident AS in the available evidence. This does not disprove the warmup content race, but it means the log cannot tie frame 33 to GLB parse arrival; source content/key instrumentation is required before calling that the exact run trigger.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: 2026-09-08 lead reconciliation in slot-6, branch codex/validation-archive-bypass. Corrected the diagnostic RT_A3A_STAGE UInt/u8 pointer mismatch while preserving the probe work in checkpoint f1c3d410c; temporary RT-A3a probe matrix and world-position experiment were then removed from the final tree by c2c9c2b04, so they do not ship. Proven readiness defect: RenderScene::warmup_pending omitted deferred topology/content AS keys. Focused test warmup_pending_includes_deferred_accel_builds failed on old logic and passed after b9dfde641. Proven stale-content eligibility defect: RT trace gate checked readiness/topology but not resident content generation, allowing new vertex bytes with an old AS during deferred settle. Focused rt_trace_gate_requires_matching_resident_content failed before the content check and passed after b9dfde641. Same-frame rt_ready capture was not changed: build and trace command buffers share a queue and commit ordering, so the prior bead claim that this necessarily traces an unready AS remains unproven. Retained separate Metal usage corrections in 219e7c62e and validation archive bypass in fb719d5c7. Historical frame-33 log had no content rebuild at failure, so neither readiness fix is claimed as that exact hang root cause. Validation: focused red/green tests pass post-fix; manifold-gpu and manifold-renderer focused clippy pass. Landing gate with RUSTC_WRAPPER= passed clippy but test/GPU proof execution failed because the sandbox exposed no Metal device (first test panicked No Metal device found; 644 cascading GPU failures). Direct release build permits were not honored by the hook, so no headless Corrosion run, original export, or validation-on/off runtime coverage was possible. Branch intentionally not landed red; BUG-qh04 remains open.

title: audition-grid page fault: pool recycling races in-flight command buffers (ParticleText)
description: RE-PROBE 2026-09-09 with fence-stamped retirement on main (35eaa8675): the original cascade is DEAD — no page fault (code=3), no SubmissionsIgnored blacklist, no exit(70). New signature: solo ParticleText faults at frame ~22 (13 faults clustered), command buffers discarded code=1 kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorInnocentVictim, queue survives (ignored=false). So the retirement fix removed the pool-recycling amplifier, but a root encoder fault (state=Faulted) remains inside the ParticleText chain — signposts cover the full chain (draw_particles.splat, resolve_scatter, anti_clump_particles, sample_image_at_particles, turbulence, move_particles...) without naming the op. Frame ~22 suggests a one-time trigger: particle capacity growth, first anti-clump pass, or atlas realloc. Repro: cargo test -p manifold-app --features journey-proofs audition_fault_each_generator_alone (note: harness doc comment still says --features gpu-proofs, which manifold-app does not have — stale). Next: bisect the signpost chain by disabling particle sub-passes.
notes:
LEAD ANALYSIS 2026-09-05: the pacing wait IS GPU-completion-based (native_event is signaled on the content command buffer, content_pipeline.rs:3357), so the live frame loop honors the pool contract — live attribution of the crash to the pool is still UNPROVEN; the harness reproduced only the unpaced condition. Export mode encodes with no presentation wait — an unpaced live path that shares the pool. BUG-rnnr (RT denoiser realloc) remains a live-attribution candidate; Peter first-error log line discriminates. Class fix stands regardless: fence-aware retirement removes the assumption (texture_pool.rs doc names it as the escape hatch).
DISPROOF (pool-fence-fix lane, commit ed287e617 on lane/pool-fence-fix): fence-aware recycling implemented and confirmed attached — repro still faults (frame moved, different preset on rerun); recycling disabled ENTIRELY — fault still reproduces (ParticleText@28). Conclusion: the faulting texture is NOT pool-recycled; the BUG-l7t4 mechanism is elsewhere. Live suspects: chain-runtime internal caches (StateStore/memo direct textures), audition surface IOSurface import, cross-encoder hazard (first fault is always a page fault on the Compositor command buffer; Generators CB runs as a separate in-flight buffer). The fence-aware pool fix landed anyway (frame-counter recycling was documented-unsound on unpaced paths — export, headless — with the named escape hatch); BUG-rnnr confirmed NOT pool-backed (denoise/RT targets are direct create_texture fields reallocated instantly on switch) — needs its own retire-before-reuse fix.
MECHANISM CONFIRMED (fault-mechanism lane, commit 5b3b09f75 on lane/fault-mechanism): heap-pool texture UAF across in-flight command buffers. TexturePool is MTLHeap-backed (device.rs:1676); heap sub-allocation memory is reusable while an in-flight CB still references the old sub-allocation. Teardown/drop paths release heap textures BARE — drop-site backtraces: MetalBackend::replace_texture_2d (metal_backend.rs:301) via PresetRuntime::install_target (preset_runtime/core.rs:2026), GeneratorRenderer per-layer (LayerId, GpuTexture) map teardown. Discriminators: per-frame queue drain → fault gone; HOLD_CHURN (no prior ContentThread drop) → no fault; defer BOTH textures+buffers 8 frames → gone; textures-only deferral → gone. The churn ContentThread teardown drops pooled heap textures; the new run reallocates the same heap memory while the churn CBs still execute → GPU Address Fault attributed to the heavy Compositor CB. The landed fence-aware pool fix covers the RECYCLE path only, not bare drops. Open sub-question: whether missing useResource on the RENDER-pass binding path (encoder.rs — dispatch path has it at 494/499, render pass does not) is also load-bearing. Probe oracle: control faults 4/4 at frame 15 (solo ParticleText, layer tap); drain/defer both clean.
Probes re-verified on main tip 2c0428e11 (lane/fault-mechanism = main + probe commit 5b3b09f75, landing-ready): control faults frame 15 exact signature; deferral clean 40 frames. New scope data: the faulting Compositor/Generators CB scopes name the StarField clip chain (gen L0 StarField) as a sampler of the racing heap-pool transient — corroborates heap-UAF attribution (fault lands on whichever CB executes at detection). Probe branch: lane/fault-mechanism, sole holder.
FINAL (heap-retire-fix lane, e84860a9d on lane/heap-retire-fix): fence-stamped drop retirement implemented and verified (manifold-gpu retire.rs; marks on every texture class + buffers; mpsc, any-thread drops; per-frame drain + teardown flush; 6 new unit tests, nextest 2133, clippy clean) — but the NO-OP discriminator (zero hold, full probe path) is CLEAN, exonerating resource drops entirely. The fault is a sub-frame-tight timing race cured only by per-frame quiescence (DRAIN) or any per-frame CPU perturbation. Refine next probe toward: encode-ahead overlap hazards NOT involving drop lifetime (e.g. shared-mode resources read by an in-flight earlier frame while a later frame rewrites/retargets them; cross-frame aliasing of transient bindings). NOTE: machine GPU driver is sticky-degraded from this session repros (BUG-gtrs reproduced on base uncontended) — any further GPU probing requires a reboot first. The retirement hardening lands post-reboot alongside BUG-rnnr; both gated on clean gpu_proofs.
2026-09-06 Astra live check on codex/ui-contract-audit (1d596aedc): empty project, insert default Plasma generator layer, expand timeline, select generator and open Change browser. At 07:45:40 UTC first logged address faults are Compositor and Frame (code 3), followed by Present; at 07:45:47 queue blacklist causes ContentPipeline fatal exit. No Basic Shapes selection had executed yet. Concurrent landing UI-flow checks were running, so clean uncontended reproduction is NOT established. Complete log preserved at /tmp/manifold-audit-generator-browser-gpu-fault.log. Native modifier mapping validation stopped. Matches the existing browser failure symptom; no new mechanism claim.
Backlog review 2026-10-09 — evidence. Remaining: Bisect the signposted ParticleText subpasses to isolate the remaining encoder fault after retirement fixes. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-09-09T23:57:00Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. Original scope and acceptance remain authoritative.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: lane/heap-retire-fix mechanism finding (2026-09-05): drop-UAF premise falsified on current code. Complete fence-stamped retirement of ALL texture classes (device/pool/heap/msaa + IOSurface imports + mip views) AND buffers — fence-gated on the content completion event, verified 150+ drops flowing through — does NOT fix the headless repro (faults ~frame 15, 6/6 runs). DRAIN=on (per-frame queue quiescence) is clean. Defer-probe cleanliness (N=2) reproduced for textures-only AND buffers-only — the probe's per-frame pump perturbation hides the race; the diagnosis's texture-class bisect is an artifact. Only semantically-trusted oracle: full per-frame quiescence. Next suspects: CPU-written shared buffers rewritten while GPU reads (ring depth), BUG-jddy residency class (resource referenced only by completed CBs), blit-path declarations. Repro logs: /tmp/heap-retire-*.log

title: Temporal-upscale conditioning: fix blur/detail loss, add global + export columns
description: Peter tried scene temporal_upscale (renders 2/3 linear = DLSS-Quality ratio, render_scene.rs:285): works but blurs and loses fine detail. The MTL4 scaler model is current (metalfx_temporal_upscaler.rs prefers Metal4FxTemporalScaler) so the model is not the problem — the feed is. Suspects in order: (1) double temporal filtering — ~40-frame irradiance accumulator under the scalers own temporal pass softens detail; (2) reactive mask unwired — movers/emissives smear into history (August notes flagged both as confounds in the rejected denoised-scaler look); (3) jitter/velocity validation — misaligned frame averaging reads exactly as fine-detail blur. Target: DLSS-Quality-like, near-native. If still soft after conditioning, bump RT_TEMPORAL_RENDER_SCALE to 3/4 (one-line constant). Also in scope: temporal upscale joins the RT_QUALITY_SETTINGS quality columns — global project toggle with per-scene override; export column defaults to native full-res (exports never need the upscaler). Pairs with BUG-eytk (spatial a-trous denoiser): a denoised correctly-masked input is what lets the temporal scaler look like DLSS.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Run controlled temporal-upscale conditioning renders and finish global/export quality columns for the selected feed. title: Export dies on AVAssetWriter WriterNotReady mid-encode (no backpressure wait)
description: Symptom: 2026-08-26 real section export (Right Where I Need You, 720x1280@24) died in section 5 at frame 318: encode_frame failed WriterNotReady → export aborted. Four prior sections fine. Root cause: MetalEncoderPlugin append path never waits on AVAssetWriterInput.readyForMoreMediaData — appendPixelBuffer failure is treated as fatal instead of backpressure. Latent in single-export too; long section runs + machine load (RT rebuilds, freeze compiles, concurrent cargo builds) make the writer fall behind. Fix shape: bounded wait/retry on readyForMoreMediaData (KVO or polling with timeout) in the append path of MetalEncoderPlugin.m before appendPixelBuffer; error only on genuine timeout. Repro: export a multi-section range on a busy machine.
notes:
Reproduced again on 2026-09-26 during the real colour export proof: fourth 64x64 4fps one-second export failed at frame 3 with WriterNotReady. /private/tmp/hdr-colour-export-proof.log. Static cause candidate: EncodeFrame still has an earlier 100ms readiness loop before pixel-buffer allocation; the existing 10-second backpressure wait only runs later, immediately before append. The earlier return can bypass the intended fix entirely, and also does not log writer state. Fix should reuse one bounded readiness helper at both existing wait sites, retaining visible writer failure and timeout diagnostics.
Slot-2 draft removes the redundant early 100ms readiness loop and leaves the existing 10-second bounded wait immediately before append as the authority. Non-writing writer state now logs status/error. The same four-export colour proof then passed (16 frames total); /private/tmp/hdr-colour-export-proof-retry.log. title: BUG-156 — fluidsim3d-4k-perf-regression-suspect-bug066-fix
description:
### BUG-156 (fluidsim3d-4k-perf-regression-suspect-bug066-fix) — FluidSim3D no longer holds smooth 60FPS at 4K — HIGH, reported by Peter 2026-07-14
**Status:** OPEN — found not fixed 2026-07-14, reported by Peter during live-rig use.

**Symptom** — FluidSim3D used to run smoothly at 60FPS at 4K output resolution; it no longer does. Peter suspects this is a regression from the BUG-066 fix.

**Root cause** — unknown, not investigated this session, but the suspected culprit is well-formed: BUG-066's fix (`eebac94d`, see the closed entry in `docs/archive/BUG_BACKLOG_CLOSED.md`) resized `edge_slope_3d`/`swirl_force_3d`'s (and the other volume nodes') dispatch grids from `div_ceil(8)` (legacy 8×8×8 workgroup) to `div_ceil(4)` against the freeze codegen's actual `@workgroup_size(4,4,4)` for 3D-volume kernels. Correcting the grid size to match the real workgroup was necessary for correctness (forces were only landing in 1/8th of the volume before), but going from an 8³ to a 4³ workgroup at the same volume resolution means 8x more dispatched workgroups per volume kernel — a real, expected throughput cost of the fix, not an incidental one. Whether that 8x is actually what's landing on the frame budget (vs. some other change since, or the 4³ workgroup being genuinely suboptimal occupancy for this GPU) is unverified.

**Fix shape** — profile FluidSim3D at 4K with the profiler (`manifold-profiler`) to confirm the volume-node dispatches (`edge_slope_3d`, `swirl_force_3d`, and any other 3D-volume kernel sized off `VOLUME_WORKGROUP_3D`) are where the frame time went, comparing against a pre-`eebac94d` build if needed to isolate it from unrelated changes since. If confirmed, the fix is not "revert BUG-066" (that reintroduces the top-right-quadrant forces bug) — it's making the corrected dispatch cheap again: a larger workgroup size for the 3D volume kernels (if occupancy/shared-memory allows), or reducing per-workgroup overhead, while keeping the grid sized correctly against whatever workgroup size is actually emitted.

title: BUG-290 — gpu-proofs-test-binary-faults-gpu-firmware
description:
### BUG-290 (gpu-proofs-test-binary-faults-gpu-firmware) — a `manifold_renderer` test binary triggered an AGX GPU fault/restart; whole-display freezes on Peter's machine correlate with GPU test runs
**Status:** OPEN, hardening LANDED 2026-07-21 @ `7cacb965` (cross-process flock in `test_device()` kills the concurrent-process trigger class; `sg_blur_dynamic` radius clamped at 2048 kills the wired-garbage watchdog class). Remaining to close: the conviction run — ONE isolated `cargo test -p manifold-renderer --features gpu-proofs smoke -- --test-threads=1` with Peter present (freezes-alone ⇒ single bad kernel still live; clean ⇒ concurrency was the trigger, downgrade + monitor).
**Severity:** HIGH — stage risk by class: a compute dispatch that can fault GPU firmware in a test could do the same from the live app mid-show. Also the likely cause of Peter's "whole screen freezes, machine still alive" reports.
**Symptom:** whole machine (all displays, WindowServer, ghostty/tmux) freezes during GPU test runs, recovers after seconds. Two distinct firmware fault classes on record (both bug_type 284):
- `gpuEvent-manifold_rendere-2026-07-17-184055.ips` — restart_reason 3 **"BIF0 page fault"**, `is_read=true`, address 4398052055936, guilty_dm 3: a kernel READ an unmapped GPU address (OOB read or GPU-side use-after-free). Directly attributed to a `manifold_renderer` test binary.
- `gpuEvent-<unknown>-2026-07-18-133620.ips` — restart_reason 2 **"progress timeout"**, command_buffer_trace_id -1: a dispatch outran the firmware watchdog (runaway/unbounded loop). Process unattributed.
**Root cause:** unknown; two independent classes to convict. Facts established 2026-07-21: `GPU_TEST_LOCK` (`manifold-renderer/src/lib.rs:87` `test_device()`) is a `static` in-process ReentrantMutex — **zero cross-process serialization**, so nextest (process-per-test) or two concurrent agent sessions running GPU work defeat it entirely; concurrent-dispatch pressure is a live trigger hypothesis (Peter observed another agent running nextest around freeze times). Readback paths use `commit_and_wait_completed` (no test callers of `commit_and_wait_scheduled`), so simple drop-before-complete on the readback path is NOT confirmed. Static audit (Codex gpt-5.4-mini pass + Fable verification, 2026-07-21): `wgsl_compute.rs` `evaluate()` (~:2324) dispatches user-supplied WGSL with no host-side bounds guard — the widest OOB surface by class; `separable_gaussian_body.wgsl:94` `sg_blur_dynamic` derives its loop bound from `i32(radius)` **unclamped** (linear branch clamps to 32 at :133) — verified real, but current gpu-proofs exercise only the clamped linear mode; Plasma's `octaves = 3u + u32(cx*2.0)` loop was flagged but is 3–5 iterations for in-range complexity (saturating cast) — weak. No specific kernel convicted yet. Prior art: `agx-0x78-crash` memory, `ui-present-content-gpu-contention`.
**Fix shape:** (1) enforce cross-process GPU test exclusion — OS-level file lock inside `test_device()` alongside `GPU_TEST_LOCK`, and/or hook-deny `nextest` with `gpu-proofs` — kills the concurrency trigger class regardless of which kernel faulted; (2) clamp `sg_blur_dynamic`'s radius like the linear branch; (3) convict with ONE isolated run (`cargo test -p manifold-renderer --features gpu-proofs smoke -- --test-threads=1`, nothing else touching the GPU): freezes-alone ⇒ single bad kernel, clean-alone ⇒ concurrency trigger. Requires Peter present — a successful repro freezes the machine. Until fixed: never run gpu-proofs while performing/recording or while another session may touch the GPU.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — evidence. Remaining: Run the isolated GPU-proof conviction run with Peter present and record whether the firmware fault reproduces. title: Matter grain texture moves with the material
description: Sand/snow/mud surface grain is world-space, so flowing material slides under it. Carry each point's rest position through matter_frame, particle_volume (splat like velocity) and tile_surface_mesh to vertex UVs, and sample the grain at rest coords. Water session owns the surface files.

title: Whole-number count wire: counts travel exactly past 16.7M
description: Scalar wires are f32 (ParamValue::Float), exact only to 2^24 (EXACT_F32_COUNT, ports.rs), so GPU FLIP refuses pools over 16.7M particles and Extra High Quality fails on big fills (waterTestV3 head: 45M). Add a count scalar type (u32) with its own ParamValue, read/write helpers and wire validation, move every count port onto it (particle_capacity, pool_tiles, body_count, epoch, tick_index, the count/live_count/frame_count/substep_count/trigger_count outputs and their readers), and delete the EXACT_F32_COUNT refusals in favour of the device memory budget. Memory is the next wall: about 430 B per particle slot, so 45M particles is about 19 GB.

title: Shaders get each buffer size as u32 and ignore the binding offset
description: manifold-gpu/src/metal/encoder.rs:4210 sizes[idx] = buffer.size as u32. arrayLength() is wrong for any binding with an offset (it reports the whole buffer) and wraps silently past 4 GiB. title: Whitewater costs the whole pool every tick, and still allocates and runs when switched off
description: whitewater_step.rs:1248-1265 reserves every field and output and runs seed and publish before checking enabled. On, it runs about 8 dense passes over the whole step pool per tick (influence :1426, cells :1458, curvature :1467, extend x3 :1477, turbulence :1751) where the liquid step uses held lists, and copies the pool in and out (:1254, liquid_state.rs:748). The four classes (foam, bubble, spray, dust) are each sized for the full capacity (whitewater_step.rs:537-539, liquid_state.rs:271-291) though together they hold at most capacity, and all four are copied into every frame-history slot (liquid_frame.rs:300). Dust scratch (40 B per liquid slot) is allocated with dust off (whitewater_step.rs:1103-1112). The budget is a fixed 100k with no Water card row (scene_family.rs:109). Sweep 28 Oct.
