Bodies stay where they are. Matter does the same (matter_state.rs:366-372). Sweep 28 Oct, read from code.

title: Only the first Water in a scene pushes bodies; every other Water only takes the solids
description: manifold-nodes-water graph_install/coupling.rs:99: the first water drawn owns the rigid world, every other water takes its solids (physics_scene.rs SharedSolidsPair). SCENE_DOCUMENT_DESIGN.md:224 says bodies couple two ways. On stage: a box floats in pool A and is pushed through by pool B. Likely; not run.

title: Two-way join between GPU FLIP and the height-field water
description:
GPU FLIP only where the action is (a dam break, a boat, a pour) inside the height-field water to the horizon, with waves and volume passing both ways at the seam. This is the answer to endless water: on the open-ground scene a FLIP sheet left to spread grew cost and memory without limit.

Prior art: Chentanez, Müller and Kim, Coupling 3D Eulerian, Heightfield and Particle Methods for Interactive Simulation of Large Scale Liquid Phenomena (SCA 2014). BUG-l2h3.31.1 is the one-way first step (the FFT ocean drives FLIP's open faces); this replaces it once the height field reacts. Relates to BUG-zdiuw (infinite domain). Open: whether the seam shows.

Test: a wave crossing the seam both ways with no reflection or step in the surface, total volume across both solvers held, stills at the seam.

title: Height-field water to the horizon that reacts: shallow water plus dispersive surface waves
description:
Large open water that reacts: boats make wakes, waves run up beaches and reflect, floods spread, for a fraction of a 3D sim's cost. Jeschke and Wojtan, Generalizing Shallow Water Simulations with Dispersive Surface Waves (SIGGRAPH 2023): each step splits the height field into a bulk flow solved as shallow water and surface waves solved with Airy wave theory, then recombines them. Exact volume conservation, real time, a 512 m scene in the paper.

The FFT ocean can't react to bodies or shores. The design decides whether this replaces it near the action or sits inside it, with FFT kept for deep water far out. A height field can't splash, pour or overturn; that stays GPU FLIP's job (the two-way join is its own bead). The same Airy waves could later drive ripples on the FLIP surface, next to BUG-l2h3.30.9 (ripple normals from the ocean spectrum).

Test: a boat wake reaching a beach and a dam break across a flat; volume held to float precision over 10 s; wave speed against the Airy dispersion relation ω² = g·k·tanh(k·h) at constant depth, which the paper corrects exactly.

title: GPU FLIP: thin walls hold water and narrow slits stay open
description:
Thin solids leak and narrow slits clog, because each cell face holds one open fraction sampled from the solid (weight[a] per low face in the tiled face records). Seen: a 0.22 m slab under the open-ground water leaked all of it with no warning, and thin closed solids are sampled two spacings across as a workaround (09c591de2).

Fix: cut-cell solid faces that keep the two sides of a thin wall apart and keep gaps narrower than a cell open. Azevedo, Batty and Oliveira, Preserving Geometry and Topology for Fluid Flows with Thin Obstacles and Narrow Gaps (SIGGRAPH 2016); Chen et al. 2020 show a dam break through slits that a ghost-fluid solver clogs. Needs a short design against the tiled face records before code.

Test: a dam break through a slatted wall at two cell sizes, a 2 cm slab holds deep water, stills and frame-clock A/B.

title: Liquid quality from recent papers: walls that only push, thin walls, horizon water, surface tension, sub-cell droplets, thick goo
description:
Techniques from recent liquid papers that raise quality for good value: real-time ones first, offline ones only where the quality gain is large. Every child ships with a same-scene frame-clock A/B and before/after stills.

Order by value: walls that only push (BUG-j4u2), thin walls and narrow slits, height-field water to the horizon and its two-way join with GPU FLIP, GPU FLIP surface tension, sub-cell droplets and sheets, then Matter surface tension and Matter thick liquids. Learned helper networks stay in docs/IDEAS.md until the 5080 training machine is ready.

Sources: Takahashi and Batty, A Primal-Dual Box-Constrained QP Pressure Poisson Solver (TVCG 2024) and a multilevel active-set preconditioner for box-constrained pressure (SCA 2023); Chentanez and Müller, A Multigrid Fluid Pressure Solver Handling Separating Solid Boundary Conditions (SCA 2011); Chen, Meier, Solenthaler and Azevedo, An Extended Cut-Cell Method for Sub-Grid Liquids Tracking with Surface Tension (SIGGRAPH Asia 2020); Azevedo, Batty and Oliveira, Preserving Geometry and Topology for Fluid Flows with Thin Obstacles and Narrow Gaps (SIGGRAPH 2016); Jeschke and Wojtan, Generalizing Shallow Water Simulations with Dispersive Surface Waves (SIGGRAPH 2023); Chentanez, Müller and Kim, Coupling 3D Eulerian, Heightfield and Particle Methods for Interactive Simulation of Large Scale Liquid Phenomena (SCA 2014).

title: Switched-off branches still cost their consumers' work
description: A switch whose card picks an unwired branch skips the producers upstream, but publishes zeros, so every consumer still runs its own pass over them: the renderer runs the water's mist march (about 2.5 ms a frame on the dam) whenever the mist is wired, whatever it holds. The renderer sees only 'wired', and cannot tell zeros from data without a GPU read. Investigate whether the graph should carry 'this input is off' to consumers (so any node can skip its work), which switch users and passes pay for switched-off inputs today, and what that costs across the shipped presets. The water's feature toggles work round it locally: each toggle also sets a flag on the water object that the renderer reads on the CPU.

title: Tracer rough reflections black in rt_r3 proofs
description: rt_r3_textured_roughness: mr_texture_multiplies_flat_factors_per_texel (texel 1, roughness 0.5, reflects 0 instead of the emitter) and anisotropy_rotation_changes_elongated_emitter_coverage (coverage 0 both ways, roughness 0.55) fail on main as of 3cf34e890. Exact-mirror and roughness-1 cases pass, so GGX-sampled tracer reflections return black. The water wave's uncommitted changes do not touch manifold_gpu::raytrace (only a Copy derive on GpuBinding).

title: One GPU visibility pass that feeds every draw
description: Fold view, occlusion, sub-pixel and per-light shadow culling into one GPU pass per frame that writes, per object and per view (camera, each light, picking), its compacted copy list and indirect arguments, built on the existing eight-word argument blocks in live_draw_args.rs. Every raster pass then draws from it, so frame cost follows what is visible. Generalise beyond render_scene where other nodes draw many items.

title: Shadow casters: cull to the light and skip shadows nobody can see
description: The raster shadow prepass (prepasses.rs) draws every copy into every light's map each frame. Cull copies to each light's frustum with the same cull kernel, skip casters whose shadow footprint is under a shadow texel, and keep the existing static-scene shadow cache valid while only receivers or the camera move. When the light moves every frame (an LFO on the sun), test whether a lower-rate shadow update stays invisible.

title: Sub-pixel copies: drop or splat copies smaller than a pixel
description: In the cull pass, project each surviving copy's box; a copy whose screen footprint is under about one pixel either drops (when its coverage is below a set threshold) or draws as a single point with its shaded colour. Far corridor cells and distant swarm copies are mostly this. Prove with 4K renders that the change stays below a pixel, including under temporal upscale and motion blur.

title: Occlusion culling: skip copies and objects hidden behind nearer geometry
description: Build a depth pyramid (Hi-Z) from the camera depth each frame. Test each copy's and object's box against last frame's pyramid in the cull pass; draw survivors, rebuild the pyramid, then re-test the culled set against this frame's pyramid and draw any that became visible (two-phase, so a camera cut or fast motion never shows a missing copy). Biggest expected win on dense swarms and Scene Loop corridors where cells hide each other.

title: Per-copy view culling everywhere it is skipped today
description: render_scene's copy cull (frame_setup.rs encode_copy_cull, ObjectDraw::culls_copies) skips: blended or transmissive copies (atomic compaction reorders them; needs an order-preserving prefix-sum compaction), arrays under 1024, meshes without a published box (deformer outputs, glTF, cut chains: publish or forward a conservative box), points mode, and the selection mask, item pick and volume optics passes, which still draw every copy. Close each gap or state why it stays.

title: Draw cost follows what is visible, not what exists (perceptually free culling)
description: Every raster draw path (render_scene copies and objects, scatter, physics, swarms, glTF scenes, every light's shadow) should pay only for what reaches a pixel. Today render_scene compacts in-view copies for the camera passes (live_draw_args.rs cull, cull_instances.wgsl); everything else draws every copy. Children cover: per-copy view culling everywhere, occlusion culling, sub-pixel copies, shadow casters, and one GPU visibility pass that feeds all of it. Rule for every child: the picture stays identical (or below a pixel), proven by 4K renders before/after on swarmTestv3, Corrosion and RWINY, plus a per-node perf-soak.

title: Scene object 'closed' param has no settings row, failing every_param_of_every_compiled_node_has_a_table_row
description: node.scene_object gained a 'closed' param (f8084ab59) with no row in the scene property tables, so it can't be set from the Scene panel and manifold-nodes scene_document::every_param_has_a_row fails on main.

title: Motion blur: camera-accurate reconstruction (no steps, streaks cross edges, depth-aware)
description:
node.motion_blur gathers 8 evenly spaced samples along the centre pixel's velocity (crates/manifold-nodes-image/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/motion_blur.wgsl and motion_blur_body.wgsl). Three faults show on stage: long streaks (scenes allow up to max_blur_px 120) break into visible steps (Corrosion vortex shards; swarmTestv3 copies once per-copy motion landed); a moving object smears only inside its own outline, never past its edges over the background; and background can smear into a nearer moving object.

Fix shape: the McGuire 2012 reconstruction filter as used by game engines. A tile pass finds each 16x16 tile's max velocity, a neighbour-max pass spreads it one tile, and the gather samples along the neighbour-max direction with a sample count that follows streak length (about 1 per 2 px, cap 32; still tiles take 1 sample) and a per-pixel random offset. Weight each sample by depth and its own velocity, so near moving objects blur over far ones and far ones never bleed in. Shutter angle stays physical (180 deg default). Paths: still pixels cost nothing extra; fused body must match the standalone kernel.

Test: existing gpu proof motion_blur_visibility plus a long-streak no-steps check and an edge-spill check; 4K swarm and Corrosion renders before and after.

title: Deforming meshes report per-vertex motion to the camera, so fragment scenes keep temporal history and refit their ray-tracing structure
description: render_scene velocity comes only from the model matrix (prev_model). Deformed vertices carry no motion, so temporal history (RT accumulation, TAA, motion blur) reprojects moving fragments with zero velocity. transform_mesh_patches and ordered_recon_mesh keep triangle membership, but declaring their topology from 'in' (mesh_output_rule) stops the per-frame history reset that hides this: tested on Everything Is Okay and Murmur, up to 38% of pixels changed (fine edge noise). The same rule turns Corrosion's 3 BLAS rebuilds per frame into refits. Needs per-vertex previous positions for deformed meshes; then land the topology rule.
notes: Raster per-vertex motion landed (render_scene prev_positions, 16 deformers keep topology). Remaining: ray-tracing history still resets on every Refit (SceneChanges.reset_history). RT accumulate runs before Pass A, so it can't read this frame's velocity. Options: velocity from the depth prepass, or accumulate recomputes the previous position from the hit triangle and stored previous positions.

title: Lumen-style cached lighting: ray-traced bounce light in a few ms
description: Goal: RT global illumination at live frame rates. Today render_scene re-traces bounce light every pixel every frame (about 87 ms in Right Where I Need You V5, 1080x1920, 'RT AO+GI translucent'). Approach: a cached simplified scene plus a per-surface lighting cache updated incrementally, bounce light traced from a sparse screen probe grid, reused across frames, screen traces for fine detail. MANIFOLD advantage: the engine knows exactly when flashes, cuts and triggers fire and what is coming on the timeline, so the cache snaps or invalidates on the exact frame (no Lumen-style lag on audio-reactive flashes) and expensive rebuilds can start a beat early. Look trade to confirm with Peter: settling behaviour between cued snaps.
notes: Live-first rule (Peter, 2026-10-26): the design must hold its frame time and look with zero look-ahead (live triggers, improvised clips, MIDI hits). Knowing when an event fires (snap the cache on that frame) is core; pre-starting work from the timeline is an optional bonus only, never relied on.

title: Nanite-style cluster geometry: native photoscans at screen-bound cost
description: Goal: full-detail photoscans, many per scene, costing what is on screen rather than what is loaded. Approach: at import split meshes into ~128-triangle clusters with a pre-built simplification hierarchy; each frame pick per cluster the coarsest level with sub-pixel error, cull clusters off screen and behind last frame's depth, draw pixel-sized triangles with a compute rasteriser. MANIFOLD advantage: the modifier stack says exactly which meshes deform and how, so only those clusters update; everything else stays cached. Hard parts: alpha-masked foliage, deforming meshes, RT acceleration structures over clusters. Builds on the per-part culling and mesh bounds already in render_scene (frustum.rs, MeshBounds CPU wire).
notes: Live-first rule (Peter, 2026-10-26): the design must hold its frame time and look with zero look-ahead (live triggers, improvised clips, MIDI hits). Knowing when an event fires (snap the cache on that frame) is core; pre-starting work from the timeline is an optional bonus only, never relied on.

title: Near-native temporal upscaling and frame generation for live output
description:
Goal: MetalFX temporal upscaling that is hardly distinguishable from native on 3D scenes, then MetalFX frame interpolation on the composited output. Peter accepts one frame of added latency for frame gen (2026-10-26). Use the classic MetalFX path: the Metal 4 scalers hang on macOS 26.6.1 (RAYTRACING_DESIGN.md DN-P, BUG-rinn).
Plan: (0) design doc docs/UPSCALE_FRAMEGEN_DESIGN.md + spikes: frame interpolator on the classic path; a FLIP-style perceptual score against native renders. (1) Fix TAA jitter: render_scene/frame_setup.rs ~1004-1016 adds jitter only into view_proj[2][0..1], correct only for a bare projection; with view_proj = P*V the shift varies across the image. Add history resets on camera cuts, clip switches and strobes. (2) Real motion vectors for deforming meshes and swarms: deformers (morph, cuts, fragments, skin, fluid) keep previous positions; instances keep previous transforms; velocity reads them (fixes motion blur on deformation too). (3) Upscale gate on the six reference scenes in tests/fixtures/projects + swarm: score + Peter's eyes. (4) Composite motion map built by the compositor; generators opt in with analytic motion; layers without motion are masked so frame gen shows the real frame there. (5) Frame interpolator, presentation cadence rework (triple-buffer handoff and display timing), per-output switch (projector/LED/recording), transport runs one frame early to keep beats on time, skip generation across cuts and strobes. (6) Final gate on real shows, beat sync measured with a click track.
notes: Architecture: upscaling and frame generation sit behind one backend-neutral interface in manifold-gpu (Peter, 2026-10-26). Our side produces the shared contract once: colour, depth, motion vectors, jitter offset, exposure, reactive/no-history mask, reset flag, camera params, frame delta, UI kept separate. Backends consume it: MetalFX (classic path) on Metal now; DLSS or FSR on the planned Vulkan backend (NVIDIA-only for DLSS). render_scene must not call MetalFX directly.

title: Flaky GPU proof: code_terminal_bounded_acceptance_and_fusion_proof (mid amount keeps live image)
description: Symptom: crates/manifold-nodes/tests/code_terminal.rs:1234 panics "mid amount keeps live image" intermittently. Red in the scene refinement landing gate and on origin/main d8eef3485 (same message), then passed on a rerun of the full binary. Root cause unknown; suspect an unseeded random input in the test or the Code Terminal preset. Fix shape: seed the randomness so the proof is deterministic, then check the fraction thresholds against the seeded result. Never mute it.

title: Physics: admission cooks every hull twice (validate_at then install)
description: Scene refinement final review item. validate_at cooks each convex hull at admission, then install cooks it again. Fix shape: a per-slot Arc<CookedSolid> cache filled at admission that take_admitted/restore_admitted, add_body_geometry, Solid::replace and CopyGroup CopyCook all take; or move the scale refusal to install time so admission does not cook. Files: admission.rs, physics.rs, copy_layout.rs (manifold-water-rigid). Cost: doubles hull cook time on load and on reshape. Parent BUG-g6p6m (Scene refinement).
notes: Peter to check in the app: on an object with a hull collider made of many hulls, drag its Scale row and watch for stutter. Each new Scale value builds the hulls twice (admission check, then install). Only hulls, only on shape or scale change; exact-mesh colliders and normal frames are unaffected. Stutter means fix this next; none means it stays low priority.

title: Mist: thin fog from spray, drawn by the water field march
description: GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md D13 and D16. Spray feeds a thin fog density on the water tiles; the same per-pixel march that draws the field accumulates it in raster. Real units: droplet size and density per metre (D14). Raster first; the ray tracer follows with BUG-651ho.4 (ray tracer hits the water field).

title: Ray tracer hits the water field: a custom hit on the level set, so ray-traced views, reflections, shadows and refraction see field-drawn water
description: Follow-up after the D2 raster cutover (GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md D2). Today the tracer holds no water at all: transmissive objects route to the raster transparent pass and collect_rt_objects skips them (render_scene/rt_frame.rs:350), so the raster march keeps today behaviour under the ray tracer and the cutover needs no tracer work. This adds new capability: water in ray-traced reflections, shadows and GI. manifold-gpu has no custom intersection today (accel.rs builds triangles only; shadow_rays.msl uses inline triangle queries). Shape: one bounding box per occupied brick from liquid_bricks; a bounding_box branch in the three walk helpers (shadow_rays.msl rt_walk_exhausted, walk_with_alpha_test_counted, walk_with_transmission) that walks the field and commits the hit; the field normal at the 4-5 decode sites; a parity proof between the WGSL raster walk and the MSL tracer walk. Fits the Vulkan plan (VK_KHR_ray_query AABB candidates). Unblocks BUG-l2h3.30.1 (traced refraction and transmission through the water).

title: GPU FLIP: torn water becomes spray, mass moved from the bulk water into real droplets
description: Wētā Loki (Avatar: The Way of Water) splits water into states with their own solvers: bulk water, spray, mist, bubbles, foam. Bulk water that tears faster than surface tension can hold becomes spray droplets of physical size, simulated on their own, with mass taken from the bulk. The bulk surface then only draws connected water and can be smoothed without erasing splashes. Test 2026-10-23 showed neighbour count alone is the wrong rule: most lone particles belong to thin sheets and removing them tears holes. The rule must be physical (sheet thickness and stretch rate against surface tension, in real units). Today whitewater is emitted alongside the water, not converted from it. Sources: beforesandafters.com 2022-12-21 (why the CG water looks so good); unity.com blog on the Avatar water technology.

title: GPU FLIP: Sheet Fill Rate 0.5 grows the Dam Break water by 61% in 4 seconds
description: Symptom: WaterDamBreakGpuFlip at resolution 64 with Sheet Fill Rate 0.5 (the FLIP Fluids default _sheetFillRate, fluidsimulation.h) and a switched-off Inflow for pool headroom: live particles go 345788 (frame 1) to 347091 (frame 20), 358400 (frame 45), 556462 (frame 240). The settled tank is visibly fuller and still sloshing hard at frame 240, where the same scene without sheeting has settled. Root cause unknown. Suspects: sheet seeds never stop in calm water (the detector keeps calling resting thin regions sheets), or the GPU fill-rate draw keeps more seeds than the engine. Fix shape: run the CPU sheeter oracle (manifold-fluids sheeter.rs) on a dumped frame-240 level set and compare its seed count with the GPU births; check FLIP Fluids itself on the same scene for its volume drift before calling it parity. Found by the level-set look prototype; preset and dumps under the session scratchpad levelset_proto/presets/r64_sheet_room.json and cap64s.
close_reason: Fixed in 3cf34e890. Root cause: the sheeter read the whitewater curvature distance, which flattens about 1.4 cells down in moving water and wobbles, so deep water passed the thin-sheet test. It now builds its own true signed distance. Dam Break 64 at rate 0.5 over 240 frames: births 210,674 -> 108,586, live +61% -> +31% (native FLIP Fluids grows 62%). A resting pool seeds nothing. The remaining gain is sheet seeds in real thin sheets.

title: AO contact shadows darken about 8 frames late under fast-moving objects
description: Symptom: with the new AO history (BUG-g6p6m (Scene refinement: simple, honest, never frozen), node.temporal_accumulate), a contact shadow on unchanged ground under a fast-sinking swarm cube or a rolling Surface Waves base reaches its full darkness about 8 frames late. It reads as a briefly paler contact shadow, not a trail. Root cause: on unchanged ground depth and normal match, so history survives, and the 3x3 variance clip is too loose on noisy input to catch a darkening shadow. Fix shape: clamp history against a tighter, spatially filtered neighbourhood (as UE TAA does). Evidence: scratchpad aofix/cmp_swarm_lag.png and cmp_waves_lag.png; lighter-than-settled pixels 10460 (swarm) and 3294 (waves).

title: A Fill is limited to a Box and says only: a fill fills a box, set shape to box first
description: Symptom (2026-10-23 12:40 recording, Peter at 5:33): switching a Water Source to Fill with a non-box shape shows the message a fill fills a box, set shape to box first; he could not tell what it meant or why Fill is restricted. Fix shape: Fill fills any shape the source offers (Sphere now, mesh-shaped fills with BUG-jk5zt), and until a shape can fill, the disabled choice names the reason in plain words.

title: Dragging the water domain restarts the water every frame, and with any body rebuilds the whole rigid world
description: Symptom (2026-10-23 12:40 recording, traced by the scene refinement review): every drag frame of the Water domain restarts the water; with any physics body in the scene the whole rigid world is thrown away and rebuilt, and colliders re-cut their water shapes. Domain Position and Size are live transform params, and a param write may never reset anything (docs/SCENE_DOCUMENT_DESIGN.md section 1 (Rulings), ruling 3). Root cause, suspected: the domain transform sits in the GPU FLIP geometry setup, and a setup change restarts the domain (gpu_flip_domain.rs, restart when setup differs), the same mechanism BUG-elwvu.28 (Water Resolution restarts on any write) names. Fix shape: the water side comes from BUG-zdiuw (GPU FLIP infinite domain): a move becomes a tile offset, never a restart. The rigid side must never rebuild on a water domain move, same family as BUG-hin53 (panel edits restart GPU water).

title: Inflow Amount and Drain Amount: litres to pour or remove before the source stops, 0 to infinite
description: From the 2026-10-23 12:40 recording, Peter at 5:54: an inflow amount, the litres you can spray in before the inflow runs out, zero to infinite. A Drain gets the same: the litres it can remove before it stops. Infinite is the default and is todays behaviour. A live performance row on the Water Source card, in litres (real units, docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md D14); Reset refills the amount. Fits the infinite domain scenes: pour a set volume into a canyon.

title: Camera Focus On: Manual, an item, or screen centre, with a focus speed
description: General scene work, not water. A Focus On field on the Camera kind: Manual (today), an item (focus tracks that item distance every frame wherever it or the camera moves), or Screen Centre (focus on what is under the centre, measured on the GPU from depth, no CPU readback). A focus speed makes it pull rather than snap. Saves re-dialling focus whenever field of view or distance changes. The lens is already physical (docs/CAMERA_AND_LENS_DESIGN.md); this only drives its focus distance. Belongs with the scene document camera work, BUG-elwvu (scene document).

title: Water binds a Material item like any Object, so the water can be re-materialled
description: The Water card in docs/SCENE_DOCUMENT_DESIGN.md section 7.10 (Water, Water Source, Ocean) has no Material binding. Direct level-set rendering (BUG-651ho.1) reads the water look from a Material item bound to the Water, inherited and swappable like any Object material, so the water can be re-materialled at any time without re-simulating. Part of the D2 spec in docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md.

title: Real units for every water look and whitewater dial, so one setup works from a drop to an ocean
description: Audit and convert per docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md D14: absorption and scattering per metre; whitewater triggers on real speed and curvature with drop size in millimetres; ripple detail in metres; march step sizes and tolerances relative to the cell; no dial tuned in scene units. Done when a 5 cm glass and a 20 m wave look right with the same material and whitewater settings, checked by headless renders.

title: Water detail normals: projected on three axes, moved along the sim velocity, sourced from the ocean spectrum
description: Fine ripple detail on the water field for almost no cost (docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md D13). The level set has no texture coordinates, so project the detail from world space along three axes and blend by surface direction. Move it with the sim own velocity, two copies crossfading to hide stretching (the flow-map method), which beats hand-painted flow maps because the velocity is exact. Strength follows the flow: fine ripples on calm water, chop on fast water, masked by the foam field. Source the detail from the FFT ocean spectrum so FLIP water and ocean match where they meet. Detail is in metres and the layer is chosen by its size on screen (D14). For close-ups the same detail displaces the surface inside the march. Needs BUG-651ho.1 (direct level-set rendering).

title: A photoscan Collider at its import fit scale is refused: Box3D drops slivers under 0.25 mm2 and the bridge refuses the whole mesh
description: Symptom: the coastal_cliff_02 scan as a Collider at scale 0.049 (the import fit size, about 2 m wide) never collides: cooking fails with "Box3D discarded degenerate mesh triangles" (crates/manifold-physics/src/cooked.rs:85), for the exact mesh and for the P2d contact mesh alike. At scale 0.25 and above it cooks. Root cause: b3CreateMesh discards triangles with area under 0.01 * B3_LINEAR_SLOP^2 = 0.25 mm2 (native/box3d/src/mesh.c, minArea), and bridge.c refuses the mesh when any triangle is discarded, since indices would shift. A scan shrunk to stage size has many such slivers. Fix shape: the CollisionShape contact mesh (crates/manifold-physics/src/contact_mesh.rs) leaves out triangles under Box3D minimum area at the cook scale; each is far under the 5 mm contact tolerance, so the measured distance still holds. Found by lane P2d (BUG-g6p6m.8 (Scan colliders)); not built there because the design doc does not name it.

title: Copies, swarm and cut-map reserves grow live past their build size
description: Count ceilings grow live instead of reserving memory up front: MAX_COPIES (copies_body.rs), swarm MAX_COUNT (scene_schema/swarm.rs) and CUT_MAP_EXTRA_RECORDS (mesh_cut_map.rs) are fixed reserves laid at build, so Count, Swarm Count and a fine cut stop at them. Each now states its memory reason on its row or error (P3c, lane/refine-loop-cuts 92f152be6). Fix shape: buffers that grow when the live count passes them, without restarting the simulation (no-arbitrary-limits rule).

title: With ray tracing on, cut modifiers still build the acceleration structure over every padded triangle
description: Symptom: with ray tracing on, a cut modifier (Vortex Fragments on a dense mesh) still builds the ray-tracing acceleration structure over the padded capacity, not the live count. Raster now draws only the live count (Phase 1 of BUG-g6p6m (Scene refinement: simple, honest, never frozen)), so the lockup case remains only with RT on. Root cause: frame_setup.rs keeps vertex_count at capacity (bound = capacity) and collect_rt_objects in rt_frame.rs builds with triangle_count = vertex_count / 3. The live count is GPU-side, and a Metal acceleration-structure build takes a CPU count. Fix shape: build over the previous frame read-back live count, rounded up and grown, or another bounded count; the runaway layer cut is the backstop until then.

title: Ray-traced reflections and refractions do not see glass objects
description: Symptom: under ray tracing, reflected and refracted rays never hit a glass (transmission > 0) object, so glass is missing from reflections and refractions. Root cause: any PBR draw with transmission > 0 is transparent (frame_setup.rs:403, render_scene.rs:1901), and collect_rt_objects (rt_frame.rs:351) and the RT material table (rt_frame.rs:32) keep only non-transparent draws; the glass surface itself also skips RT reflections (rt_frame.rs:477). Fix shape: add transparent draws to the RT scene, which changes RT shadows, AO and GI for every glass object including imports. Decision needed: what glass does to RT shadows and AO (Blender Cycles: glass stays in the scene; Eevee: shadow mode hashed). Found by scene refinement P1d, epic BUG-g6p6m.

title: Perceptually lossless optimisation of photoscan and heavy meshes for drawing
description: Photoscans (the coastal cliff is about 943k triangles) cost draw time, ray-tracing build time and memory. Goal: reduce them with no visible loss. Industry methods: error-bounded simplification (meshoptimizer simplify with a screen-space error target), cluster LOD chosen per frame by projected error (Nanite-style), and baking the removed detail into a normal map so lighting keeps it. Applies on import, cached by scale; the drawn result must match the original in a side-by-side render. Related: scene refinement P2d (contact meshes, epic BUG-g6p6m), BUG-js61b (photoscan collider cost on the water side).
notes: Target: Nanite-style cluster LOD (Unreal 5): mesh cut into ~128-triangle clusters, a hierarchy of simplified cluster groups, per-frame pick of the coarsest version under about one pixel of screen error, so detail is spent only where visible with no popping. First cheap step: error-bounded simplification on import. Building blocks exist in meshoptimizer (meshlets, cluster LOD). Metal mesh shaders make it feasible on Apple GPUs.

title: Ray tracing treats a Spot light as a Point (no cone); light shafts read layer 0 as the sun
description: Symptom: with ray-traced shadows or lighting, a Spot lights and shadows in every direction, like a Point. Light shafts read shadow layer 0 .r as the sun whatever slot 0 holds, and with RT shadows on they sample stale or dummy raster maps for point lights. Older than the scene document wave. Fix shape: pass the cone to RT lights; shafts find the sun by kind in the shared caster table. Seed streams also assume at most 8 casters (RT_CASTER_SEED_STRIDE = 8 in shadow_rays.msl; legacy path only). Found by the review of fix lane M.

title: A Scale change on a Copies prototype reshapes every copy in one frame
description: Symptom: physics.rs apply_authored_edits (manifold-water-rigid, the copies loop) calls reshape() for every installed copy when a Copies prototype is reshaped. Each copy cooks its own hulls, allocates, and Box3D destroys and recreates its contacts. Up to 65,536 copies; an LFO on prototype Scale stalls the content path and loses warm starting. Root cause: each copy owns its own cooked hulls (OwnedGeometry::Hulls per body record), so a shared prototype shape is cooked N times. Fix shape: copies of one prototype share one cooked hull set (refcounted hull data in manifold-physics, one cook per reshape, each copy swaps its shape to the shared hulls). Box3D shapes are per body, so contacts are still rebuilt per copy; deciding whether a continuously modulated prototype Scale should instead be setup-only (stage vs setup) is part of the design. Not a small change, so fix lane J2 logged it instead of building it.

title: Renderers share one growable scene interface; remove the remaining hard limits
description: After the scene document wave lands. Raster and ray-traced renderers each keep their own fixed tables, hand-mirrored between Rust and Metal source, so their limits drift (shadow casters were 4 vs 8; lane M moves lights and shadow casters to one shared growable table). Remaining: RT material textures 64 (MAX_RT_MATERIAL_TEXTURES, params.rs:744) and glowing triangles 4096 (MAX_RT_EMISSIVE_TRIANGLES, emissive.rs:16) move into the same shared growable interface; swarm Count 100,000 (scene_schema/swarm.rs MAX_COUNT, comment says not a memory limit) grows live; whitewater pool 250,000 (whitewater.rs MAX_CAPACITY); glTF joints 512 (gltf_skeleton_pose.rs) and morph targets 64 (gltf_morph_weights.rs, morph_targets_blend.rs). Shader-side layouts generated or proof-checked from Rust, never hand-copied. Also sweep unnamed fixed-size arrays, which a MAX_ search misses. Ruling 23.
notes: Also: the light-shaft light list goes through a 4 KB setBytes (about 64 lights) and assumes the sun is caster slot 0; the R16 hold-history diagnostic clears only layer 0 (found by fix lane M, which moved shadow casters to one shared growable table). Shatter shared partition and 64-part cap: BUG-s6hd0.

title: Shatter: one shared partition per shape revision; drop the 64-piece cap
description: Symptom: every node.mesh_fragment piece (Shatter, N pieces) runs load_vertices, subdivide and select_fragment on the whole shape whenever the shape changes, so a Tube radius on an LFO with Shatter 64 runs 64 full partitions with allocations every frame on the content thread; imported meshes parse the whole file twice per piece. MAX_PIECES=64 (manifold-foundation mesh_partition.rs) exists only to bound that cost, which ruling 23 (no arbitrary limits) does not allow, and it also caps built-in shapes and curve solids that parse no file. Root cause: no shared partition result; each piece and each body hull recomputes it (MeshSource::Fragment::load_vertices). Fix shape: partition the source once per shape revision and let every piece and hull select from that one result (needs a shared cache keyed by source+count+detail, which is new shared state: lead or Peter approves the home), then drop MAX_PIECES, the Pieces clamp in scene_compile/modifiers.rs and shatter.rs, and the 64-parts refusal in scene_schema/modifier.rs shatter_refuses. Found by review-fixes2 (items 12 and 14 of fix lane J); too big for the fix pass.

title: Scene Loop cell size follows live Copies rows and swarm spread
description: Goal (lead decision, keeps ruling 8 pure compile): the corridor cell follows the live Copies rows (count, columns, spacing, layout, turn) and each swarm spread and Transform, like Blender Array relative offset, so changing those rows moves the tiles with no recompile; Spacing adds on top. Today (lane/scene-doc-fix-l d71bbaaf8) the default cell is measured at compile from row defaults plus a fixed 6 m swarm box, so a grid with rows along the corridor (Columns 3 Count 9, or Count over 16) overlaps until Spacing is raised. Why it is not a small change: (1) node.scene_array and node.loop_camera take cell_size as a param only, no port, so both need port-shadowed cell_size inputs, and every Loop camera must take the same wire or the wrap breaks; (2) the layout extent per Layout (Grid, Scatter, Line, Ring, Spiral, Random) lives in manifold-water-rigid physics/copy_layout.rs (pub crate) and needs the copy box width the physics world measures from the installed hull, so a CPU node needs that math moved to a shared place plus the width; (3) the cell must be the union box over every drawn item, copied object, swarm (with emitter position and scale) and group offsets, not a max of depths; (4) Spacing changes meaning from absolute cell metres to a gap on top, which changes the card row and the Home, Near and Far defaults that scale with the cell. Fix shape: section 2.5 audit, then one corridor-extent node fed by those rows, port-shadowed cell_size on scene_array and loop_camera, Spacing as added gap.

title: Scene compiler: measure, then optimise the small nodes around mesh, physics and water
description: After the scene document wave lands. The scene compiler emits one small node per transform, param and camera, as hand wiring did; fusion merges only per-element maths, not the mesh, physics or water jobs or the small CPU nodes around them. Step 1: profile one frame of a big scene and measure the share spent in small nodes (profiler-guide skill). Step 2, only if it matters: a scene-level pass that collapses transform and param chains on the CPU and bakes items that never move into constants.

title: uniform_layout_proof red: reflect_array ReflectUniforms drifted from its codegen layout
description: Symptom: manifold-nodes --test main uniform_layout_proof::hand_uniform_structs_match_codegen_layout fails on the scene-document wave branch: reflect_array.rs struct ReflectUniforms matches no type_id in its file (layout drift). Seen by fix lane E at base 84595595c; the lane never touched reflect_array.rs (last changed in L22c 8aa814bc4). Root cause: unknown; suspect L22c added or reordered a reflect_array param without updating the hand uniform struct. Fix shape: align ReflectUniforms with the PARAMS order (or move run() to the generated layout), then rerun the proof. A drifted hand struct feeds the shader wrong values, so mirrors on stage may read the wrong axis or plane.

title: Two Swarms cannot draw the same Object or Group
description: Symptom: a second Swarm whose Draw As picks an item another Swarm already draws draws nothing. Fix E greys that pick with a reason and the compile keeps the first swarm in tree order, a named stopgap. Root cause: scene_compile keys swarm_draws by the drawn item (one copies source per item; object.rs and group.rs take one Frame.copies body), so an item has one draw. Fix shape: a concat-copies stage (N copy arrays, each placed by its emitter frame, into one array) or one draw per swarm per item; needs the DECOMPOSING_GENERATORS 2.5 audit first.

title: Water Resolution, Particles per Cell and Seed restart the liquid on any write yet are mappable rows
description: Symptom: in scene_schema/water.rs, Resolution (FLIP and MPM), Particles per Cell (MPM) and Seed (MPM) are setup() rows, so they are manifest params the shared row core offers for mapping and modulation. Every write restarts the liquid: Resolution changes geometry.setup (gpu_flip_domain.rs restart = self.setup != Some(geometry.setup); matter_domain likewise), and Particles per Cell and Seed sit in MatterSetup. A mapped or modulated Resolution restarts the water every changed frame. SCENE_DOCUMENT_DESIGN.md ruling 3 (Stage versus setup) and section 7.4 say a control that restarts its simulation is a structural field, never mapped. Surface Detail does not restart the liquid (it drives the surface mesher resolution only) and stays a live row. Root cause: FieldControl has no numeric control (only Closed, ClosedOrItem, Item, ItemSet, ClosedOrLayer, File, Listed), so a numeric structural setting has nowhere to live but a manifest param. Fix shape: add a numeric structural field control (integer stepper with a range) to scene_schema/fields.rs and the scene card row core (RowAffordance::Field), move Resolution and Seed onto WaterFields with it, move Particles per Cell (8 or 27) onto WaterFields as a Closed field like Solver, and have scene_compile/water.rs write them into the template node params at compile. Found by scene document fix lane F.

title: Crash test never ticks a Water scene: every_kind_and_choice_survives has no GPU device
description: every_add_entry_and_field_choice (manifold-nodes --test main scene_document) builds, saves, reloads and undoes every Water and Water Source case, but its CPU tick stops at the first frame because the water nodes ask for a GPU encoder. A Water choice that only fails while running would pass. Fix shape: a gpu-proofs twin that ticks the Water cases 120 frames on a device through scripts/gpu_queue.py, or a CPU stand-in for the water nodes' tick.

title: Nightly trunk_health should yield the GPU to overnight lanes without a kill
description: Symptom: on 2026-10-23 at 05:30 the 04:30 trunk_health GPU legs held the GPU lock while two overnight lanes waited for one GPU run each. The memory rule says the lead kills the nightly, but auto mode's classifier refuses kill -TERM on it (Interfere With Workloads) and even reading trunk_health.py for a stop switch. Fix shape: a sanctioned yield. trunk_health skips or defers its GPU legs while any agent worktree slot holds a live lease (scripts/agent-worktree.py), or gpu_queue gives queued lane jobs priority over trunk_health legs (see BUG-4q2v9, gpu_queue lock starves waiters). Then the memory rule feedback_overnight_beats_nightly drops the kill step.

title: Extrude's solid is inside out: normals and winding face in for a counter-clockwise outline
description: Symptom: an Extrude of the built-in Circle (and any counter-clockwise outline) has its normals and triangle winding facing into the solid (signed volume negative, every normal toward the centre), so Surface Waves, push along normals and copies On Surface move or sit inward. The draw hides it because shading flips normals to the viewer. Cause: extrude_grid's side normal is (-ty, tx) times the depth sign, the left normal of the outline, which points in for a counter-clockwise outline; the cap normals follow the same sense. Fix shape: orient by the outline's signed area (shoelace) in both curve_sweep::extrude_grid and extrude_curve_body.wgsl, reversing the column order for one sense so winding and normals both face out; open and self-crossing outlines keep a fixed sense. L22a fixed the same fault for Tube (the ring now turns clockwise down the path).

title: Group frame parts carry position only; rotated or scaled parts deform in the wrong frame
description: Symptom: a modifier acting on a Group whose parts are rotated or scaled treats each part as if only moved, so the effect lands in the wrong place or direction on those parts. Cause: scene_compile modifiers.rs placement() sums positions only, and the live place node's pos_x/y/z is the only part offset the expand reads (SourceOffsetX/Y/Z). transform_components already decomposes rotation and scale. Fix shape: the expand wraps each shared-frame part's vertices stage with a part-to-frame rotate and scale and its inverse, or the recipes take the full placement; about 25 recipes read the translation-only offsets. Medium-large. Found in L22a (item 7).

title: Copy Blend's second layout is centred on the scene origin, not the target's centre
description: Symptom: Copy Blend morphs Copies toward a second layout that sits around the world origin, so a target moved away from the origin blends its copies toward a point far from it. Cause: node.arrange_copies has no origin input, and a recipe reaches the owner only through contexts; SourceOffset is frame-relative, not the target's world centre. No instance-translate atom exists besides displace_copies, which needs per-copy weights. Fix shape: give node.arrange_copies an origin (or frame Transform) input, or add a translate-instances atom, and feed a live target-centre context into the Copy Blend recipe. Port change, so the node catalog regenerates. Found in L22a (item 3).

title: Mirror and Spatial Echoes on Copies lose the mirrored half
description: Symptom: Scene Mirror (or Spatial Echoes) over an object with Copies draws only the original copies. Root cause suspect: the copies instance_count wire into the render clamps the drawn count to the pre-modifier count, so the doubled array from reflect_array is cut. Shared expand-path issue, not Scene Mirror specific. Fix shape: render count follows the last instance stage output, not the host count.
notes: L22a confirmed the cause: reflect_array writes originals at [0,cap) and mirrors at [cap,2cap) with cap = MAX_COPIES (65536), while the render draws only the copies body's live count, so the mirrors are never drawn. Dropping the count wire is wrong (it would draw 131072 instances, most zero-scale). Fix shape: instance stages carry a live count. reflect_array and analytic_echo_instances take the incoming count, pack their extra copies at [n,2n) and output count 2n; the expand rewrite routes instance_count from the last instance stage. That is a GPU atom port change plus fused codegen and a node-catalog regen, too big for L22a.

title: beat_ramp bars param counts beats, not bars
description: Symptom: node.beat_ramp param "bars" sets rate = 1/bars cycles per BEAT, so bars=8 loops every 8 beats (2 bars in 4/4). The label lies to anyone wiring it. Root cause: the primitive names the param bars but divides the beat clock directly. Fix shape: rename the param to beats (with catalog regen) or multiply by beats-per-bar from FrameTime. Scene Loop row works around it by labelling the row Beats (lane L21).

title: GPU proof fixtures still wire legacy render_scene per-object ports
description: node.render_scene takes one object_i port per object (node.scene_object); these proof fixtures still wire mesh_i/transform_i/material_i/*_map_i straight in and so likely fail to load (no input port mesh_0): render_scene_map_set, render_legacy_parity, rt_r2_accumulation, render_scene_ao_mask, rt_w0_gbuffer, motion_blur_visibility, render_scene_shadow_cache, rt_object_motion_shadow, gbuffer_depth, gbuffer_velocity, render_scene_pbr_fidelity, scene_viewport_session (crates/manifold-nodes/tests/gpu_proofs). Not run. Fix shape: pass each graph through manifold_nodes::testkit::scene_objects::bundle_scene_objects before loading, as rt_p3_emissive_texture and render_scene_subsurface now do (both green), or delete proofs that test removed behaviour.

title: Live Matter: the fill seeds through a Fixed body standing in a coupled pool
description: Symptom: gpu proof matter_bodies::matter_fill_skips_colliders fails after its fixture moved to the real API (a Fixed node.rigid_body in a node.physics_world coupled with the domain): 0 unused seed slots where about 5898 are expected; the liquid seeded inside the box is pushed out on the first tick. On stage: water in a pool around a submerged rock jumps at the start. The other three collider proofs pass on the same fixture. Root cause: unknown. Suspects: at the epoch the fill seeds, the coupled body rows or body_count the domain publishes do not yet hold the owner bodies (the fill only reads rows 0..body_count of bodies at the epoch start), or the owner arrives one epoch after the fill copied its seeds. Fix shape: make the epoch that seeds the pool the one that already has the coupled bodies (publish owner rows at prepare on owner_fresh) and rerun the proof.

title: Scene document: a Scene panel edit still restarts GPU water; removing a body restarts coupled water
description: Symptom: any Scene panel edit that recompiles the scene layer restarts a running GPU FLIP or Live Matter water, and removing a body from a coupled world restarts the water. Root cause: WaterRuntime carry_physics_state_from adopts only node.physics_world, rigid_body, fluid_role_source and time-integrating nodes; the GPU liquid domains and their persistent arrays and substep-boundary buffers are not carried across a graph rebuild, so the domain starts fresh. Removal: RigidSimulation rebuilds its world when a held body leaves (port_map refuses), so LiquidRigidOwner::admit returns false and the owner starts a new epoch. Adding a body to a running coupled world no longer restarts the owner (fix lane C: admit + rebind between ticks). Fix shape: carry GPU domain state (domain node, persistent arrays, history) across a rebuild when the domain setup is unchanged; for removal, remove the body from the live Box3D world and rebind instead of rebuilding. Ruling 23: growing never restarts a simulation.
notes: Sweep 28 Oct: a coupling error also restarts the pair. gpu_flip_domain.rs:1267-1273 and :790-793 drop the rigid owner on a dead reaction or failed step ("the pair restarts with a fresh rigid owner"), so bodies snap back and the water refills; the card error lasts about a frame. Matter: matter_domain.rs:1218-1222.

title: Scene document: a Body is pushed only by the first Water it touches
description: Symptom: with two or more Water objects, bodies float only in the first Water; later Waters take the solids massless (SharedSolids rows) and never push back. Blender pushes a body from every fluid it touches. Root cause: the first Water owns the Box3D world (LiquidRigidOwner, manifold-water-liquid coupling.rs); other Waters get SharesSolids/SharedSolidsPair (manifold-nodes-water physics_scene.rs), which carry rows but no reaction path. Fix shape: one rigid owner per physics world shared by every coupled Water; each Water tick contributes its reaction, and Box3D steps once per tick on the summed impulses. Needs the Waters ticking on one interleaved tick grid (engine substep region feature), not a one-frame-late reaction, which would be frame-rate dependent in export. Found by fix lane C (item 1), not attempted.

title: Copies Count: warn on the row when the frame budget is at risk (ruling 23)
description: Ruling 23 (no arbitrary limits): MAX_COPIES is now 65536, a memory ceiling (instance buffers allocated up front). Peter asked for a warning on the Count row instead of a block when many copies with Body physics put the frame budget at risk. No row-warning mechanism exists in the param surface (PropertyRow has no warning slot). Fix shape: a warning facet on scene card rows fed from the physics world copy count / setup_check, drawn by the param surface recipe. Found by lane L19.

title: Scene-doc wave reds outside the fix lane: matter collider proofs, render_scene mesh_0 fixtures, OceanCliff paddle, Mirage fixture
description: Seen by the phase B fix lane on lane/scene-doc-fix-b (base bddba532f); none touched by its diff, base status not rerun. (1) GPU: manifold-nodes gpu_proofs matter_bodies::{matter_fill_skips_colliders, matter_solid_lattice_matches_bodies, matter_collider_penetration_bounded, matter_open_mesh_collider_holds_liquid} panic "the colliders never became ready" (MatterScene colliders are fluid_role_source roles; root cause unknown, suspects the L4 mesh-only shape admission and L7 Matter state). (2) GPU: rt_p3_emissive_texture::emissive_uv_transform_applies_at_hit_sample and render_scene_subsurface::closed_white_random_walk_conserves_environment_energy fixtures wire render_scene mesh_0, a port that no longer exists; fix: port the fixtures to scene_object wiring or delete. (3) CPU: catalog_tests::physics_sampling::ocean_cliff_paddle_is_replayed_per_tick: OceanCliff.json lost its paddle node in L7 (paddle_transform feeds nothing). (4) CPU: renderer_contracts saved_copy_shows::mirage_physics_plays_as_it_did_on_main fails to deserialize its old saved show (an old-show proof; pre-release rule says old shows may break: delete or regenerate).

title: Ruling 23: a rigid body takes at most 64 parts (static part_k/mesh_k ports)
description: From the phase B fix lane, item 7 remainder. rigid_body is a primitive! node with 64 static part_k/mesh_k ports (physics_mesh.rs PART_PORTS/MESH_PORTS, RIGID_BODY_MAX_PARTS in scene_surface.rs), so a Group body takes at most 64 objects (scene_schema/physics.rs disabled-control text) and Copies of a group the same (scene_schema/copies.rs MAX_GROUP_PARTS). No physics or memory reason: the hull cap behind it is gone. Fix shape: give rigid_body node-owned ports that grow with a parts count param, as node.physics_world now does (PortNames grow, count_param), and drop both disabled-control refusals.

title: Swarm emitter gaps left by L6: Box volume, all Group parts, world-space forces, drawn Group keeps its Copies
description: From the phase B fix lane (lane/scene-doc-fix-b), item 8, not done there. Four gaps in scene_compile/swarm.rs against SCENE_DOCUMENT_DESIGN.md section 7.11 (Swarm): (1) Emit From Box scatters on the cube surface; node.spawn_from_mesh has vertex and surface modes only, so a volume mode is primitive work. (2) Emit From a Group seeds from its first part only (first_mesh); no node merges several meshes with their part transforms, so this needs a multi-mesh seed or a mesh merge primitive. (3) Forces act in the swarm frame (a Wind turns with the emitter): node.swarm_forces lays the world-space field at emitter-local lattice positions; fix shape is a frame input on swarm_forces that samples the field at the frame-mapped position and turns the vector back into the frame (TickForces fill, FillWorkers and the impulse lattice all take it), with the frame in the lattice cache key. (4) A Group drawn by a swarm ignores its own Copies: needs composed instance sets. Each is primitive work under DECOMPOSING_GENERATORS.md section 2.5 (audit by analogy) with a GPU proof.

title: HDRI always read at 2048x1024 whatever the file size
description: Symptom: a 4k HDRI shows a softer sky than the file. Root cause: node.hdri_source width and height params stay at their defaults (also on main). Fix shape: size the source from the file header when the file is picked. Found by the scene document phase A review.

title: Dynamic RT perf acceptance has no frame-budget test after the scene document cut
description: rt_dynamic_held_out.rs (held-out and reference-content app perf tests) was deleted with the old scene path, so scripts/rt_dynamic_acceptance.py perf mode reports the live content-thread budget as not evaluated and stays blocked. Fix shape: one new app perf test on a scene-document scene with a mesh modifier under dynamic RT, wired into the script. Found by the phase A merge of the scene document run.

title: Per-display camera pick: each output or display renders its own scene camera
description: Ruling 11 of docs/SCENE_DOCUMENT_DESIGN.md wants each output or display to pick its own camera (multi-display rigs). Outputs today are placements of one composited frame (stage.rs, presentation.rs), so a camera per display means rendering the scene once per distinct camera in use and compositing per display. Needs a design: where the pick lives as a mappable param (outputs have no param surface), how many cameras render at once, and the cost. The overnight run builds the per-layer live camera cut only (L8b).

title: Scene-doc base reds: impulse fire proofs and two scene-modifier catalog tests fail at df95dd7ce
description: Symptom: failing on wave/scene-document at df95dd7ce with no lane changes (verified by running them on the clean tree): manifold-app content_pipeline::trigger_lane_force_tests (scene_impulse_fired_after_a_forward_seek_in_the_same_drain_lands_once, a_fire_waiting_for_an_occluded_scene_across_a_bpm_up_edit_never_lands_ahead, scene_impulse_refusal_never_blocks_the_next_fire, scene_impulse_waiting_for_an_occluded_scene_lands_once, scene_impulse_fired_before_its_scene_renders_lands_once_after) log "Body(0) is out of the world: a body needs a mesh" and refuse with "impulse target body slot 0 is absent"; manifold-nodes contracts catalog_tests acceleration::all_objects_force_picks_up_body_added_after_attachment and validate::every_bundled_scene_modifier_qualifies_on_a_real_scene. Root cause unknown; suspects: the raw-graph fixtures predate the CollisionShape admission (a body whose shape is not ready is held), and the old scene-modifier path deleted in L2. Fix shape: port the fixtures to the scene document or delete tests on removed behaviour. Found by lane F1.

title: Scene document: RecursiveSkeletons draws different skinned geometry than its golden
description: glb conformance RecursiveSkeletons: the new import (lane/scene-doc-l3 at 0d154394c) draws several skinned columns of different heights, larger and right of centre; the golden from the old importer shows one skinned column near centre (mean abs 8.93). Root cause unknown. Suspects: old importer collapsed the skins to one draw, or the new skinned path poses away from bind pose. Check against the Khronos sample reference image before touching the golden. Compare image: scratchpad cmp_RecursiveSkeletons.png from the glb sweep lane.

title: GPU FLIP pressure solve on Auto seems to run far past its normal 11 to 14 rounds on churning water; lowering Max Iterations from 900 eases the export GPU kills
description:
Symptom: in Downloads/scene testing.manifold, Peter observed on 2026-10-22 that lowering the water Max Iterations from 900 (the default, FLIP Fluids cap) to 10 seemed to help the export GPU watchdog kills, though export still fails; not measured. Rounds past the stop are meant to cost nothing (gated template, see the MAX_ITERATIONS doc in crates/manifold-water-gpu-flip/src/primitives/gpu_flip_pressure.rs), so the cap should only matter if Auto runs well past the 11 to 14 rounds seen on saved problems.

Root cause: unknown. Suspects: TOLERANCE is 1e-9 relative on the max residual, at the edge of f32, and may be unreachable on large churning problems or with bodies, so the solve stalls to the cap; or gated rounds past the stop are not actually free.

Fix shape: read the solver recorded progress (PROGRESS_FLOATS residuals) on this scene to get the real round count per solve, pressure and density both. If it stalls, fix the stop (a reachable f32 tolerance or a stall detector) rather than lowering the cap. A realtime-sane default cap around 50 is only a named stopgap. Related: the Impacting Interactivity export watchdog bead, BUG-j8clo (pressed-lid first solves hit the 64-iteration cap unconverged).

title: Verify lane tool trim took effect
description: In a fresh session, spawn a trivial lane and check its transcript: tool count in agent-*.prefix.json and first-call context size. Before: 44 tools, ~59k start. Target: no mcp__ tools, ~30k start. If mcp__ tools remain, disallowedTools: mcp__* in ~/.claude/agents/lane.md is not honoured by the desktop app (2.1.299); fall back to naming the servers or a tools allowlist (keep SubagentHandback, SendMessage, Monitor, TaskStop, ToolSearch, Skill).

title: G2a Transform chains and nested scene groups
description: Model: Opus, high. Wave 1 (parallel with G1). compound_model_design.md D1, D2 and section 7 G2a: transform_3d parent input, Transform::world composed on the CPU, Group row kind at any depth, gizmo in the parent frame, recursive Scene tab tree.
notes: Merges into the redesign branch of epic BUG-elwvu first (docs/SCENE_DOCUMENT_DESIGN.md section 11, lane L1). Keep open until that branch lands.

title: G1 Renderer instance space for copies of a group
description: Model: Opus, high. Wave 1 (parallel with G2a). compound_model_design.md D11 and section 7 G1: scene_object instances_space (Object default, Group), shader world = A·T·B, raster/points/shadows/velocity/RT descriptor kernel/selection mask, one GPU proof. Already started.
notes: Merges into the redesign branch of epic BUG-elwvu first (docs/SCENE_DOCUMENT_DESIGN.md section 11, lane L1). Keep open until that branch lands.

title: Scene groups: imports arrive as groups of the file's pieces; Cmd+G and Cmd+Shift+G; physics by placement
description: Design: side-session notes compound_model_design.md (approved 2026-10-22). Imports keep the glTF node tree as nested groups (pass-through nodes collapse); Combine Meshes switch, off by default; Cmd+G/Cmd+Shift+G group and ungroup scene objects; group card with parent-times-child transform, group material for parts without their own; physics and water roles decided by where they sit (group = one body, a hull set per part; part = own body); Copies of a whole group (renamed from Copy Group). Nine lanes G1, G2a, G2b, G3, G4a, G5, G7, G4b, G6.

title: Move physics membership compile out of node-engine (engine physics-word ratchet back to 51)
description: Move the physics membership compile (crates/manifold-node-engine/src/load/physics_members.rs, its mod.rs line, and the physics_members uses in validate.rs, graph_loader.rs, acceleration.rs, shatter.rs) out of node-engine into the physics side (manifold-nodes-physics), so the engine physics-word ratchet in crates/manifold-app/tests/crate_layering.rs (ENGINE_WATER_WORD_FILES) goes back from 53 to 51 or lower. title: Order golden red on main
description: ui_snapshot::order_golden::paint_and_hit_order_match_full_build fails on main: paint and panels hashes differ from the recorded golden. Seen by two lanes on 2026-10-21 bases (e10811d15 era and 98abbfecb), unchanged by their branches.
