title: Half-resolution march with full-resolution refine for 4K and multi-display
description: Direction doc D2 consequences. The direct level-set march costs per pixel: 1080p takes a few ms, 4K live takes 4x that without help. Search at half resolution, then refine at full resolution with one or two exact steps per pixel from the coarse hit, so the picture stays full-res. Multi-display is the same cost story. Part of direct level-set rendering, kept as its own bead so the 4K and multi-display numbers get measured on their own. Exports do not care about the cost.

title: Whitewater detail: a foam field on the surface and draw-time child particles
description: Peter's condition on 2026-10-08 18:12: children, a foam field and real motion blur only come later, if the renders still look thin. Foam is stored on the surface itself and read by the tracer on purpose (review correction the same day). Gate on Peter's look after the whitewater-as-spheres bead lands.
notes: Foam as a surface field is pulled forward: third in the look stack (D13), carried by the flow, gathering where water converges, read by the march and the tracer. Child particles stay conditional on renders looking thin.

title: Water mesh ray-tracing acceleration structure: suspected 400 B per vertex and a double copy during rebuild
description: Symptom: GPU memory at 128 carries 6 to 8 GB nobody can name. Root cause: unknown. Suspect the per-frame rebuild keeps the old acceleration structure alive while it builds the new one. Fix shape after the memory ledger bead names it: refit or rebuild in place, and build from the indexed mesh. Evidence: the lead's fit on 2026-10-17 18:23, about 400 bytes for every mesh vertex, best guess the ray-tracing structure. Direct level-set rendering (direction doc D2) removes the mesh structure from the live path, so this is the interim and export-path fix. Belongs in the Memory budget too: report the saved bytes there.

title: Whitewater particles and the water surface report their own velocity to the camera motion blur
description: The motion blur node only knows camera and object motion, so flying spray never blurs. Each particle reports its own velocity, and the camera blur already there handles the rest. Evidence: Peter, 2026-10-08 18:13, asked whether this is the camera's responsibility; the answer, with an estimate of a day or two. With direct level-set rendering the water surface has no mesh to carry motion, so it needs its own motion vectors (direction doc D2 consequences).
notes: For the water surface the motion vectors come straight from the sim velocity field in the march (D13); whitewater reports per particle.

title: Whitewater as true spheres: impostors on screen and analytic spheres in the ray tracer, landed together
description: Today each whitewater particle is a 20-sided mesh with a full material. Draw sphere impostors on screen (depth-correct) and hit analytic spheres in the tracer, in one landing, so ray tracing never drops whitewater from reflections. Evidence: session 286cd13d, 2026-10-08, lead estimate 2 to 3 weeks; Peter at 19:11: we shouldn't leave partial ray tracing support. BUG-imy3.7 (whitewater pool full: replace oldest) notes that sphere impostors were discussed in the same session as separate, later work. Supersedes the remainder of BUG-ddba (whitewater spray and bubbles as plain blend layers).

title: GPU FLIP water under the ray tracer: traced refraction and transmission through the water
description: On main the water refracts only through raster screen-space refraction plus Beer-Lambert (RAYTRACING_DESIGN.md:1708). The tracer carries only a sun-transmission tint (manifold-gpu/src/metal/raytrace/tracer.rs:324). Trace refraction and absorption through the water, across separate water bodies along one ray, with a bounded path, through manifold-gpu so Vulkan can follow. Per direction doc D2 the trace walks the level set through a custom intersection on the water's tiles, not an indexed mesh; the mesh version is the interim path only if direct rendering slips. Replaces BUG-vglg.1 (native water RT entry bracketing) and BUG-vglg.2 (disconnected liquid intervals), which target water_raytrace.metal on the unlanded wave/live-water branch (8f3cdd23f) and are absent from main.

title: One level set for solver and render: build the high-quality surface field once and feed both
description: Free-performance class (direction doc section 4): remove work, do not speed it up. The solver keeps a signed-distance grid and the surface build makes its own from the particles. Build the high-quality field once and feed both the solver and the render, so nothing is built twice. Its quality step is BUG-uvdu (liquid surface level set is a homegrown hybrid, not Yu-Turk), so size the two together. Reports its cost against the fresh frame split.

title: Overlap the next sim tick with this frame's render
description: Free-performance class (direction doc section 4): the GPU never idles. Encode and run the next sim tick while this frame's render is still on the GPU, so neither waits for the other. Today a coupled liquid runs encode and GPU in series per tick: see BUG-r6bjf (content thread spins on the previous tick's reaction) and BUG-gqzj0 (res 16 coupled box at 18 fps, 0 ms GPU wait). Pairs with BUG-6qo32 (draw the newest water frame without waiting for the CPU readback). Measure with the GPU busy percent bead in the Measurement sub-epic.

title: GPU FLIP display history P3: lead-run 60 fps and GPU-bound Dam Break, Peter looks
description: GPU_FLIP_DISPLAY_HISTORY_DESIGN.md status is IN PROGRESS: P1 and P2 landed, owed P3, Peter's stage look (section 5). Its bead BUG-ckvpp (display shows every third tick, never interpolated) is closed, so P3 has no owner. The lead runs a 60 fps and a GPU-bound Dam Break, then Peter looks. Watch list from section 5: holds in the first second after load or re-pour, and holds after a Speed step.

title: GPU memory budget per resolution, reported per landing: 128 live under 2 GB, 256 solver state under 1 GB, 512 export inside 36 GB
description: Direction doc D4. Memory follows the water, with a budget per resolution: 128 live stays under 2 GB total, 256 keeps its solver state under 1 GB, and 512 export fits inside this machine's 36 GB. Every landing in the programme reports its GPU memory against the budget, so a landing that grows memory shows it. Done when the budget is written into the design spec, the ledger from the measurement sub-epic gives the starting numbers, and the first landing reports against it.

title: GPU FLIP: one scratch pool for transfer, extend, solve and density scratch
description: Advection, solve and transfer scratch never coexist inside the step, so one pool can serve them all. Evidence: same seven-lever list, item 6; the audit found the opposite, separate copies everywhere. BUG-l2h3.6 (substep region arrays never released) covers only the graph planner's substep regions, and BUG-kipwz (mesh held as five copies) covers only the mesh. Reports memory against the budget.

title: Dispatch to live counts, never capacity, across the step
description: Free-performance class (direction doc section 4): passes should size their work from the live count on the GPU, with no CPU readback, never from capacity. Existing instances are BUG-htgr (whitewater live-bound pool passes by indirect dispatch) and BUG-g75v.5.4 (sort tail re-zero: every cell sort re-zeroes the whole tail up to capacity). Audit the rest of the step for passes still sized by capacity, and move each to an indirect dispatch off the live count. Measure each against the fresh frame split.

title: APIC transfers on GPU FLIP, the bridge to one shared grid with MPM
description: Direction doc D3. Each particle carries one affine matrix (36 B at f32, 18 B at f16). That gives less noise at the same particle count, it is Houdini's default, and it is the bridge to one shared grid with MPM, which already transfers this way. Peter, 2026-10-06 13:40: our FLIP needs APIC to integrate with MPM properly. Particle memory roughly doubles; particles are not the budget (D4). Split out of BUG-jk5zt (APIC transfer option and mesh-shaped or mid-run fluid objects): the mesh-shaped and mid-run fluid objects half stays there, in the Instrument sub-epic. The engine offers APIC through its bridge (fluidsimulation.cpp:7323); GPU FLIP has FLIP and PIC only. GPU_FLIP_PRESSURE_SOLVE.md section 10 holds the deferred row APIC on faces. Prove it look-identical or better, and against the long-run settled-pool gate BUG-0cbzb (GPU FLIP default has no long-run agreement gate). Design spec before build. Whether it becomes the default is Peter's call once proven.

title: GPU FLIP pressure: warm start from last pressure, fuse smoother levels
description: Both are rows in GPU_FLIP_PRESSURE_SOLVE.md section 10 (Deferred). Warm start begins each solve from last tick's pressure. Fused smoother levels run the smoothing of several multigrid levels in one dispatch. The fused-smoother trigger (the smoothing row passes half the solve) looks met: pressure.smooth was the single largest dispatch ratio at 64 on 2026-10-03 (13.7). Measure after the fresh frame split. Output must stay inside the solve tolerance and iteration counts get reported. Free-performance class: fewer passes (direction doc section 4).

title: GPU FLIP: Sheet Fill Rate refuses to run with Narrow Band
description: read_sheet_fill_rate (gpu_flip_step/read_params.rs:30-35) refuses sheeting when Narrow Band is on, because the band resorts break sheet seeding. Sheeting is an engine feature (port the whole reference) and narrow band is the particle-cost lever for 128, so a scene cannot have both today. Fix shape: make sheet seeding follow the band's resorts, and prove it with the sheeting step proofs under both settings. Evidence: the code, and the lead's answer on 2026-10-18 that it also can't run together with Sheet Fill Rate yet. Whether narrow band becomes the default for deep scenes is a separate call for Peter: bubbles sealed deep below the band lose their particles.

title: Report GPU busy percent in the frame split; find the idle bubbles
description: The GPU should never idle. Add GPU busy percent to the frame split, next to the per-node times, so the gaps where the GPU waits on the CPU show up as a number. Two beads already show CPU-bound frames with zero GPU wait: BUG-gqzj0 (res 16 with a coupled box at 18 fps, 0 ms GPU wait) and BUG-r6bjf (content thread spins on the previous tick's reaction, encode and GPU never overlap). Done when the frame split prints busy percent for 64 and 128 and the idle bubbles are listed. Feeds the overlap-the-next-tick bead in the Live timing sub-epic. Direction doc section 4 (the GPU never idles).

title: Review unlanded water branches before anyone rebuilds their work
description:
Six unlanded branches hold water work nobody has judged: lane/velocity-extension (b9bf7c137, WIP tiled extension for BUG-g75v.5.5 (velocity extrapolation 12 full-grid layers)), archive slot-5 lentine-coarse-solve (a8aa29c7c), archive gpu-flip-absent-solids (6589251a2, marked unverified experiment), diag/gpu-flip-feel (a469ad451, a probe), wave/live-water (8f3cdd23f, holds the only native water ray-tracing code), feat/fft-water (the retired solver). For each one: land it, salvage it into a named bead, or delete it with Peter's yes.

BUG-30pa6 (review the forgotten unlanded branches) covers tooling lanes only. perf/liquid-surface already has BUG-loysi (unlanded surface wins).

title: GPU FLIP as an instrument: performer controls that shape the water
description:
Sub-epic 7 of the GPU FLIP end game (docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md section 3).

Water-specific performer features. Generic setup UX (gizmos, out-of-domain feedback, object model, takes, bake) stays in BUG-gm927 (water setup you can see and trust), BUG-8gjbd (scene setup programme) and BUG-vglg (shared liquid physics). This sub-epic holds only what makes the water itself playable.

End state on stage: driven bodies, audio-shaped waves, wave tanks that do not resonate, the ocean feeding the tank, and action areas inside a height-field sea.

title: GPU FLIP water rendering: one look under raster and ray tracer, caustics, whitewater as spheres
description:
Sub-epic 5 of the GPU FLIP end game (docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md section 3).

How the water and whitewater are lit and drawn once the surface comes straight from the level set: material, refraction and transmission, the ray tracer, caustics, motion blur. Peter's rule from 2026-10-08: no partial ray tracing support, so raster and ray tracer land together. No quality dial and no separate export path.

Caustics and an underwater camera are assumed in at priority 3, after traced water (direction doc section 6 item 4, Peter's call).

End state on stage: the same water under raster and ray tracer; refraction and caustics that read as water; spray as spheres; particle velocity in the motion blur; foam as a field on the surface.

title: GPU FLIP memory: memory follows the water, with a budget per resolution
description:
Sub-epic 2 of the GPU FLIP end game (docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md D4 and D5).

Memory follows the water. BUG-7wna (GPU FLIP sparse tile storage) then BUG-zdiuw (GPU FLIP infinite domain, the world-keyed tile table) make lattice memory proportional to wet tiles and the domain unbounded. Today the work is sparse but the memory is still the dense box, the surface mesh is held as five copies, and 6 to 8 GB at 128 is still unaccounted for. The mesh capped Peter's 128 Surface Detail 1 and 192 exports on 2026-10-17.

Budgets: 128 live under 2 GB total. 256 under 1 GB of solver state. 512 export inside this machine's 36 GB. Every landing in the programme reports its memory against the budget.

16-bit is storage, never arithmetic (D5). Particle position is a 16-bit integer offset inside the particle's tile, about one eight-thousandth of a cell. Velocity in f16 is gated by BUG-0cbzb (GPU FLIP default has no long-run agreement gate); if a resting pool jitters, velocity stays f32 and the particle is 24 B. The pressure solve stays f32. Grid fields may be stored f16 where a pass only reads them. The 2D texture sims quantised because the whole state lived in f16 across steps; here particles are the state and the grid is rebuilt every step.

The mesh itself leaves the live path through the Surface sub-epic. BUG-kipwz (mesh held as five copies) lives here only as the stopgap that unblocks exports until then.

End state on stage: memory follows the water; the budgets are met and reported per landing.
notes: Design: docs/WATER_SHARED_GRID_DESIGN.md (28 Oct, e34a7180f). Today ~730 B per sim cell, ~61-85 B per display cell, ~430 B per particle slot; a full water cell is ~4 KB and particles are four fifths of it. Phases filed as children.

title: Editor flows over TextMeasureMiss ceiling on main
description: Red on main at 0823a8957: work-editor-open open_click TextMeasureMiss 11 > 8 and work-node-param-drag card_lane_drag TextMeasureMiss 6 > 0. Identical on the P7c branch. Root cause unknown; suspect text-measure cache warmth depending on flow batch order, since lanes saw counts change with batch composition. Fix shape: make the text-measure miss count independent of batch order (cold cache per flow window) or find the editor-side remeasure.

title: GPU FLIP infinite domain: lattice memory bounded by the water, not the box
description:
Idea (Peter, 2026-10-21): make GPU FLIP domain size free so GPU memory limits how much water is live, not the space it can cover.

Today: the sparse tile table from BUG-jyot (GPU FLIP at 128 for 60 fps) skips work on empty tiles, but every lattice buffer is still allocated dense over the fixed T^3 box, and the extend pass writes every record on purpose because the box walls are a velocity source (GPU_FLIP_SPARSE_BLOCKS_DESIGN.md D-4, the dense extend). Memory is still the domain, not the water.

Shape: key the tile table by world tile coordinate through a hash or page table (SPGrid / OpenVDB style, how Houdini FLIP works), size lattice buffers to a tile pool instead of T^3, make the extend frontier-only on active tiles (already named as a deferred option in the sparse-blocks design), make the box walls optional. The pressure solve is already per-tile list and mostly carries over. Once the origin is a tile offset, a moving domain is free because particles already live in world space: a camera can follow one wave, a river can cross the whole frame. Changing cell size wholesale is a resample (FLIP tolerates it, particles carry velocity, expect a pop).

Remaining limits after this: particle count (the real memory), the sort key range, float precision far from the origin (tile-relative coordinates fix it).

Out of scope: true multi-resolution / adaptive lattices (octree, Aanjaneya 2017 adaptive liquids) are a different and much harder solver; not where to start.

Depends on BUG-jyot sparse blocks finishing (tile lists, per-level solve lists). Stage meaning: the only knob that costs is how much water is on screen.
notes: Decided 2026-10-23 (docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md D4): proper world-keyed tiles, no box-shifting stopgap. The Water box becomes an optional Bounds setting, off by default: off, water goes anywhere in the scene; on, it is the region water may live in and water leaving it is removed, and moving it live keeps the water inside. Water ends only by falling below the lowest thing in the scene, or when GPU memory is full, where sources stop adding water and the card says why, never a crash. Priority 2, straight after BUG-7wna (sparse tile storage); the scene document makes the domain position a live param that may never reset the sim. Target scenes: an inflow filling a canyon, water pouring over a cliff.

title: Paste across layers drops the source clip's Model File override
description: Symptom: pasting a scene object onto another layer gives the copy its own Model File id (model_file_duplicate) that starts at the spec default, the original import path. If the source clip had swapped the Model File on the card (a per-clip override in clip.string_params), the pasted copy loads the original scan, not the one the source shows. Duplicate on the same layer carries clip overrides since lane/import-identity-scale; Paste goes through ReplaceGeneratorStateCommand and the destination layer has no matching clips, so nothing carries. Root cause: the one metadata copier (manifold-editing binding_transfer::transfer_bindings) copies specs at their defaults and has no notion of a per-clip value. Fix shape: input to the typed identity one-metadata-copier work (BUG-aszjq typed identity): the clipboard captures the source's effective string value at copy time and the paste seeds the copy's spec default (or every destination clip) with it. Test: copy an object whose clip swapped Model File to B, paste on another layer, the copy resolves to B.
notes: 2026-10-22: closes with the scene groups epic BUG-8k8ko (Scene groups); lane named in compound_model_design.md section 10.

title: With the clock stopped at 0, adding a force changes what a physics scene shows
description: Found by the import lane (lane/import-identity-scale f0a9814a1) with render-generator-preset --hold-time on the migrated cliftest: without a force the frame renders fully black and settles; with a Radial Force it renders the cliff and never settles. Motion is off in that show (34_motion=0). Root cause unknown; suspects: physics_world.rs holding pending outputs until the clock moves, or pose seeding when the clock never advances, with the force path forcing an output. Check: the same pair at a nonzero fixed time, and the app stopped at bar 1. A stopped transport must show the same picture with or without a force.

title: Cheap gate should run the god-file regrowth check
description: Two lanes on 2026-10-21 (gizmo-selection, water-inflow-column) passed the --cheap gate and then went red at landing on no_file_regrowth_past_its_ceiling (manifold-app tests/godfile_regrowth.rs), costing a landing round each. The check is a line count and runs in well under a second. Fix shape: scripts/landing_gate.py --cheap runs godfile_regrowth for any touched file, so lanes see it before their commit.

title: Measure GPU water cost with the 2^20 inflow pool; run passes over the live count if it shows
description: From the inflow review (review_inflow.md): with an Inflow the GPU FLIP pool is 2^20 slots, and the move, sort and narrow-band passes dispatch over every slot each substep even when only a trickle is live, possibly a few ms a frame. Measure: one gpu_queue profile of the cliftest scene at Resolution 64 with its inflow. If the cost shows, dispatch those passes over the live count (indirect dispatch from the live counter) instead of the pool. Also fix the liquid_fill purpose text that calls the pool slots past the fill count (it is the total pool) with the column lane, which edits liquid_fill.
notes: Sweep 28 Oct: the pool stays at 1M slots with the Inflow disabled (presence, not Enabled, gpu_flip_domain.rs:312). Display passes size by capacity, not the wired live count: sort_particles_into_cells.rs:555 clear_tail, shape_particle_blobs.rs:79-110, surface_weights.rs:307-312, wet_map.rs:349, spray_mist.rs:250 (~29 MB of tail writes a frame at 1M slots, 100k live).

title: Domain walls need free body slots that authoring does not reserve
description: From BUG-aszjq (typed identity) design 2.1. Symptom: a full physics world with closed domain faces fails at runtime. Root cause: domain walls take the highest free body slots at runtime (manifold-water-liquid coupling.rs:118-150); authoring capacity does not reserve them. Fix shape: authoring reserves the wall slots (or walls live outside the body table).

title: Shatter fragments share one free slot pool across Shatters
description: From BUG-aszjq (typed identity) design 2.1. Symptom: changing one Shatter Pieces count moves another Shatter fragment slots and their per-slot state (fragment_parent_released[MAX_BODIES]). Root cause: fragments take the lowest free slots of the compiled graph (manifold-node-engine load/expand/compiler/shatter.rs:206-209), one shared pool. Suspect also: hits miss fragments, since impulse recipients come from the authored owner so only the parent slot bit is set (manifold-nodes-water runtime/physics_impulses.rs:200). Fix shape: per-Shatter slot ranges or typed membership from the identity work.

title: Duplicate: independent copy or linked to the same model file?
description: Lead default D-117 (Blender Shift+D): Duplicate makes an independent copy; its model-file binding starts at the same path but is its own, so changing one object file never changes another. Linked duplicates (Blender Alt+D) would be a later feature. Peter may overrule. From the typed identity design (BUG-aszjq).

title: Water surface mesh reports a NodeError for one frame while its buffer grows
description: Symptom: a GPU FLIP scene whose surface needs more vertices than the mesh buffer holds (100-cube fixture: 119748 needed against 93636) fails frame 1 with a NodeError while the buffer grows; found in the CG0 fix round (lane/copy-group-world 30cb801d6), worked around in the fixture by raising max_capacity to 262144. On stage a scene can flash an error frame when the surface grows. Root cause: the surface mesh capacity is sized ahead and growth is reported as an error instead of being absorbed. Fix shape: grow the buffer at setup from the domain plan, or grow before use without a failed frame; never surface a NodeError for a capacity the node can fix itself.
notes: Superseded for the live path when direct level-set rendering (docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md D2) lands; stays open as the export-path item until then.

title: Gizmo: pick a scene object by its mesh bounds, not its origin
description: After BUG-6u36g (domain box cannot be picked) every helper shape is picked by its own drawn edges, but a scene object (photoscan, mesh) is still picked only within 22pt of its origin, because its declared box is the transform, not the mesh extent. Fix shape: give the object target an outline from its mesh bounds (render_scene already knows them) through ShapeOutline in crates/manifold-nodes-scene/src/node_graph/viewport_gizmo.rs, so a click anywhere on a large photoscan selects it, as Blender does.

title: Decimate the WaterInScan cliff scan: 19.2 ms p50 at 1080p, over the 60 fps budget
description: Water in a Photoscan (F1 starter) measured 19.2 ms p50 / 22.6 p95 GPU at 1080p vs 12.7 ms for stock Dam Break; the 2.9M-vertex cliff scan costs about 6.5 ms. The collider SDF is built once and cached, so the cost is drawing and coupling. A welded, simplified scan at 15-25% of the triangles with the existing normal map should look the same. Fix shape: decimate offline, ship the lighter asset, re-measure through gpu_queue. Related: BUG-ozxss (bundled asset library) for where the asset lives.

title: Host drivers and envelopes on a physics param are held between frames
description: Symptom (derived from code, not reproduced): a host param written by a driver (host LFO) or an envelope, feeding a simulation (Speed, a force strength), reaches tick starts with the frame's composed value, so the simulation depends on display rate. Root cause: the physics replay (crates/manifold-nodes-water/src/runtime/physics_sampling.rs) holds external params between frames; automation lanes (lane read at each sample's beat) and audio hops are the only host sources it evaluates per sample. Composition (compose_param) lives in manifold-playback, which the replay cannot call. Fix shape: evaluate the full host composition at replay sample times, for example by moving compose_param's driver and envelope evaluation into manifold-core so the replay can run it, then drop the drivers/envelopes exclusion in PhysicsInputSnapshot::set_automation. Proof: a driver-ramped Speed ticking bit-identically at 30/60/120/144 fps live and export.

title: gpu_queue lock starves waiters: a holder that re-acquires between legs never yields
description: Symptom: on 2026-10-21 trunk_health.py (nightly) held the GPU lock for 1h40m+, re-acquiring it between its gpu legs, while lane renders through scripts/gpu_queue.py waited 50+ minutes and never got a turn. Root cause: the lock is a bare flock on ~/.cache/manifold/gpu.lock, which is not fair; a holder that releases and immediately re-acquires wins the race against waiters. Fix shape: a fair ticket queue (waiters take a ticket file in order; release hands to the next ticket), or trunk_health holding one lock across all its gpu legs only when nobody waits and yielding between legs when a ticket exists. Scheduled nightly runs should also avoid the overnight lane window or yield to lanes.

title: Duplicate copies: offset by the object's width instead of a fixed 0.5 m?
description: C2 (rigid add and copies) places each copy 0.5 m further along X, per PHYSICS_ENGINE_BOUNDARY P6a. A photoscan wider than 0.5 m overlaps its copy, and with physics on the two bodies blow apart when play resumes. Option A (lead's pick): offset each copy by the source's bounds width along X plus a 0.5 m gap, so copies never overlap; needs the mesh bounds at duplicate time. Option B: keep the fixed 0.5 m and let the user spread copies. Industry: Blender duplicates in place and enters grab; Maya Duplicate Special uses a user-set translate; neither auto-spaces by bounds.

title: Flow work-browser-search red on main: FrameAlloc 445 over its 443 budget at type_query
description: Symptom: the work-browser-search UI flow fails at the type_query step with FrameAlloc=445 > 443 (per-frame allocation count over the flow budget). Seen on main's tree and on lane/one-add-menu (scene setup programme wave 2 keep-going gate, 2026-10-21). Root cause unknown; suspects: a recent main landing adding two allocations to the work browser search typing frame, or a stale recorded budget. Fix shape: find the two new allocations on the type_query frame and remove them (hot-path discipline); re-record only if the budget is proven stale.

title: History snapshot restore skips the app load steps
description: Symptom: restoring a history snapshot runs load_project_snapshot_with only (crates/manifold-app/src/app_lifecycle.rs:1112,1141) and never the app load steps that open_project_from_path runs, now one function prepare_loaded_project in project_io.rs (bindings by node id, scene bounds, migrate_project_scene_graphs with the material, exposure, modulated-row and D-103 old-show card pins). A snapshot taken before 1.22.0 restores with an empty scene card, and the next save writes 1.22.0, so its card rows are lost for good. Root cause: snapshot restore has its own load path. Fix shape: route snapshot loads through prepare_loaded_project like file opens and ui-snap project scenes. Found in the lane/one-add-menu B2b review (F3).

title: World Reset may lose its trigger after Add Water lifts it onto a node.value
description: Symptom (suspected, seen in the editing test stub, not yet seen in the app): when share_world_controls lifts a World control onto a shared node.value, the param lookup join (manifold-core param_lookup.rs overlay) reads the descriptor of the bound node type (node.value), so World Reset is_trigger becomes false and the card may show Reset as a slider after Add Water. Root cause suspect: the join takes trigger/units from the bound node, not the World descriptor the control was lifted from. Oracle: Add Water in a scene with a World, then read the Reset card spec is_trigger. Fix shape: the lifted control keeps its source descriptor (record the source type on the binding or resolve through the value node to its consumer). Found in lane/one-add-menu (scene setup programme B2a).

title: Swarm shaders compile on first use: 128 ms first frame
description: Symptom: first swarm frame takes 128 ms while the pipeline compiles; a visible hitch when a swarm first appears on stage (steady state is 0.28 ms for 100k). Root cause: move_swarm and swarm_to_copies compile their pipelines on first use, like the matter atoms. Fix shape: compile at preset install or prewarm with the other pipelines.

title: Mixed open and closed mesh: closed part still builds brute force at liquid cell size
description: After the narrow band (scene setup programme C1, 33ad9b0fb), a mesh with both open and sealed parts builds the sealed part by checking every lattice node against every closed triangle at the liquid cell size (crates/manifold-physics/src/sdf.rs:145-163), so a photoscan with sealed debris can still take minutes. Fix shape: a triangle grid or BVH for the closed part, or sign from a coarse closed lattice plus the narrow band near closed triangles. BUG-8gjbd, scene setup programme epic.

title: Water solid size warning reaches the role card, not only the log
description: When an open-mesh water solid hits MAX_LATTICE_NODES its lattice coarsens and the thin-collider warning fires, but only as log::warn (scene setup programme C1, f60684a25 on lane/open-mesh-solids). A silent coarsening on stage breaks the no-silent-clamp rule. Fix shape: carry the warning into the role source card through the existing diagnostic or inactive-reason path; one CPU test. Related: B3 setup check (BUG-gm927, water setup you can see and trust).
notes: Sweep 28 Oct: water-liquid bodies.rs:887-902 warns once per run (warned_thin never resets), so a second thin body logs nothing; the lattice-capped case (MAX_LATTICE_NODES) is log-only too.

title: Initial Fill level handle on the liquid domain box
description: Part of BUG-gm927 (water setup you can see and trust). The liquid domain's Initial Fill (fill level) gets no viewport handle: its param is a fraction of the domain height, and a SceneShapeDecl can only name world-space values (D-79). Needs: a declaration form for a level relative to the owner box's floor (a plane whose height is a fraction of the owner box size), then a Plane handle on the domain derived from it. The column is already declared as a box via initial_volume.

title: Synthetic test for migrate_legacy_param_values (Mirror 0/1/2 to 6/7/8) and its macro-mapping resolve
description: The Liveschool and old-show load tests were deleted 2026-10-20 (obsolete, Peter). migrate_legacy_param_values in crates/manifold-core/src/project/load_migration.rs (Mirror mode 0/1/2 -> 6/7/8) and its macro-mapping resolve step have no test; the converted 1.21 fixtures already stored the new values so they never exercised it. Fix shape: a small in-code project with an old Mirror value and a macro mapping, loaded through the migration, asserting the new value and the resolved mapping.
notes: Also untested: resolve_macro_mapping, both its parked legacy_effect_addr -> EffectId step and its legacy-index step (macro_bank.rs tests only that deserialization parks the address).

description:
Peter: mark these for me to review and understand properly later; unrelated to the scene setup programme. A read-only sweep on 2026-10-20 classified every local branch with commits not on origin/main. Nothing was deleted, merged or landed.

Forgotten, real work, never reviewed or gated (all 2026-10-13 tooling lanes, each with an open P1 bead):

- lane/regen-first: BUG-zezjf.9 (regenerate generated files before the gate) and BUG-dh1yd (docs index conflicts). land_branch resolves generated-file conflicts hunk by hunk, then regenerates. 5 main commits since.

Peter calls:

Already ruled into the scene setup programme (BUG-8gjbd): lane/scene-lighting-one-place folds into B2; lane/physics-overlay-shapes merges into A1.

title: Quit decides unsaved from the content thread, not the last UI snapshot
description: quit.rs:43 reads content_state.editing_is_dirty before this frame state is taken. On a clean project an edit made within one content tick of Cmd+Q (longer if the content thread stalls) quits without asking and the edit is lost; a param drag or text field still in progress at Cmd+Q is never sent. Fix shape: commit any in-progress gesture, then a synchronous dirty query to the content thread (like PrepareProjectSave) before deciding. Found by the daytime review of BUG-akqgc (quit loses unsaved changes).

title: Recovery autosave for untitled projects
description: An untitled project has no recovery copy. Autosave (autosave.rs) only runs when the project has a path, and every recovery route keys on that path: the history/ journal lives inside the project archive, and the --resume breadcrumb is a sidecar of the project file. BUG-akqgc (quit loses unsaved changes) added a Save / Dont Save / Cancel prompt on quit, but a crash or power loss in an untitled session still loses everything since launch. Open questions for Peter: where the recovery file lives (Application Support/MANIFOLD/Recovery, one file per session, how many kept, pruned when); what cadence (same 60 s debounce as autosave, or shorter); how the next launch offers it (the crash notice gains a Recover button, a File menu item, or an automatic reopen as an untitled copy); whether a clean quit with Dont Save deletes it; whether perform mode writes it (autosave is parked there today).

title: Gate treats every .txt as a doc, so golden fixtures select no test
description: Symptom: a diff touching only a golden fixture runs nothing at landing. scripts/diff_scope.py:210 drops every .md and .txt as docs, and observing_packages skips DOC_SUFFIXES too. Affected: crates/manifold-nodes/tests/fixtures/gpu_flip_body_golden.txt, fused_wgsl_snapshot.txt, whitewater_tick_golden.txt, crates/manifold-water-gpu-flip/tests/fixtures/gpu_flip_pressure_golden.txt, crates/manifold-app/src/ui_snapshot/order_golden.txt, crates/manifold-physics/native/box3d/src/CMakeLists.txt. Root cause: suffix-based doc detection. Fix shape: only paths under docs/ (and top-level *.md) count as docs; a .txt under crates/ is owned by its crate. Found by the batch 6 review, pre-existing.

title: Frame-exact transport: rig test, constant tuning, P4 video locking
description: Frame-exact transport remainder after BUG-gqhep (live-transport-nondeterministic-frame-clock) closed: P1 to P3 are on main (ff922660e, 2d64b50e1). Owed: Peter rig test of the P3 follower (docs/FRAME_EXACT_TRANSPORT_DESIGN.md section 6, P3 demo), constants tuned from the sync log, P4 video locking.

title: MIDI and OSC input received during an export may apply when it ends
description: Suspected (read, not run): MIDI and OSC are not ContentCommands. They are polled in the live content tick (content_thread.rs:630 tick_midi_input, :1698 osc_receiver.update), so the export drop rule (BUG-v2o9y, content_export.rs export_disposition) never sees them. If the export loop does not run the live tick, notes and OSC messages queue up and fire on the first tick after the export: phantom clips, clip launches and param writes from input that came in while the show was meant to be frozen. Verify: send NoteOns during a headless export and log what tick_midi_input sees on the first tick after it. Fix shape: drain and discard the MIDI and OSC queues when an export ends (or drain them each export frame), the same rule as dropped commands.

title: math_view_grid_app_control_journey fails: Math mode with all diagrams off is not black
description: Symptom: scene_modifier_journey::math_view_grid_app_control_journey (journey-proofs, scene_modifier_journey.rs:696) asserts a black frame and gets 6370 non-black pixels, found while running the journeys for BUG-bzid9 on lane/overnight-small-fixes. Root cause: unknown; suspects: a grid or backdrop that now draws with all diagrams off, or a render path change since the test was written. Fix shape: render the frame to PNG, decide whether the test or the output is wrong.

title: Math View historical-snapshots journey: second migration pass flips a sample_mode Enum 1 to 0
description: Symptom: legacy_math_view_historical_snapshots_migration_journey (journey-proofs, scene_modifier_journey.rs, idempotence assert) fails after the BUG-bzid9 notice filter: migrating the already-migrated graph again changes one node sample_mode param from Enum 1 to Enum 0 (first JSON diff at byte 419094, era Nested Multi Material Scan Baseline). Root cause: unknown; suspects: upgrade_math_views or migrate_legacy_math_views rewriting a sample_mode default on a pass that should be a no-op (92fe0c63c made the upgrade run on every load). Fix shape: find the node and the rewrite, make the pass idempotent, rerun the journey.

title: Design pass: the standard D/E/A modulation buttons on scene switches and pick lists
description: Peter 2026-10-20 on BUG-yloek: a scene switch or pick list (Cast Shadows, light Type, environment Mode, Whitewater on/off, box Arrangement) should ideally carry the same three standard buttons for adding a driver, envelope or audio mod as every slider; how modulation works on a non-slider control may need rethinking (what a driver or audio mod does to a choice). Since lane 14 (ff49632e2) these controls show no D/E/A buttons until something is attached, so nothing can be added from them. Design first (docs/DESIGN_AUTHORING.md), then build. BUG-n39yw (pick lists outside scenes) waits on this.

title: Scene colour row: mark the unmarked RGB triplets in the scene table
description: The one colour row (lane/overnight-one-colour-row) groups a triplet when its rows carry a colour mark: PBR material colours via material_role, lights via SceneParamDesc.colour. Other scene RGB triplets carry neither, so they still draw as three loose sliders on the Scene tab: unlit and cel material colour_r/g/b and emission_r/g/b, fog (atmosphere) colour, render-mode clay and line colours, projected grid colour. Fix shape: add .colour(RgbChannel::R|G|B) to those rows in crates/manifold-nodes-scene/src/node_graph/scene_surface.rs; colour_rows in projection/material.rs then groups them with no UI change. ColourGroup has only Material and Light, so a non-light scene colour needs its own group or ColourGroup::Light renamed to Scene. Check rgb_ids_editable accepts each node type.

title: Percussion orchestrator stem sends also capture the system mic
description: Symptom (suspected, not run): the detect-and-split path (crates/manifold-playback/src/percussion_orchestrator.rs ~line 762) creates one send per stem with AudioSend::new, which defaults to channels [0,1] (capture on), and leaves the project device as is. In a project on System Default (device None) the stem send then sums the live system input into the stem analysis, so room noise or a mic can fire that stem clip triggers. Lane 19 (audio defaults) left this path out on purpose. Fix shape: stem sends are layer-fed only (channels empty), or the orchestrator applies the same new-source device default as + Add Source. Verify first with a printline on the send capture signature after a detect.

title: Duplicate param ids reach ParamManifest::from_params at load (debug panic, silent duplicate in release)
description: Symptom: building an instance manifest at deserialize trips the debug_assert "ParamManifest built with duplicate param ids" (crates/manifold-core/src/params.rs:283, reached from effects/instance_serde.rs ~540). Debug and test builds panic; a release build carries two params with one id, so which one a card, mapping or automation reaches is undefined. Lane 26 hit it when a registry rename (paramAliases old to new) met an instance graph that already carried the new id. The PhysicsBoxes trigger is gone (e4746e1d6), but any preset rename table plus an instance graph holding both ids reaches it from file data. Fix shape: when a renamed saved entry lands on an id already present, merge into the existing param (saved value wins) or drop it with a load-report note, so no duplicate is ever built. Test: a saved instance whose graph has both ids loads with one param.

title: Should effect and generator cards outside scenes draw labelled params as pick lists and switches
description: Lane 14 (draw by kind) applies the kind rule on the scene card and the Scene tab only: ParamRow::kind(scene) in crates/manifold-ui/src/param_surface.rs. On every other card a labelled param (value labels over whole numbers, about 17 effect presets carry one) stays a slider, because the slider row carries the D, E and A buttons and a driver stepping through modes is a performance tool there; a pick list or switch has no modulation lane. Call needed: keep sliders off-scene, or draw by kind everywhere and accept losing card-side drivers on choices (a driven row stays a slider either way). Changing it is one argument at the three build sites.
notes: Peter 2026-10-20: unsure until the modulation question is settled; waits on BUG-gptz9.

title: Verify Scene tab rebuilds when a selected light changes type (live app)
description: Lane overnight-light-env-gates (02fe7c42b) gates light rows by type in the Scene tab. With the light selected, a type change must rebuild the rows. The input is in place: ParamSpecDef::row_fact reads a mode switch by its whole value, and ChangeGraphParamCommand reports Effects (unit test row_fact_reads_a_mode_switch_whole). The headless harness cannot show it: a SetParam step dispatches Scrub Begin/Move/Commit, and the commit only sends ChangeGraphParamCommand to content (ui_bridge/scrub.rs ScrubPhase::Commit), which the ui-snap runner never executes, so AssertFresh fails after SetParam on 7_mode (incremental frame differs from a full rebuild). Re-selecting the item rebuilds correctly. To do: check in the live app (select Sun, change Type to Spot, cone rows should appear without reselecting); separately decide whether the headless SetParam should run its commit command so flows can prove scrub-driven row changes.

title: No headless check covers the editor and main-window composite gates
description: The ui-snap script runner paints every frame (crates/manifold-app/src/ui_snapshot/script.rs, offscreen_dirty comment near :474), so flow passes say nothing about whether the live app composites after an input. A missed repaint (frozen or one-frame-late editor or main window) is invisible to every flow and to AssertFresh. Lane 9 (f483c6ec6, f8299d689) deleted 59 offscreen_dirty writes and relies on its two unit tests (planned_work_redraws_and_an_idle_frame_does_not, canvas_gestures_composite_through_the_canvas_view) plus reading. Fix shape: have the runner, under a flag, run editor_frame::needs_composite and the main present gate (dirty || composited_size), and fail a flow step that changed the screen image while the gate said no composite. Compare the full-repaint image against the gated one, as the freshness check does for trees.

title: A trimmed video clip can flash its file-head frame when the start seek takes over 100 ms
description: Symptom (by reading, unverified on a real file): a trimmed clip or split tail opens on the file head, and check_preparing_clips seeks it to its in point on the ready tick and restamps recently_started_times, which hides it for RECENTLY_STARTED_TIME (100 ms). VideoRenderer::seek_clip (crates/manifold-media/src/video_renderer.rs) leaves has_frame set and the render target still holds the file-head frame, so if the seek result (DecodeResultStatus::Seeked) lands later than 100 ms, for example a far in point in a long-GOP file or a busy decode worker, the compositor shows the file-head frame until it does. Root cause: the hide-until-seek-lands gate is a fixed time window, not tied to the seek result. Fix shape: seek_clip marks the clip as waiting for its seek (clear has_frame or a seek_pending flag) and is_clip_ready or the compositor gate holds the clip back until the Seeked result arrives; then the 100 ms restamp in check_preparing_clips can go. Not changed in lane/overnight-playback-seek-fix by brief.

title: Two tests red on batch 2 tip: legacy generator load and gpu_scope audited catalog
description: Seen in the lane/overnight-switched-off worktree on top of 16c858475, unrelated to relight or shadows; not proven on the bare batch tip. (1) manifold-editing command_roundtrips legacy_generator_layer_loads_with_its_instance: a loaded legacy generator layer yields generator_type None instead of Plasma; suspect the old-format drop (commit 2b3dd62fc) removed the migration the test still expects. (2) scripts/test_gpu_scope.py test_audited_catalog_edit_selects_three_owned_harnesses: planning bundled_presets.rs selects extra harnesses (manifold-editing lib, manifold-water-gpu-flip lib, manifold-water-whitewater lib, manifold-app renderer_gpu_proofs); fails with the original gate_policy.py too, so landing_gate.py --cheap reports it red. Fix shape: bisect against 16c858475, fix or delete the stale expectation.

title: Leftovers from overnight lane 27 (load floor at 1.11): lossy project upgrade, misleading error for non-object JSON, old history snapshots, kept-rung coverage
description: From the overnight 2026-10-19 batch 2 review of 76a08b599 and 2b3dd62fc. (1) project_tool project upgrade (crates/manifold-app/src/bin/project_tool/timeline_verbs.rs:178-203) prints load-report repairs and drops but saves anyway; a show using a non-embedded user-library preset loses that preset values in the output because project_tool links only the bundled set. Fix: refuse when the load report is non-empty or any instance type is unregistered; its doc should say it now converts 1.11+ files only. (2) A pre-1.11 show opened in the legacy build and saved in place keeps its old history/ blobs verbatim; restoring one on main fails with TooOld, and the advice to save once does not convert history. Tell Peter old snapshots become view-only through the legacy build, or convert history blobs on save in the legacy branch. (3) loader.rs:155-162: JSON that parses but is not an object, or has a non-string projectVersion, reports too old (1.0.0) instead of a shape error. (4) No real 1.11-1.20 file exercises the kept migration rungs end to end any more; the Liveschool and legacy_param_id_resolution tests read already-converted files. (5) graph_schema.rs:27 still names the deleted migrate::fold_user_param_bindings.

title: MIDI Clock position sync is dead in the app: the snapshot guard always returns
description: Symptom (reasoned from code, not observed live): under MIDI Clock, a Song Position Pointer or cursor move in the DAW while MANIFOLD is stopped never moves the MANIFOLD playhead, and the clock hard-seek path never fires while playing. Root cause: content_thread passes SyncTargetSnapshot to MidiClockSyncController::update; SyncTargetSnapshot::current_project() returns None, so sync_position_to_playback returns on its first line every frame. Commit 86906b315 kept this on purpose to stop a second position setter fighting derive_external_beat, so the disable is load-bearing by accident, and CORE_ENGINE_MAP section 7 (External sync) still describes nudge/hard-seek as live. While playing, the follower (external_follow.rs, SEEK_ERROR 50 ms) already relocates on large errors, so only the stopped case is actually lost. Fix shape: decide which owner moves the playhead on a clock jump; then either delete the playing branch of sync_position_to_playback and run the stopped branch through an explicit gate, or delete the whole method; drop the current_project guard either way and fix the map text. BUG-mmct0.3 (constant-BPM compare) made the snapshot conversion tempo-map correct, so re-enabling no longer hard-seeks every frame under a tempo map.

title: Leftovers from overnight lane 23: dead generator uniform arena paid every frame, dead display_norm_override param, error log can repeat after clock resets
description: From the overnight 2026-10-19 batch 2 review. (1) After 0681d8308 nothing calls GpuEncoder::uniform_arena_mut (manifold-node-engine/src/gpu/gpu_encoder.rs:121) or pushes to any arena, yet GeneratorRenderer still allocates a 64 KB shared buffer and resets, points and flushes it every frame (manifold-compositor/src/generator_renderer.rs:741-742, 1051-1053, 1680-1734). Delete the UniformArena type, the GpuEncoder.uniform_arena field, the pointer copy in render_scene/scene_viewport.rs:81 and the flush in generator_renderer_warmup_tests.rs:301. (2) After e8bc8172f every caller passes None for push_slider_value display_norm_override (param_slider_shared/row_host.rs:1174-1185); delete the parameter and its snapback doc. (3) engine.rs:1262-1266 and :2126-2130 log once per latch, but reset_trigger_delivery (engine.rs:1903, on an external clock stepping back) clears the latch, so a jittery clock with a sustained overflow can log several errors a second; latch the log on the error kind across resets. Also midi_input stop() does not clear backlog_warned.

title: Export requested while the GPU is behind is silently dropped
description: Symptom: pressing Export while the content thread waits on a busy GPU surface can do nothing. Root cause: wait_for_surface_draining_commands (crates/manifold-app/src/content_thread.rs) sends every non-seek command to handle_command_with_preparation, which only intercepts LoadProject; StartExport falls through to handle_command, whose StartExport arm is a no-op (content_commands.rs, comment says handled in run() loop). Found by lane 22 (overnight 2026-10-19) while fixing census bug 2. Fix shape: route StartExport in handle_command_with_preparation through the same arm drain_commands uses (clear automation previews, stop recording, flush pending seek, run_export), ideally one shared helper for both loops.

title: Hooks-only changes pushed direct to main skip the hook tests
description: The landing gate now runs every .claude/hooks/test_*.py when .claude/hooks/ changes (scripts/codex_checks.py:80-83), but CLAUDE.md lets .beads/+docs/+.claude/hooks/ changes go direct to main without the gate (preToolUseBash.py _BEADS_DOCS_PREFIXES), so a broken hook can reach main untested. Found by the overnight 2026-10-19 lane 10 review. Fix shape: drop .claude/hooks/ from the direct-push prefixes, or have land_pass_guard require the hook tests for a hooks diff. Interim: the overnight lead lands hook changes through land_branch.py.

title: Matter node stiffness fit is stubbed, so the substep cap is silent
description: Symptom: high Stiffness at fine resolution runs with too few substeps and no warning; the limited_by_substeps output is always 0. Root cause: crates/manifold-water-gpu-mpm/src/primitives/matter_domain.rs:891-892 sets fitted = stiffness. Fix shape: Peter's call: wire the fit as GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md:228 promises (changes stiff scenes' look) or delete the dead path. Source: docs/evidence/simplification_census_2026-10/REPORT.md (bug 8, rescreen-014). Found by the BUG-yn979 (Simplification pass) census; read from code, not reproduced.

title: Unreadable audio becomes a 0-beat clip and Replace Audio saves duration 0
description: Root cause: crates/manifold-app/src/project_io.rs:1426-1438 falls back to zero duration. Fix shape: refuse the import with an error. Source: docs/evidence/simplification_census_2026-10/REPORT.md (bug 24, fallbacks-034). Found by the BUG-yn979 (Simplification pass) census; read from code, not reproduced.

title: 33 undo bodies skip silently when their graph is missing
description: Symptom: history and project disagree after undo. Root cause: do_undo bodies in crates/manifold-editing/src/commands/ return early with no error. Fix shape: reject and drop the step. Source: docs/evidence/simplification_census_2026-10/REPORT.md (bug 21, fallbacks-025). Found by the BUG-yn979 (Simplification pass) census; read from code, not reproduced.

title: Edits on a missing target still record an undo step and clear redo
description: Symptom: about a hundred commands do nothing on a stale target, the next Cmd+Z undoes nothing and redo is gone; Add Graph Node does the same (node_edit.rs:135-139). Root cause: crates/manifold-editing/src/command.rs:49-51 counts a no-op as applied. Fix shape: reject, as fire_param.rs does. Source: docs/evidence/simplification_census_2026-10/REPORT.md (bugs 20 and 22, fallbacks-024 and 027). Found by the BUG-yn979 (Simplification pass) census; read from code, not reproduced.

title: Generator card shows a fader for a binding whose node is gone
description: Symptom: a fader that moves nothing; 11 in 3 projects. Root cause: crates/manifold-node-engine/src/runtime/build.rs:455-470 skips silently where the effect path records a chain error. Fix shape: same error path as effects. Source: docs/evidence/simplification_census_2026-10/REPORT.md (bug 13, fallbacks-029). Found by the BUG-yn979 (Simplification pass) census; read from code, not reproduced.

title: Corrupt enum values load silently as defaults
description: Symptom: a damaged file opens with a layer turned into Video or an effect into Transform, and the next save keeps it. Root cause: crates/manifold-core/src/types.rs:190-215. Fix shape: fail the load with a clear error, as the version guard already does for newer files. Source: docs/evidence/simplification_census_2026-10/REPORT.md (bug 12, fallbacks-028). Found by the BUG-yn979 (Simplification pass) census; read from code, not reproduced.

title: Kernels hard-code param ranges, so remapping a slider past them does nothing
description: Symptom: many sliders stop having any effect past a point because the shader or kernel clamps the param to its own hard-coded range, so widening the range with remap is silently ignored. Rule: a kernel never clamps a param unless the math requires it (divide by zero, sqrt of negative, NaN guards); the manifest range is a UI default, not a kernel limit. Root cause: clamps copied into kernels alongside manifest ranges. Fix shape: audit every shader and kernel for clamp/min/max on uniform params, remove the ones that are not mathematically required, keep and comment the ones that are, and add a check (test or lint over the shaders) that flags new param clamps. Pairs with the slider Remap feature.

title: Right-click any slider -> Remap, opens the graph editor remap panel in place
description: Any slider on any panel (Scene panel, inspector, cards, every manifest-backed param surface) gets a right-click Remap item that opens the same remap panel the graph editor uses, right there. Today a quick range change means opening the graph editor, which is clunky mid-session, and Scene panel ranges cannot be set at all. Shape: one context-menu entry on the shared param-surface slider (docs/WIDGET_TREE_DESIGN.md section 5b, crates/manifold-ui/src/param_surface.rs), reusing the existing remap panel and its mutation path through EditingService, not a second remap UI. Related: BUG-2b0 (card-param-range-remap-doesnt-stick).

title: Scene tab water Lattice readout ignores the layer Resolution card and shows the node's stale saved value
description: Symptom: water layer Resolution card set to 128, but the Scene tab readout says Lattice 64 x 64 x 64, 6.2 cm cells (Peter, Hung Up Audio Reels project, 2026-10-17). The sim itself uses the card value. Root cause: the inspector builds SceneVm from the raw layer graph (crates/manifold-app/src/ui_bridge/projection/inspector.rs:161-167), and trace_fluid_domain reads the domain node own resolution param (crates/manifold-nodes-scene/src/node_graph/scene_vm.rs:1406-1408). It never applies card bindings. The viewport does, via fluid_domain_edit::authored_def plus apply_runtime_domains (fluid_domain_edit.rs:34-126). Also scene_vm falls back to 24 when the param is missing, while the runtime falls back to 64 (gpu_flip_domain.rs:164). Fix shape: the inspector uses the same authored def or runtime accepted layout as the viewport, so there is one source for the readout.
notes: Fix landed in overnight batch 5 (d07bef8af, Scene tab SceneVm built from the authored graph). No cure-test and no headless render (the scene-setup fixture does not expose Resolution). Close after Peter's live check; silent-fallback follow-up BUG-sfquf.

title: Water Smoothing Value allows 0-10 but any value above 1 tears the surface into shards
description: Symptom: Water Look > Smoothing Value above 1 turns the liquid surface into sharp glittering shards (Peter export Water Test v2, value 3, 2026-10-17). Root cause: smooth_surface_mesh (crates/manifold-water-surface/src/primitives/smooth_surface_mesh.rs:31) is a Jacobi umbrella step, v += s*(neighbour mean - v); s>1 overshoots past the mean and s=2 mirrors each point, so it diverges instead of smoothing. The param range 0-10 and the preset metadata range (mesh_relaxation in WaterDamBreakGpuFlip.json and every water preset) both invite it. Fix shape: clamp range to 0-1 in the node param and every preset metadata entry; check relax_surface_mesh Strength (already 0-1). Note: FLIP Fluids accepts any value but only 0-1 is meaningful.
notes: Superseded for the live path when direct level-set rendering (docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md D2) lands; stays open as the export-path item until then.

title: GPU proofs gate runs all of manifold-nodes GPU tests for a one-shader change
description: Symptom: landing a whitewater_step.wgsl change ran the full manifold-nodes GPU proof package for over 15 minutes against a 6 minute budget. The gate log says: whole packages (filters do not limit these): manifold-nodes. The mapped filters (catalog_tests::whitewater_scene, whitewater_emitters and so on) were already right, but the whole-package rule overrides them. Root cause: gpu_proofs_gate.py path-to-test mapping escalates to a whole package for some paths. Fix shape: find why manifold-nodes is whole-package for this path and make it filter-scoped, so a shader change runs only the tests that load that shader.

title: UI flow scene-forces-controls red on main
description: Symptom: flow scene-forces-controls fails at step 35 on main 1f1950ccf: expected a match for query text "✓ Physics Solids / Uniform Force / Strength" type Button, found none. Reproduced from the main checkout, so it predates lane/stale-intent-ids. Root cause unknown; suspects: force card label or menu text changed without updating the flow, or the Physics Solids force menu entry moved. Fix shape: find the commit that changed the label (git log -S on the label text), then fix the flow or the UI, whichever is wrong.
notes: Root cause (lane 1, 2026-10-19): INV-16 violation. sync_project_data (crates/manifold-app/src/ui_bridge/projection/timeline.rs:122) reads clip trigger assignments: it rebuilds TriggerRoutingCatalog (:133), refreshes the open trigger-target picker ticks (:134) and sets each trigger lane header trigger_targets_label (:187). Clip trigger assignments live in the Effects part (UI_INVALIDATION_DESIGN.md line 186), but PROJECT_SYNC_PARTS (crates/manifold-app/src/frame_plan.rs:482) has no Effects, matching design table line 425, and SetParamClipTriggerSourceCommand touches Effects only (crates/manifold-editing/src/commands/trigger_source.rs:186). So an assign or unassign never reruns the projection; the picker tick and the header label stay stale. Evidence (solo runs with prints): scene-forces-controls step 34 dispatched AssignClipTriggerSource(... strength ... Lane), the command applied, no refresh followed, step 35 found no tick. Same root reddens trigger-lane-assignment (step 16, re-assign after unassign: stale header button caught the click). Independent of the headless settle timing (03e1afca4): red with the extra frame disabled. Fix shapes: (1) add Effects to PROJECT_SYNC_PARTS, one line, but every Effects write (card collapse flags included) reruns the whole timeline sync and work-flow counts rise; (2) a TriggerRouting projection keyed on Layers|Effects that rebuilds the catalog, refreshes an open picker (overlay rebuild as P5a does for project sync) and sets trigger-lane header labels in place, moving those three out of sync_project_data, plus a section 4 table row and input-matrix coverage, about 60 to 100 lines. The shape is a design call (UI_INVALIDATION section 4 table) for the next design pass. Both flows are expected_fail against this bead.

title: Gradient Map (node.color_ramp) divides by alpha like the broken Infrared fix
description: Symptom (suspected, not checked): Gradient Map on luma-keyed sources like Particle Text (a = luma, rgb == a) would read every lit pixel as white and land on the top of the ramp. Root cause suspect: node.color_ramp reads luma from rgb/a, the same shape removed from lut1d.wgsl on lane/infrared-additive. Fix shape: same as Infrared, luma from src.rgb, coverage ramp clamp(max(a, max rgb)*255) so only empty pixels lose the ramp colour.

title: Main-window present drops its preview read lease on early returns, wedging one bridge slot until restart
description: Found reading frame/present.rs while reasoning about BUG-o13fa (content thread waits out the timeout). The preview lease is taken at ~present.rs:207 (acquire_read), but the early returns before the Present encoder (window missing, surface None, next_drawable None with the No drawable available warning, blit pipeline or sampler None) drop it without retire_read. BridgeReadLease has no Drop, so reads_in_flight on that slot stays above zero for the session: every content frame that wants that slot waits the full 5 s. Not the cause of BUG-o13fa (its dumps show reads_in_flight=0 and no drawable warning), unverified by a run. Fix shape: make the lease retire on every path (a guard that retires on drop through a marker buffer, or route every early return through retire_leases_via_marker as the resize path already does); check perform_mode/render.rs and editor_bridge.rs for the same shape.

title: Content thread stalls one frame per 5s with GPU done and bridges free (Oscilloscope project, before export)
description: Symptom: Murmur Audio Project V3.manifold (Oscilloscope generator, live capture input), main 669d40d8d, 2026-10-16 19:18 Sydney. Content thread made one frame every 5 s: every frame hit the surface-wait deadline in wait_for_surface_draining_commands (content_thread.rs). At each timeout the GPU event was already past the pending value (signal=82337 signaled=82339) and all three bridges reported the slot reusable (front off slot, reads_in_flight=0), so the wait was over at the deadline. AudioMod capture gaps of ~4.7 s every 5 s follow from the stall. Export started during it; Peter reports it later exported fine on its own. Root cause unknown. Suspects: a readiness input that changes without sending SurfaceReady (preview front moving off the write slot; is_reusable_ephemeral quiet check uses frame_count, which does not advance during the wait); node.audio_waveform on live capture. Fix shape: every input to is_surface_ready sends a wake, proven by a CPU test; reproduce first with printlns.
notes: Recurred 2026-10-16 20:45 Sydney on 04 - Triptogram breakdown.manifold: three project saves 7-57 s before the first timeout, a DigitalDrift FUSED kernel line before that. Then export opened, sat at 0%, and Cancel only changed the button to Cancelling export. Restart cleared it. Next time: sample the stuck process before restarting.

title: Automation lanes: pro-grade editing UX
description: Bring automation lane editing up to Ableton-grade feel. Audited 2026-10-15 against Live 12. Children cover the drag bugs, the lane header redesign, readouts, quick-edit muscle memory, recording, clip-follow and reach. Already good: Shift fine / Cmd no-snap / Alt bend, typed values, shapes, clipboard, override indicator, one undo per gesture.

title: HDR export range and matrix unconfirmed: Apple encoder does the RGB to video conversion
description: Symptom: unknown on real output; same shape as the SDR bug fixed by lane/sdr-range (SDR data was full range under a TV-range label). The HDR path hands RGBA half-float to HEVC and lets AVAssetWriter/VideoToolbox convert RGB to YCbCr, so range and matrix are unverified. Check: ffprobe + signalstats on a real HDR export (10-bit limited luma should sit in 64..940). Fix shape if wrong: convert to 10-bit limited BT.2020 YCbCr in our shader and hand the writer x420-style biplanar buffers, mirroring the SDR fix.

title: Headless export of the Murmur project panics in the node engine
description: Symptom: a headless export of the Murmur project (journey_proof headless_content_thread + warm_project + run_export, beats 124-136, 1080x1920 SDR) panicked in the node engine before any frames were encoded. Seen 2026-10-15 by the SDR export lane, which was stopped before it found the location. Root cause: unknown; the panic message was not captured. Suspects: a debug-only assertion in graph eval on a project-load path the app never takes, or state that warm_project leaves out. Fix shape: re-run the same headless export, capture the panic location, then fix the cause or bring the headless path in line with the app. Also note there is no headless project-export command; one would make export checks a single command.

title: Stepped envelopes on session-detached layers after stop/seek
description: From BUG-0xwux review (lane/step-envelope-origin e89d8860a). session_override survives stop and seek, so stopping, seeking back before the launch beat and playing steps the envelope on arrangement clips that are muted from playing; SessionStarts::through cuts only at the launch beat (manifold-playback/src/clip_controls.rs:253). Back to Arrangement drops the cutoff, so the value jumps by every start skipped while detached. Deterministic. Peter: should detachment clear on stop/seek, and should Back to Arrangement jump or not?

title: Find what holds 22 GB of live GPU allocation on Liveschool at 1080p headless
description: Liveschool V6 LEDS, perf-soak --work-idle --start 128 at 1080p: the device reports 22076 MB allocated of a 28753 MB recommended working set, with the free texture pool at 0 MB, so this is live allocation, not a measurement or pool artifact. Memory admission (75% ceiling, 21564 MB) then refuses any new buffer (a chain needing 1 MB was refused). Suspects: simulation or scene buffers sized independent of output resolution, chains kept alive past CHAIN_GRACE_FRAMES, generator runtimes for layers not playing at beat 128. Oracle: per-owner allocation census (residency manager or a pool report) at beat 128. Found while fixing BUG-kdxkx (failed chain rebuilds every frame).

title: Test builds overwrite target/debug/manifold with the change audit on
description: Symptom: cargo test -p manifold-app rebuilds target/debug/manifold with feature change-audit (via manifold-playback testkit dev-dep), so a later launch of that binary (launch_live_ui.py) fingerprints the project on every command and can panic on an audit assert. Release unaffected. Root cause: dev-dep feature unification into the bin target under cargo test. Fix shape: keep change-audit off the bin (cfg(test) only, or a separate test target dir for the audit), or have launch_live_ui.py build explicitly. Also: the guard test command_runs_only_through_the_audit (command.rs 190-215) only matches one-line signatures; and no test pins that execute returns WHOLE_INSTANCES and the service stamps it.
