title: Scoped nextest in two lanes deadlocks on GPU tests
description: Symptom: two lanes ran cargo nextest -p manifold-app (and -p manifold-ui etc.) at once; GPU-backed tests (cache_path_full_render, editor_window_harness, overlay_fidelity_proof, renderer_contracts ui_color_swatches, also led_edge_identity and trigger_lane_force_tests) sat at 0% CPU for ~30 min until killed. Root cause: unknown; suspect the per-process GPU device lock taken by nextest's process-per-test across both slots, ordering inversion between lanes. Fix shape: the default nextest profile excludes GPU proofs (they run only through scripts/gpu_proofs_gate.py under cargo test), or the device lock gets a timeout that fails loudly instead of waiting forever.

title: Inspector and dock re-anchor in place on a rect change
description: UI_INVALIDATION after P5b: an inspector width drag (work-inspector-resize) still rebuilds 180 regions per second: the inspector, the audio dock and the layer headers (the headers rebuild on a new left edge or width because row controls sit at panel-local x). Layer headers and viewport already lay out in place on a top or height move (ViewportMoves.relayout, LayerHeaderPanel::try_relayout). Fix shape: give the inspector and dock a relayout like the viewport's (their scroll containers and hit rects take the new rect), and let LayerHeaderPanel::try_relayout move controls horizontally when the left edge moves at the same width. The three chrome bars also lay out together whenever any chrome push runs; keying each bar on its own shown values would cut playback chrome layouts from 3 to 1 per shown-digit change.
notes: lane/ui-perf-leftovers (8dd008400): inspector width drag 180 region rebuilds to 60. The drag was rebuilding inspector, header bar and split handle (not dock/headers as first written); header and split now resize in place, the dock slides. Left: the inspector rebuilds because every card kind sizes to the width at build time; in place needs a width relayout per card kind. Layer header sideways move not needed (left edge never moves).

title: frame_exact_app opens a GPU device outside nextest's gpu test group
description: Symptom: manifold-app's frame_exact_app::same_values_per_index_through_content_thread (crates/manifold-app/src/frame_exact_app.rs, cfg(test, macos), not feature-gated) opens the test GPU device but is not in the [test-groups] gpu filter in .config/nextest.toml, so a default nextest run of manifold-app runs it concurrently with other tests and outside the GPU lock (the cross-process lock only exists under gpu-proofs). Root cause: the filter list was not updated when the test landed with frame-exact P1/P2. Fix shape: add (binary_id(manifold-app::bin/manifold) & test(/^frame_exact_app::/)) to both profile overrides (default and ci), or gate the module behind gpu-proofs so it runs only through gpu_proofs_gate.py as the design doc says.

title: Scene card: rows with a macro mapping are not kept on the card (D6)
description: Symptom: a Setup or Hidden scene control that only has a macro-bank mapping drops off the scene card, so the performer loses sight of a mapped control. SCENE_SURFACES_DESIGN.md D6 (attached rows are always shown) lists macro mapping with driver, envelope, audio, Ableton and automation. Root cause: ParamRow carries no macro-mapping fact; scene_card.rs has_attachment can only read driver/envelope/automation/audio/Ableton, and gen_params_to_surface has no project/macro-bank access. Fix shape: add a macro-mapped flag to RowMapping filled in cards.rs from the project macro bank (MacroBank in manifold-core macro_bank.rs), read it in scene_card::has_attachment, and extend scene_card::tests::attached_rows_stay_on_card with a macro case. Found in the BUG-pmbd3 P4 lane (feat/scene-surfaces-p4).

title: Shrink the sync rig log after P3 constants are tuned
description: The C0 sync rig log (5244cd11e, BUG-gqhep live-transport-nondeterministic-frame-clock) is about 1900 lines incl. tests and a 416-line report script, built for one tuning pass. Once the P3 constants are set from Peters rig log, cut it to one small always-on sync health line (authority, phase error, corrections, dropped count) and delete the rest: rotation, EDID/ioreg probing, raw MIDI byte logging, sync_rig_report.py and its dev.py verb.

title: sync_build and sync_clip_positions disagree on clip alpha (255 vs 219)
description: Symptom: the headless fixture build (ui_snapshot sync_build -> sync_project_data) leaves ViewportClip base_color alpha 255, while sync_clip_positions (clip_base_color(layer, clip, 0.86)) gives alpha 219 for the same clip. Found by P4a AssertFresh (UI_INVALIDATION_DESIGN.md) on every timeline work flow before the runner ran a structural first frame. In the live app every structural frame runs sync_project_data then sync_clip_positions, so the 219 value always wins and nothing visible differs today; any frame that runs sync_project_data without the clip resync would show different clip alpha. Where: crates/manifold-app/src/ui_bridge/projection/timeline.rs sync_project_data clip projection vs sync_clip_positions (:498). Root cause: two projections build ViewportClip colors independently. Fix shape: one clip projection function both call, so the color is derived once.

title: Detect stalled Claude lanes in fleet_health
description: scripts/fleet_health.py only sees Astra (Codex) jobs, orphaned slot edits, disk, GPU lock and the nightly. Claude Agent-tool lanes are invisible to it: a lane that goes idle without reporting, or stops writing its slot, raises nothing until its slot edits go stale for 30 minutes. Fix shape: read the live Claude subagent transcripts (session jsonl under ~/.claude/projects, or slot leases plus last-write times) and flag a running lane with no tool call or slot write for N minutes, and a completed lane whose report was never reviewed. Docs (AGENT_ROUTING.md lane health bullet, memory orchestration rules) now say fleet_health does not see Claude lanes; update them when this lands.

title: Export warm-up re-seek drops the clip-edge step of a clip already active at export start
description: Symptom: with export warm-up, a clip already active at the export start loses its clip-edge step, so step-envelope params differ from live at the first exported frames. Root cause: production export seeks, plays, warms up, then re-seeks to the start; the second seek resets clip-control starts and trigger delivery while the clip is already active. Pre-existing (base 09a44cb4c). Fix shape: warm up without resetting trigger delivery, or replay the start edge after the re-seek. Found during BUG-gqhep (live-transport-nondeterministic-frame-clock) P2.

title: Step-envelope param follows its step one frame late
description: Symptom: a param driven by a clip-edge step envelope changes one frame after the step (step at index 132, level at 133), in live play and export alike; a step-on-cut lands one frame after the cut. Pre-existing (base 09a44cb4c). Root cause unknown; suspect the envelope step is evaluated after the param read in the tick order. Fix shape: evaluate the step before params are sampled for the frame. Found reviewing BUG-gqhep (live-transport-nondeterministic-frame-clock) P2.

title: frame-time aborts on Liveschool V6 fixtures: device offers 0 MB GPU buffers
description: Symptom: manifold frame-time (perf-soak release) on V6 LEDS and V6 EFFECT_GEN_UNIFIED aborts at layer-chain warm-up with exit 70: scene needs N MB of GPU buffers; the device offers 0 MB, then Metal Insufficient Memory. Same on main b54cedc5c and feat/frame-exact-clock, GPU idle, 52 percent memory free, 36 GB machine. Crash: ~/Library/Logs/com.latentspace.manifold/crash-1791931626.log. Root cause unknown; suspect the GPU buffer budget reads 0 in headless frame-time (recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize or budget init). Blocks the L2 transport-log check of BUG-gqhep (live-transport-nondeterministic-frame-clock).

title: Clock jitter forces full UI rebuilds through sync_driver_bpm
description: Symptom: under Link or MIDI clock jitter the UI does full structural syncs and rebuilds. Root cause: each snapshot with a new bpm calls sync_driver_bpm, which scans every driver (ui_root/mod.rs:411); any frame-aligned period flip sets needs_structural_sync and needs_rebuild (app_render.rs:347-353). Fix shape: the driver period readout updates in place; the scan keys on the Effects stamp and the quantized period (UI_INVALIDATION_DESIGN.md D20).

title: Ableton trim drag rebuilds every listener every content frame
description: rebuild_listeners walks every mapping in the project and allocates two hash maps (ableton_bridge.rs:2061-2063); during a trim drag it runs once per content frame (decided in UI_INVALIDATION_DESIGN.md item 11). Fix shape: a scoped update rewrites the one WriteTarget range in place per tick; the full rebuild runs once on commit (UI_INVALIDATION_DESIGN.md D20).

title: push_state and the modulation snapshot copy run every frame with nothing to key them on
description: push_state (ui_bridge/state_sync.rs:49, about 700 lines, 93 setters) runs every UI frame unconditionally; the content thread captures and clones the modulation snapshot buffer every tick (content_thread.rs:1237-1238). No FrameInputs field and no WorkKind covers either, so an idle frame cannot be zero work. Fix shape: ContentState carries a live-values sequence that moves only when a captured value changed; the copy is skipped and push_state runs only when that sequence or the Values stamp moved (UI_INVALIDATION_DESIGN.md D15).

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Review: push_state also drives the insert cursor, selection band, layer highlight, toasts, modifier selection and chrome, so keying it on values alone freezes them while paused. Split into value push, selection push (selection_visual + cursor), O(1) event drain, chrome push (Settings, Mappings, MappingRanges, Layers, ChromeInputs). UI_INVALIDATION_DESIGN D15, P4b/P4c.

title: ui-snapshot test build broken on main, and no gate compiles it
description: Symptom: cargo test -p manifold-app --features ui-snapshot fails to compile on origin/main: crates/manifold-app/src/ui_snapshot/mod.rs:1865 sets automation_lanes: &[], a field that no longer exists (compiler suggests automation_latched). Root cause: the landing gate and nightly never build manifold-app tests with the ui-snapshot feature, so the ui_snapshot unit tests rot unseen. Found overnight 2026-10-13 by the lane moving material-inspector flows to CPU tests (lane/material-flow-tests). Fix shape: fix the field, then add ui-snapshot to the manifold-app test build in the gate (or move the CPU-only ui_snapshot tests out from behind the feature) so they run on every landing that touches them.

title: Show the firmware GPU reset warning in the app export UI
description: The firmware_reports reader (manifold-gpu, branch fix/rt-blas-rebuild-cadence) logs a warning at export start when macOS has reset the GPU since boot, and fatal GPU reports name the reset reason. The in-app export flow shows neither: surface the warning in the export dialog/status so Peter sees "reboot before a long export" without reading logs. UI crate depends on foundation only, so it goes through ContentState as a value.

title: Stale Link tempo after peers vanish writes beat-0 tempo point
description: Symptom: when Link peers disappear, the last live tempo persists and can be written into the beat-0 tempo point, making the beat jump. Root cause: content_thread.rs ~2083-2111 keeps the stale live tempo. Fix shape: drop the live tempo override when Link has no peers; never write it into the tempo map implicitly. Found during BUG-gqhep (live-transport-nondeterministic-frame-clock) impact map.

title: render_scene memoryless MSAA overflows parameter buffer on dense geometry
description: Symptom: 2026-10-13 03:27 UTC session-1791858862792-27413.log, node.render_scene faulted with kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemoryForParameterBuffer (Too much geometry to support memoryless render pass attachments). Root cause: 4x MSAA attachments are memoryless and cannot spill when tiler parameter buffer overflows. Fix shape: non-memoryless attachments when geometry is dense, or always.

title: Teach the inline-python and cd rules up front
description: Audit 2026-10-13: inline python denied ~20 times a day, 239 times in 52 sessions over 14 days, mostly heredoc edits or JSON reads; CLAUDE.md never states the rule. Persistent cd denied ~60 times a week, mostly a learned prefix (cd /dev/null 2>/dev/null; or cd /tmp;) 89 hits. Deny messages are fine; cost is ~300 wasted turns a week. Fix shape: one hard-rule line in CLAUDE.md and the lane brief template: throwaway python goes in a scratchpad script run by path, jq for JSON, Edit for files. Needs Peter yes for the CLAUDE.md line.

title: A red rerun reruns the whole test group, not the failed tests
description: Symptom 2026-10-13: one red test in the ~500-test manifold-nodes group meant the whole group ran again after the fix. Pass reuse is per leg (package filterset), and a regenerated docs/node_catalog sits in every nodes key, so nothing is reused. Fix shape: reuse at test-binary or test level: record per-test pass with the inputs of its binary, and on a rerun run the previously failed tests first (fail fast), then only binaries whose inputs changed. Measure first how often a rerun follows a single-test red (BUG-woi67 red classes).

title: automation-insert-shape
description: Right-click a lane → Insert Shape: sine, triangle, saw up, saw down, square, ramp. Fills the automation time selection, else the bar under the mouse. One cycle = current grid step (grid follows zoom, so zoom sets speed). Empty range: shape spans lane min..max. Range with existing automation: ADD, the shape rides on the existing curve (existing value + bipolar shape, clamped to the param range) — Peter 2026-10-13: add, clear first for a clean template. Use curved segment shapes so a sine is a few breakpoints, not hundreds. One undo entry via EditingService. Reuse: automation_time_selection, grid snap, segment shapes, paste path. Est ~1 day, unverified.

title: automation-effect-on-off-lane
description: Automate an effect on/off seamlessly. Shape (agreed with Peter 2026-10-13): the card ON button keeps its current real on/off (rebuild, no GPU cost). Only an effect that has an on/off automation lane stays in the chain wrapped like a one-effect group: the existing group wet/dry Mix (manifold-node-engine/src/runtime/groups.rs, never rebuilds per build.rs topology-hash doc) with the lane driving wet 0/1, Hold shape. ON button mirrors the lane (dim at 0, lit at 1); pressing it on an automated effect overrides like any touched param until Back to Arrangement. Lane opens via right-click Show Automation on the ON button. Cost: a lane-automated effect renders while hidden. Est ~1 day, unverified.

title: switch_texture with a wired selector prunes from last frame's value, so cuts land one frame late
description: Symptom: Math View mode changes (Scene/Math/Overlay) show one frame late; first frame runs every branch. Root cause: live-step pruning (execution.rs selected_input_branch ~1339-1363) reads a wired selector's previous output, not this frame's. Affects every node.switch_texture/mux with a wired selector, e.g. Stylized Feedback Mode. Fix shape: resolve selectors fed by pure param chains (node.value -> node.math) at frame start before computing live steps, or run the selector's upstream before pruning.

title: Math View Ghosts toggle does not hide the ghost outline
description: Symptom: Ghosts Off or Ghosts Brightness 0 still shows the undeformed outline. Root cause: standalone views set incoming = reference (compiler.rs capture), so the Fragments-gated reference block and the Ghosts block in render_mesh_diagram.wgsl draw the same triangles. Fix shape: drop or Ghosts-gate the reference block for standalone views.

title: Math View output clipped to a hard rectangle in the canvas
description: Symptom: in Peter screenshot (2026-10-13, flower scan, Math View Overlay + Depth occlusion, layer with Mask Yaw/Pitch controls) the grid stops at hard left, right and top edges with lines at full brightness, about x 57-672 and y 255+ of a 1180-wide preview. The grid shader cannot make these: it is a fullscreen triangle with soft fades. Root cause unknown. Suspects: the layer effect mask clipping the Math View output; the layer transform or generator render size; Math View sets its output fully opaque (node.set_alpha 1.0 in compiler.rs compose path) so any clip is invisible except where grid lines end. Oracle: toggle the mask in that project, or headless-render it. Fix shape depends on the cause.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: New suspect from the 2026-10-13 review: runtime/math_view.rs Overlay copies target into background at target size, then Mix samples by normalized UV; presentation is sized from the runtime width/height and nothing checks they match. A smaller target would show the scene in a sub-rectangle with a hard edge. Unproven.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: 98ea0b5ce rewrote Overlay compositing in-graph (node.switch_texture + node.over); the target/presentation size-mismatch suspect no longer exists. Needs Peter to confirm the rectangle is gone.

title: Split manifold-app into a library plus a thin main so builds can be cached
description: manifold-app (about 123k lines) has only [[bin]] targets and no lib.rs. sccache cannot cache binary crates and the gate turns incremental off, so the biggest crate fully recompiles for each build variant (39-204s each, per the 2026-10-13 review). Fix shape: move the code into a lib target; the binaries become thin mains. Measure gate build time before and after.

title: Preset overlay install rescans and re-parses every bundled preset
description: Suspect for slow 3D/water headless tests and flows (2026-10-13, from code, unmeasured). set_project_presets and clear_project_presets (crates/manifold-node-engine/src/load/preset_loader.rs) call apply_reload, which rescans the preset folders on disk, rebuilds all three catalogs and re-parses every preset metadata, even when only a one-entry project overlay changed. Every glTF/project scene installs an overlay (ui_snapshot fixtures.rs installs_preset_overlay: gltfscene, mushroomscene, gltfanimscene, heldoutmerge, project:), so each such flow pays a full catalog rebuild, and tests that install and clear several times pay it each time. Evidence it matters: project_local_preset_reload (a tiny CPU test) runs about 60s in 10 landings; gltfscene flows run 8-12s even for one click. Also check water_family_recognizers_agree (37s), trigger_lane_force_isolation (40s), paused_mutation_publishes_snapshot (45s) for the same cause. Measure first: time one apply_reload in a debug test build. Fix shape: keep the scanned stock and user catalog cached and merge only the overlay on install; rescan disk only from the file watcher.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Review 2026-10-13 weakened this: project_local_preset_reload normally takes 11-14s (25 logged runs); the 62.8s was one run under load. The 60.000s and 30.000s rows are nextest SLOW markers that landing_metrics.py counts as extra entries. One catalog reload is about 1.5s (112 files, 2.9 MB) and the test does 7. Still worth fixing for glTF flow fixtures, lower priority.

title: Label review: fetch online-only inputs so more songs play masters and stereo
description: The label review build (tools/audio_analysis/lab/review_project.py build) lists online-only files it would read but never fetches them. At the 2026-10-13 build: late_night (ALEX REMASTER V2), go_with_you and desire keep the labelled file because the latest master is online-only; 12 songs play mono because their bounce or stems are online-only (cold_remix, worship, gerrit, burn_stems, eat_sleep, renew, default_haze, staged, control, desire, skyline, plus drmendez with no lab_mix row). Peter decides which to bring down with catalog.py download PATH --why, then rebuild; the build prints the exact list.

title: Slot cache reclaim frees almost nothing; landed slots keep 15-38 GB targets
description: Symptom: 2026-10-13 the disk fell to 13 GB raw free; landing-gate reclaim and agent-worktree.py reclaim removed 0 GB while landed/idle slots held 38+30+16+23 GB of Cargo targets. Manual cargo clean of slots 0,1,2,4,7 freed 107 GB. Root cause: reclaim only deletes stale incremental sessions (KEEP deps/examples: 'direct launches have no exclusion lock'), and refuses any slot whose branch is unlanded even though target/ is pure cache. A released landed slot keeps its whole target. Fix shape: on release of a landed slot, clean its target entirely; let reclaim clean whole targets of lease-free, process-free slots regardless of branch state (the branch is protected, the cache is not); keep the open-file/process check as the only guard.
notes: Also: reclaim keeps unlanded or dirty slots whole, so mid-programme it frees nothing. Waiting slots carry 14-21 GB of target/debug/incremental that gates never read; reclaim should drop it for process-free slots when below the goal.

title: tick_midi_input unsafe split borrow aliases live_clip_manager (UB, false SAFETY comment)
description: Agent-reasoned, lead-unverified. engine.rs tick_midi_input holds a raw-pointer &mut to live_clip_manager while commit_live_clip calls host.stop_clip -> PlaybackEngine::stop_clip -> live_clip_manager.notify_clip_stopped. Nothing observed; latent miscompile. Fix: manager returns stop requests instead of calling back into the host.

title: MIDI file parser panics on a truncated file (UI-thread crash from import dialog)
description: Agent-reasoned, lead-unverified. midi_parser.rs track_end is never clamped to data length, so data[pos] indexes out of bounds; read errors elsewhere silently return no notes. Fix: bounds-checked reader returning Result, surfaced to the import dialog.

title: Link-initiated play never caches the Link beat offset
description: Agent-reported, confirmed by its search, lead-unverified. link_sync.rs: the offset is only set by app Play/Seek commands; after Stop or project load it is NaN, so a Link start plays on MANIFOLD clock unlocked to Link position or jumps with a stale offset. Fix: cache the offset on every Link-initiated start.
notes: Merged BUG-0u1al (Link-initiated Play never caches the Link beat offset): root cause, found with the BUG-gqhep impact map: only MANIFOLD Play and Seek cache the Link offset; Stop and load set it NaN; a Link-started play never re-caches it, so after any Stop Link stops steering position until MANIFOLD seeks. Fix shape: cache the offset on every transport start regardless of source. Note: the P3 landing (2d64b50e1) reworked the offset into LinkOffset in external_sync; re-check before fixing.

title: Looping video clips drift off the beat and three loop rules disagree
description: Agent-reasoned, lead-unverified. check_custom_loop_boundaries wraps by seeking to in_point, losing overshoot plus seek latency each wrap; drift correction skips looping clips, so lag accumulates. Natural loop length is media_length in engine::compute_video_time, media_length - in_point in video_time::compute_video_time, and the renderer wraps to 0.0. Fix: wrap to the beat-anchored phase; one loop rule in video_time.rs.

title: MIDI Clock beat advances in 1/24-beat steps with no smoothing; BPM estimated from poll times
description: Agent-reasoned, lead-unverified. midi_clock_sync sets beat to the tick count at poll time; at 120 BPM ~every fifth frame holds still, so LFOs and beat-driven motion judder under clock authority. BPM noise about 1% because midir timestamps are discarded. Possible spec deviations: clocks advance position while stopped; position one tick ahead after Start/SPP. Fix: timestamp ticks, extrapolate beat with a phase-locked loop, derive BPM from timestamps.

title: Quantized record commit stops then restarts the same clip (decode dropout on release)
description: Agent-reasoned, lead-unverified. live_clip_manager commit keeps the live clip id, host.stop_clip kills the renderer, then the committed span still covers now and the next sync restarts it from scratch. Fix: skip the stop when the committed span covers now.

title: Node file-path params declare their file kind instead of name-guessing
description: The graph canvas Browse button (BrowseGraphNodePath, app_render.rs; gate is_path_param in manifold-ui graph_canvas/model.rs:627) decides whether a node param gets a picker, and file-vs-folder, by checking whether the param NAME contains folder/dir/path/file, and the picker has no file-type filter. Root fix: look up the node type in manifold-core file_loader.rs file_loader_kind(type_id) (File/Folder plus AssetFamily, the one list with an exhaustiveness test) and derive the filter extensions from the family; carry that kind on a foundation-side snapshot so manifold-ui can gate the button (ui depends on foundation only). Do not extend StringParamSpecDef.is_file_picker (outer-card metadata nothing in ui/app reads). The dialog itself already routes through crates/manifold-app/src/file_dialogs.rs (NodeFile/NodeFolder actions) since feat/file-dialogs; add the extensions there.

title: Add Cadence kicks once its offset is corrected
description: Cadence's project has 173 kick notes; built at its recorded offset (-29.0325 s) its 76 kick labels sit 9.0 ms after the mix attacks (band onset; click -11.4) and its existing snare labels 11.3 ms after, outside the -8..+3 ms the lab holds. fix/label-timing-2026-10-13 (held) moves Cadence's offset by -12.4 ms. After it lands: set kick_labels.PROJECT_KICKS = ('cadence',), rebuild kick_labels.py project, re-run the attack timing check, registry build, audit kick.

title: Offset proof: should a fit carried by a minority of the set's notes count?
description: The grid fit (lab/offsets.fit_map, detector_wip) can prove an offset whose bar puts only a small share of the set's notes inside the bounce: All In For You 'proved' at bar 166 with 27 of 102 possible kicks and 38 of 114 snares (false; see its bug). A rule like 'the proven bar keeps at least 90 percent of the notes the best-covering bar keeps, for at least one pattern' would have refused it, but on recorded proofs it would also refuse dream (kick 92 of 164, snare 175 of 239) while break passes only on snare (kick 112 of 330). Peter decides whether to add a coverage rule (and its threshold) or keep the current rule plus manual review of low-margin proofs.

title: All In For You: set kick notes miss the mix after the tempo ramps; earlier offset proof was false
description: Symptom: All In For You (catalogue comp all_in_for_you, Growth project) cannot join the lab. The 2026-10-11 proof (-252.42 s, Growth V4 LIVE EDITS set vs ALBUM FINAL 1.wav) was false: the fit picked bar 166, the live-edit block after the song's Done locator, where only 27 of 129 kicks and 38 of 152 snares land; margins 0.32 and 0.19 sd; attacks not measured. The song itself starts at the Intro locator (beat 96, offset -35.12 s, bounce 190 s vs set 192.4 s). Against the T2 PREMASTER KICK STEM (lag 0 to the album mix, z 28.6) with offset -35.12: beats 0-368 (before the ramps) 41 of 41 kick notes have a stem hit within 60 ms (median -11.9 ms); 368-396 (164 to 110 ramp) 7 of 13; 416-464 (110 to 164 ramp) 4 of 21; after 464 none. Neither linear-in-beat (als_extract), step nor linear-in-time ramp readings line the later notes up. Root cause unknown; suspects: als_extract.beat_seconds misreads Ableton's tempo automation (curved segments or a different interpolation), or the album bounce's second half is a different arrangement from both local sets. Fix shape: measure the true beat-to-second map from the kick stem per segment, compare to the automation envelope (look for curve values in the FloatEvent XML), fix als_extract if it is the reader, then prove with prove_seconds. Kept out of detector_wip.PAIRS until then. Scratch: album/segshift.py, stemcheck.py, kscan.py in session 2b3491aa scratchpad.

title: water: unlanded liquid-surface perf wins on perf/liquid-surface
description: Branch perf/liquid-surface (origin too), tip d4502525a, 3 commits 2026-10-01, never landed. fbcdd9456 trims the particle volume and running total (out-of-place scan); 8043f531f adds node.particles_near_bins so empty lattice nodes skip the 27-bin search (particle_volume 5.37 to 3.83 ms on Dam Break 64 frame 90); d4502525a skips the redundant nearest-surface draw for filled transmissive meshes (0.65 ms). Level set bit-identical, stills byte-identical, critical path surface+render 15.06 to 12.79 ms. Measurements live in BUG-l24y (liquid surface cost) notes, but that bead never asked for the landing. Why it matters: about 2 ms off every water frame at no look change. Landing needs: the branch predates the water crate split (paths under crates/manifold-renderer and nodes-image now live in manifold-water-surface and siblings), so re-home by merging main in (expect heavy rename conflicts) or port onto a fresh branch; section 2.5 audit already done in 8043f531f; rerun the bit-identical proof and a GPU proof of particles_near_bins on the freeze path; land via scripts/land_branch.py. Found by the 2026-10-13 unlanded-branch audit.

title: Run the Code Terminal GPU proofs deferred at landing
description: feat/code-terminal-upgrade landed with --skip-gpu while networks trained. crates/manifold-nodes/tests/code_terminal.rs gpu module was edited blind for the new reveal (gaps-before-strokes share, untouched and faded fractions) and Fresh Text off in Controls; it compiles but has never run. Run scripts/gpu_proofs_gate.py when the GPU is free; fix thresholds against a real render, not by loosening contracts.

title: Offsets: prove project songs from the snare fit instead of the kick fit?
description: Snare lateness tracks the kick-vs-snare fit gap across songs: stem-proven kicks sit +1..+5 ms, kick-fit songs -2..-9 ms, suggesting the snare fit is the better estimator generally. Switching moves about 30 songs offsets (all families). Peter decides. Evidence: label-fix lane report 2026-10-13, lead scratchpad labelfix/.

title: midnight_patience: export offset wrong for its snares (+22 ms) once timing_shift is gone
description: Its offset comes from kick-stem vs project kick notes; the +24 ms timing_shift slide was hiding that the offset is wrong for its snares (rise at +22 ms). Bass and synth labels on the song may already be off. Needs a proof from its drum stem or an exclusion before any label rebuild. Evidence: lead scratchpad labelfix/.

title: Detector labels: on_attack baseline window drops real hits once timing_shift is gone
description: With timing_shift removed (fix/label-timing-2026-10-13, 93b4526d8), snare positives drop: waypoints 46->22, crush 68->41, 48_hours 141->122, midnight_patience 42->27, control 137->130, skyline 70->65. The dropped events are as loud as the kept ones; at the true time their rise over the -60..-20 ms baseline is ~8 dB vs the 9 dB cut because earlier sounds sit in that window (the slide was gaming this). They become unscored, not negatives. Fix shape: a baseline that excludes the previous event (e.g. min or low percentile of the pre-window, or the window before the previous onset), proven on the old songs to change nothing there. Evidence: lead scratchpad labelfix/why_drop.py.

title: GPU FLIP: draw the newest water frame without waiting for the CPU readback (about 2.5 frames less lag)
description: Peter asked for it (2026-10-13): the live water trails the music by about 42 ms at 60 fps because each published frame particle count and worked/failed flag only reach the CPU about three frames later, and every consumer is launched with CPU-known counts. Work = GPU_FLIP_DISPLAY_HISTORY_DESIGN.md section 7 deferred row (GPU-resident count and acceptance): consumers read counts from a GPU buffer, the interpolation search gets a sentinel, fused kernels gain two gathers, a rejected tick repeats the last good frame on the GPU. Runtime cost near zero; sim and physics unchanged. Needs a design pass to DESIGN_DOC_STANDARD, then GPU proofs through gpu_queue. Related: BUG-ciboy (live water forces 75-110 ms late).

title: Detector labels: timing_shift moves control, skyline, waypoints, 48_hours labels; echo kick offset locked on the sub swell
description: Symptom: control kick labels sit 22 ms after the kick attack (snares +9 ms); snare labels on skyline +12, waypoints -27, 48_hours +20 ms; echo kick labels about 18 ms late. Every other new song is on time (attack -8 to +3 ms vs label). The 15-30 ms lateness read from the detector (earliest confident candidate) is a metric artifact: LAB_TOL 35 ms trains candidates before each kick as positive. Root causes: timing_shift in tools/audio_analysis/lab/detector_labels.py (line ~109, applied ~454/534) runs after the offset proof with a lopsided attack window; echo kick fit locked on the 40-150 Hz swell (fixed ENV_BIAS 6.6 ms). Fix shape: delete or replace timing_shift with a proof-checked onset measure; re-prove echo (per-song bias or snare fit when the fits disagree beyond the usual gap). Verify with the attack-onset summary (lead scratchpad kicklate/summary.py): fixed songs within -6..+1.5 ms (kick), -3..-9 ms (snare); every other song byte-identical. dream snare at -31.6 ms unexplained. Awaiting Peter go-ahead (labels).

title: Snare: hardneg and coincident near-misses on the 2026-10-12 overnight A/B
description: Overnight A/B vs snare_v2_mid, 3 seeds, 43-song exam: coincident +0.66 F1 (90% interval -0.16 to +1.49; old exam +0.65, -0.44 to +1.73; coincident recall 0.550 to 0.584), hardneg +0.63 (-0.59 to +1.91; coincident recall 0.550 to 0.622). Neither cleared zero, so snare_v2_mid shipped (snare-2026-10-13-fd1412d9d). Peter decides whether to rerun both with more seeds (the interval is wide at 3) on the new kick verdicts. Full texts: ~/.cache/manifold/detector-lab/compare/snare_v2_mid_vs_snare_v2_{hardneg,coincident}.txt

title: waypoints: listen before trusting its 46 snare labels; shipped snare is silent on the whole song
description: The shipped snare fires 10 times in the whole of waypoints and catches 1 of 46 labels; its snare label shift (-27 ms) disagrees with its kick shift (0). Either the labelled sound is not a snare the detector should fire on, or the offset is wrong. Peter listens; then keep, relabel, or drop from the snare family.

title: Muted drum tracks audible in the bounce: concentrate 618 kicks, imitation and cadence about 106 snares
description: Symptom: concentrate entered the lab with 0 kick labels because its three kick tracks are muted in the saved set, yet the shipped kick is confident at 90-95 percent of those 620 note times against 11 percent at random, so the bounce has them. Root cause: export_groups tests muted groups, not muted tracks. Fix shape: extend the muted test to tracks, rebuild concentrate. Harmless today (unknown windows), but a wasted exam song.
notes: Measured 2026-10-12 evening with the labeller own attack test per muted kick/snare-named MIDI track (scratch muted_audible.py): kick 993 candidate notes in 49 songs, in-master: concentrate Ghost Kicks 318 and Kicks 300 (on-attack 0.75-0.78 vs random 0.19), corrosion 44-DS Kick 149 and murmur 55-DS Kick 190 (likely already labelled via their drum stems, confirm), default_haze LinnDrum not in master, waypoints 8 unclear. Snare 178 candidates: imitation Clap 44 and cadence QFF Drums 62 in master, skyline 43 Snares 72 unclear. The earlier 4000/5900 figure counted every drum-class note and is withdrawn. Fix stays: track-level export test in detector_labels, then rebuild those songs with re-proof and audit.

title: Kick labels about 25 ms late on 10 of the 19 songs labelled 2026-10-12
description: Symptom: on affect break control dream echo paces running skyline touch waypoints the shipped kick first confident candidate precedes the kick label by a median 15-30 ms; old songs sit within 5 ms. Root cause: kick_labels timing_shift reports 0.0 on 18 of 19 songs, so it is insensitive for these sets. Inside the 35 ms training window, so training is valid; fix the shift estimate and re-prove offsets before these songs enter a release exam. Found by the 2026-10-12 adversarial review (shipped-kick oracle).

title: Release holdout leak: stage cutoffs see holdout songs
description: stage.train chooses its training-time cutoffs on every project song including holdout songs, so a staged config read with --release is slightly flattered on the stage layer. Found while building the holdout (feat/mix-variants-training). Root cause: stage.train pools cutoffs over all project songs; release.py calls it the same way. Fix shape: pass the holdout set into stage.train and drop those songs from its cutoff pools when not releasing; must land before the first --release read of the holdout.

title: Variant matcher re-judge: trust audit and landing of feat/detector-catalog-fix
description:
Sonnet 5.5 session died (usage exhausted) after committing but before verifying. Slot-6 branch feat/detector-catalog-fix now holds 3 commits: 34561c12f (windows match on four-band onset significance vs own other-lag correlation, not fixed ncc>=0.5), 5d7bd8d74 (drift and lag-peak gates use band-onset significance too; download_candidates promoted from scratch cands.py into variants.py, no size/tag dedupe; lab_variants prunes rows distinct() drops), 4f810fbef (catalog.sqlite re-judged). Mechanical checks done 2026-10-12 by GLM: test_tree.py 25/25 green; re-judge diff vs previous committed catalog: rows 354->387, needs_check 56->27, different 153->66, same 145->294; shared-key flips: 82 different->same, 47 needs_check->same, 18 different->needs_check, 5 needs_check->different, 2 same->needs_check, zero same->different; 17 lab_mix rows re-keyed to stem_sum refs, 10 pruned duplicates, 60 new rows (45 same) incl. stem_sum refs. REMAINING (strong-model judgment): trust audit of the flips — the 82 different->same gain is large and gates are looser, spot-check borderline verdicts to separate fixed false-rejects from newly accepted false-accepts; then land via the gate and decide whether download_candidates needs its next bounded round.

## Context
Related: BUG-1gpjo, BUG-8dy68

title: [bug] Trained kick detector train run dies with MPS out-of-memory when the gain probe's larger nets hit the 47.74 GiB pool cap
description: lab/compare.py AB runner (2026-10-12, slot-0 worktree) died ~2.5 h in: kick_v2_final_probe seed 0 finished and saved (s0.json/s0.npz under ~/.cache/manifold/detector-lab/runs/kick-ffa0eda6c15e), but during kick_v2_gain_probe seed 0 training (layers [0] 585 s, [1] 768 s already spent) train_model -> kick_goal_nn.py:234 torch.cat of drawn song slices raised RuntimeError: MPS backend out of memory (38.86 GiB allocated, tried to allocate 10.25 GiB, max 47.74 GiB). Gain probe run dir kick-6715c810e2d1 is empty — no output written. Remaining 5 scheduled runs never started. No crash recovery: one OOM kills the whole run. Fix direction: cap/wrap MPS memory (PYTORCH_MPS_HIGH_WATERMARK_RATIO) or bound the drawn-slice batch in kick_goal_nn.py; also consider per-seed checkpointing so partial layer fits survive a crash. Related: BUG-9ngk8.19 (lab speed), BUG-9ngk8.8 (parallel seeds would worsen GPU pressure).
notes:
Verified root cause (code read, slot-0): eval/kick_goal_nn.py:213-236 builds the ENTIRE epoch's training tensor on the device at kick_goal_nn.py:234 (torch.cat of every song's .to(dev) slices, ~65-75k slices x 38 KB each ~= 2.5-3 GB) on top of spectra resident on MPS. The 10.25 GiB single alloc = torch.cat output while the MPS pool cache holds freed temporaries from prior epochs/trainings; live-vs-cached pool accounting not yet verified. Quality-neutral fix: keep x on CPU and move only x[order[b]] per batch to MPS (draw RNG at :226-227 and permutation at :236 unchanged -> byte-identical batches/gradients). Also: savers are non-atomic (np.savez straight to s{seed}.npz; meta.json read-merge-rewrite) so a crash mid-write can corrupt a run dir.
Adversarial review (GLM-5.3) verdict: adopted better fix - keep ALL Song tensors on CPU (drop data[t].to(dev) at run.py:185) and move only per-batch xb to MPS. slices() is exact on either device (integer gather + amax + elementwise IEEE ops), so results stay bit-identical, gated by a byte-compare. Kills the OOM, the ~39 GiB MPS pool residency (probable BUG-xd15a swap-stall driver), and makes the build phase GPU-free for pipelining. Concretely: gate = fixed config+seed, byte-compare all s{seed}.npz arrays, validated twice on unchanged code first.
Lane A gate evidence 2026-10-12: (1) MPS retrain byte-determinism DOES NOT HOLD - seed 0 rerun drifted on 438/2136 arrays (max理学 0.2-0.9 in net/logit/staged outputs; trees byte-identical), so byte-exact retraining gates are structurally unachievable on MPS; new verdict standard: exact byte-gates only on CPU determinism + behavioral checks on MPS (completes, no wedge/OOM, RSS). (2) WEDDING evidence: the unchanged-code gate child hard-wedged at run.py:185 .to(dev) (Metal submit thread stuck in dispatch_sync/waitUntilCompleted, 38 GB footprint on a 36 GB machine <RSS) - worse than the OOM: a deadlock. Sample + byte-compare artifacts archived under the lane scratchpad. Bites that concurrent lanes sharing one hardcoded cache dir also broke gate isolation - gates must run serialized on a drained queue.
Per Peter: all retrain gates retired and the GPU smoke run dropped altogether. Standing verification standard for this campaign: (1) seconds-scale property battery committed into lab/test_lab.py - slice equality CPU-vs-device on a small fixture, sampled RNG draw/permutation equality old-vs-new code paths, single forward/backward CPU gradient-step equality - plus (2) test_lab suite pass. Full-seed retrains and proof runs are out; Fable will review the delivered changes.
LANE A CLOSED GREEN (final report): (1) BYTE GATE PASSED - old code (HEAD clean worktree) vs new code (memo + CPU-resident Songs + per-batch GPU upload) on CPU: byte-identical across 1404 arrays, s0.npz file sha256 identical (c29646f718960db6); only run_id/module fields differ as expected. (2) test_lab 44 tests OK. (3) MPS sanity probe (under gpu_queue hold): 2-epoch train + predict in ~10 s, peak RSS 603 MB, NO wedge, NO OOM - vs the old-path 38 GB Metal dispatch_sync deadlock. Anti-freeze evidence complete. (4) Re-confirmed: unpinned MPS run diverges on all 1404 net arrays (trees match across devices) - MPS net training is not run-to-run deterministic, device must be pinned for any byte comparisons. HAZARD discovered for follow-up: device is NOT part of model_key, so an MPS-trained layer npz could be silently reused by later CPU runs (or vice versa) - Lane A deliberately did NOT restore its archived MPS layers to avoid poisoning the cache; needs either a device term in model_key or a documented device pinning rule.

title: Detector labels: co-hits count for both families (both-count rule), density report and co-hit goldens
description:
Peter, 2026-10-12, live: a kick and snare together now fires only the kick, not both. Root cause (reasoned, not yet reproduced): the design intent holds (lab/kick_verdict.py header: a kick and snare together still count as a snare), the runtime publishes kick and snare on separate band features with per-detector refractory, and the kick2 feature carries a real-valued verdict — but kick-confident candidates that are snares are rare in the corpus while kick-confident non-snares are abundant, so the trees learned kick2 as a near-veto; the snare's own upper-band evidence is also weakest exactly under a loud kick. No release check caught it.

Fix:
1. Both-count rule, default on: a foreign positive inside the clash window of a target positive is a positive for both families, never a negative (today the far_s rule only keeps them out of hard_neg).
2. Co-hit density report per family pair in every lab run — low density flags augmentation before a model ships with a learned veto.
3. Densify with the remix renderer: layer a kick stem under snare hits (seeded, unity-checked) until the pair has enough co-hit positives.
4. A co-hit golden per family pair in the release parity sets: one clip where a genuine kick+snare together must fire both. The missing kick-snare golden is the test that would have caught this at release.
5. Lab A/B whether density alone recovers it or the snare needs kick-robust upper-band evidence (rise relative to the kick's own spectral shape).

Generalisation: per-pair clash windows in family config; the both-count rule lives once in the labels builder, so every future family pair inherits it. Expected: snare recall on backbeat co-hits recovers (four-on-the-floor claps on 2 and 4), +1-2 snare F1 on co-hit-heavy songs, kick unchanged. Related: BUG-7v4ta (clap/snap confusion), BUG-9ngk8.13, BUG-9ngk8.14.

title: Detector runtime: general verdict measures and a detector feed DAG (verdict tier)
description:
Generalise kick2 to verdict.<family>: any detector may read any other shipped detector's verdict (window before/after, none default, the referenced model's train_id).

- Rust: KickFed becomes a small feed DAG — detectors run in dependency order on the detector worker, each feeding every decision (fired or not) to its readers in emission order; unknown verdict families and cycles refused at load.
- Contract v2: verdict.<family>.* entries replace the kick2.* names (same shape: window_s, none_dt_ms, the referenced train_id).
- Release: for each declared verdict input build the upstream family's held-out predictions per song (the lab/kick_verdict.py rule, made generic) and pin the upstream train_id.
- First proof on a second link: snare2 — the kick reads the snare's verdict (claps and toms read as kicks are the named error class); both detectors decide at 40 ms so the window works. Expected +0.5-1 kick F1.

Runtime needs no change for simultaneous fires: per-detector refractory, separate band features. Design constraint (Peter, 2026-10-12): per-family models with shared evidence — no joint multi-class network.

title: Detector Lab: cross-family negatives (label tier), config-driven
description:
Every family's positives become vouched negatives for every other family, driven by one shared rule in the labels builders instead of per-family hand-wiring. Family config gains negatives_from: [kick, snare, bass, synth, ...]; the shared function pulls those families' positives per song and emits them as hard_neg, with the family's clash window (kick_clash_s) excluding co-hits (BUG-9ngk8.15).

Use note spans, not just note starts: the kick's bass-line fires in Bad Guy are mid-note hits (~40 fires in 15 s where the drum stem shows no attack), which note-start negatives miss.

Data already collected and unused: the catalogue holds 7,053 bass and 20,930 synth positives (52 songs each), parked at lab P5. First A/B: kick with bass note spans as negatives. Expected +1-2 kick F1, precision-led; the named kick error classes (bass lines, toms, claps) are exactly cross-family.

Design constraint (Peter, 2026-10-12): per-family models with foreign-evidence columns only — no joint multi-class network. Specialists with shared evidence.

title: Bass candidates barely line up with bass note starts
description: Found 2026-10-11 moving bass into the Detector Lab. Symptom: bass held-out F1 0.24 (bass_base, 5 seeds, 78 false fires a minute) with labels at the note start and the 5 ms before to 50 ms after window. title: Snare labels count hits in muted audio clips and misplace hits in warped clips

Found 2026-10-11 building the bass labels (cadence and got_it were full of muted bass clips). Root cause: clip selection ignores disabled/speaker state; placement ignores warp markers and loops. Fix shape: on the snare path use note_labels.playing_clips and pass the tempo map to clip_hits (detector_labels.warped_hits, already on feat/detector-labels-v2), regenerate snare_labels.json, measure the label change, retrain the snare net and compare with detector_compare over 5 seeds. title: Bass and synth detector families: labels and precision before any model
description: Feasibility 2026-10-11 (toolkit: bass_labels.py, synth_labels.py, family_cands.py, detector_net.py). Labels from project notes and clips on bass/synth tracks, prominent = 6 dB rise in the family band within 6 dB of the song main level, kick-clash 30 ms unscored: bass 1360 events in 28 songs, synth 1577 in 26. Candidates (4.5 dB band rise) find 98% of both at 21 and 10 candidates/s. The snare-recipe net held out, 3 seeds: bass F1 .21/.23/.26 (R ~.44, P ~.16), synth F1 .25/.25/.25 (R .41-.63, P ~.16). Not usable. Precision is the blocker: most fires land where no labelled event is, likely real but unlabelled parts (bass inside resampled audio, layered synths, unnamed tracks) and kicks. A spectral-change measure fires on 57% of non-prominent bass notes and 84% of synth ones, so it cannot define prominence alone. Next: label from stems where they exist (bass/synth stems), inspect what false fires sit on (snare_what_fires analogue), then retry; Peter wants prominent events only.

title: Subsurface materials cost seconds per frame at full HD
description: Symptom (measured 2026-10-10 from the render_scene_subsurface tests, scaled per pixel): the shipped default subsurface material (Diffusion, 8 samples, one light) costs about 0.3 s per frame at 1920x1080 when it covers the screen; random walk at 64 samples costs about 25 s per frame. On stage a subsurface object close to camera drops the show to a few frames per second or stalls it. Not a GPU fault: the work is tiled into command buffers of 12 ms or less. Root cause: full sample count traced every frame at full resolution. Fix shape: a per-frame subsurface budget with progressive accumulation across frames (the RT history path already accumulates), reduced-resolution trace with the existing reconstruct and filter kernels, and an opaque-first boundary query (exact: run the filtered query only when the first hit is another instance). Needs a design call on what quality drops first under budget; that call is Peter.

title: Kick net: test four time segments at the shipped 150 ms slice
description: Snare sweep 2026-10-10: a 190 ms slice (which switches the net's final pooling from one time segment to four, so it keeps where in the window things happen) lifted snare F1 .617 -> .672 at zero extra latency. The kick sweep's 500 ms history test also used four segments and was flat, but it changed history length too. Test: shipped kick recipe with TBINS 4 at 150 ms (and 190 ms), 3 seeds, grouped held-out; adopt only above seed noise.

title: Snare detector: fast breakbeats and rolls

For now the labels mark them unscored: runs of labelled hits under 200 ms apart, padded 250 ms (scratch snare_labels.py dense_spans). Fix shape unknown; suspects: the candidate finder needs a 4.5 dB rise over the last 21 ms, which a roll may not give, and the net has no training examples of dense breaks it is told to fire on.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Simulation 2026-10-11 (tools/audio_analysis/eval/snare_roll_sim.py; released snare model; 4 one-shots from Cold remix snare stem over Pattern NO KICK bed, 174 bpm): candidates exist for every backbeat, eighth and sixteenth hit (100%; rising roll 95%; break 78%, the misses are ghost notes 12 dB down). Caught: backbeat .94, eighths .93, sixteenths .03, rising roll .14, break .38. Root cause: the candidate finder is fine; the net rejects hits closer than ~100 ms because dense runs were unscored in training, so it never saw a positive inside one. Fix shape: train on the prominent hits inside dense spans (labels already have them) while keeping main-set scoring unchanged, and report dense-span recall separately.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Dense-run training (SNARE_DENSE=1: the 617 prominent snares inside fast runs train as positives; main scoring unchanged), 3 seeds vs the shipped recipe: main-set F1 .702/.704/.683 mean .696 vs .678 (+1.8); fast-run recall .50-.52 vs .45-.47. Per song (recall, mean over seeds) it swings both ways: imitation -28.6, just_the_way -16.0, set_me_free -15.1, burn_stems -11.1; basalt +40.4, default_haze +22.9, worship +18.6. title: Scene-modifier plug-ins stage 4: Math View moves to manifold-scene-modifiers through ChainView hooks; engine load/expand spells zero family ids
description:
DESCRIPTION:

title: GPU hang flake: rt_t38_multibounce bleed_region_reads_above_the_probe_pin_threshold hangs late in a long gpu-proofs run
description: Symptom: in the post-T2 water batch landing gate (2026-10-10, slot-1, gpu-proofs leg 2938 s) manifold-nodes gpu_proofs rt_t38_multibounce::bleed_region_reads_above_the_probe_pin_threshold panicked at manifold-gpu/src/metal/encoder.rs:2928, command buffer status 5, kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang. 177 of 178 in that binary passed. Root cause unknown; suspects: GPU watchdog under sustained load after 45 min of proofs, or accumulated device state across tests in one process (cargo test shares the device). Fix shape: reproduce by running the full manifold-nodes gpu_proofs binary twice in a row, then decide determinism fix versus moving the multibounce proof off the landing set. Next oracle: rerun with MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 and capture which test owns the first non-victim error status.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Diagnosis lane 2026-10-10 (lane/rt-hang-diagnosis, HEAD 82754f0cf). (1) System log silent, but /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/gpuEvent-gpu_proofs-91184-2026-10-10-161348.ips and -161350.ips name process gpu_proofs-91184, restart_reason_desc CDM Kill timeout, guilty_dm 3: the GPU reset was caused by our own test binary (a compute dispatch hit the watchdog), not another process. Older gpuEvent-gpu_proofs reports exist from 2026-10-09. (2) One whole-binary run with MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 aborted after about 6 tests with: setRenderPipelineState failed assertion, color attachment 0 texture sample count (1) does not match pipeline colorSampleCount (4), same for depth. A 4x MSAA pipeline (render_scene.rs MSAA_SAMPLES=4 is the only 4x user) is bound in a 1-sample pass. Owning test unknown because tests run in parallel threads. Unproven whether this causes the CDM timeout; it is real undefined behaviour either way. Next oracle: rerun the debug layer with --test-threads=1 to name the test, then fix the render_scene pass/pipeline sample-count mismatch, then rerun the full binary with the debug layer to look for the next error.

Fix shape: cache a single-sample pipeline variant (add sample count to the pipelines key) and use it for blend_entries in Pass B. Not edited (production GPU code). title: Static procedural producers churn semantic revisions and invalidate SSS history
description: Discovered while proving BUG-5l4o.9 on materials-fixes: node.arrange_copies (generate_instance_transforms.rs) and node.linear_gradient are deterministic for unchanged inputs/params but omit pure:true and do not mark content unchanged. Executor commit_mesh_revisions therefore advances semantic versions per dispatch. Static SSS fixtures using these producers remained at history count 1 before fixture isolation. Static source audit shows instances/env versions are included in the conservative SSS scene key. Audit safe purity declarations and output lifetime/memoization before changing; do not weaken renderer invalidation for truly changing or unknown inputs. Acceptance: bounded stable-producer content-version proof plus mutation invalidation, and static SSS integration accumulation with production producers. This is a newly discovered producer contract issue, separate from sampling-jitter reprojection.

description: Review follow-ups, not benchmarked performance claims: (1) StereoAnalyzer calculates and publishes peak-style L/R dB arrays whose GUI read methods have no callers; reuse balance path or remove unused work. title: 3D scene engine internals: nodes at user boundaries, modular code inside
description: Peter, 2026-10-09: the one-composable-thing rule fits TouchDesigner-style 2D effect and generator graphs, not 3D scenes. A 3D scene's render passes and kernels are static engine internals nobody rewires; the scene panel is their interface, like a traditional rendering engine. Nodes split only where a user would plausibly rewire, swap or insert (mesh sources, materials, lights, camera, post effects after the scene). Code inside such a node still splits into modules, one pass or stage per module behind a clean interface; god-file guards apply. Rule lives in DECOMPOSING_GENERATORS.md section 1.2 and CLAUDE.md. Work under this epic: (1) audit 3D-scene nodes and atoms against the new boundary: atoms nobody rewires that should fold inside a scene node, and scene internals exposed as ports; (2) split render_scene.rs (9,665 lines: raster, RT, lights, prewarm in one file) into per-pass modules without changing the node boundary; (3) same review for gltf_load.rs (5,921) and the other 3D files over the god-file threshold. Starts after renderer crate split Tier 1 lands (render_scene.rs moves to manifold-nodes-scene in P2).

description: Symptom: hand-authored 3D presets (WaterDamBreakGpuFlip, likely others) ship a bare orbit camera wired straight into render_scene, so the Camera card has no focus, f-stop, shutter, or DoF/motion blur toggles. The cinematic chain only arrives via the GLB importer (gltf_import/scene.rs + cinematic_tail.rs) or the one-time v1.13 load migration; nothing enforces it for authored presets. title: App startup pipeline warmup takes ~3 min every launch despite the on-disk pipeline archive
description:
Symptom: every manifold launch spends 160-181s in the startup warmup pass, and it hits its time limit before finishing (rt-capture logs: "warmup pass took 168294ms (completed=false)", 181330ms, 159945ms, on three back-to-back runs of the same binary, 2026-10-07). The RT noise gate launches the app once per capture, so a 6-capture re-baseline costs ~20 min of warmup alone; Peter pays it on every app launch too.

Root cause: unknown. crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/archive.rs already wraps MTLBinaryArchive to cache compiled pipelines on disk, so the second launch should be near-free. Suspects: (1) the archive is not saved, or is saved to a path that is not reloaded; (2) the archive only covers the Metal compile step, and the real cost is our WGSL->MSL translation and codegen, which nothing caches; (3) pipeline descriptors differ run to run (for example codegen output not deterministic), so archive lookups miss.

Fix shape: time one launch with a warm archive and split the warmup into translate vs Metal compile to pick the suspect. Then cache whichever step is uncached, keyed by shader source hash, so only the first launch after a shader change pays. Verify: second rt-capture launch logs warmup well under 10s with completed=true.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — evidence. Remaining: Time warm-archive startup, separate translation from Metal compilation, cache the uncached stage, and verify the second launch. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-10-07T02:07:33Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. title: Whitewater floats above the water surface when surface shaping params are pushed
description: Symptom (Peter, 2026-10-07, Water — Dam Break (GPU FLIP), screenshot: Surface Particle Scale 1.2, Stretch 8.13, Centre Smoothing 0.45, Smoothing Iterations 2): foam and other whitewater particles hover above the rendered water mesh instead of sitting on it. Leading suspect: two different surfaces. whitewater_step classifies and places foam against the solver level and solid grids, while the rendered mesh comes from liquid_blobs (particle_scale, stretch, smoothing) then liquid_smooth_mesh and liquid_mesh_relaxation. Stretch, centre smoothing and Laplacian smoothing all pull the displayed surface inward, so foam that is correctly on the simulated surface ends up above the visible one. Check first how FLIP Fluids keeps foam on its smoothed mesh (whether it accepts the gap at default settings or offsets foam), per follow-industry-standards. Fix shape candidates: keep foam on the displayed surface (project or offset foam against the display mesh level), or bound the display surface drift from the sim surface. title: Whitewater: lowering Whitewater Budget mid-run leaves existing whitewater stuck
description: Symptom (Peter, 2026-10-07, Water — Dam Break (GPU FLIP)): once whitewater exists, lowering the Whitewater Budget does not remove it. The existing foam/spray/bubbles stay stuck in the scene. Only Reset then lowering the budget clears it. Root cause: unknown. Suspects: the budget only caps new emission (spawn_whitewater_body.wgsl reads capacity), so the live population above the new cap is never trimmed; the lifecycle storage (whitewater_lifecycle.rs) grows in 4,096 steps but may never shrink, and the age/keep passes may stop touching particles whose index is past the new capacity, so they neither move nor die. Check what FLIP Fluids does when its max whitewater particle limit drops mid-sim before choosing the fix. Fix shape: a budget change trims or retires the population above the new cap in one defined operation, never leaves particles outside the stepped range; a CPU reference test that lowers capacity mid-run and asserts the population falls to the cap and every survivor still advects.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Trim or retire whitewater above a lowered budget during a live run and add a regression that checks population reaches the new cap. title: Liquid colliders sample a fixed 32-node distance field and hull pieces, so FLIP water misses photoscan rock
description: Symptom: in Ocean Cliff the GPU FLIP water reads as clipping into or stopping short of the cliff scan. Root cause (read, not yet confirmed by a still): fluid_role_source builds each collider as convex hull pieces (Collider Detail, up to 64), and fluid_role.rs build_distance samples their union on DISTANCE_NODES_ALONG_LONGEST = 32 nodes along the longest side, whatever the water grid (about 7 cm at Res 128). Hulls bridge every hollow and the field blurs the rock. Also, in OceanCliff.json the back cliff is drawn whole but only fragments 0 and 2 have colliders; 3 crashes the hull cook (BUG-ra759, hull assert) and 1 is missing for unknown reasons, so water can pass through those parts. Fix shape: for fixed colliders skip hulls and build the signed distance straight from the scan triangles (the builder already signs by generalized winding number, which tolerates open meshes; relax validate_closed_mesh for this path), at a spacing tied to the liquid cell size. Hulls stay for moving Box3D bodies. Oracle: a still of the solid field drawn over the scan, before and after.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — evidence. Remaining: Run the photoscan collider scene and replace the fixed field or hull approximation if confirmed. title: Camera Sky: visible seam where the HDRI wraps (looking along -x)
description: Symptom: Camera Sky draws a thin vertical seam in the sky when the camera looks along -x. Root cause: the equirect lookup u = atan2(d.z, d.x)/2pi + 0.5 wraps at u=0/1, but the sampler is GpuSamplerDesc::default() (ClampToEdge on U), so bilinear filtering at the seam clamps instead of wrapping. Fix shape: repeat on U, clamp on V for the standalone pipeline (camera_sky.rs run) and the fused path (the sampler the freeze codegen binds for this input), plus a GPU proof that renders a ray straddling the seam and checks it against a wrapped CPU bilinear reference. None of the Ocean Cliff hero cameras sees -x, so the shipped renders are unaffected.

title: GPU FLIP: water volume drains while a light Moving box sits on the floor
description: Symptom (Peter, 2026-10-06, res 32, /Users/peterkiemann/Downloads/waterLossTest.manifold): with a box3d physics object on Moving (density 20, friction 0.5, bounce 0.15), the water volume drops over time; the box feels stuck to the floor and jittery. Root cause unknown; nothing has been run yet. Suspects, read from code only: (1) faces_to_particles in gpu_flip_step.wgsl removes any particle still inside a solid after resolve_solid. In the wedge between a box resting on the floor and the floor, the push out of the box lands in the floor or wall, is refused, and the particle is deleted. Each twitch of the box sweeps fresh water into that wedge. (2) Density 20 (2% of water) is the unstable light-body case for two-way coupling: added-mass buzz, plus noisy lift in shallow res-32 water, plus stick-slip on Coulomb friction. First oracle: run the file headless and log the live particle count per tick, box Moving vs Static, then again at density 500. Fix shape depends on which of these it is.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text:
Measured 2026-10-06 (headless `manifold frame-time <file> --frames 1800 --frame-clock`, RUST_LOG=gpu_flip::schedule=debug, live count per retired tick; Sim Rate 30 Hz, one liquid step per tick). Live particles after ~30 s, from 42,524:
- Moving, density 20: 8,402 (80% gone, steady drain)
- Fixed, density 20: 42,524 (no loss)
- Moving, density 500: 27,723 (35% gone; still draining ~22/tick after the box comes to rest on the floor)
- Fill height 1.0 m so the box floats (from 82,668): density 500 lost 8; density 20 lost 2,054 (box pressed against the back wall)
Every other removal path is ruled out for this scene: all walls closed, no outflow regions, push_refused 0, speed limit far above the water's speed, crowding cap 250/cell.
Verdict: suspect (1) confirmed in refined form: water is deleted only where a dynamic box touches the floor or a wall (the inside-solid rule), not in open water. Suspect (2) killed as the cause, kept as an amplifier: density 20 drains 2.3x faster and never settles (body speed 0.3-0.7 m/s above the gravity term for the whole run), density 500 settles.
Unproven: which resolve_solid branch deletes (push lands in floor/wall and is clamped back into the box, vs the box twitching over water). Next oracle: a temporary per-branch deletion counter, plus the same scene in CPU FLIP to see whether the engine drains too.
Code-read suspects for the root, unmeasured: the liquid predicts each body as v + external accel * t + its own reaction, so Box3D floor/wall contacts are invisible within a tick (a resting box is told to the water as falling at up to g/30 = 0.33 m/s); a box flush on the floor has no water cell beneath it at 12.5 cm cells, so it gets no lift however light (stuck to the floor). Fix shape is pending a talk with Peter.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Still pool, 1 m deep, no dam: a density-2000 box resting dead still on the floor (motion under 1 mm/s) drains 717 particles/s at Sim Rate 30, 429/s at 60, 904/s at 15; 66% of the water in 60 s at 30 Hz. Density 500 ends on the floor and drains the same. So the drain needs no body motion. It grows with tick length, which fits the water predicting a resting body as falling at g*dt (contacts invisible), but it is not proportional and 60 Hz still drains, so that is probably not the whole cause. A Fixed box (no prediction) drains nothing.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Measured 2026-10-06 on feat/liquid-body-handoff with the v1.20.0 contacts-wire upgrade (saved projects had no domain.contacts to step.contacts wire, so the support fix never reached them; the upgrade adds it on load). Headless frame-time, live particles: still2000 65532 to 65532 (was 22061 on main), still500 65532 to 65532 (was 22611), moving20 (light density-20 box on Moving, 30 Hz, 1800 frames) 42524 to 36186 (was 7585 on main, 16185 on the branch without the wire). Still boxes: fixed. Light moving box: 15% still lost, mostly 2.7 s to 8 s while the dam wave throws the box, then about 1 particle a tick. push_refused 0 throughout, all faces closed, max particle speed under 5 m/s (speed removal needs about 9 m/s), so the remaining path is unknown: suspects are crowded-marker removal (over 250 per cell where push-out stacks water against the box) or the narrow-band delete. Next oracle: a per-path removal counter in the tick stats.

title: GPU FLIP over-noding: fold surface mesh, whitewater internals and no-op passes into optimised stage kernels
description: Astra audit 2026-10-06 (read-only, Peter asked: "find if we are over noding ... instead of writing sensible optimised compute kernels. Users won't touch these GPU FLIP nodes"). Solver stage boundary (gpu_flip_step) is right; render is not over-noded. All savings unmeasured; bit-identical targets unless noted. Ranked after the approved particle_volume gather: (1) mesh rebuild as one stage (count/edge-count/offsets/volume_surface_mesh/smooth_surface_mesh/surface_mesh_normals): mesher computes gradient normals that the final normals pass replaces; relaxation moves 80-byte vertices when only positions change; keep positions packed, assemble once, keep separate Jacobi iterations and final normals; preserve original UVs. (2) whitewater_step runs ~15 internal standalone atoms: emitter chain 7->1, spawn+classify 2->1, advect+retype+age 3->1 (nine dispatches per tick), keep RNG streams and order. (3) surface no-op passes: with Fill Pits 0 and Smoothing 0, grow/redistance/shrink/smooth x,y,z pass through, and the final clamp repeats particle_volume's own solid clamp; a surface stage bypasses them (replaces the parked array-passthrough P3 of PARTICLE_VOLUME_BRICK_GATHER_DESIGN.md). (4) unused copies: liquid_frame publishes face components nobody reads (3 dispatches + 3 history blits per publication); whitewater reads 3 face_sample_component arrays it could sample packed; two zero-padding pad_distance_lattice copies and an influence ping-pong copy in whitewater. (5) solver: particle_distance -> phi_into_solids -> water_from_phi as one cell kernel on the normal path (2 dispatches per substep). (6) spherical-blob fast path: build blobs in the sort's final pass (1 dispatch, 64 B/particle). Unified grid: share solid distance with nearest-object metadata (static scenes now; moving bodies need timestamped fields); do NOT replace whitewater liquid_cells with solver water (the engine also keeps its own diffuse material grid; replacing changes typing, away from parity). Other presets with the same surface chain: WaterDamBreakGpu, WaterStillPoolMatter, WaterDamBreakMatter, WaterFloatingBoxMatter; WaterDamBreakParticles has the whitewater pattern. Next: a design doc per stage (mesh stage, whitewater fusion, surface bypass + unused copies), Astra review, measured A/B per landing.

title: Sharing one CARGO_TARGET_DIR across worktrees reuses stale workspace-crate builds
description: Symptom (2026-10-06): building slot-8 with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=slot-1/target after building slot-2 linked manifold-renderer against a manifold-gpu built from slot-2 (missing GatedRecorder), so the build failed; with additive differences it would have silently tested the wrong code. Root cause: Cargo dep-info paths are package-relative and freshness is by file mtime, so a worktree whose files are older than the shared artifact is judged fresh even when its content differs. The overnight lead used a shared target to land cold slots under the disk reserve (land_branch with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=slot-1/target), so those gates could have run mixed trees. Fix shape: land_branch and gate_runner refuse a CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the worktree being landed (or touch every workspace source before building when one is shared), and the slot ring frees disk by cleaning landed slots instead of sharing targets.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Make gate_runner reject shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR use across worktrees or otherwise guarantee source freshness without shared-target measurements. title: Coupled bodies creep under a steady sideways water reaction below their friction limit
description: Symptom: a body resting on the GPU FLIP tank floor walks a little every tick under a steady sideways push below mu. Seen by the body-friction lane (lane/body-friction-contact 3436c1677): a push decoded as one lumped impulse per tick measured an apparent threshold of 0.23-0.25 for every friction, before and after the wall-friction fix. Root cause (suspected): the water reaction is applied once per tick before Box3D contact stepping (coupling.rs:484-490, physics.rs:1394-1396), so the first substep sees the whole tick impulse as a velocity kick that friction only partly cancels; tick-lumped coupling, not a simultaneous solve. Fix shape: spread the reaction across Box3D substeps as a force, or apply it inside the contact solve. Related: BUG-3ypk (GPU FLIP body friction is linear drag, not Coulomb).
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — verification. Remaining: Run the body-friction threshold probe against the landed steady-force fix before making a closure decision. title: GPU FLIP water tangential grip is one-way; a two-way exchange must account for the FLIP transfer
description: The constrain pass blends cut faces toward the body velocity (f*v_s + (1-f)*u, gpu_flip_step.wgsl:1824-1861) and tells the body nothing, so a light body moves water for free. Native FLIP Fluids has the same one-way blend (fluidsimulation.cpp:6872-6936), so this is beyond engine parity. Fable proposed an implicit 6x6 per-body exchange (scratchpad fable_friction_design.md D2); Astra review (astra_friction_result.md) blocks it: both new and saved faces are constrained to the same solid velocity (gpu_flip_step.rs:1780), so the correction cancels in the FLIP difference (gpu_flip_step.wgsl:2258) and the composed step can create energy (unit masses, f=1: 0.5 -> 0.625 at FLIP=1). Also: the exchange is not purely tangential, must use the physical wet mask not l.solve_water (pinned pockets), needs clock gating, light-body cancellation handling, and real transfer-level regressions. Fix shape: decide new/saved-field treatment and particle-transfer accounting first, then the exchange. Split from BUG-3ypk (GPU FLIP body friction is linear drag, not Coulomb).
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Decide saved/new field semantics and particle-transfer accounting before implementing two-way FLIP/body momentum exchange. title: Live GPU FLIP display may hold frame B below 60 fps: fenced publication trails the accepted pair by one frame
description: Symptom (modelled, not yet observed in the app): since particle blending pass 2 (c6c150bfa), a live GPU FLIP frame publishes a tick only after that tick's fence retires, on a later frame; export publishes on the same frame. So the published A/B pair trails the accepted pair by one display frame. D7 (docs/LIVE_SIM_CLOCK_DESIGN.md) keeps the display inside the accepted pair, but the blend reads the published pair, so below 60 fps the shown time can step unevenly or hold at B: model /tmp/slot9_published_pair.py gives 60 fps smooth at every Sim Rate; 30 fps at 20 Hz steps 17/50/33 ms and at 60 Hz sits past B every frame; 24 fps uneven at every rate (30 Hz: 67/33/33/33 ms). Matter, CPU FLIP and export are unaffected (same-frame publication). Oracle: a live GPU FLIP run at 24 fps logging display_time against B's simulation time. Fix options: keep the count and accept flag on the GPU so B advances on the frame it is encoded (no CPU wait), or add one display frame of latency for fenced publishers. Found by the wave clock-reds lane (2042c96c5).

title: Implicit body-side friction for GPU FLIP coupled bodies
description: GPU FLIP bodies feel only the pressure reaction (engine parity, rigidfluidcoupling.cpp has no friction term). The removed explicit friction reaction rho*h^3*w*f*(u - v_s) per cut face has per-step gain k = rho*h*f*A_wet/m and diverges once k > ~2. k table: Floating Box 62.5 kg 0.30; Collision ratio 0.1 (0.8 kg) 1.56; Dam Break obstacle 1 kg h=4/64 0.5 m2 wetted 15.6; fully wetted 136. Shape for an implicit version: accumulate C = sum c_f b_f b_f^T (6x6, linear+angular) per body in impulse_finalize, solve (I + M^-1 C) dv = M^-1 P per body, fluid side uses the post-exchange body velocity. Unconditionally stable for any k.

title: Driven bodies: a performed object that feels the water (target spring on a Box3D body)
description: Today a MIDI- or automation-driven object is a scripted collider: it goes exactly where the control says and the water never pushes back (infinitely heavy in the coupled solve). Add a Driven mode on a physics object: the control sets a target pose; each tick Box3D applies a spring-damper impulse toward it (strength and damping params), so the body lags on a dive, bobs on release, and stalls when the water has nowhere to go. Uses the existing apply_impulse path (manifold-physics lib.rs) and the existing liquid coupling (LIQUID_SOLVER_SEAM_DESIGN.md section 3.3 (Two-way Box3D coupling)); no solver change. title: Liquid surface level set is a homegrown hybrid, not Yu-Turk or Zhu-Bridson
description: particle_volume: the doc cites Yu and Turk 2010, but the field is distance to the nearest ellipsoid, capped at 0.1 bin outside, with reach <= 0.9 bin; k_s/k_n are unused. It is then binomial-smoothed 0-3 passes (silently clamped). Look-only effect: about +6% meshed volume, a 35 mm skin at 64^3, and blobby sheets that shrink when smoothed. Fix: a faithful Yu-Turk anisotropic kernel sum or Zhu-Bridson 2005. Also, resolution_scale is clamped 1..8 in code but its param range is 1..4, which is silent. Look phase.

title: GPU FLIP coarse levels re-derive L at 2h with no check that r·z keeps its sign
description: Review item 6 on 987220079. The V-cycle coarse levels use the masked Laplacian re-derived at 2h (gpu_flip_preset.rs v_cycle, the pressure_smooth and pressure_residual nodes at level h·2^k), not the Galerkin product R·L·P. PCG needs an SPD preconditioner; with masked full-weighting restriction, masked trilinear prolongation and a re-derived coarse operator, symmetry holds by construction (R = Pᵀ/8, symmetric sweeps, exact symmetric coarse inverse), but positive definiteness is not proved. Symptom if it fails: r·z ≤ 0 in some iteration, β or α flip sign, CG stalls or diverges. Nothing checks it today. Fix shape: a CPU check in scripts/mgpcg_reference.py and a GPU proof that r·z > 0 every iteration on the Dam Break, deep pool and splash problems (read rz from node.conjugate_gradient state in a test), plus a refusal or Galerkin fallback if a case goes non-positive.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — verification. Remaining: Resolve the r·z sign proof failure with a focused CPU check or explicit fallback. Evidence in record: verification-gap (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-10-02T01:13:13Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. description: Since BUG-ca67 (RT proofs time out the GPU) the three never_stalls_past_20ms gates (rt_p1_region_probe, rt_r1_reflection, rt_t2b_temporal_wiring) run only under rt-perf-proofs, because a wall-clock frame time in the parallel gpu_proofs binary measures the other tests.
