title: Run-time node errors reach only stderr, never the performer
description: Symptom: anything a node reports through EffectNodeContext::error at run time (the MPM non-finite tick halt, the Liquid Surface mesh-capacity overflow, FLIP and matter coupling failures) is printed as "[graph error] node ..." by the executor (node_graph/execution.rs, the error_scratch drain) and goes nowhere else: no node badge, no panel line, no ContentState field. On stage the water just stops or blanks with no reason shown. Seam invariant I11 (overflow is counted and reported) only holds in the log; the P4 conformance suite reads these errors through a gpu-proofs-only tap (NodeErrorTap) because nothing else carries them. Root cause: the executor has no channel for run-time node errors beyond eprintln. Fix shape: keep the latest error per node on the runtime (bounded, deduplicated), carry it in the content state snapshot, and show it on the node and the layer the way setup refusals already show; then point the conformance suite at that channel and delete the tap.

title: Impulse cannot be fired at a body coupled to Live Matter water
description: Symptom: a scene impulse aimed at a Box3D body that shares a scene with a Live Matter (node.matter_domain) liquid fails at capture with "Impulse: graph has no prepared physics ancestry". prepare_scene_impulse resolves the body and redirects it to the matter domain fine; capture_scene_impulse_at_source then calls observe_physics_at_source, which needs physics_sample_steps. physics_sample_steps (preset_runtime/physics_sampling.rs) leaves out a matter-coupled pair on purpose (the domain records controls per display frame and owns its world), so a scene whose only physics is that pair gets None and every capture is refused. fire_scene_impulse (the product Fire path) goes through the same capture, so an Impulse modifier on a box floating in MPM water cannot fire. MatterDomain::physics_impulse_stamp and enqueue_physics_impulse already handle rigid targets, so the domain side is built. Found by the liquid conformance collision check (seam P4) trying to kick the box. Fix shape: when no node replays history, observe_physics_at_source has nothing to sample; record the observation time and admit the capture, then prove a kick on WaterFloatingBoxMatter through fire_scene_impulse on the GPU.

title: WaterDamBreakMatter differs between two direct runs in one process

title: GPU FLIP: walls that only push, so water peels off lids, containers and ceilings
description:
In the pressure solve a wall face can pull as well as push. With no flow through the face, suction holds water against lids, ceilings and moving containers, and splashes come out small. A separating wall lets water leave the face: flow away from the wall is allowed and wall pressure is never negative.

GPU FLIP's pressure is a multigrid-preconditioned CG with solid face weights and ghost fluid at the surface (gpu_flip_pressure.wgsl). CG can't take the inequality directly, so the solve needs an active set: re-solve with the faces where the wall pulls opened, warm-started, only on ticks where some wall pulls. Methods: Chentanez and Müller, A Multigrid Fluid Pressure Solver Handling Separating Solid Boundary Conditions (SCA 2011), built for multigrid; Takahashi and Batty, multilevel active-set preconditioner for box-constrained pressure (SCA 2023) and the primal-dual box-constrained QP solver (TVCG 2024, the sloshing sphere). Matter's box walls already separate: matter_bounds.wgsl only stops motion into a wall.

Evidence from the earlier SWASH solver (2026-09-30, 64³ Dam Break): a crude max(p, 0) in every wall-touching cell took the share of particles above 3 m at frame 134 from 0.088% to 0.011% and emptied the lid by frame 119, but left about 180 times the divergence, so that version can't ship. BUG-h8or's wall-placement question was for SWASH; GPU FLIP already matches the FLIP Fluids engine's walls, and Dam Break lid rain is still open, so measure it first on GPU FLIP with the same share-above-3 m count.

Test: Dam Break lid and a shaken closed container, stills before and after, frame-clock A/B, pressure iteration count on ticks with pulling walls. Cost is unknown until measured.
notes:
2026-09-30: the wall-placement question from BUG-h8or (lid slabs) could not be settled with a particle margin as a stand-in (see that bead). A faithful test needs fractional wall cells, the P3b solid machinery. Re-judge this task after that test.

title: SWASH Dam Break splash flattens into slabs along the lid at 1.5 s
description: Symptom: at 64 cubed, frame 90 (1.5 s) of the SWASH Dam Break render, the left and middle splash columns reach the 4 m lid and spread into flat horizontal strips along it. The FLIP exports and the WaterDamBreakGpu preset at the same frame only touch the lid at the far right corner; their left columns stop short. Root cause unknown. Suspects: SWASH loses less energy than FLIP, so the columns climb higher (compare the race motion reports, highest point per frame); or the lid acts no-slip or sticky, so water that touches it clings instead of falling. Fix shape: compare the highest-point curve of SWASH vs the engine race over frames 60-120 first; if the heights match, look at the lid boundary condition. Seen in look/water-material stills (swash_look_variants_64, frames 90 and 240).
notes:
2026-09-30, 64 cubed, fft_water_splash_causes_64 against fft_water_engine_race (whitewater off, no obstacle). Geometry matches WaterDamBreak.json. Energy matches: speed mean, p99, top and highest point per frame are within a few percent of the engine. The gap is how long water stays at the lid. Particles within 10 cm of the lid at frames 59/74/89/104/119/134: SWASH 495/676/916/662/370/179, engine 86/90/105/82/13/0. Share above 3 m at frame 134: SWASH 0.157%, engine 0.010%. Not the density correction: rate 0 holds more. Cause 1: node.faces_to_particles clamps particles 0.001 cells off a wall face, where the grid wall-normal velocity is about 0, so a particle pressed on the lid barely moves off it. The engine keeps particles 0.2 cells off a wall that sits half a cell past its last free face, where the normal velocity is 70% of the interior. A 0.2-cell margin: frame 134 above 3 m 0.088%, lid empty by frame 149, packing 0.3 points worse. 0.3 cells: 0.042%. Cause 2: suction. A no-penetration lid lets the pressure hold a water layer up. A crude max(p, 0) at wall cells plus the 0.2 margin gives 0.011% at frame 134, matching the engine, but leaves about 180 times the divergence (left undone rms 0.42/s against 0.0023), so it cannot ship. The proper version is a separating wall condition in the solve. Not explained: at frames 59-89 SWASH still holds 3-5 times the engine lid layer with both changes (sep + 0.3 margin: 514/520/353), so the frame 90 slabs shrink by about half but stay. Tried and refuted: zeroing the FLIP old grid wall faces (the engine convention) made it worse (1084 at frame 89).
2026-09-30, side-wall sheet probe (fft_water_splash_causes_64 and fft_water_engine_splash_64, water within 25 cm of the side walls, every 5 frames), with the 0.2-cell margin shipped. Same mass and speed: share above 2 m 0.47-0.59% SWASH against 0.41-0.51% engine at frames 39-59, mean rising speed within 0.3 m/s at every frame. So the frame 59-89 lid layer is the thin wall film running up to the lid. Wall placement test, margin as a stand-in for the engine wall sitting half a cell past its last free face: 0.45 cells gives 448/574/526 lid particles at frames 59/74/89 (0.2 gives 477/632/843); 0.7 gives none, but the stand-in is not faithful: SWASH wall cells stay full water cells in the density and pressure solves, so water kept off part of them crowds (past rest last 30 frames 12.5% at 0.45, 23.5% at 0.7, against 6.8% at 0.2) and the 0.7 run lost energy (top speed 9 against 12.6 m/s, splash above 2 m at frame 74 0.42% against the engine 1.74%). title: GPU FLIP whitewater simulation: spray, foam and bubbles always refilling, matched to the engine, solver-agnostic
description:
Sub-epic 6 of the GPU FLIP end game (docs/GPU_FLIP_END_GAME_DESIGN.md section 3). Reused from the whitewater epic, now a child of BUG-l2h3 (GPU FLIP end game).

The emitter, lifecycle and pool on the particle-frame seam. Drawing lives in the Rendering sub-epic. The FLIP Fluids engine (Ihmsen 2012 diffuse particles as the engine runs them) is the bar. Peter waived the side-by-side against surf and his exports on 2026-10-07 ("no need for this"), which settles call 1 of GPU_WHITEWATER_DESIGN.md section 8.

End state on stage: spray, foam and bubbles are always refilling, match the engine's emitters and lifecycle, and feel wind and solids.

Original charter, kept below.

Peter, 2026-09-30: the GPU water must beat the FLIP Fluids engine it replaces, and whitewater is a large part of that look (reference exports: ~/Downloads/waterExportTestVert80Res.mp4, waterBoxTest64.mp4). Today whitewater is generated only by the vendored FLIP Fluids CPU engine (crates/manifold-fluids/native/flip_engine/diffuseparticlesimulation.cpp). SWASH (FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN.md) plans none; GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md P6 plans whitewater atoms for MPM only; GPU_FLUID_SURFACE_DESIGN.md P8 only routes FLIP-generated whitewater. Work: one design for GPU whitewater atoms that read the particle-frame seam (positions, velocities) plus the surface level set, porting FLIP Fluids diffuse model (wavecrest + turbulence + energy emission potentials, spray/foam/bubble classification, ballistic spray, advected foam/bubbles with buoyancy, lifetimes), so SWASH, MPM and FLIP feed the same generator. Gate: side by side with the FLIP Fluids engine on the same particles, Peter judges. Supersedes the MPM-only P6 whitewater plan.
notes:
Inventory measured 2026-09-30 (CPU FLIP, res 64 Dam Break, 343k particles; the full report is in the lead session transcript). Look ranking by pixels changed: renderer scattering 7%, volume path length 6.5%, subdivision 6%, mesh smoothing 4%, whitewater 1.3–2.3% (local, high contrast; almost all foam from wavecrest emission), absorption tint 1%. Bubbles ≤0.23%, spray ≤0.09%, turbulence emission inert at rate 175. Cost: whitewater 42–55 ms/tick, of which ~92% is the emitter scan over all liquid particles (serial classification ~12, turbulence ~11, inside emitters ~6, surface emitters ~4) plus a 10–14 ms curvature grid; the whitewater particles own lifecycle is ~1 ms. Plan: port the emitter scan (wavecrest + energy potentials, emission count, jitter, type split) to GPU atoms fed by the solver velocity field and liquid SDF; keep the lifecycle (advection, buoyancy/drag, collisions, lifetime, removal) as the unchanged FLIP C++ fed through shared memory (needs a MAC velocity grid: SWASH has one; the liquid SDF must come from the GPU). Drop turbulence emission unless recalibrated. Traps: emission rounds per emitter per substep, so amount depends on dt and needs recalibration; there is no bit-exact oracle, so oracles are statistical (counts over time, spatial histograms). Renderer optics, instancing and materials are already solver-agnostic.
Design 2026-09-30: docs/GPU_WHITEWATER_DESIGN.md on feat/gpu-whitewater, PROPOSED, six phases (P1 is the liquid seam P10 grid outputs). Awaiting approval before P1.

title: Gatekeeper first-run scan starves cargo builds: find why checks degrade 0.4s to 25s, cut fresh-binary count
description: macOS Gatekeeper first-run scan (syspolicyd + XprotectService) serializes every freshly built binary: build scripts, nextest test binaries, hello-world alike. Normal cost 0.4s/file; on 2026-09-29 evening it degraded to ~25s/file with 3 cargo sessions building fresh worktrees (565 build-script scans + ~50 test binaries in 70 min), so cargo run --release sat at "manifold-renderer(build)" for minutes with the build script parked at _dyld_start. Same starvation hit the nightly trunk_health run 05:00-07:00 (90s medians). Diagnostic signature: process 0% CPU, ~80KB RSS, sample shows only _dyld_start. Fix: add Terminal (and the Codex app) to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Developer Tools so binaries launched from them skip assessment; document in docs/DEVELOPMENT_REFERENCE.md and guide_debugging_doctrine memory. Peter rebooted to clear it.
notes:
2026-09-29 after a machine restart: syspolicyd at 56-73% CPU doing per-binary notarization lookups plus XProtect scans; fresh build scripts in slot-9, slot-1 and main sat in _dyld_start at 0% CPU for 5-7 min, and a scratchpad python script waited ~3 min. The queue drains slowly; kill-and-retry does not help because the relinked binary re-enters the queue.

2026-09-30: the terminal here is Ghostty, not Terminal.app, so the Developer Tools entry to add is Ghostty (plus the Codex app). spctl developer-mode enable-terminal only adds Terminal.app, so it does not cover this setup. Unverified: whether a tmux server started from Ghostty inherits the exemption, and whether launchd-started nightly jobs can be covered at all.

2026-09-30 Peter: no Developer Tools exemption, not for Ghostty and not for a cargo-only launcher app. Fix shape is now (1) find the root cause of the 60x slowdown (watch syspolicyd logs during a fresh worktree build: network notarization lookups? cold cache after reboot? concurrency?), and (2) cut how many never-seen binaries a build makes: fold 52 test binaries into a few, and check whether byte-identical rebuilds (sccache across slots) skip the rescan.

2026-09-30: slot acquire already picks the warmest slot, but enforce_target_cap wipes a slot's whole cache once it passes 25G, which turns the next build into ~500 fresh build scripts. The 25G cap may be what makes cold builds common. Check before designing a cold-build queue.

2026-09-30 (later): the 25G-cap-forces-cold-builds theory is wrong. The cap almost never deletes anything (see the storage_budget recognition bead). Cold builds last night came from fresh slots instead (slot-3, slot-9 show cold).

title: Implement two-way FLIP and Box3D coupling with a numerical feasibility gate
description:
Include two-way FLIP/Box3D interaction in the active slot-9 workstream through manifold-physics, existing collision proxies and native solvers. No landing or public push is authorized.

Verified foundations: mass-aware native pressure PCG/preconditioning (4b36ff307), actual mesh boundary interpolation/transpose (f8a835c2c), generic BodyDynamics/BodyImpulse API and prescribed viscous stress capture (6014327d4). Delayed viscous feedback was rejected by an eight-case energy test (58bd9d506), especially for light bodies/high viscosity.

Checkpoint 9d5b02dab adds joint viscosity, which extends the same native PCG with normalized body velocity changes, full world inertia, shared strain cross terms and the exact body diagonal. The ordinary fluid matrix remains native. A two-body independent physical-mass oracle gives solution error 2.48e-7 and reaction/response error 5.74e-7, zero measured symmetry/diagonal mismatch, and passive energy ratio 0.780411. Thirty-three frozen-geometry native cases cover translation/rotation, density ratios 0.1/1/10, viscosity 1/10 m2/s, dt 1/60 and 1/120, and a varying boundary constraint derivative. Maximum energy ratio is 0.949469, body response mismatch 6.42e-6 and transpose mismatch 5.36e-14. Fixed mobility exactly preserves the original solve. Eight cases put a planar free surface through or just above a light translating/rotating body; their maximum energy ratio is 0.168593 using independently calculated staggered liquid volume. Failed, invalid and empty captures are checked; the coupled path rejects the ordinary loose iteration-limit fallback. Twelve coupling tests and two ordinary native regressions pass.

Production native integration now passes five short CPU tests using real rotated Box3D hulls. Owner-driven FLIP substeps accept full body snapshots, use physical density and combined viscosity/pressure, and expose linear/angular impulses plus solved changes. Across three frames at density ratios 0.1/1/10 and kinematic viscosity 0/1, immediate Box3D response mismatch is at most 1.77e-7 (limit 5e-5). Empty/disabled recipients, prescribed density scaling, invalid tensors, stale output, pending-offer mutation and abandonment are covered. Box3D advances geometry after each reaction; this is not sustained moving/floating acceptance.

Remaining: qualify sustained moving geometry/advection, floating equilibrium and contact alignment; connect existing app owners at shared substeps and coherent accepted poses; author physical density through existing params; verify stale/duplicate epoch handling and replay/export. Prepared native storage currently uses conservative O(grid faces x bound bodies) capacities and requires memory/cost qualification before dense multi-body production use. No user tuning knobs or silent degradation.

P8b in docs/FLUID_ENGINE_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md remains authoritative. Reuse existing native PCG. A substantial underlying solver replacement requires the scope discussion Peter requested. No heuristic buoyancy/drag, arbitrary damping/caps or altered authored mass to conceal instability.
acceptance_criteria: P8b numerical gates establish physical reaction units, buoyancy, angular exchange, viscous response and stable coherent stepping; otherwise record evidence for the requested separate-solver scope discussion. title: Handle long physics input gaps with bounded catch-up and clear recovery
description:
Observed on slot-9 while running physics_boxes_render_motion_and_latch_count_until_reset: a preview jump from frame 185 to 600 at 60 Hz generates over 1,600 authored samples before either solver can drain them. RigidSimulation retains 256 samples, while sample_physics_history samples at 240 Hz. The history correctly latches exhaustion, preserves accepted state and reports reset required, but this leaves only about one second of unconsumed input and floods the graph error log on a longer jump.

Improve the live/offline scheduling and visible recovery contract without dropping unread input, silently changing quality, or increasing unbounded work/memory. Keep the explicit overflow safety. P5/P9 should determine whether to chunk deterministic offline catch-up and retain/spool live take input independently of the render observer. Confirm pause/seek/reset semantics and show the affected simulation status.

title: Refine Blob detection visuals, responsiveness and group masks
description:
Initial bounded diagnosis, 2026-09-24. Peter wants useful visual attention/tracking and selective effects via group masks. Initial checks only were authorized; no app implementation changed.

Evidence: compiled pre-decomposition V1 native source at d192ee19cd4efe67e63ac14c6222b79f52a26f71 and current native source at ca2d2393c50e6efffce51076df2c79e4ff3ee377 against the same Homebrew OpenCV 4.13.0. Compared native calls on 50 frames at 25 fps from each supplied clip (people 5-7s; liquid 14-16s; TV 2-4s) and two controlled moving-shape/polarity sequences. V1 defaults threshold=.65/sensitivity=.85; current V1 additionally applies the authored area/aspect/size filter. V2 brightness preparation is CPU-mirrored Rec.709 luma and separable radius-1 denoise at longest dimension 320. Both decoded RGB and sRGB-linearized RGB were checked because this bypasses the app's video colour path. Results are detector probes, NOT a historical app playback comparison, tracking smoothness proof, or GPU mask equivalence proof. Original V1 analysis dimensions are normalized to the same dimensions for this comparison. Colour/motion variants, actual bundled generators, playback latency, full HUD, group wet/dry and identity continuity were not exercised. Initial attempt mixing bundled/current and Homebrew/old libraries failed with duplicate OpenMP before results; isolated builds resolved it without bypassing runtime protection.

Measured: liquid old V1 had 3-7 detections and zero empty frames in decoded RGB; current V1 had 0-5 and 13/50 empty. Linearized check preserved direction: old 3-6/zero empty; current 0-5/10 empty. This supports a detection regression candidate, not universal old-version superiority. People: old decoded RGB empty in all 50, linearized one region each; current empty 17/50 decoded or 14/50 linearized. V2 brightness selected 1-2 broad regions; decoded-RGB contact sheets show sky coverage, not people. TV: old V1 and V2 both detected two regions throughout both input encodings; current output was more variable, strongly encoding-dependent. Controlled bright rectangle: all detect except the deliberate gap. Dark rectangle on white: both V1s detect; V2 brightness returns zero because the connected white background exceeds max area. Post-detection mask Invert cannot turn this into detecting the dark shape.

title: Coincident optional array pre-reads unguarded — short wired weights reads OOB (standalone + fused)
description: Coincident array input pre-reads are eager and unguarded: standalone.rs:673 (let e_<port> = buf_<port>[idx];) and fused_buffer.rs:558 (let e_<e> = src_<e>[idx];) read at every dispatched idx. For OPTIONAL inputs (the deformer family weights planes) dispatch is bounded by required inputs only — a wired-but-short weights buffer (weights_len < count, which run() explicitly tolerates with a warning) reads out of bounds where the body gate idx < weights_len would have discarded the value. Metal storage OOB is the AGX page-fault/hang class (BUG-84fv (gpu hang hard lockup) history). Pre-existing for most of the optional-weights family (they declared Coincident all along); 7c9b76e6b extended it to mesh_spatial_mask (gather to coincident). Unwired is safe: standalone binds the count-sized src as dummy, fused threads a zero literal. Fix shape: clamp optional coincident pre-reads — select(zero, buf[min(idx, len-1)], len > 0) — gated on the port being optional so required-input kernels keep byte-identical WGSL. Add a GPU proof wiring a deliberately short weights plane.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Guard optional-array pre-reads and add standalone and fused regression coverage. title: Unwired frame-time input that is also a declared param breaks fused derived-uniform marker accounting (BUG-e3p6.4 follow-up)
description: When a frame_time_input is ALSO a declared param (node.ripple_mesh time), the fused buffer codegen emits n0_time in the Params struct at its PARAM position (fused_buffer.rs skips re-emitting it in the derived block to avoid a duplicate field), but emit_derived_uniform_markers computes the marker word count from effective_derived = [weights_len, time] — so the marker claims 2 words starting at n0_weights_len, covering n0_weights_len + n1_weights_len, and NOTHING refreshes n0_time (the generic pack writes the seeded param default 0). Symptom: fused ripple with unwired time renders the undisplaced mesh (proven while authoring rt_dynamic_fusion: fused y == input y). The rt_dynamic_fusion proof wires time from a value node (the documented beat-ramp pattern) to stay clear. Fix shape: make the marker/struct accounting agree — either emit frame-time params only in the derived block, or make the marker cover the actual contiguous emitted fields and have the generic pack apply the frame-clock fallback for unwired frame-time param fields.
notes:
2026-09-17 k3 review note: corner is PRE-EXISTING (noise_displace/glitch_jitter had [time]-only recomputes against 2-word [weights_len, time] blocks before 7c9b76e6b — has_recompute was already true, so they could already fuse into it). 7c9b76e6b did not widen exposure; their array_ports are empty so no mapping is emitted. Fix remains the marker/struct accounting agreement.
Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Repair fused derived-uniform marker accounting for dual time and parameter inputs and add parity coverage. title: Audit GPU-produced inputs consumed by CPU array_math
description: Static finding during wave-pilot audit at f925a1277: primitives/array_math.rs run() reads shared input buffers via mapped_ptr on the CPU and writes at most 4096 elements. Existing graph vocabulary also produces arrays on GPU (for example split_xy and noise fields). No same-frame fence is visible in ArrayMath. Runtime corruption has NOT been reproduced in this task. Audit actual scheduling/readback and affected consumers before diagnosis; pilot deliberately keeps its entire array chain on GPU. Do not broaden wave pilot into this fix.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: ASTRA RULING (via codex-rescue pipe, verbatim): timestep-halving escalation RESOLVED. (1) Run t=0.1s pre-slosh refinement probe FIRST: coarse/fine >= 1.5 = chaotic growth confirmed; < 1.2 with fine > 1e-4 m = dt-scaling defect (suspects: stress momentum dt factor, gravity, advection), hard fail + escalate; grey 1.2-1.5 = rerun at 0.05s by trend. (3) S4 ACCEPTED with gate open conditional on probe resolving before S7; S5/S7 proceed; c0=20 deferred to Peter at S7, do not entangle. Also: fix wrong ratio-interpretation comment at water_solver.rs:1174 (ratio~1 post-Lyapunov is CORRECT, defect oracle only pre-slosh). Observation: ~0.35 m/s slosh at 2s plausible at mu=0.001 free-slip; if it fails the KE decay envelope, surface to Peter, don't tune.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: SUPERSESSION — the earlier 'ASTRA RULING' comment came through the codex-rescue pipe and was NOT Astra (Peter confirmed). Real Astra ruling 2026-09-09: (1) run ONE bounded matched 0.1s three-timestep probe (96/192/384 substeps), record position RMS/max, density diffs, KE, max density-dependent acoustic CFL; (2) NO ratio thresholds — a refinement ratio proves neither chaos nor defect outside an asymptotic regime; (3) if refinement fails early, inspect first divergence (stress/gravity/advection dt-scaling AND fixed-point stress-rounding at small dt AND transfer-count dissipation) before any solver/parameter change; (4) S4 implemented but NOT accepted, gate open; S5 provisional mechanical; S7 gated on S6 + this investigation, no realism sign-off yet; the 31% density delta needs precise definition/explanation before any bulk-metric acceptance; KE-decay-to-25% unjustified for low-viscosity free-slip. c0=10 and Q=2^20 unchanged. Lane constraint verbatim: run the matched 0.1s three-timestep probe without tuning, report absolute errors and acoustic CFL without classifying chaos from a ratio, return evidence to the lead before changing acceptance criteria or solver parameters.

title: scene-loop-seam-cut-under-live-param-modulation
description: Scene Loop seam cuts when card params are modulated by non-phase sources. Math: wrap purity compares the phase-0 frame against the phase-1 frame one loop apart; any scene-visible param whose value differs across that boundary produces a hard cut. One-shot live rides cost exactly one cut then settle (both sides agree after the wrap); continuous beat-driven modulation (LFO/envelope on Jitter, Spacing, etc.) cuts EVERY wrap — the D8 aperiodic-driver class. Built-in movement controls (sway/look/zoom/flow) are phase-periodic with integer cycles so they never cut. Product gap: nothing warns when a non-phase modulation binds to a loop row. Options: (a) binding-time warning, (b) phase-periodic envelope support for loop rows, (c) document as performer knowledge. Raised by Peter 2026-09-06 while diagnosing Stone Effects wrap hitches (see also scene-loop-far-edge-hole-fog-default and BUG-jvlq).

title: Design the remaining closed-loop 3D scene feedback seam
description:
Extension direction from Peter 2026-09-05 on top of Scene Loop: "3D scene stylised feedback... 3D scene mirrors, twists, pulses, explosions, steps."

Survey: SCENE_FX_DESIGN shipped P0-P4 2026-08-22 — mesh deformers (bend/twist/taper/morph/shatter/ripple/melt/voxelize/noise_displace/glitch_jitter), the per-object modifier rack in the scene panel, and Skin Video (a layer output bound into another layer scene graph as a texture). Twist/explosion/step aesthetics are therefore one rack-add away on looped scenes.

Genuinely new:
1. Closed-loop 3D feedback — the scene previous-frame render re-bound into the same scene (trails/echoes in world space). render_scene is Terminal so its output is not consumable. Two-layer workaround exists today (layer A renders the scene, layer B skins A output onto the same model via Skin Video = world-space video feedback with one extra frame of latency). The real version needs render_scene output exposed as a texture plus one-frame feedback loop handling (SCENE_FX D5 already allows previous-frame reads for layer skins).
2. True scene-space planar mirror — fold_mesh mirrors one mesh across a plane; a mirrored-room reflection (reflect the whole scene, second render pass) does not exist.

Placement decision (Peter, 2026-09-05): deformers stay in the per-object rack (Scene Setup, object-level Add Modifier) — they are object properties, and on a looped scene a deformer on the object already hits every copy via scene_array instancing; duplicating them as clip-level modifier cards would create a second home for the same control. Scene Mirror and Scene Feedback are genuinely scene-wide: new modifier kinds in the + Add Modifier menu (today: Scene Loop, Scene Fog) — each is a descriptor + plan builder + trace signature, zero new UI.

Note: deformer animation on a looping camera must stay phase-driven (beat_ramp) or the visual loop seams even when the camera path wraps pure (INV-3).

title: jitter-seam-visual-seamlessness-call
description: SCENE_MODIFIER_FRAMEWORK P4 escalation, Peter call: per-instance jitter makes the loop seam swap the nearest copy orientation — position-continuous and deterministic, exact-seam pixel gate stays 0, but the near-seam (phase 0.99999) pixel diff measures 113 with jitter live vs 0 without. A constant-per-index hash (the only way to zero the near-seam) is no jitter at all. Options if the seam ever reads visibly with jitter live: (a) accept — the wrap is beat-locked and the swap lands exactly on the downbeat, arguably musical; (b) window the jitter amount by sin(pi*phase) so copies are identical at the seam and maximally varied mid-loop (loses the static-corridor feel, adds a breathing quality); (c) key jitter on (idx mod window) so the seam sees identical orientations at the cost of a periodic corridor. The P4 lane did NOT build any of these. Deferred until Peter sees it live on the sakura.

title: flow-gate incremental marker misses flows whose driven surface is deleted without a path overlap
description: Symptom: on the SCENE_MODIFIER_FRAMEWORK P3 lane (lane/scene-modifier-p3), deleting the Scene Setup panel Scene Loop section (scene_setup_loop.rs + the SceneSelection::SceneLoop outliner row) regressed four gltfscene flows — scene-setup-light-intensity-drag, scene-setup-shadow-softness-dropdown, scene-card-convergence-c-p1d-light-scrub-drawer, scene-setup-modifier-stack — but scripts/run_ui_flows.py --touched <range> (the landing gate's incremental pass) did NOT re-run any of them on the deleting HEAD, so the breakage only surfaced in the full flow gate. Fix shape (named, not executed here): make the incremental pass conservative on deletions — any deleted .rs path under crates/manifold-ui/src/panels/ (or any path whose removal shrinks a panel layout) widens the re-run set to every flow mapped to scenes that panel builds, or simpler: a deleted file re-runs the full manifest for its former path_triggers prefixes' scenes. P3's four regressed flows were re-calibrated in the P3 fixup commit; this bead is the gate hole itself.

title: LED blend dispatch sized by compositor, not LED target — partial black LED composite
description:
Found by the BUG-2ptv (LED output dead) oracle-test lane. Symptom: with a 64x64 compositor and 8x120 LED grid, blend_layers_to_led leaves rows 64..119 of led_main black (448/960 pixels), while the screen composite is correct.

Root cause: BlendResources caches compositor width/height at construction (crates/manifold-renderer/src/layer_compositor.rs ~line 68-70, dispatch at ~line 149) and always dispatches that many workgroups. The blend shader guards on textureDimensions(t_base) (generators/shaders/compositor_blend_compute.wgsl line 24-26), so threads beyond the compositor-sized dispatch never run for the LED-sized base. In production (fullscreen compositor >= LED grid in both dims) the dispatch covers the LED target, which is why the rig path looks alive — but any config where the LED grid is taller/wider than the compositor output (small window, headless/test, tall LED walls) silently blacks the overflow region. Same class applies to any future cross-size blend_pass user.

Fix shape: dispatch from the target (or base) texture dims per call — e.g. blend_pass takes explicit dispatch dims, or reads dims from the bound textures via a small uniform/push constant. Root fix, not a LED-only special case.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Size LED blend dimensions by the target and add a compositor regression. title: RT glitches when FPS target is missed (temporal path vs dropped frames)
description: Symptom (Peter, live app, helmetGlitches.manifold): with RT on and the helmet rotating, bright flash/"glitch" frames appear; capping FPS to 30 makes them stop. Correlates with MISSING the FPS target, not motion speed — at 30fps the per-frame rotation step is larger yet clean. Headless rt-capture (--frame-clock, every frame on time) cannot reproduce it: 240-frame RT-on vs RT-off A/B shows identical flash statistics, so the artifact lives in the missed-deadline path. Suspects: (a) temporal accumulation/history-rejection logic reacting to irregular frame times or catch-up ticks, (b) the async accel refit stale-trace window (BUG-320 latch) interacting with dropped frames. Fix shape: audit the RT temporal path for assumptions of uniform dt (accumulate weight, reset detector, refit scheduling) and make behavior deadline-miss-safe. Note: this bug class is invisible to frame-clocked harnesses — the RT gate needs a deadline-miss mode or live soak to cover it.

title: MetalFX scaler dropped synchronously on generator rebuild — residency hazard
description: Found by pro-freeze-audit during the BUG-84fv audit. MetalFX Temporal Scaler internals (history textures created by the framework at newTemporalScalerWithDevice) never pass through our encoder, so no useResource covers them; when install_layer_generator drops an old PresetRuntime (forced-outputs rebuild, watched flip, relight toggle, type swap) the scaler ObjC object deallocs synchronously while a prior-frame Generators command buffer may still be executing. If MetalFX does not internally declare usage, the driver can reclaim the history textures mid-flight — the BUG-jddy residency class in a black box. Rule-out for the 2026-08-02 incident: every drop path has a logged prerequisite or needs user action; the log was quiet for 58s before the hang, so this is a LATENT hazard, not that nights cause. Also in scope: pool-cycled textures handed to the scaler via setColorTexture/setOutputTexture carry the same gap. FIX SHAPE: defer the scaler drop until the frames fence signals completion (retire list keyed to the shared-event value), same contract the texture pool documents but for opaque ObjC resources.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Define a fence-safe MetalFX scaler lifetime and prove generator rebuilds do not release history resources before command completion. title: Scene camera orbit/tilt card params do not match the in-app camera convention
description: Peter reported a view of tests/fixtures/gltf/khronos/NormalTangentMirrorTest.glb at orbit -273, tilt 17, distance 3.98, FOV 34, and the plate faces the camera in his screenshots. Stamping those exact values onto the imported scenes camera card params (5_orbit, 5_tilt, 5_distance, 5_fov_y) in a headless gpu-proofs harness renders the plate almost edge-on instead: non-black fraction 0.0006, essentially an empty frame, vs 0.0883 at the import default camera with the same lighting. Consequence: a camera pose read off the app UI cannot be reproduced headlessly, which makes any bug report that depends on framing hard to reproduce in a test - that is how it was found. Root cause unknown. Suspects: degrees-vs-radians on one side of the boundary, orbit sign or zero-azimuth reference direction, or the glTF Y-up import rotation being applied after the orbit. Fix shape: find the single conversion point between the camera UI readout and the camera card param and make one of them authoritative, then add a round-trip test that a pose set through the UI path reproduces the same view matrix headlessly. Not chased further on the lane that found it, by direction.

comments.text:
## BUG-ukg R2 Specular Accumulation — Design Synthesis Report

### What R1 Built (3 sentences)

R1 traced reflection rays in the existing `trace_shadow_rays` kernel, writing raw per-frame samples to `out_refl` (Rgba16Float: rgb=radiance, a=hit_distance), then substituted the prefiltered env sample in `fs_pbr` (`render_scene.wgsl:1513-1541`) with `rt_reflection` when `rt_enabled && rt_reflections` (binding 43). The raw signal rode the irradiance pipeline (half-res trace → upsample → à-trous → accumulate) but **accumulation was pass-through only** — no temporal history, no reprojection, so every frame was 1-spp noise. Key anchors: kernel block at `raytrace.rs:1040-1116`, WGSL substitution at `render_scene.wgsl:1513-1541` (including anisotropic branch), `GiMaterial::metallic_roughness` populated at `render_scene.rs:3976`.

### What Section 9 Specifies for R2 That Is NOT Yet Built

**R2 is already LANDED** (2026-07-26). The design doc section 9.6 records the full shipped implementation. The epic title "stable reflections R2 — specular accumulation" refers to work that **already exists** in main. From the section 9.6 phase record:

- **R2 Step 1** (inert plumbing): `rt_refl_history` ping-pong pair added alongside irradiance history, wired to the same reset detector (I-R2).
- **R2 Step 2** (virtual-hit reprojection): `accumulate_irradiance` reprojects through `world_pos + hit_dist * R` (the VIRTUAL image mirror point), lerping to surface reprojection as roughness rises via `RT_REFL_VIRTUAL_REPROJ_ROUGHNESS_BLEND`.
- **R2 variance clamp** (BUG-dx6w, 2026-07-29): `clamp_refl_history` clips reprojected specular history to mean ± RT_REFL_CLAMP_GAMMA·stddev of current frame's 3x3 neighborhood before the blend, killing D-61's camera-sweep trails (tone-mapped variance in BUG-axe9).
- **D-64 motion scaling** (2026-07-30): `cam_motion` scalar widens the reflection change gate band (`motion_band = 1 + 60*cam_motion`), and specular history carries a motion-scaled alpha floor `min(cam_motion*5, 0.9)` because specular is view-dependent. Specular taps at `bt=1` (rough surface reprojection) now take the same depth test the diffuse channel passes.

**Everything section 9.6 specified for R2 is shipped**, including the variance clamp and motion gate fixes that came after the initial landing. The bug report's "R2" framing is accurate to the design, but the work is done.

### Current RT Accumulation Path (File:Line Anchors)

**Accumulation kernel**: `crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/raytrace.rs:1935-2700` (`accumulate_irradiance`)
- **Specular history reprojection**: lines 2485-2565 — reads `history[ping].rgb`, reprojects through virtual hit point `wp + hit_dist*R`, applies variance clamp `clamp_refl_history`, blends at `alpha = max(min(cam_motion*5, 0.9), refl_samples / (refl_samples + 1))`
- **Validity test**: lines 2510-2540 — depth test for `bt=1` (rough surface reprojection), normal test only for glossy (`bt<1`), fallback to current frame on rejection
- **Motion gate**: line 2612 — `motion_band = 1.0 + cam_motion * RT_MOTION_GATE_SCALE` scales the reflection change gate
- **Running mean**: line 2567 — `refl_samples = history.a` carries the per-texel sample count

**Temporally-accumulated channels** (all ride the same pipeline):
- **Irradiance**: `rt_irr_history` ping-pong (lines 905-906 in render_scene.rs) — diffuse AO+GI, accumulated via running mean `1/n` with alpha floor
- **Specular**: `rt_refl_history` ping-pong (lines 908-909) — reflection radiance, accumulated via running mean with variance clamp
- **Shadow-visibility**: `rt_sv_history` / `rt_sv_m1_history` / `rt_sv_m2_history` (lines 911, 917-918) — SVGF temporal accumulation with moments
- **Snap-hold counter**: `rt_sv_hold_history` (lines 922) — the SV-ACCUM snap countdown for BUG-sz0u's motion-leg gate

**Upsample/filter**: `atrous_filter` (`raytrace.rs:1107-1800`) — edge-stopping weights that narrow with roughness for specular

### rt_noise_gate Channels — What R2 Must Keep Green

**Static stability leg** (baseline: `scripts/rt_noise_baseline.json`):
- `composite` (mean 0.0768, p999 6.0) — final RT output
- `irr_full` (mean 4.675, p999 142.0) — diffuse irradiance channel
- `refl_history_read` / `refl_history_write` (mean 0.1445, p999 12.8) — specular history input/output
- `refl_raw` (mean 0.6371, p999 30.6) — raw per-frame reflection samples before accumulation
- `mask` / `mask_half` (shadow visibility channels)
- `moments` (SVGF m1/m2 temporal variance)

**Motion leg** (D-64 / BUG-sz0u):
- `sv_hold_median` ceiling 0.0263 — snap-hold counter for SV gate under motion
- `moments_center_min` floor 0.0003 — SVGF moments at frame center
- `history_ratio_min` ceiling 0.1425 — ratio of accumulated vs current-frame signal

Any specular-accumulation change must re-baseline with `--record` OR pass existing ceilings. The gate measures **per-pixel |delta| between consecutive frames on a static scene**; a dead channel (zero motion) fails as inert rather than passing.

### Risks — Where Specular Accumulation Touches Motion Leg and Rebuild Churn

**Motion leg interaction (BUG-sz0u coverage)**:
- Specular accumulation's `motion_band` scaling (line 2612) is the SAME mechanism that widens the SV gate (D-64 addendum). The fix correctly scaled both gates; any regression here would re-break the SV gate's motion-leg coverage.
- The variance clamp `clamp_refl_history` (BUG-dx6w) is what killed D-61's sweep trails — if a regression weakens it, Peter's camera-sweep verdict returns.
- Specular's motion-scaled alpha floor `min(cam_motion*5, 0.9)` (line 2626) is SPECIFIC to reflections because they're view-dependent. Irradiance doesn't have this. A wrong value breaks motion stability or kills convergence.

**Rebuild churn interaction (BUG-665r rebuild loop)**:
- Specular history is cleared on RT accel rebuild (section 10 contract: "On invalidation: seed, don't clear" — but a rebuild IS invalidation). If rebuilds churn every frame (BUG-665r class), specular accumulation never converges and the image stays at raw 1-spp noise.
- The `rt_accel_topo_key` + content-settle key split (BUG-320) is what prevents rebuild churn on deforming meshes. If that split regresses, specular history resets every frame on animated objects.
- The `vertices_generation` tracking (line 820-825) is what distinguishes a topology-only change (refit) from a content change (rebuild). A stale generation causes a blind accel — all rays miss → reflections read env-only ≈ no RT.

### Contradictions Between Section 9 Spec and As-Built Code

**No contradictions found.** R2 shipped exactly as specified:
- RD6 virtual-hit reprojection is implemented (`wp + hit_dist*R`, line 2495)
- Roughness blend `RT_REFL_VIRTUAL_REPROJ_ROUGHNESS_BLEND` is live (line 2503)
- Variance clamp `clamp_refl_history` is in place (line 2467) with tone-mapping (BUG-axe9)
- Motion gate scaling `motion_band` is wired (line 2612)
- Depth test for `bt=1` specular taps (line 2535)
- Motion-scaled alpha floor (line 2626)

The only gap is the **deferred shading-normal prepass** (section 9.7), which was intentionally deferred and then replaced by in-kernel normal-map sampling (BUG-wytp). That's a design evolution, not a contradiction.

### Staged Implementation Plan (For Future RT Work, Not R2)

Since R2 is already shipped, this plan is for **hypothetical future work** on RT reflections (e.g., if a new reflection feature is proposed):

**Stage 1 — Fix regressions first (smallest visible stability improvement)**
- Files touched: `crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/raytrace.rs` (~50 lines), `render_scene.rs` (~20 lines)
- Oracle: `scripts/rt_noise_gate.py` static + motion legs must pass existing ceilings
- Re-baseline: NO — any regression should fail the existing gate
- Risk: Low — only touches accumulation logic

**Stage 2 — Add new reflection feature (e.g., multi-bounce specular)**
- Files touched: `raytrace.rs` kernel (~100 lines), `render_scene.rs` bindings (~30 lines), WGSL substitution (~10 lines)
- Oracle: New GPU value test (`tests/gpu_proofs/rt_*.rs`) + `rt_noise_gate` must still pass
- Re-baseline: YES (`--record`) if new channel or noise floor changes
- Risk: Medium — touches the hot path, may destabilize existing gates

**Stage 3 — Perf optimization (e.g., reflection-specific resolution)**
- Files touched: `render_scene.rs` trace dispatch logic (~50 lines), possibly new texture targets
- Oracle: `trace_ms` delta report + visual PNG pair (Peter's L2 look)
- Re-baseline: Likely YES if noise characteristics change
- Risk: High — resolution changes re-baseline EVERYTHING

### Summary

R2 specular accumulation is **already complete and shipped**. The design doc section 9.6 accurately records the landed implementation, including post-landing fixes (variance clamp, motion gate). The BUG-ukg epic title suggests work to be done, but the code matches the spec. If there's a specific symptom Peter is seeing (e.g., "reflections still smear under X condition"), that's a NEW bug, not an R2 implementation gap. The next step is Peter's L2 verdict on the shipped R2 behavior.

title: BUG-227 — madmom-onset-detector-not-gain-or-timestretch-invariant-on-real-mixes
description:
### BUG-227 (madmom-onset-detector-not-gain-or-timestretch-invariant-on-real-mixes) — the current onset detector (madmom CNN, pre-P2/P6) fails two of the three P1 metamorphic invariant checks on real babyslakh mixes — found 2026-07-17, AUDIO_ANALYSIS_ACCURACY_DESIGN.md P1, by the eval harness's own metamorphic suite (`eval/metamorphic.py`) run against real audio for the first time
**Status:** OPEN — MED (accuracy, not correctness — the pipeline still runs; but it means onset timing/counts are measurably gain- and tempo-sensitive on real polyphonic material, which the P1 gate literally asks the metamorphic suite to rule out and it currently does not).

**Symptom:** `python -m eval.run --set dev` (scoreboard: `tools/audio_analysis/eval/scoreboard/dev_2026-07-17.json`) shows, on 3 babyslakh tracks: `noise_floor_silence` passes cleanly on all 3; `gain_invariance` fails on 2/3 (max matched onset-time shift 80-210ms under ±6dB, well past a 21ms tolerance already loosened once to absorb the detector's own 10ms frame quantization); `time_stretch_invariance` (±5%) fails on all 3 (matched-pair shift 244-250ms, alongside event-count drops of -2 to -12 out of 50-88 base events — i.e. 4-18% of onsets disappear or relocate under a 5% speed change). Diagnosed directly (not inferred): Track00001 goes from 66 detected onsets at normal speed to 54 at +5% speed, with several closely-spaced onset pairs collapsing into one detection.

**Root cause:** the madmom CNN onset activation (100fps, 10ms hop) has real per-onset sensitivity to both absolute level and playback-rate changes on dense polyphonic material — plausibly the peak-picking threshold/combine window interacting with closely-spaced onsets whose relative spacing shifts under time-stretch, or gain shifting which of two nearby candidate peaks wins. Not a harness bug: the two implementation bugs the harness itself had (a noise-floor renormalization step that defeated its own test, and an unbounded nearest-neighbor matcher that force-paired unrelated events into a fake "shift") were found and fixed in the same session — see `eval/metamorphic.py`'s `check_noise_floor_silence` and `_max_matched_time_shift`. What's left after those fixes is the finding above.

**Fix shape:** this is exactly what P4 (Precision post-processing pass, D6: rolling-median adaptive baseline + refractory windows applied to onset activations, non-causally) is designed to fix, and/or what the P2/P6 detector swaps (Beat This, SuperFlux) are expected to improve on incidentally. No action needed before P2 lands — P4's gate should re-run this exact metamorphic suite and treat "gain/time-stretch invariance now green" as evidence the precision pass is working, in addition to its named P/R/F1 gate. Escalate to Peter only if P4 lands and these still fail.

title: BUG-118 — render-scene-fog-washes-out-instead-of-depth-grading
description:
### BUG-118 (render-scene-fog-washes-out-instead-of-depth-grading) — atmosphere fog reads as uniform washout, not distance-graded haze — MED look-quality / render_scene
**Status:** DEFERRED — Peter, 2026-07-14: "I don't want bug-118 worked on." On hold at his call; no session touches it until he revives it. Prior state, kept for that day: root cause CHARACTERIZED by the V6 sweep (2026-07-13, VOLUMETRIC_LIGHT_DESIGN.md P1, numbers below); the shafts design (P1–P3) has now SHIPPED (2026-07-13), but whether it actually resolves this bug's original complaint is UNVERIFIED, not confirmed: P2/P3's own acceptance demos don't produce a visually legible light-driven sculpting effect (see that design's landing report and its status line) — no session has re-rendered the original Apricot Weather macro-scale repro scene with shafts on to confirm the milk-washout symptom is actually gone in practice. Do not mark this FIXED until that re-render happens and someone looks. **Absorbed-by: `docs/VOLUMETRIC_LIGHT_DESIGN.md` (2026-07-13, D4/P1–P3)**.
Verified-open-despite: VOLUMETRIC_LIGHT_DESIGN (shipped, but its acceptance demos never re-rendered the original Apricot Weather repro, and Peter froze this bug 2026-07-14 — the verify+mark step is done: still open by his call).

**Symptom** — `node.atmosphere` fog at even low density (0.04) washes out the whole
frame uniformly: near geometry loses contrast as much as far geometry, so fog reads
as a milk filter instead of depth. Seen live in Apricot Weather (macro scale, camera
distance ~9), 2026-07-11. Stopgap: fog card removed from the preset, density zeroed.

**Root cause (CONFIRMED by V6 measurement, 2026-07-13)** — `apply_fog` IS correctly
distance-scaled (`fog = 1-exp(-density·dist)`, `shaders/render_scene.wgsl:516-526`);
the washout isn't a math bug, it's saturation: the visible depth RANGE across a
bounded subject (a photoscanned plant a few world-units deep, viewed from ~9 units
away) is small relative to fog's characteristic decay length `1/density` (25 units
at density=0.04), so the fog fraction barely changes across the subject's near/far
extent — reading as uniform milk — even though the SAME density differentiates
strongly across a scene with a wide depth range (e.g. a ground plane extending to
the horizon).

Measured via `render-generator-preset` (a temporary scratch preset — grazing-angle
200×200 ground plane, orbit camera, one overhead Sun, `node.atmosphere` at
density 0.04 vs 0.0 — deleted after the sweep, not committed) at camera distances 9
and 30, `--size 640x360 --frames 3`:

| camDistance | wide-range near/far ratio-of-ratios (bottom-of-frame vs near-horizon band) | narrow-band ratio (two adjacent bands near the bottom of frame, ~subject-scale depth) |
|---|---|---|
| 9  | 1.1828 | near=0.9797, far=0.9689 → Δ=0.0108 (1.1%) |
| 30 | 1.2951 | near=0.9355, far=0.9102 → Δ=0.0253 (2.5%) |

The wide-range columns confirm the formula differentiates near vs far when the
depth range is large (far attenuates 15–30% more than near across the full scene).
The narrow-band columns are the diagnostic: across a subject-scale depth slice near
the camera, the attenuation delta is only 1–2.5 percentage points — exactly the
"reads as flat milk" signature Peter saw, and it gets WORSE (not better) at the
farther camDistance=30, because both near and far surfaces are then farther from
the camera (more overall fog) while their relative depth range stays the same.

**Fix shape** — not a fog-curve tweak (rejected, D4): the analytic exponential fog
is correct and stays. The fix is VOLUMETRIC_LIGHT_DESIGN's marched light shafts,
which read the scene per-light rather than as a single constant-color blend —
light-driven inscatter can sculpt depth on a bounded subject where a distance-only
fog curve saturates. P2/P3 land the march; this entry closes when Peter's look-pass
on the P2/P3 acceptance demo confirms the "milk" complaint is resolved.

title: BUG-155 — camera-rotation-params-missing-smooth-360-wrap
description:
### BUG-155 (camera-rotation-params-missing-smooth-360-wrap) — camera orbit/tilt/rotation controls don't smooth-wrap at 360 degrees, so a full rotation can't be modulated cleanly via a saw wave — MED, reported by Peter 2026-07-14
**Status:** OPEN — found not fixed 2026-07-14, reported by Peter during live-rig use.

**Symptom** — the camera orbit, tilt, and rotation params jump/discontinue at their wrap boundary instead of wrapping smoothly through 0/360 degrees. A saw-wave LFO driving a full rotation (the standard way to drive continuous spin from a modulation source) hits the seam and snaps instead of reading as continuous rotation.

**Root cause** — unknown; not investigated. Likely candidates: the param's range/wrap handling doesn't treat 0 and 360 (or -1/1 in normalized units) as identified endpoints, or downstream consumers (orbit-to-radians conversion, Euler composition) don't handle the wrap consistently across all three rotation axes — related to the BUG-096 orbit/tilt phase investigation already on the backlog.

**Fix shape** — audit each rotation param (orbit, tilt, and any other rotation axis in the camera/orbit primitives) for wrap behavior; ensure all use a consistent smooth-wrap convention (e.g. modulo into 0..360 with identified endpoints) so a saw wave bound to the param produces a continuous, seamless spin. Cross-check against BUG-096 (rotate-sliders-jump) — may share root cause or fix site.

title: BUG-263 — no-app-level-harness-for-pending-actions-gesture-paths
description:
### BUG-263 (no-app-level-harness-for-pending-actions-gesture-paths) — mapping drags (and the whole `pending_actions` loop in `app_render.rs`) are untestable end-to-end; only the `ActiveInspectorDrag::apply` mechanism has coverage
**Status:** OPEN (logged 2026-07-19, Fable; deferred by Peter — covered mechanism-level in BUG-262, harness build deferred until more gesture-lifecycle work lands).
**Severity:** MEDIUM (test-coverage gap, not a live defect) — the wiring (set/update/clear of the drag guard in the Snapshot/Changed/Commit arms) has no test that exercises the real path.
**Symptom:** a regression in the `pending_actions` mapping-drag wiring (guard set on Snapshot, updated on Changed, cleared on Commit, `commit_mapping_with_reverse` bookkeeping) would not be caught by any test; the 46-test `undo_baseline` matrix drives the inspector host, which the mapping trios bypass.
**Root cause:** the mapping drags dispatch through the `pending_actions` loop on the monolithic `Application` struct (`app_render.rs` ~1650–1830), reaching for `self.watched_reshape`, `self.mapping_target`, `self.commit_mapping_with_reverse`. No test can stand up enough of `Application` to drive that loop, and no mid-gesture `data_version` bump can be injected.
**Fix shape:** an app-level harness — construct `Application` (or a factored mapping-drag slice of it) headless with a real `EditingService` + `Project`, feed the Snapshot/Changed/Commit action sequence with an injected mid-gesture snapshot acceptance, assert one undo entry. Cheaper now that the pattern (44+2 tests) exists in `ui_bridge/inspector.rs`. Justified when the next gesture-lifecycle bug lands in this area; until then the `apply` round-trip tests (BUG-262) cover the mechanism.

title: BUG-170 — gltf-crate-missing-field-node-parse-failure
description:
### BUG-170 (gltf-crate-missing-field-node-parse-failure) — five Khronos assets fail at `gltf::import()` itself with `missing field 'node'` — a crate-level JSON-shape parse gap, not an extension-support gap
**Status:** OPEN, deferred to GLTF_ANIMATION_DESIGN.md — crate-bump pre-flight run 2026-07-16 during GLB_XFAIL_BURNDOWN_DESIGN P2, verdict: no bump exists. `cargo info gltf` confirms 1.4.1 is the latest published version on crates.io (no newer 1.x at all — `cargo update -p gltf --dry-run` correctly reports "Locking 0 packages"); this isn't a case of a fix being available and unapplied, there is nothing to bump to. Re-repro'd 2026-07-16 against the new `import_glb` slice-based parser (which still calls the crate's own `Gltf::from_slice_without_validation` + JSON deserialization) — `AnimatedColorsCube.glb` fails identically: `gltf parse failed: missing field 'node' at line 1 column 750`. The failure is in the crate's serde deserialization of the JSON itself, upstream of any validation or extension gate D1 touches, so D1's slice-based import change cannot and does not affect this bug. Per D8, the three assets (`AnimatedColorsCube.glb`, `CubeVisibility.glb`, `LightVisibility.glb`) move to `GLTF_ANIMATION_DESIGN.md`'s scope (pointer-targeted animation / `KHR_animation_pointer` / `KHR_node_visibility`) rather than staying open here — no JSON surgery attempted (forbidden move, D8). Extended 2026-07-16 during GLTF_MATERIAL_EXTENSIONS_DESIGN.md E6's deferred-3 sweep: `AnimationPointerUVs.glb` and `PotOfCoalsAnimationPointer.glb` (both `KHR_animation_pointer` assets, found in the material-extensions manifest's leftover `deferred-3` bucket, not the animation-focused sweep that found the original three) fail identically — `missing field 'node'` at a different byte offset each, same crate-level parse gap, so folded into this bug rather than filed separately. Five assets total now: `AnimatedColorsCube.glb`, `CubeVisibility.glb`, `LightVisibility.glb`, `AnimationPointerUVs.glb`, `PotOfCoalsAnimationPointer.glb`.

**Root cause (identified 2026-07-16 during GLTF_ANIMATION A1, absorbed from the duplicate BUG-200 at the 2026-07-17 dedup):** `KHR_animation_pointer` channels legally OMIT `target.node` (the pointer replaces node-targeting entirely, per the extension's own spec). The pinned `gltf-json` 1.4.1's `animation::Target` struct declares `pub node: Index<scene::Node>` with no `#[serde(default)]`, so serde hard-fails deserializing any channel target that omits it — a crate-level gap one step upstream of `import_glb`'s validation-filter trick (that trick only patches `json::Root::validate()`'s output; this failure happens at raw `serde_json` deserialize).

**Fix shape:** ownership is back in this backlog. GLTF_ANIMATION_DESIGN shipped 2026-07-17 without this (its D5 deferred `KHR_animation_pointer` property targets; A1's held-out smoke test substituted `InterpolationTest.glb` and documented the substitution) — ownership is back here. Two real options, either is scoped work, not a one-liner: (a) patch/fork the crate to make `Target::node` an `Option<Index<Node>>` with a hand-rolled `Deserialize`; or (b) pre-process the raw glb JSON, injecting a dummy `"node": 0` into any channel target carrying `extensions.KHR_animation_pointer` before `Gltf::from_slice_without_validation`, then detect and skip-report those synthetic-node channels downstream (matches the existing raw-JSON-sniff doctrine for clearcoat/sheen/iridescence, but for a structural field). Queued behind Peter's call on GLTF_ANIMATION follow-ups; crate bump ruled out (1.4.1 is the latest published).
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Handle the five Khronos assets that fail gltf::import with missing node fields and add a regression for the accepted JSON shape. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-07-25T06:09:36Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. Original scope and acceptance remain authoritative.

title: BUG-187 — meshoptcubetest-khr-mesh-quantization-unsupported
description:
### BUG-187 (meshoptcubetest-khr-mesh-quantization-unsupported) — `MeshoptCubeTest`'s glTF variant requires `KHR_mesh_quantization`, which MANIFOLD does not implement — found 2026-07-16 during GLB_CONFORMANCE_DESIGN.md G-P7 sidecar-fetch sweep
**Status:** OPEN — correctly rejected (no silent misrender), xfail'd as `xfail:BUG-187`.

**Symptom:** `render-import tests/fixtures/gltf/khronos/MeshoptCubeTest/MeshoptCubeTest.gltf` fails immediately: `extensionsRequired[..] = "KHR_mesh_quantization": unsupported extension (MANIFOLD does not import this extension)`.

**Root cause:** the asset's `extensionsRequired` list names `KHR_mesh_quantization` (normalized/quantized vertex attribute encoding — separate from `EXT_meshopt_compression`, which this same asset also uses for its buffer views and which is likewise unimplemented). `gltf_load.rs`'s extensionsRequired veto correctly identifies and rejects both as unsupported before attempting to parse geometry, working as designed (`EXT_texture_webp` was the same clean-veto path until IMPORT_ANYTHING_WAVE_DESIGN.md W1 implemented webp decoding and closed BUG-186 — that extension is no longer vetoed). No misrender risk; the asset is simply unrenderable until one or both extensions are implemented.

**Fix shape:** implement `KHR_mesh_quantization` (dequantize normalized integer attribute accessors per the extension spec — read as normalized ints, scale to float range, same accessor pipeline just with a decode step) and/or `EXT_meshopt_compression` (meshopt buffer-view decompression, a well-known open-source algorithm) in `gltf_load.rs`'s buffer/accessor resolution path. Neither is in `GLB_CONFORMANCE_DESIGN.md` D5's originally-scoped deferred-extension list (sheen/iridescence/anisotropy/volume/Draco/KTX2/meshopt IS actually named there as deferred — meshopt itself was already a known gap; `KHR_mesh_quantization` is the new addition this session's fetch surfaced). Low priority — no other manifest asset depends on either extension.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Implement KHR_mesh_quantization and/or EXT_meshopt_compression, or explicitly retain the current clean rejection in the conformance contract. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-09-01T02:24:50Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. title: BUG-203 — fluidsim2d-count-dims-display
description:
### BUG-203 (fluidsim2d-count-dims-display) — FluidSim2D: raising Particle Count dims the image instead of reading as more particles — MED
**Status:** OPEN — found 2026-07-10 (Peter screenshot session). (Renumbered from BUG-097 2026-07-17 — id collision with the archived ui-snap overlay-traversal bug, which keeps 097.)
**Symptom:** same as FluidSim3D's count-dimming (fixed 2026-07-10): more particles = same total splat light spread thinner, so the image dims.
**Root cause:** per-particle display energy normalized ~1/count (legacy design). NOTE: the 2D graph differs from 3D — `scaled_energy_calc` (Resolution Scaling id 2) computes `active_count * 4.096e-6 + 0.5` (energy apparently ∝ count?!), one `scatterEnergy` feeds the Render Density group (which is BOTH the force field and the display source), and Display gets only `intensity`/`zoom`. Read the whole graph with the probe before changing anything — the observable (dimming) contradicts the naive reading of that formula, so something else divides by count downstream.
**Fix shape:** mirror the 3D fix at the DISPLAY stage only: forces must stay count-invariant, display light should scale ~sqrt(count), anchored at the default count so the stock look is unchanged. node.math now has Sqrt (op 14). The 3D recipe: count binding → sqrt node → energy divisor, constant retuned by 1/sqrt(default_count). For 2D, if sim and display share one density, apply the sqrt slope to the display `intensity` instead of the splat energy.
**Also open (same family):** BUG-096 remainder (rotate degrees readout + slider-jump observation); param-surface dual source of truth (preset JSON params vs core generator_metadata_submissions.rs, which still lists the pre-turb_detail surface — reconcile or delete one).

title: BUG-037 — glp-first-render-stall
description:
### BUG-037 (glp-first-render-stall) — First render of a glTF scene layer stalls the content thread ~37ms (warm-up on the frame, not at load) — MED
**Status:** PARTIAL, further reduced 2026-07-14 (bug-wave lane B) — `render_scene`'s and `gltf_texture_source`'s GPU pipeline compiles (both asset-independent, fixed shader source) are prewarmed at app startup via `GeneratorRegistry::prewarm_all` (`dea66221`). BUG-146 (landed after this entry was first written, not previously cross-referenced here — supersession-sweep gap, now closed) added `prewarm_all_atom_codegen_pipelines`, sweeping all ~144 codegen-path atoms and independently cutting BlossomField's frame 0 to ~95ms. This session found and closed the next-largest remaining gap: `node.scatter_on_mesh` (a barriered multi-pass scan/reduce, exempt from the codegen path per CLAUDE.md, so BUG-146's sweep never reached its three hand-written pipelines) was still compiling `area_main`/`scan_main`/`place_main` lazily on first `run()` — confirmed the dominant remaining cost via `freeze-profile attribute BlossomField` (steady-state: `node.render_scene` 80.8%, `node.scatter_on_mesh` 15.0% of frame time). Fix: `ScatterOnMesh::prewarm_pipelines` (`crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/scatter_on_mesh.rs`), wired into `GeneratorRegistry::prewarm_all` alongside the other two. The shadow-pass pipeline (`ensure_shadow_pass`) was *already* covered by `RenderScene::prewarm_pipelines` from an earlier VOLUMETRIC_LIGHT_DESIGN P3 pass — the backlog's "remaining gap" list above was stale on that item. Fresh `MANIFOLD_RENDER_TRACE=1` frame-0 measurement on BlossomField: **95.1ms → 40.6ms**. Full chain: 308.5ms (original) → 194.5ms (P1) → 95.1ms (BUG-146) → 40.6ms (this session). Still over the 20ms bar. **Remaining gap:** `push_mesh`/`mesh_edges`/`gltf_mesh_source` were not contributors on this trace (mesh_edges isn't even in this preset's graph); the per-asset mesh/texture buffer upload (`gltf_mesh_source.rs`, `gltf_texture_source.rs`) is genuinely per-asset and already backgrounds via a spawned thread — only amortizable via an "arm before play" phase, not a startup prewarm. Test: `scatter_on_mesh::gpu_tests::prewarm_pipelines_populates_the_shared_compute_cache` (order-independent per the BUG-144 cross-test-ordering class).

**Symptom** — trace run 2026-07-06 (`meshImportTests.manifold`): the first frame after the
project's glp layer became active showed `generators=37.1ms` (RENDER_TRACE frame=421) —
one-off, distinct from the recurring BUG-035 spike. On stage this means launching a glp
clip mid-set drops ~2 frames on its first render.

**Root cause (probable, unmeasured beyond the one trace line)** — first-touch work in the
generator path: glTF texture decode hand-off / mesh buffer upload / pipeline+PSO creation
happens lazily on the first rendered frame instead of at load/schedule time. The repo
already has the machinery pattern for this class (`plugin_prewarm.rs`, generator pipeline
pre-warm at startup, pipeline archive).

**Fix shape** — pre-warm at project-load / clip-schedule time: when a glp generator clip
is loaded (or armed on a timeline), run its first-frame resource creation off the hot
path so frame 1 of the clip renders at steady-state cost. Verify with the same
MANIFOLD_RENDER_TRACE run: no >20ms frame on first clip render.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Bring first GLB render latency below the 20 ms bar or document an accepted exception while retaining lazy per-asset upload behavior. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-09-01T02:03:01Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. Original scope and acceptance remain authoritative.

title: BUG-188 — meshprimitivemodes-non-triangle-primitive-blanks-whole-object
description:
### BUG-188 (meshprimitivemodes-non-triangle-primitive-blanks-whole-object) — a mesh mixing POINTS/LINES/LINE_STRIP/LINE_LOOP/TRIANGLE_STRIP/TRIANGLE_FAN alongside TRIANGLES renders fully black instead of drawing at least the TRIANGLES primitives — found 2026-07-16 during GLB_CONFORMANCE_DESIGN.md G-P7 sidecar-fetch sweep
**Status:** OPEN — found while wiring `MeshPrimitiveModes` (Khronos glTF-Sample-Assets) into the conformance manifest; xfail'd as `xfail:BUG-188` rather than blocking.

**Symptom:** `render-import tests/fixtures/gltf/khronos/MeshPrimitiveModes/MeshPrimitiveModes.gltf` never converges (300 frames, non-black fraction stays 0.0000 the whole time) — the object never draws anything, even though one of its seven primitives (mode 4, TRIANGLES) is fully within spec.

**Root cause:** `MeshPrimitiveModes.gltf` has one mesh with seven primitives, one per glTF primitive mode (0=POINTS .. 6=TRIANGLE_FAN), all assigned to the same (single) material. `flatten_primitive` (`gltf_load.rs:462`) returns `Err` for any primitive whose `mode() != Triangles`; `walk_gltf_node` (`gltf_load.rs:581`) propagates that `Err` with `?` from inside its per-primitive loop, so the FIRST non-Triangles primitive it iterates aborts `load_gltf_mesh` for the entire material/object — including the five/six other primitives that would have flattened fine. The asset's one true TRIANGLES primitive never gets a chance to render because a sibling primitive earlier in iteration order fails first.

**Fix shape:** two independent, composable pieces — (1) the narrower root fix: `walk_gltf_node` should not let one primitive's failure blank an entire object; catch `flatten_primitive`'s `Err` per-primitive, log/report it (e.g. into `ImportReport.report_lines`, the existing informational-gap channel `MandarinOrange`'s normal-scale note already uses), and continue accumulating the primitives that DO flatten. This alone would make `MeshPrimitiveModes` render its TRIANGLES primitive instead of nothing. (2) the broader feature gap: actually drawing POINTS/LINES/LINE_STRIP/LINE_LOOP topology needs a real point/line rendering path (not a triangle-list mesh) — out of scope for the mesh-flattening loader alone, a `render_scene`/primitive-topology design question. TRIANGLE_STRIP/TRIANGLE_FAN, by contrast, are mechanically convertible to a triangle list in `flatten_primitive` itself (standard fan/strip-to-triangles index expansion) and would be the cheapest partial win. Not attempted this session — found during a fetch-and-classify sweep, not a rendering-feature session.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Make gltf_mesh_source report per-primitive flatten failures without blanking an otherwise valid object, retaining WholeScene errors only for fatal cases. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-09-01T02:24:50Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. Original scope and acceptance remain authoritative.

title: BUG-180 — large-glb-import-oom-risk
description:
### BUG-180 (large-glb-import-oom-risk) — importing a large glTF/GLB (multi-hundred-MB, dozens of images) can get the app SIGKILLed by the OS, and intermittently succeeds/fails on the same file
**Status:** OPEN — found 2026-07-16, reported by Peter (not caused by GLTF_MATERIAL_EXTENSIONS_DESIGN E1/E2, landed the same session — confirmed the reproducing asset uses only `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`, no transmission/volume extension, so E1/E2's new code paths never activate for it).

**Symptom:** `tests/fixtures/gltf/abandoned_warehouse_-_interior_scene.glb` (114.8MB, 35 objects, 31 images) killed `cargo run --release` (bare `zsh: killed`, no panic message, no MANIFOLD-side crash log written for the event — `~/Library/Logs/com.latentspace.manifold/` had nothing newer than 2026-07-05) on one run; an immediate rerun of the identical file imported successfully (~7s) with no code changes in between. Points to a memory-headroom race rather than a deterministic bug: the import likely holds every source image fully decoded (CPU + GPU) at once with no downsampling/streaming, so it sits close enough to the machine's available memory that unrelated system load tips it into an OS-level kill.

**Also observed (same logs, same on both the failing and succeeding run, so NOT the differentiator — checked before treating it as one):** `[presets] hot-reload applied; catalog generation = 1` immediately followed by `catalog generation = 2` in the same second right after the glb import. This is the STOCK preset catalog (effects/generators) hot-reloading twice, not the glb re-importing — `[Import] Added 3D model` appears exactly once in both logs. Worth a look on its own (possibly the import triggering two filesystem-watch events), but ruled out as the cause of this crash.

**Fix shape:** cap imported texture resolution (downsample oversized source images before GPU upload — this is what lets browser glTF viewers handle the same files comfortably), and/or stream/free CPU-side image buffers as soon as each GPU upload completes instead of holding all 31 decoded images in memory simultaneously. Next: profile actual peak RSS during import of a large asset to confirm the headroom theory numerically before picking a fix, and check whether the double preset hot-reload on import is wasteful (separate, smaller fix).
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — evidence. Remaining: Profile peak RSS during a large GLB import, then cap decoded texture memory or stream/free CPU image buffers; keep duplicate preset reload as a separate follow-up. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-09-01T02:24:48Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. Original scope and acceptance remain authoritative.

title: BUG-191 — perf-soak-start-seek-first-frame-spike
description:
### BUG-191 (perf-soak-start-seek-first-frame-spike) — `cargo xtask perf-soak --start <beats>` produces a ~34-37ms content-thread frame right after the transport seeks, tripping I1 on that one frame — found 2026-07-16 during PERF_BUDGET_GATE_DESIGN.md P2, confirmed pre-existing
**Status:** PARTIAL FIX @ Lane 6, 2026-07-17 — the `node.spawn_from_image` contributor is closed (prewarmed, gated green); the dominant remaining contributors (`node.wgsl_compute` × several instances, `node.blob_tracker`) are ATTRIBUTED but not fixed — fix shape queued for next wave.

**Symptom:** `cargo xtask perf-soak "Liveschool Live Show V6 LEDS.manifold" --seconds 10 --start 400 --profile` shows a single ~52ms GPU / frame-0 spike immediately after the transport seeks to the `--start` beat, well over I1's 20ms hard-fail line.

**Diagnosis (Lane 6, this session):** the `--profile` per-node breakdown on frame 0 (the post-seek frame) directly attributes the cpu_us outlier: before the fix, `node.spawn_from_image` (`seed_particles_from_texture.rs`, type_id `node.spawn_from_image`) alone cost **66.4ms cpu_us** on frame 0 — its four hand-written compute pipelines (`count_main`/`scan_main`/`compact_main`/`place_main`) were being lazily compiled on this project's first live use of that node. Root cause: this primitive is a barriered multi-pass hand-written-pipeline atom (same class as `node.scatter_on_mesh`, exempt from the codegen path per CLAUDE.md's fusion rule), so BUG-146's codegen-sweep prewarm never reached it — and no bundled preset happens to reference `node.spawn_from_image` either, so `GeneratorRegistry::prewarm_all`'s bundled-preset loop never exercised it. It had **no prewarm coverage at all**, identical to BUG-037's original `scatter_on_mesh` gap, just never closed for this sibling primitive.

**Fix shipped:** `SeedParticlesFromTexture::prewarm_pipelines(device)` (`crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/seed_particles_from_texture.rs`), mirroring `ScatterOnMesh::prewarm_pipelines` exactly (compiles all four entry points against the fixed, asset-independent shader source), wired into `GeneratorRegistry::prewarm_all` (`crates/manifold-renderer/src/generators/registry.rs`) alongside `RenderScene`/`ScatterOnMesh`. Gated: new `gpu_tests::prewarm_pipelines_populates_the_shared_compute_cache` test (mirrors `scatter_on_mesh`'s identical gate) — green. Verified against the actual repro: re-running the same perf-soak post-fix, `node.spawn_from_image` no longer appears anywhere in frame 0's per-node cpu_us breakdown.

**Remaining gap (fix shape for next wave, NOT this session's scope):** frame 0's cpu_us is still dominated by several `node.wgsl_compute` instances (79.2ms / 30.5ms / 23.6ms / 13.2ms / 10.8ms / 10.2ms cpu_us on the six worst — clearly six distinct node instances, each a distinct pipeline compile) plus `node.blob_tracker` (28.6ms cpu_us) — worst frame is still ~53ms GPU post-fix. Unlike `spawn_from_image`, `node.wgsl_compute`'s shader source is genuinely PROJECT-authored data (arbitrary WGSL text baked into this project's own JSON, not a fixed asset), so there is no generic app-startup `prewarm_all` target — BUG-037's precedent doesn't transfer directly. The correct fix shape is a **project-load-time prewarm sweep**: when a `.manifold` project loads, walk its graphs for every `node.wgsl_compute` instance and compile its specific pipeline before playback begins (once per unique (shader_src, entry_point) — the device's `compute_cache` already dedupes by hash, so a naive sweep over every instance is safe and cheap to reason about even if some instances share source). `node.blob_tracker`'s 28.6ms cpu_us is a separate, unexamined contributor this session did not dig into — likely a DNN/FFI init cost on first use, same first-use-resource-creation class, needs its own attribution before fixing. Neither of these was attempted this session (out of the "obvious and small, <~50 lines" bar for this lane) — whoever picks this up next should NOT re-derive the diagnosis, it's already attributed above; go straight to designing the project-load sweep + attributing blob_tracker.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Prewarm project-authored wgsl_compute pipelines at project load and separately attribute blob_tracker startup cost; verify the frame-0 budget. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-09-01T02:03:01Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. Original scope and acceptance remain authoritative.
