description: SetFrameRate mutates project settings directly instead of through EditingService, breaking the sole-mutation-gateway invariant. Route it through a command. Found during BUG-gqhep (live-transport-nondeterministic-frame-clock) impact map.

title: Effect frame_count seeds are tick counts; generators always get 0
description: Effect frame_count is a tick count since launch, not a transport frame; generators always receive frame_count 0 (generator_renderer.rs ~922). Decide what frame_count means after BUG-gqhep (live-transport-nondeterministic-frame-clock) lands (likely the transport frame index) and wire it consistently.

title: Math View small defects batch
description: hue uses fract().abs() so -0.25 becomes 0.25 (render_mesh_diagram.rs); profiling/encode-replay not forwarded to view variants (instrumentation.rs); whole-mesh mask re-dispatches during scans with Connect off (math_view_events.rs); Duplicate refuses any selection containing a Math View (scene_modifier_edit.rs); standalone views hard-require every __math_view_* node with no upgrade path, so adding a control later breaks every saved project; surface-depth size mismatch returns without clearing and logs every frame.

title: Math View trails lag a frame and scale with frame rate
description: render_mesh_diagram.rs draws with pre-capture history then captures, so trails end one frame behind; history is 32 frame samples so 30 fps export draws twice the trail length of 60 fps live. Fix shape: capture before draw; sample history by beats or seconds.

title: Math View echo copies: arrows start from the original, frames ignore copies
description: render_mesh_diagram.wgsl arrow tail uses un-copied incoming centroid while ghosts and heads use apply_copy; representative axis frames use un-copied current. With echo copies every arrow fans from the original spot. Fix shape: apply_copy to tails and frames.

title: Label review: add review-proven masters to variant_proofs.json?
description: The label review proves latest masters that offsets.py --variants never judged with the same code in memory (cached under ~/.cache/manifold/detector-lab/review/proofs, never written to lab/variant_proofs.json): back_to_you T3, set_me_free T2, imitation T2 PATCHED, sol REMASTER FINAL, touch T3, waypoints T2, running Remaster 02. Writing them into variant_proofs.json would add training copies under sampling.mix_variants and move run ids, so it is Peter call.

title: Undo of the first edit to a generator layer saved without genParams leaves genParams behind
description: Symptom: a generator layer with no genParams (Layer::new(Generator), or a file missing the key) gains genParams {generatorType: None} after any GraphTarget::Generator edit, and undo does not remove it, so the saved file differs. Root cause: with_preset_graph_mut and about 88 other call sites use Layer::gen_params_or_init, which creates the container on write. Same class as BUG-rr482 (undo leaves empty lists). Fix shape: make every generator layer carry genParams from construction and load, so gen_params_or_init never inserts; then the lazy-init path can go. Found by first_add_into_each_optional_list_undoes_to_the_same_saved_bytes in manifold-editing command_roundtrips.

title: Playback audit hygiene: dead ported code, stopped-clip drops, per-call clones, stale CORE_ENGINE_MAP section 13
description: From the playback audit pilot, agent-reasoned. (a) session-slot clips excluded by filter_ready_clips, so they would render nothing once session P4 UI exists; (b) tick clears stopped_this_tick first, dropping stops from seek/stop/gestures; (c) seek_to live-slot clear leaks active_clip_layers and looping_clip_ids; (d) dead code with wrong rules: sync_clip_loop_state, compute_clip_playback_rate, TempoRecorder track_clip_start/finalize_clip, eight uncalled TransportController methods, six never-installed engine hooks, get_current_absolute_tick, set_randomize_in_point, cited KNOWN_DIVERGENCES.md missing; (e) scheduler micro-clip looping bypass checks the active-only set, test micro_clip_skip_bypassed_for_looping pins an unmet contract; (f) renderer refusal retried every frame with warn plus library scan; (g) LiveClipHost::get_bpm_at_beat clones the tempo map per call, use get_bpm_at_beat_immut; (h) prewarm allocates a HashMap and walks the tempo map per clip every 0.5 s; (i) OSC router addresses effects by type so a second same-type effect is unreachable; (j) CORE_ENGINE_MAP section 13 stale: 13.1 and 13.3 fixed, 13.2 partial, 13.7/13.8/13.13 still open; (k) Port of C# line-number comments reference a Unity tree no longer used.

title: tooling: unlanded codex-provenance-guard hook
description: Branch lane/codex-provenance-guard (origin too), tip 4638eb0a7, 1 commit 2026-09-09, never landed. Adds .claude/hooks/codex-provenance-guard.py (UserPromptSubmit: a teammate message mentioning codex triggers a codex-companion status check; no task record injects a PROVENANCE WARNING), a settings.json hook entry and an AGENT_ROUTING.md section. Written after a codex-rescue forwarder returned a fabricated Astra ruling (memory feedback_codex_rescue_provenance.md records the rule, but nothing enforces it). Why it matters: the rule is memory-only today. Landing needs a call first: is it still wanted now that Astra is launched directly via codex-companion task, and is a settings.json hook add allowed under docs/PERMISSION_BOUNDARY.md; then merge main in, rerun its hook tests, gate, land via scripts/land_branch.py, or delete the branch if declined. Found by the 2026-10-13 unlanded-branch audit.

title: project_tool parses floats one step off (no serde_json float_roundtrip)
description: project_tool clip add-bulk reads JSON beats through serde_json without float_roundtrip, so a value can land one ulp off; a clip cut exactly at the next clip start was then refused as an overlap. Stopgap in tools/audio_analysis/lab/review_project.py: cut clips stop 1e-9 beats short (remove it with this fix). Fix shape: enable serde_json float_roundtrip for manifold-io (check the workspace feature unification cost on project load), add a round-trip test on adjacent clips.

title: dream: snare labels sit ~30 ms after the snare attack
description: dream snare attack lands -31.6 ms vs label before and after the timing_shift fix, while its kick labels are on time. Cause unknown; suspects: a snare-specific sample delay or a layered clap starting before the labelled pad. Evidence: lead scratchpad kicklate/summary_snare.txt.

title: lab/run.py trains when --plan comes after the config name
description: Symptom: run.py snare_v2_mid --plan trains the config with default seeds (it ran seeds 3 and 4 on 2026-10-13) instead of printing the plan; main() only treats --plan as a mode when it is the first argument and ignores unknown trailing flags. Fix shape: parse flags with argparse or refuse any unknown argument, so a misplaced --plan or --warm exits instead of training.

title: Detector lab reference: window sums are differenced whole-clip prefix sums
description: Symptom: Rust history parity on the 2026-10-13 snare showed stage.x 1.4e-11 against the Python reference (level column), while p.stage, p.final and every fire were exact. Root cause: eval/kick_goal_selfsim.self_features and relative_levels take np.cumsum over the whole clip and difference it per window, then divide by the window weight, so the error grows with clip length and with small window weights; the Rust history sums each window directly. Fix shape: sum each window directly in the reference (changes training numerics slightly, so every run id moves; do it between campaigns), then tighten the part check in crates/manifold-audio/src/trained/tests.rs back to 1e-12 on stage inputs.

title: Detector labels: a muted track silences a playing track of the same name
description: Symptom: Concentrate (Faux.als) has two tracks named Kicks in group Drums, one muted, one playing (302 notes). note_labels.silent returns track names, and project_parts / playing_clips test tr name in quiet, so the playing Kicks is treated as muted: its 302 kicks become unknown and the kick labels for concentrate have 0 positives (kick_labels_project.json). Snare labels on the same song take the kicks as vouched negatives through detector_wip.kick_beats, which checks each track own mute. Root cause: tracks are identified by name in silent(), playing_clips() and project_parts(); names are not unique in Ableton sets. Fix shape: key silence by track id (als_extract already records id), rebuild every labels family, and diff the labels of the existing songs (only songs with duplicate names should move, toward more known notes). Found 2026-10-12 adding the label-ready catalogue songs (feat/label-ready-songs).

title: Detector Lab: bf16 net training A/B (precision dial)
description: kick_goal_nn.train already takes precision (lab design D1). A/B bf16 vs float32 on one known pair (e.g. snare_v2_mid vs snare_v2_base): expect about 1.5-2x net throughput on MPS. Adopt only if scores hold — training-level agreement is reported, scorer parity is the gate (lab design D11). Measure with the interleaved timing run (BUG-9ngk8.16) so net time and score land in one run. Nets are small (12 s, batch 256, backward-bound), so this only pays if net training actually dominates after BUG-9ngk8.8 (parallel seeds).

title: Detector Lab: screening funnel (fewer folds, optional exam subset) — labeled, never ships
description: First-pass screening at fewer folds (e.g. 4 groups vs 8: half the trainings per seed) and optionally a fixed stratified subset of exam songs, chosen once by seed stability and kept fixed so screening runs stay comparable. Final A/B verdicts and every release always run full folds and the full exam; screening results are labeled as screening in every report and never quoted as verdicts. Guard: a report flag or test that marks screening runs so they cannot be mistaken for full verdicts. Do after the timing breakdown (BUG-9ngk8.16) says fold count actually dominates.

title: Snare v2: false fires on generated songs rose 25.6 to 30.9 a minute
description: In the snare_v2_base vs snare_v2_mid A/B, F1 on the 78 generated songs rose +3.9 points but false fires rose from 25.6 to 30.9 a minute (generated songs never set the cutoff). Real songs fell 8.3 to 6.9. Check which generated sounds fire (likely clap and snap one-shots labelled differently) before it matters live.

title: Kick detector CPU 25 to 42 ms per audio second: profile the v2 parts
description: The v2 kick (kick-2026-10-12-60984540f) costs 42 ms CPU per audio second in release (was 25); the snare pair with its kick is 70, under the 100 ms ceiling for all detectors. Profile note13 (YIN and two 2048-point FFTs per candidate), cdom4 (2048-point FFT per hop) and the perc channel's medians; cut what is cheap to cut without changing outputs (parity must stay exact).

title: Detector training: WIP mixes of a song as augmentation
description: Peter's WIP folders hold mix and master variants with the same timings. Folding the variants that match the final timings in as extra draws of the same song (grouped so a song never sits in train and exam) could add robustness; risk is near-duplicate data. A/B it in the lab.

title: Slow headless UI flows: modifier group 37.7s, fluid role lifecycle 26.5s
description: Symptom (landing gate flow leg, 2026-10-11): most scripted UI flows finish in under 3s, but inspector-modifier-group takes 37.7s, scene-fluid-role-lifecycle 26.5s, inspector-blob-mask 23.0s, scene-fluid-object-lifecycle 15.6s, envelope-modulation 14.9s, scene-forces-controls 14.3s, scene-fluid-role-assignment 13.0s. Clicking through panels headless should be seconds. Root cause: unknown. Suspects: fixed-frame waits or sleeps in the flow scripts, a real simulation stepping (fluid scenes) or GPU warm-up per flow, per-frame rebuild cost in those panels. Fix shape: profile inspector-modifier-group first (frame count and time per frame), remove fixed waits in favor of waiting on state, and make flows that do not need a running simulation skip it. Code: scripts/run_ui_flows.py and the flow definitions it runs.
notes: Scale (2026-10-11 detector landing): 4 touched UI files (param_slider_shared/state.rs, types.rs, audio_trigger_section.rs, a test) selected 41 required flows, run one at a time: 430 s and counting. Two levers beyond per-flow speed: run independent flows in parallel (they are separate headless processes), and narrow the file-to-flow mapping (a test-only file and a 3-line enum addition should not pull in every inspector and scene flow).

title: Score an offline drum transcriber on the lab exam songs
description: Peter, 2026-10-11: later, not now. Run one offline drum transcription tool over the kick and snare exam songs and score it with the lab scorer (same labels, cutoffs, windows), to see whether the causal specialists beat a tool that hears ahead.

title: Frame-wise causal drum model (TCN): deferred, current architecture first
description: Fable consult 2026-10-11: a causal dilated-conv frame model (one trunk; kick, snare, hats heads; look-ahead as a setting) might reach kick 0.88-0.93 and snare 0.82-0.88 at 30-50 ms delay (extrapolated from published drum transcription, not measured), but costs a new model, a Rust port with parity, and an estimated 5-15 min per net. Peter, 2026-10-11: not worth it now given the longer training and rebuilds; optimise the current net + trees first (weight averaging, generated-then-real curriculum, snare trees blend, training length, finder recall check). Revisit if latency becomes the limit or the finder check shows candidates capping recall.

title: Detector Lab: registry verify for generated sections
description: lab/registry.py verify compares mix() with the legacy loader (detector_songs.audio), which reads GOAL/snare_wip/{song}.npy for generated songs; snare_generated no longer writes those and Modulations sections (mod_*) never had them. Verify generated sections by slicing the export directly instead.

title: Detector Lab: stem-remix augmentation of generated sets
description: Generated sets ship Full Mix plus Leads, Bass and Drums stems, sample-aligned. Remix stems at varied gains as extra training songs; Peter rule: if a stem is muted or heavily ducked, drop that stem s labels. Needs a section source kind of stems plus gains in lab/registry.py and the builders.

title: Modulation labels: read macro automation from the Modulations project
description: Peter, 2026-10-11: macro automation (the movement labels) is in Labels and Timings - Modulations.als but als_extract does not read automation yet; not usable until added. Not needed now (focus kicks and snares).

title: Detector Lab speed: test two seeds in parallel on the GPU
description: Kick seed on 8 groups = 36 trainings, nets about 12 s each (GPU-bound per cProfile: backward 55%). The kick CNN is small (batch 256); two seed processes sharing MPS might nearly double throughput. Settle with one interleaved timing run through gpu_queue before changing run.py; results must stay identical per seed.

title: Roll detector for kick and snare rolls
description: Peter, 2026-10-11: rolls confuse the main nets, so they are now left out of kick and snare training; a separate detector should handle them. Stage use: a roll reads better as one rising intensity (roll on, rate, density) than as 32 separate flashes; the main triggers cannot follow a fast roll anyway (60 ms refractory). Data: generated sets keep the roll snares as dense_pos and the roll spans in unscored (snare_labels_generated.json), project songs keep dense_pos. Related: BUG-9ngk8.2.1 (fast breakbeats and rolls).

title: RT normal-fetch debug proof reads vertex buffer without declaring residency
description: Symptom: under MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1, rt_t1b_vertex_normals fetch_interpolated_normal_2tri_matches_cpu_oracle and fetch_interpolated_normal_uses_inverse_transpose_for_nonuniform_scale return [0,1,0] (fallback normal) and fail; they pass in normal runs. Root cause: MetalShadowRayTracer::debug_fetch_interpolated_normal (crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/raytrace/tracer.rs about line 1466) builds its own encoder and binds only normal_sources/params/out; the kernel reads vertex data through RtNormalSource.vertex_base_addr, and that vertex buffer gets no useResource, so GPU validation blocks the read. Production dispatch_compute_with_accel declares geometry_buffers; only this test surface misses it. Fix shape: pass the vertex/index buffers into the debug surface and useResource them (Read) before the dispatch.

title: Kick goldens: about 8 MB of binaries re-committed per retrain
description: crates/manifold-audio/tests/fixtures/kick/clip_*.mkick hold audio_i16 and net_spec (f32, 10k x 64) and change every retrain. Consider dropping net_spec (debug only) or storing the clip audio once in a separate unchanging file.

title: Kick model: try one net over the spectrum plus the 69 measurements
description: Today trees (69 measurements) and the CNN (spectrum) are blended by mean logit. Test a combined net that also takes the 69 measurements. Expected small gain at 30 songs; about an hour with run_kick_goal_fast.py. Ships via kick_release.py if it wins.

title: Kick labels: Weight and Waypoints drum stems as trigger songs; audit Cold
description: Weight and Waypoints have drum stems that could become trigger-labelled songs. Cold (no project) has unaudited labels. Facade 82-110 s (WIP 4 vs newest .als) is unverified: Peter can listen for a kick there; if present, unscore sections where project and bounce disagree.

title: Kick labels: prove recall-only WIP offsets with kick-solo bounces
description: Lowkey, Default Haze and Overwhelming Force are used recall-only because their WIP export offset rests on the constant ~50 ms MP3 lag argument. A kick-solo bounce from each project would prove the offset and let them count for precision too.

title: Kick model: rebuild tail caches with the causal past-4 s max and retrain
description: kick_goal_tail_features.py now uses a causal past-4 s max (it used scipy reflect, reading up to 4 s ahead for onsets in the first 2 s). The trained model kick-2026-10-10-99b606172 was fitted on the old tail_{t}.npy caches; kick_release.py self-check masks those early rows. Regenerate the tail caches, retrain, drop the mask.

title: SimStep has no Default: every executor and generator states live or export at construction
description: After BUG-hkbdp.6.8 (explicit step context), SimStep::default() is export at 60 Hz (crates/manifold-node-engine/src/exec/effect_node.rs:143). That matches the old thread-local default (offline when no preview budget was set), so nothing changed on stage, but a silent default hid a wrong ordering in the whitewater harness (set_sim_step after Show::restart ran warm-up and restart frames as export). Fix shape: delete impl Default for SimStep; Executor, GeneratorRenderer and the test harnesses take the step at construction, so the compiler names every place that must choose. Check app warm-up and thumbnail paths choose deliberately. No behaviour change intended; prove with the render oracle and the water conformance proofs.

title: Kick goal follow-ups: percussive residual, pitch-settling trajectory, loose-truth training
description: Untested ideas from the 2026-10-10 Fable consult, each expected to move the oracle ceiling about a point: (1) causal percussive residual (past-only median per bin) so bass plucks and sustained notes stop adding low-band rise (Back to You); (2) causal instantaneous-frequency trajectory of the 40-250 Hz band (where the pitch drop settles: kick ~50 Hz, tom ~120 Hz), inside the 40 ms window since 50 ms failed; (3) train on loose truth to test BUG-gh7sj fairly (loose scoring with strict-trained models gives ceiling 0.837). Harness: kick_goal_eval.py, run_kick_goal_frontier.py FEATS [loose], run_kick_goal_preds.py, run_kick_goal_selfsim2.py.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Item 3 is now the primary-truth fix: BUG-gh7sj ruled rolls are kicks, so whole-song training truth must include fresh notes over a ringing tail (the strict 10 dB fresh-onset rule drops them), and every kick-goal number should be re-reported on loose truth.

title: Kick detector past the 84/84 ceiling: small neural net on the features, or more labelled stemmed songs?
description: Every hand-built feature family moves the per-song oracle ceiling about one point (0.815, 0.832, 0.841, 0.846); the song-relative stage fixes cross-song cutoff transfer, not ranking. Limiting cases: soft long sub kicks inside a constant bass bed (Cold, Heavy 67-69 s), non-kick drum hits with low end (Burn toms, Heavy percussion, Back to You claps), bass plucks and impacts, Midnight rolls under strict truth. Options: a small causal network on the existing features or spectrogram patches (no GPU needed at inference), or more stemmed songs auto-labelled from kick stems (Cold-like four-on-the-floor dominates now: 642 of 1313 labels). Peter's call; CLAUDE.md research constraints said no neural nets this campaign.

title: Kick lane and Bad Guy bass-line fires: errors to remove?
description: Confirm the definition. In Bad Guy every kick model fires ~40 times in 15 s where the drum stem shows no attack (45-140 Hz drum rise 0.8 dB at extras vs ~60 dB at kicks; bass is the loudest low stem at 29 of 42). They are bass-line fires, not missing kicks; the labels hold. Night research treats them as errors and reports every total with and without Bad Guy. If the show wants bass-driven hits, that is a separate bass lane, not the kick lane. Evidence: ~/.cache/manifold/kick-research-2026-10-10-night/stem_audit.json, docs/AUDIO_EVAL_HARNESS_GUIDE.md night section (branch codex/kick-attack-upgrade). Related BUG-5to (kick discriminator).

comments.author: Peter Kiemann

title: How long should warmup wait for one heavy layer before giving up
description: After BUG-7qz2l (warmup frame cap) warmup waits up to 10 s per layer and 60 s for the whole project open (WarmupBudget::default in crates/manifold-core/src/warmup.rs; docs/WARMUP_DESIGN.md). Heavy glTF photoscans load in about 2-3 s today (Apricot 2.2-2.6 s, Rosetta 0.7-0.8 s), so 10 s has headroom, but bigger scenes could exceed it and would then finish loading on stage. Peter may want longer limits, a per-project setting, or a visible warning when a layer misses warmup. Open question for Peter, not scheduled.

title: Wave absorption zone for FLIP wave tanks
description: Ocean Cliff drives its cove with a piston paddle in a closed tank. Waves reflect off the cliff and the paddle, so energy only leaves through breaking; the stroke period has to sit between slosh modes (2.8 s for a 6.7 m, 1.25 m deep cove) or the tank resonates into chaos within 8 s. Industry method: a relaxation (sponge) zone that blends velocity and level toward a target wave over a band near the generator (Jacobsen et al. 2012, waves2Foam), or active absorption at the paddle. Same infrastructure is the open-face half of ocean-to-FLIP coupling (OCEAN_SURFACE_DESIGN.md section 9).

title: Physics offline-to-live handoff writes an earlier timestamp into input history
description: Symptom: when a physics world runs offline and then gets a live scope without a reset, the frame fails: "physics input history cannot move backward within an epoch", node.physics_world output empty (seen in physics_boxes_render_motion_and_latch_count_until_reset). Root cause (Astra, read-only): historical sampling calls clock.observe_speed while the clock still remembers offline mode (physics.rs:942); the full advance then switches to live (clock.rs:282), caps and reanchors time, and physics.rs:1121 records the earlier simulation timestamp, which history correctly rejects. Unknown whether any stage path reuses a runtime across this mode change (export after preview is the suspect). Fix shape: decide the mode switch before sampling, or reset history on a mode change; add a focused offline->live handoff test.
notes:
Checked (2026-10-06): export runs on the same engine and generator runtimes (content_export.rs:412-500), but on finishing it seeks back to the saved beat, and any backward time jump resets the physics world (physics.rs:908-922), so offline and live never share an epoch. Remaining narrow case: an export range that ends before the playhead; the restore seek is then forward, no reset, and the next live frame could hit the backward-history write. Peter: likely a non-issue; parked at P3.
Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Leave the accepted scrub-then-play blank frame unchanged unless Peter reopens the narrow offline-to-live export-range handoff case. title: GPU FLIP pressure template rebuilds on every Auto/fixed Iterations switch
description: Symptom (static review by Astra, 2026-10-06, not yet observed live): the round template inlines the stop tolerance (-1.0 for a fixed Iterations count, TOLERANCE for Auto; gpu_flip_pressure.rs Stop::tolerance). The template store replaces the least-recently-used idle slot on a miss (crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/template.rs build()), so with one idle slot, a performer toggling Iterations between 0 (Auto) and a positive count rebuilds the template on every switch (a CPU walk and ~1280 command writes per solve on that frame). Changing positive counts alone keeps the tolerance and does not rebuild. Root cause: tolerance is baked into the round params instead of read from a buffer. Fix shape: move the tolerance into the GPU-side stop record (a buffer the template reads), so one template serves both stops; or key the store so both variants stay resident. Verify first with a live toggle and the template stats (builds, command_writes).
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — evidence. Remaining: Cache pressure templates by iteration mode so Auto/fixed switches do not rebuild every time, and add a focused proof. title: Dispatch-granularity profiling reports zero-threadgroup dispatches as invalid spans
description: Symptom: frame-time --stamp-granularity dispatch on the GPU FLIP oracle reports ~519k invalid spans and unusable per-dispatch numbers. Root cause (Fable audit 2026-10-06): a zero-threadgroup dispatch never executes, so its boundary samples keep an older frame value and resolve_stamps drops the pair as invalid (manifold-gpu/src/metal/profiling.rs:361-366, 401-406); every dead gated round does this once replay is off. Fix shape: classify a pair whose stamps are both stale as skipped (zero length, counted per node), keep invalid for COUNTER_ERROR/0/reversed; frame-clock abort (frame_time.rs:875-879) fires on invalid/overflow only. The skipped count then measures dead dispatches directly.

title: Mix Arrays output capacity grows but never shrinks
description: Symptom: changing the GPU FLIP Dam Break Resolution card 64 -> 32 made node.mix_arrays (solid_blend) refuse: "output capacity must follow a (a=186624 bytes, out=1257728 bytes)". title: GPU FLIP sheeting: per-solid sheeting strength multiplier
description: Native _updateSheetSeeding multiplies the sheet fill rate by the nearest solid object sheeting strength within 2h of a solid (fluidsimulation.cpp 7158-7170, MeshObject::getSheetingStrength, default 1). title: GPU FLIP surface: brick nodes rewrite the canonical exterior into every inactive slot each frame
description: Overnight goal item 2 (free speedups). Each brick-scheduled surface node (particle_volume, smooth_lattice, volume_surface_mesh, smooth_surface_mesh, surface_mesh_normals) runs pass 2 of liquid_bricks::dispatch every frame: a dense dispatch writing the canonical exterior value into every inactive slot. Measured 2026-10-05 on the GPU FLIP Dam Break oracle (res 64, 30 Hz, engine defaults, dispatch-stamped): the profiler tags by node, so the pass could not be split out, but smooth_lattice costs 0.082 ms for all four of its dispatches including its exterior pass, which bounds the exterior pass near 0.04 ms a node and about 0.25 ms a frame across all five (under 1% of a 33 ms frame). Blocked as not worth the risk now: skipping it needs the lattice outputs kept intact across frames (graph buffers can be reused between frames) plus a retired-brick list so only bricks that just went inactive get rewritten. Revisit when the frame is near budget and a split profile shows it above ~1%. Fix shape when it matters: pin the outputs, keep last frame mask, exterior-write only (last active AND now inactive).
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — parked. Remaining: Keep inactive-brick exterior-write optimisation blocked until the frame is near budget and a split profile exceeds ~1%; then qualify buffer lifetime and retired-brick handling. title: Liquid solid distance drops body lattice nodes past a thin body's padding
description: Symptom: none seen yet. Thin, wide-scaled colliders get a solid band of only a fraction of a liquid cell. Root cause: build_distance (fluid_role.rs) pads by 2 lattice nodes in local units. Under scale (4 m by 0.4 m lid) that is 0.025 m in y, under half a 64^3 cell. liquid_solid_distance_body.wgsl, region_distance and the nearest-body lookup (gpu_flip_step.wgsl:365, 678) and grid_to_matter_body.wgsl:156 skip nodes past it, so those nodes read only the walls. A CPU proof showed this does not unseal the sealed-lid pool (BUG-ekb3 (sealed-lid water speed)). Fix shape: extrapolate past the lattice (the value at the nearest lattice point plus the distance to it), matching how the engine mesh level set covers the whole grid.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — evidence. Remaining: Extrapolate solid-distance values beyond the body lattice and add a thin-body padding regression. title: Whitewater W6: sign-bit prepass for surface_crossings
description: Dam Break 64 probe (2026-10-02, feat/whitewater-speed-1 after W1-W7): node.whitewater_step.crossings is the biggest whitewater dispatch at 0.325-0.334 ms p50 (p95 0.54-0.57) of a 1.84 ms stamped whitewater step, so 0.33 ms is the ceiling; realistic gain 0.1-0.2 ms after paying for the pack pass. Shape: a pass over the refined level-set nodes packs sign bits (32 nodes per word along x, ~350 KB); surface_crossings reads 9-18 words per cell for the sign test instead of 27 scattered f32 and does the edge walk (same reads, same arithmetic) only for cells that change sign, so output stays bit-exact. Proof: the existing CPU-expected surface_crossings proof unchanged plus the cross-frame proof and fused-vs-unfused. Kill lines (plan): crossings under 0.2 ms, or the prepass costs more than it saves on the first measurement; survives the first at 64. title: Whitewater W2: live-bound pool passes by indirect dispatch
description: Dam Break 64 probe (2026-10-02, feat/whitewater-speed-1 after W1-W7): live whitewater p50 6262 / p95 9314 / max 9432 of capacity 100,000, pool_full on 0 frames; the 11 candidate pool kernels (advect, retype, age, sort.count/clear/scatter, keep, live_flags, compact, split_flags, split; preserve_foam already skipped) sum 0.196 ms p50 in the timestamped split, so that is the ceiling of the gain. title: Freshly linked app binary pays ~40 s on its first launch (flow gate pays it once per gate)
description:
Symptom: the first run of a freshly linked ui-snapshot app binary takes ~40 s longer than every later run. Measured 2026-10-02 on slot-8: run_ui_flows.py scene-setup-add-object took 57.9 s on the first run after the link and 17.4 s on the second, with cargo confirming no rebuild in between (binary mtime unchanged, "Finished 0.40s"). Root cause: unknown. Suspects: macOS first-exec scan (syspolicyd / XProtect) of the new ~174 MB unsigned binary, or Metal's shader compile cache being keyed per binary so the UI pipelines compile cold.

If the scan is the cost, an ad-hoc codesign after link or excluding target/ from the scan is the fix shape; if it is shader compile, a persistent Metal binary archive is.

title: Measure naga's loop bounding in every kernel loop
description: naga 28 SPIR-V Options default force_loop_bounding: true, which the shared shader pipeline (manifold-gpu shader_common.rs compile_to_optimized_spirv) keeps. It adds a two-word countdown to every loop in every compiled kernel, seen in the MSL as a uint2 counter checked and decremented each iteration (for example in the workgroup-zeroing proof kernels). It is there so the Metal compiler cannot assume an infinite loop away. The cost per iteration is a few ALU ops in every loop app-wide: marching cubes, reductions, P2G loops, the Krylov kernels. Unknown whether it is measurable. Next: time one loop-heavy kernel with it on and off. Only if the difference is real, weigh turning it off; that needs a guarantee every loop terminates, the same kind of guarantee the workgroup-zeroing work weighed and did not need. Found while fixing the workgroup-memory zeroing (perf/workgroup-zero-init).
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — verification. title: Re-test the MTL4 temporal scaler after each macOS update
description: The MTL4 temporal scaler is off by default since BUG-ca67 (RT proofs time out the GPU), 2026-10-01, macOS 26.6.1 on M4 Max. Temporal upscale uses classic MTLFX. Symptom it guards against: an MTL4 temporal scaler that follows an earlier one on the same device hangs its MTL4 command buffer until the MTL4 queue watchdog kills it at about 4 s (MTL4CommandQueueErrorTimeout); the classic frame waiting on it stalls 4 s or times out, and a classic timeout makes macOS ignore the process queue. Repro, with the gpu_proofs binary built by cargo test -p manifold-renderer --features gpu-proofs --test gpu_proofs --no-run: (1) MANIFOLD_MTL4FX_TEMPORAL=1 <gpu_proofs binary> --test-threads=1 rt_p4_metalfx_temporal rt_t2b_temporal_wiring (was: 4 s stall 4 of 4 runs, timeout 2 of 4; each module alone clean); (2) MANIFOLD_MTL4FX_TEMPORAL=1 cargo test -p manifold-gpu m4_temporal_scaler_encodes_one_frame (smoke). Re-enable only when (1) is clean 3 of 3 and the full gpu_proofs binary is clean in parallel with the flag set. Before re-enabling, also fix two latent races in metalfx_m4.rs MTL4Bridge under concurrent use: event values are handed out at encode time but signalled in commit order on one shared timeline, and the allocator ring slot claim is not atomic.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — verification. Remaining: Re-run the focused MTL4 temporal-scaler check after a macOS update before enabling it by default. title: Fan-out buffer regions: split a fused component at the escaping output instead of refusing it whole
description: Found in GPU whitewater P5 (whitewater_spawn_chain_fuses in whitewater_extent_tests.rs). A fused buffer region writes one output (FREEZE_COMPILER_MAP.md section 4, region gates: fan-out buffer region refused). When a coincident chain has two consumers outside it, partition_regions unions the whole chain and build_region then refuses it, so every member runs unfused. Whitewater: jitter, sample, energy, wavecrest and count fold into one kernel while the counts are the only way out, but spawn_whitewater also gathers the sampled particles and the energy, so all five now run as five dispatches. Fix shape: when a buffer component would be refused as fan-out, cut it at each member whose output escapes, materialise that output, and build the pieces separately (with spawn gathering energy that gives 3 dispatches; with spawn recomputing the energy potential from the gathered velocity, 2). Needs the fused-against-unfused proofs and the GPU proofs gate, since it changes fusion for every preset with such a shape. Measure first: P6 reports the whitewater GPU cost against its 2 ms budget.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — verification. Remaining: Split fused buffer regions at each escaping output and add fused/unfused proofs for the whitewater fan-out shape. description: Symptom: render_preset_thumbnail (preset_thumbnail.rs) runs a fixed 60-frame warm-up with advancing time, then pumps more frames until io_pending and warmup_pending settle. title: MPM fixed-point accumulator overflow is never reported
description: Symptom: the matter P2G grid accumulates into i32 fixed point. node.matter_stats measures the peak accumulator magnitude (max_accum) and the clamped node count every tick, but only GPU proofs read them (matter_scene.rs headroom check, matter_look.rs); the domain never reports an accumulator at or near overflow, so a wrapped sum would move water wrongly with no error. Fix shape: when max_accum reaches the saturation band, report it by name through the node error path (and the run-time error channel once that reaches the UI), naming the controls that raise it; add the case to the MPM row overflow check in liquid/conformance.rs.

title: Matter buoyancy reads 4.35% under Archimedes once the push-out pays the body
description: With D30 (GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md, grid_to_matter adds the push-out momentum to the body reaction words, BUG-n97i) matter_coupling_hydrostatic_force reads 600.5 N from the reaction (602.5 N from body rows) against rho0*g*V = 627.8 N, -4.35%, inside its 5% gate by 0.65 points; the neutral density-1 box sinks from 0.386 m to 0.050 m over 2 s. Before D30 it read -0.44% because the uncounted push-out momentum acted as a ghost force holding up part of the liquid above the box. The exchange itself is now closed (matter_coupling_energy_light_body residual <= 0.075% of momentum exchanged), and matter_coupling_floating_equilibrium improved (offset 0.328*dx -> 0.216*dx). Open question: is the 4% a boundary-layer discretization deficit (check convergence 32 -> 64, never above 64 per BUG-bnp9) or a top-face artefact (gravity presses the top particle layer into the box every substep and the push-out takes that load)? Verification task: run the hydrostatic scene at res 32 and 64 and at two box sizes; if the error shrinks with dx it is discretization and the gate stands; if not, look at the top-face push-out.

title: Qualify inherited RT material parity boundaries
description: Static source audit during scene-modifier RT design found existing material limitations: shadow_rays.msl omits nonemissive KHR UV transforms (around552), ignores authored TANGENT.w (478), samples mask texture alpha nearest/repeat without material alpha factor (586); RtNormalSource normal matrix uses a documented nonuniform-scale approximation (params.rs325); raster shadow_depth.wgsl lacks base-color alpha-mask sampling. These are documented existing boundaries, not newly reproduced runtime regressions. Kept separate from current-frame modifier geometry implementation to avoid silently claiming raster/RT material parity. Reuse existing BUG-wytp, BUG-wfxe and BUG-1gqt history when designing focused follow-up.

Remaining hybrid capability boundary is explicit in GLTF_MATERIAL_EXTENSIONS_DESIGN section 7: secondary hits omit coat/sheen/iridescence/SSS/full Phong-Cel and punctual specular; glass/Blend absent from acceleration; mip0 ray-hit sampling lacks ray cones; anisotropic env and secondary lighting remain approximations. title: Skin feeds RT GI and light shafts
description:
RT emissive light table is built from d.uniforms.emission (static factor) at accel-build time — never the map. Work: texture-aware table weights + mean power. Lead-seat design.

DESIGN 2026-09-01 (k3 lead): the per-frame live-texture half this bead was written for already landed via BUG-1gqt. RtObjectGeometry is rebuilt EVERY FRAME from opaque_draws (render_scene.rs:5462, `emissive_texture: d.emissive_map`); ensure_normal_sources (raytrace.rs:4462) rebuilds the material-texture indirection per frame; the GI kernel samples the live map with UV transform at the gather point (raytrace.rs:1980-1996), mirroring resolve_emissive. Textured emissive GI is proven by the rt_p3_emissive_texture fixture. So a video/generator skin already lights the scene through RT GI today — correctness needs no per-frame table rebuild.

What is genuinely static (texture-blind), all in build_emissive_table (raytrace.rs): (1) table membership gates on luma(GiMaterial.emissive factor) > 0 and alias weights are area x factor luma — skinned objects enter because skin.rs apply_emissive_binding whites the factor to 1.0, but a mostly-dark texture still gets uniform-area sampling: variance, not correctness; (2) emissive_table_mean_power feeds the RS8 firefly cap and the probe floor (render_scene.rs:310) from the factor alone.

Remaining work (one budgeted piece): per-emissive-object GPU mean reduction of the live emissive texture (mip chain, 1-frame-lagged readback), scaling that object table weight and the shared mean_power; alias-table rebuild hysteresis-gated on material mean change. Budget call against RT quality settings — Peter decides whether the noise win justifies the reduction pass. Full per-triangle textured-power rebuild per frame: rejected (weights shift variance, not correctness; RIS + firefly clamp already hold).
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — parked. Remaining: Decide whether remaining skin RT GI and shafts texture weighting belongs in parked texture work. title: rt-capture is not pixel-deterministic — A/B pixel diffs need a control run
description: Found during the rt-quality landing (2026-08-18): two identical rt-capture runs of RtNoiseTesting on the SAME main binary (--frames 360 --frame-clock) differ by up to maxdelta 255 on accumulation channels and maxdelta ~200/meandelta 0.28 on early composite frames (frame 30, mid-convergence). The overnight rt-quality bead expected branch-vs-main maxdelta <= 1 — unreachable with this harness. Consequence: any PNG-level A/B verdict must run a same-binary control pair first and compare distributions, or trust the rt-capture channel stats (which DID match to print precision) instead of pixels. Fix shape: either seed the RT RNG per frame under --frame-clock to make captures deterministic, or document the control-run requirement in rt_capture.rs + RT_QUALITY_SETTINGS_DESIGN-style landing checklists. k3 (lead)

title: audio capture ring has no NaN filter — analysis state can be poisoned persistently
description: From the BUG-84fv NaN audit (pro-raytrace-lifecycle-audit + lead, 2026-08-02): audio features are provably finite from valid audio (silence → 0.0, all divisions guarded), so a NaN can only enter via the capture layer — a CoreAudio/ProcessTap glitch (device-state transition, format change) delivering NaN samples into the ring buffer, which has no isfinite filter (cpal_input.rs:118-122, and check the ProcessTap path too). NaN FFT input → NaN magnitudes → analysis state (kick tracks, flux history) can be poisoned PERSISTENTLY upstream of the audio_mod sanitize landed in c1a0e377. GPU hang risk is already closed by the two landed guards (condition() sanitize + RT kernel rt_finite); this bead is the analysis-state integrity item. FIX SHAPE: isfinite sweep on the analysis worker input hop (off-RT, cheap), count-and-log glitches, and a state-reset if a NaN lands in persistent feature state.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — engineering. Remaining: Add isfinite filtering and logging at audio analysis input, then reset persistent state when NaN arrives. title: Clean the 10 SHADOW_BASELINE presets that bake a card-owned node param
description: Ten bundled presets bake a value onto a node param that an outer card owns, so the baked value is discarded at build and the card default is what renders. All ten are dead authoring residue, not intent — six bake amount=0.0 under a card shipping 1.0 (ColorGrade, Dither, EdgeDetect, Glitch, Strobe, VoronoiPrism), and SoftFocus bakes radius 4 under a card default of 6. A runtime log or warning would be the natural completion of "make it loud", but it would fire on all ten of these on load, so the order is: clean the residue here first, THEN wire a runtime warning. Doing it the other way ships noise on shipped content. Fix shape: strip the shadowed node-param values from the ten preset JSONs (the card default is the shipped look, verified), shrink SHADOW_BASELINE to empty, then open the runtime-visibility follow-up.

title: Concurrent rt-capture runs clobbered each other via a shared /tmp dir (was: intermittent all-zero RT channels)
description: ORIGINAL REPORT: 10 identical rt-capture runs on origin/main gave 3 alive, 7 with every RT channel at exactly 0 and mask pinned at 255 while the composite still rendered. REFRAMED 2026-07-30 after re-measuring: not reproducible under single-tenant release conditions. Release build, nothing else touching the GPU: 5/5 alive, run-to-run spread 1-4% (composite mean 0.080-0.083, refl_raw 0.626-0.632). Debug build at 120 frames: 2/2 alive. Two confounds identified, both present when the original numbers were taken. (1) SHARED OUTPUT PATH, the main one: rt_capture.rs wrote to a fixed /tmp/rt_capture and cleared it on entry, so two concurrent captures destroyed each other frames. Three sessions were capturing in parallel that evening, and the lead independently ran rm -rf on that directory between its own captures, which is very likely what emptied the agent runs. FIXED: the directory is now overridable via MANIFOLD_RT_CAPTURE_DIR and rt_noise_gate.py always uses a private per-process one. (2) BUILD PROFILE: the dead runs were a debug binary, which is several times slower and can land on the other side of the D17 async accel-build race; the gate now builds release. WHAT IS STILL UNEXPLAINED and why this stays open at P3: the original alive runs disagreed with each other by ~12 levels of mask mean (252.147 twice, 239.820 once), which clean release runs do not show, and no one has demonstrated a genuinely dead RT frame under isolated release conditions. If deadness ever appears again in a single-tenant release run, that is a real accel-readiness race and belongs back at P1 with the BUG-jddy residency class as the second suspect.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — parked. Remaining: Keep the retracted RT diagnosis parked; reopen only after an all-zero channel run with a private capture directory and no concurrent capture process. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-09-01T01:55:53Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Rate, 10 runs on origin/main b10d9d94 (same binary, same project, same command, back to back): 3 ALIVE / 7 DEAD, so roughly 30% alive. Dead is always the identical signature — refl_raw exactly 0.000 mean level, mask exactly 255.000. Alive runs are not identical either: refl_raw 38.193 / mask 252.147 in two of them, refl_raw 39.620 / mask 239.820 in the third, so visibility/AO coverage itself varies run to run by ~12 levels of mask mean. That second-order variance matters for any gate ceiling drawn from a single run.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: RETRACTED as a measurement artifact — my error, recording it so nobody chases it. The all-zero RT channels were almost certainly shared-directory contention, not an RT defect. rt_capture dumped to a hardcoded /tmp/rt_capture and cleared it on entry, while three RT sessions (this gate, petal shadows, NormalTangentMirror) captured in parallel all night: each run wiped the others frames mid-flight and could read a foreign projects channels, which is exactly how refl_raw reads 0.000 with mask pinned at 255 on a project that traces fine. Two pieces of evidence. (1) With no other capture running, 3 of 3 consecutive 300-frame runs came back clean, zero discarded, and the spread across them is tiny — composite mean 0.079 to 0.079, refl_raw 0.704 to 0.711, irr_full 1.305 to 1.311. Nothing like a 30% alive rate. (2) The two "alive but different" runs I cited (mask 252.147 vs 239.820) are better explained by reading two different projects frames than by RT variance. Not airtight: I did not manage to reproduce the dead state by deliberately running two captures concurrently (the binary got rebuilt without perf-soak under me and that experiment never ran), so this is inference from the mechanism plus the clean isolated runs, not a positive repro. Fix is in: rt_capture now honours MANIFOLD_RT_CAPTURE_DIR and the gate sets a per-pid private dir. What would reopen this: an all-zero channel run with a private capture dir and no other capture process on the machine.

title: project_tool cannot strip a .manifold down to a committable fixture
description: The RT noise gate (scripts/rt_noise_gate.py) needs a project fixture, but no .manifold can be committed: RtNoiseTesting.manifold is 53MB — 28MB of undo history and 11MB of embeddedPresets around ~0.5MB of actual timeline. title: BUG-116 — fire-meter-display-ballistics-reads-as-low-fps
description:
### BUG-116 (fire-meter-display-ballistics-reads-as-low-fps) — fire meters read as updating at low FPS despite a 60fps capture/snapshot/UI pipeline — LOW (deferred by design)
**Status:** DEFERRED — Peter 2026-07-11 ("leave this slow update for now"), found while adding the producer/consumer fire-meter round-trip test (`bug/fire-meter-unification`).

**Symptom** — a card's/clip-trigger's Amount meter visibly reads as updating slowly, more like a
peak-hold VU meter than a live level bar, even though nothing downstream of the content-thread
capture is actually throttled.

**Root cause — intentional, not a bug in the pipeline itself.** The pipeline is 60fps end-to-end:
the audio-analysis worker's hop is ~5.3ms, `evaluate_all_audio_mods`/`LiveTriggerState::evaluate`
push a fresh `FireMeterCapture` every engine tick, the `ContentState` snapshot carries it to the UI
thread every tick, and `ParamCardPanel`/`AudioTriggerSection::update_fire_meters` write it into the
meter every UI tick. What the performer actually sees is display-side peak-hold smoothing added
deliberately by BUG-109 P5: `MeterIds::update` (`crates/manifold-ui/src/panels/drawer.rs` ~245-306)
snaps a rising level up instantly, then HOLDS it for `PEAK_HOLD_SECONDS = 0.25` before decaying at
`PEAK_DECAY_PER_SEC = 5.0` (full-scale 1.0→0.0 in ~200ms) — added specifically so a millisecond-
scale transient's shaped envelope (which decays faster than the UI's own tick cadence can sample)
stays visible at all between snapshots, per that fix's own comment. The tradeoff is exactly the
symptom: a steady/fast-changing signal reads as chunkier and slower than the raw 60fps capture
underneath it.

**Fix shape** — not a wiring bug, so no root-cause removal; two ballistics directions if revisited:
1. Tune the constants down (shorter `PEAK_HOLD_SECONDS`, faster `PEAK_DECAY_PER_SEC`) — trades away
   some of BUG-109 P5's "the transient stays visible" guarantee for a snappier feel.
2. The pro-audio split: an instant, unsmoothed live bar (tracks `level` every tick, no hold) plus a
   separate thin peak-hold TICK mark riding above it (only the tick keeps BUG-109 P5's hold/decay).
   Keeps both properties instead of trading one for the other, at the cost of a second draw
   primitive per meter.

**Instrument impact:** cosmetic/feel-only — the underlying signal a mod fires on is unaffected (the
edge-detector reads the raw conditioned value, never the display-smoothed one); this is purely
"does the meter look as fast as the audio is," which is why Peter deferred it rather than folding
it into the round-trip test session.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — parked. Remaining: Keep the slower visual response deferred unless Peter changes the intentional 0.25-second peak-hold product decision. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-09-01T01:55:55Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. Original scope and acceptance remain authoritative.

title: BUG-115 — mux-multiblend-dynamic-arity-blocks-codegen-conversion
description:
### BUG-115 (mux-multiblend-dynamic-arity-blocks-codegen-conversion) — dynamic port count can't be expressed in the static spec the codegen reads — LOW (decision recorded: stay as-is)
**Status:** DEFERRED — Peter's call, 2026-07-14: leave `multi_blend` AND `switch_texture` as dynamic-arity
fusion boundaries. The static-max conversion's runtime costs (always-8 texture samples on multi_blend's
common 2-wired case; 32 always-bound slots + loss of the 5x→1x branch-pruning short-circuit on
switch_texture) plus the loss of the shrink-to-fit editor affordance outweigh fusability here — the
current dynamic kernels are the more optimal shape for live performance. Remains a tracked codegen gap
(dynamic-arity support), NOT a de-facto exemption from the codegen mandate; revisit only if dynamic-arity
codegen support is designed for real or the fusion-boundary cost shows up on the rig. Spike evidence below
kept as the record.

**Symptom** — `node.switch_texture` (mux_texture, 5 shipped presets — and mid-chain by its
nature, it selects between texture chains) and `node.multi_blend` are fusion boundaries.

**Root cause** — both have a dynamic port list: `num_inputs` rebuilds the ports per instance, and
multi_blend synthesizes its WGSL for N inputs at runtime (multi_blend.rs ~124). The freeze
codegen reads a static `PrimitiveSpec` (`standalone_for_spec::<Self>()` is type-level), which
can't express variable arity.

**Fix shape** — half-day spike first: convert at a fixed max arity (declare the max as optional
`Coincident` texture inputs; the texture-region machinery already folds unwired optional
coincident inputs as `0u` use flags per FREEZE_COMPILER_MAP §4 region gates), body selects/sums
over the wired flags. If the spike shows dynamic ports can't square with the static spec, growing
dynamic-arity codegen support becomes a design decision for Peter — flag it, don't improvise.

**Spike (2026-07-14)** — done, half-day scope, no landing. Evidence:
`crates/manifold-renderer/tests/bug115_dynamic_arity_spike.rs` (two `#[ignore]`d tests, run with
`cargo test -p manifold-renderer --test bug115_dynamic_arity_spike -- --ignored --nocapture`).

*Spike verdict: yes-with-caveats.* The static-max-arity + optional-`Coincident` + `0u` use-flag
shape is not a new mechanism to invent — it already ships in production for `node.pack_rgba`
(`pack_channels.rs`: 4 always-present optional `Coincident` texture inputs, a `use_<name>: u32`
flag per input injected into the uniform, body falls back to `default_*` when unwired). The spike
built a throwaway 8-input `MultiInputCoincident` spec (mirroring `multi_blend`'s sum-not-pack
semantics) directly against `generate_standalone` — bypassing the `primitive!` macro so no fake
node registers in the palette — and confirmed: (a) `generate_standalone` accepts it and emits
valid WGSL naga parses cleanly; (b) region-fusion already admits this shape into a region without
new work — `region.rs`'s own comment at the unwired-optional branch says explicitly "this is what
lets `pack_channels` fuse with only r/g wired," so multi_blend/mux converted this way would fuse
exactly like pack_rgba does today, no region.rs changes needed.

**The real tradeoff for Peter's call:**
- **Perf, measured, not asserted.** The codegen wrapper pre-reads every DECLARED texture input
  unconditionally (`textureSampleLevel` per input, before the body's `if use_N != 0u` gate even
  runs) — this is separate from the use-flag folding, which only gates the *contribution*, not the
  *sample*. The spike's generated 8-input kernel has exactly 8 `textureSampleLevel` calls and 11
  `@binding` declarations (1 uniform + 1 sampler + 8 textures + 1 output) — always, regardless of
  how many of the 8 are actually wired. Today's `multi_blend::shader_for(k)` samples exactly `k`
  textures and binds exactly `2+k+1` slots. A live-show preset with 2 wired inputs (the common
  case per multi_blend.rs's own doc comment — "the summing shader is generated for the number of
  *wired* inputs... so a 2-input blend... compiles a tight kernel with no dead taps") would go from
  2 samples/dispatch today to 8 samples/dispatch always-8 — a 4x texture-sample increase with no
  possible naga/backend DCE rescue, since the use-flag is a runtime uniform value, not a
  compile-time constant, so the sample call can never be proven dead. `switch_texture`'s case is
  worse in shape (not degree, since it already short-circuits to 1 dispatch via
  `selected_input_branch`): its `MAX_INPUTS = 32`, so a static-max conversion would mean 32 always-
  bound texture slots per instance — the perf hit isn't sampling (mux only reads the selected one
  per the executor's branch-pruning) but the sheer binding-table size and uniform layout, and 32
  static ports is a much bigger vocabulary jump than multi_blend's 8.
- **UI/editor implications — a real blocker, not a nuisance.** The blanket `EffectNode` impl for
  any `Primitive` (`primitive.rs` line ~549) reads `inputs()` straight off `P::INPUTS`, a
  compile-time `&'static` const array — there is no per-instance override hook once a node goes
  through the `primitive!` macro / `Primitive` trait. `MultiBlend`/`MuxTexture` currently hand-roll
  `EffectNode` precisely so `reconfigure()` can mutate the live `inputs: Vec<NodeInput>` field and
  visually grow/shrink the node in the editor as `num_inputs` changes. Converting to the codegen
  path via `PrimitiveSpec::INPUTS` freezes that list at compile time — `standalone_for_spec::<Self>()`
  always reads the same 8 (or 32) ports. It's *possible* to keep a hand-rolled `EffectNode` for the
  live authoring surface while separately implementing `PrimitiveSpec` for codegen (nothing enforces
  the two agree), but that means hand-maintaining two divergent pictures of the node's shape — the
  editor's dynamic list and codegen's static 8 — which is exactly the kind of invariant this
  codebase avoids elsewhere. The `pack_rgba` precedent doesn't have this problem because it never
  had a dynamic port count to begin with: its 4 ports are always visible, wired or not. Converting
  multi_blend/switch_texture this way means giving up the "the node shrinks as I dial down
  num_inputs" editor affordance and replacing it with "the node always shows all 8 (or 32) sockets,
  wire only the ones you need" — a real UX change for an authoring surface Peter uses live.
- **Codegen-side complexity if pursued for real:** low. No changes needed to `region.rs` or the
  fusion-admission logic — the unwired-optional-Coincident path is already generalized and proven
  by `pack_rgba`. The work is entirely in the primitive files: rewrite `multi_blend.rs` off its
  hand-rolled `EffectNode` (dynamic ports, runtime `shader_for(k)`) onto the `primitive!` macro
  with 8 static optional Coincident inputs + a `wgsl_body` fragment, prove generated-vs-hand parity
  (mirroring the `pack_channels`/`trig_texture` parity tests in `codegen.rs`'s test module), and
  decide the num_inputs/UI question above. `switch_texture`'s conversion is harder in a different
  way — its `selected_input_branch` executor-level branch-pruning optimization (5-mode case: 5x → 1x
  render cost) has no equivalent in the static-Coincident-sum shape; a mux converted this way would
  need a different body strategy (a `select`/switch chain over 32 pre-read texture samples, which
  reintroduces the "sample all N always" cost multiplied by mux's much higher `MAX_INPUTS`) or would
  lose the short-circuit optimization entirely. That makes `switch_texture` a materially different,
  harder problem than `multi_blend`, not just a bigger version of the same one.

**Recommendation (spike input, not a decision):** worth doing for `multi_blend` if Peter accepts
the UX tradeoff (always-8 static ports, no more shrink-to-fit) and the preset(s) using it don't hit
the common 2–3-wired case hard enough for a 4x sample-count increase to matter on stage — the
codegen-side work is small and the mechanism is already proven in production via `pack_rgba`.
`switch_texture` is a harder call: its dynamic short-circuit (5x → 1x via branch pruning) is a real
perf win today that a naive static conversion would give up, and its `MAX_INPUTS = 32` makes the
always-bound-N cost much larger than multi_blend's 8 — recommend treating it as a separate, later
decision from multi_blend's, not bundled into the same conversion.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — parked. Remaining: Keep dynamic arity as a fusion boundary unless Peter approves static-max conversion after the recorded UX and performance decision. Evidence in record: proposal (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-09-01T01:55:59Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. Original scope and acceptance remain authoritative.

title: BUG-217 — non-lerp-mix-alpha-passthrough-kills-trails-on-transparent-sources
description:
### BUG-217 (non-lerp-mix-alpha-passthrough-kills-trails-on-transparent-sources) — BUG-181's "non-Lerp blends pass `a`'s alpha" makes feedback trails invisible whenever the source has a transparent background — found 2026-07-17 during the depth-relight look probe
**Status:** OPEN — LOW (documented idiom shipped @ f2684402; the alpha-mode enum on `node.mix` is still undecided — see below).

**Symptom:** a Max/Add feedback blend over a generator source with alpha-0 background (any SDF shape on transparent black) accumulates trails in RGB but every trail pixel outside the current source's alpha footprint carries alpha 0, so the display path culls them — the preset renders as if feedback were off.

**Root cause:** deliberate BUG-181 contract — non-Lerp `node.mix` modes are RGB-only and pass `a`'s alpha through so an AO map's alpha=1 can't overwrite a display chain's real alpha. Correct for masks; for feedback accumulation it means the blend's alpha never widens to cover the trail RGB it just wrote.

**Fix shape:** don't revert BUG-181. D7's cheap fix (the `set_alpha`-before-blend idiom, documented in `node.mix`'s and `node.feedback`'s `composition_notes` @ f2684402) is shipped and is the current answer for anyone who hits this. Still open/undecided: an explicit `alpha` mode enum on `node.mix` (PassA / Lerp / Max) so accumulation graphs can opt into alpha-max without the extra `set_alpha` node — Peter's call, no consumer has asked for it since the idiom shipped.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — decision. Remaining: Decide explicit non-Lerp feedback alpha semantics while retaining the shipped set_alpha workaround until that authoring contract is settled. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-07-25T06:09:36Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. Original scope and acceptance remain authoritative.

title: BUG-232 — harmonix-matched-audio-carries-multi-second-timing-offset
description:
### BUG-232 (harmonix-matched-audio-carries-multi-second-timing-offset) — YouTube-matched Harmonix audio isn't timing-aligned with the annotation reference — found 2026-07-17, AUDIO_ANALYSIS_ACCURACY P3
**Status:** OPEN — LOW-MED (data-integrity gap in a newly-added fixture source; doesn't affect anything already shipping, but blocks using Harmonix-matched audio for beat/downbeat tuning as-is).

**Symptom:** P3 matched real audio to 107/129 Harmonix electronic-slice tracks via `eval/fetch/harmonix_audio.py` (yt-dlp) and scored Beat This against the existing `beats_and_downbeats/<id>.txt` annotations (`eval/full_pack_baseline.py::run_baseline_beat_downbeat_harmonix`). On a 15-track sample, raw beat_f1 came back 0.11 mean (near-zero) despite predicted/truth beat counts being the same order of magnitude and near-identical spacing — the signature of a constant time OFFSET, not a detector failure. Confirmed via a difference-histogram cross-correlation (`_estimate_constant_shift`): per-track offsets of 2.9–7.3s were found, each backed by 150–215 of ~200–450 truth beats (a clear majority). Applying the estimated offset recovers beat_f1 to 0.65 mean (up to 0.95 on individual tracks); downbeat_f1 after the same correction stays low (0.23 mean) — a secondary, likely separate downbeat-phase-lock issue (which beat is "1") worth its own look later.

**Root cause:** the specific YouTube upload `yt-dlp` matched for a given `youtube_urls.csv` entry is not guaranteed to be frame-accurate to whatever recording Harmonix's original annotators used — extra intro/outro content, a different edit, or ad-supported lead-in on the matched video all produce exactly this symptom (one track's audio duration was measured at 241.65s vs the annotation's ~150.38s coverage, consistent with extra unannotated content). This is intrinsic to matching arbitrary YouTube videos against pre-existing third-party annotations, not a bug in the matching script itself (which only checks that a download succeeded, not that it's timing-aligned — it can't check the latter without already having a working alignment step).

**Fix shape:** productize the offset estimator already built for measurement (`eval/full_pack_baseline.py::_estimate_constant_shift`) into an actual per-track alignment step run once at match time (store the estimated offset alongside the matched audio, e.g. a sibling `<track_id>_offset_sec.json`), analogous to D14's decode-stage correction table. Until that exists, Harmonix-matched audio should not be used for beat/downbeat tuning or acceptance gates — it's fine for anything that doesn't need frame-accurate timing (e.g. spot-listening, section-boundary sanity checks at bar-level tolerance may be more forgiving).
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — parked. Remaining: Keep this deferred; if alignment is reprioritized, productize the existing offset estimator as a per-track match-time alignment step. Evidence in record: observed (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-09-01T01:55:57Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. title: BUG-045 — gap-ring-down-chase
description:
### BUG-045 (gap-ring-down-chase) — Tracker chases the transform's kernel ring-down during inter-note gaps — LOW (2.4 points on the notes gate; real-clip impact small)
**Status:** PARKED 2026-07-14 (bug-wave3 lane D, 1-attempt timebox per session brief) — reproduced and confirmed unchanged: `cargo run -p manifold-audio --example mod_harness --release -- --selftest` still reads `P2c notes: pct_sounding_hops_within_1st_of_gt_post_acquisition=87.6481 (gate >= 90) FAIL`, exact match to this entry (no drift since 2026-07-06). Did NOT attempt the two named do-not-retry tunings (already swept, confirmed dead ends), and did not attempt the untried value-trend discriminator either — the entry itself declines that direction as "knife-edge" (a new tuned constant between two distributions with only ~2x separation, where a genuine musical fade-out sits on the wrong side of it) needing either "a plateau-demonstrated sweep on real material or a smarter shape," neither of which fits a 1-attempt timebox without risking exactly the untested-magic-constant anti-pattern the entry warns against. No code changed.

**Found 2026-07-06 while fixing BUG-042** (its remaining accuracy misses after the
re-acquire-window fix). After every note release, the VQT's kernel memory presents a
DESCENDING salience artifact (energy decays slower in lower/longer kernels, so the
apex slides down: measured 149→144→133→118→100 Hz over ~6 hops on `notes`). The
early part of that slide moves at ≤ MAX_SLEW bins/hop, so continuation legitimately
follows it 2–4 bins down during the gap; the next attack then starts ~1–4 st low
until the onset re-acquire window rescues (~5 hops). Two partial guards shipped with
BUG-042: super-slew+moving continuation candidates are refused (hold instead of
clamp-chase), and a static super-slew peak in the MAX_SLEW..SLEW_RADIUS dead zone is
snapped to (tremolo-trough recovery). What remains is the sub-slew early chase.

**Oracle:** `P2c notes` accuracy line (87.6% vs gate 90 — the only known-failing
selftest line). **Fix direction (untried):** a value-trend discriminator —
ring-down decays ~0.90/hop at kernel rate while tremolo decays ~0.985/hop and a
real glide holds value — but that bar is a NEW tuned constant between two measured
distributions with ~2× separation, and a genuine fade-out slide (musical) sits on
the wrong side of it. Declined this session as knife-edge; needs either a
plateau-demonstrated sweep on real material or a smarter shape. Do NOT re-try:
raising SETTLE_STREAK (swept 2/3/4 — 69.2/87.6/86.1, K=3 is the plateau), or
re-clamping super-slew continuation (resurrects the 7-st gap-chase).
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — parked. Remaining: Leave the confirmed gap-ringdown finding parked unless a product decision reopens it. description:
### BUG-157 (editor-perf-hud-never-ticked-shows-dashes-forever) — the graph-editor window's own `perf_hud` overlay, if opened, would render permanently blank "—" values — LOW (currently unreachable: no keyboard/UI path opens it on the editor's own `UIRoot` today)
**Status:** PARTIAL — found 2026-07-14 during `EDITOR_WINDOW_UNIFICATION_DESIGN.md` P2, while building the phase's perf-HUD-in-editor acceptance demo. The shared root mechanism — the editor's `UIRoot` never sets `built`, so its own `update()` (which is what ticks `perf_hud`, along with the inspector) always early-returned — is fixed as of `GRAPH_EDITOR_INSPECTOR_UNIFICATION.md` Change 4 P2 (`d85ab207`, 2026-07-15): `UIRoot::tick_inspector` is now called directly from `present_graph_editor_window`, so the INSPECTOR half of this mechanism (drawer tweens, collapse, value-flash) advances every frame in the editor. The perf-HUD half remains open: that phase wired only `tick_inspector` + `update_fire_meters`, not `self.perf_hud.update(...)` — `perf_hud` is still never ticked on the editor's `UIRoot`, so if it's ever opened there it would still render permanent `"—"` values. Still currently unreachable in the live app (no keyboard/UI path opens it on the editor's own `UIRoot`), so it still blocks nothing — but the fix, if picked up, is now precedented: mirror `tick_inspector`'s call shape for `perf_hud.update(&mut self.tree)`.

**Symptom** — `PerfHudPanel::build_at_xy` seeds every value row with the placeholder text `"—"`; real numbers only appear once `PerfHudPanel::push_values(tree)` runs (called via `Panel::update` → `UIRoot::update()` on the MAIN window's `self.ws.ui_root`, `app_render.rs:3087`). The graph editor's own `UIRoot` (`self.graph_editor.as_mut().ui_root`, a separate instance) never gets `.update()` called on it — and even if it did, `UIRoot::update()` early-returns on `if !self.built`, which the editor's `UIRoot` never sets (it's built via `build_overlays_for_screen`, never the main-window-only `UIRoot::build()`). So if the editor's own `perf_hud` were ever toggled visible, it would render its full chrome (background, rows, graph bars) but every value would sit at `"—"` forever, un-ticking.

**Root cause** — two compounding gaps: (1) no call site anywhere in `manifold-app` invokes `perf_hud.push_values()` outside the `built`-gated `UIRoot::update()` path; (2) the editor's `UIRoot` is permanently `!built` by design (P1's `build_overlays_for_screen` wrapper deliberately avoids the main-window-only `build()`), so the one existing route to `push_values` can never fire for it.

**Currently unreachable, so LOW:** confirmed via `rg "toggle_performance_hud"` — the only call site is `input_host.rs`'s `AppInputHost`, constructed exclusively with `self.ws.ui_root` (the main window) inside `window_input.rs`'s `is_primary`-gated `InputHandler` shortcut-dispatch block. There is no keyboard shortcut, button, or other path that opens the perf HUD on the *editor's own* `UIRoot` instance today — this was only surfaced by directly calling `ui_root.perf_hud.toggle()` in the P2 headless demo harness (`ui_snapshot/render.rs`'s new `open_perf_hud` param), which also had to call `push_values` explicitly to get real numbers into the demo PNG (`docs/landings/EDITOR_WINDOW_UNIFICATION_P2_perf_hud_in_editor.png`).

**Fix shape** — either (a) give the editor window its own perf-HUD toggle path plus a per-frame `ws.ui_root.perf_hud.push_values(&mut ws.ui_root.tree)` call in `present_graph_editor_window` (gated on `is_visible()`, no `built` dependency needed since it's a targeted call, not the whole `update()`), if a live editor-window perf HUD is ever wanted; or (b) leave it unreachable and out of scope until that's asked for. Low priority either way — no live path exercises it.

title: BUG-153 — ui-snap-inspector-scene-172px-nondeterministic
description:
### BUG-153 (ui-snap-inspector-scene-172px-nondeterministic) — the `ui-snap inspector` headless scene is not run-to-run deterministic — LOW (test-determinism only, no correctness impact)
**Status:** PARKED (partial progress) 2026-07-14 (bug-wave3 lane D) — attempted, root cause not isolated within budget. Prerequisite found+fixed first: `--features ui-snapshot` didn't even compile on this tip (`view.canonical_def` changed from `EffectGraphDef` to `Arc<EffectGraphDef>` in an unrelated session, 8 call sites in `ui_snapshot/mod.rs` never updated) — fixed as BUG-162, logged separately since it's a distinct regression, not this bug. With the binary building, reproduced the exact 172-pixel/same-bbox diff on this tip. **Ruled out (verified, not guessed):** (1) the `update_fire_meters(&|_| Some(0.9), 1.0/60.0)` call the `inspector` scene makes after the base build — diff is byte-identical with that call stubbed out entirely, so it's not the meter peak-hold path. (2) `InspectorCompositePanel::motion_last_tick` being seeded to `Instant::now()` at construction, so the FIRST `update()` call measured "however long scene setup took" as its `dt_ms` instead of 0 — this was a real bug (fixed in this session, see the `motion_last_tick: Option<Instant>` change in `inspector.rs`, kept even though it didn't close this one) but had zero effect on the diff, so it isn't the source either. Both rule-outs used the actual harness re-run (`cargo run --features ui-snapshot --bin manifold -- ui-snap inspector`, twice, byte-diffed), not inference. **Still open:** the nondeterminism lives somewhere in `sync_build`/`reconcile_state`'s build path itself (structural sync → zoom → build → push-state), before either ruled-out point — candidates not yet checked: HashMap-backed registry iteration order feeding param/card construction order (would shift adjacent-row anti-aliasing at seams without moving whole rows, matching the sparse 172-pixel/full-bbox-not-solid pattern), or float-accumulation order in row-y-offset stacking. Next step: bisect by diffing the tree dump (`--dump`) between two runs to see which node's bounds/style differs, rather than guessing at the render level.

**Symptom** — `cargo run --features ui-snapshot --bin manifold -- ui-snap inspector`, run twice in a row with NO code changes in between, produces two PNGs that differ in exactly 172 pixels, always the same bounding box: x 1258-1274, y 450-854 at the scene's 1536×1216 render size — a narrow vertical band. Confirmed on unmodified `origin/main` (same 172-pixel, same-bbox diff reproduces there too) — unrelated to the P1 diff. The `timeline` and `states` scenes do NOT show this (byte-identical across repeated runs).

**Root cause** — unknown; not investigated beyond isolating it. The narrow x-band and full-height y-span suggest a scrollbar thumb, a hover-state color blend, or some other element whose color depends on a source of nondeterminism (timing, an uninitialized/stale value, float rounding on a borderline hover test) rather than the deterministic layout inputs the rest of the scene uses.

**Fix shape** — reproduce with a diff script (`PIL`/numpy pixel diff, or the repo's own `readback.rs` machinery) pointed at the bbox, then trace what draws in that rect (likely `inspector.rs`'s scroll container or a param-card element) and find the nondeterministic input. Low priority (doesn't affect the live app — only a headless test scene — and doesn't block any other test), but worth fixing before this scene is ever used as a byte-identical regression gate for something else, the way `EDITOR_WINDOW_UNIFICATION_DESIGN.md` P1 tried to use it.

title: BUG-231 — beat-this-no-tempo-hint-api-for-octave-fix
description:
### BUG-231 (beat-this-no-tempo-hint-api-for-octave-fix) — `beat_this` has no BPM-range/tempo-prior parameter anywhere in its production-safe inference path — found 2026-07-17, AUDIO_ANALYSIS_ACCURACY P3
**Status:** OPEN — LOW-MED (diagnostic finding, not a functional regression; matters because it forecloses the simplest fix for the `liveshow_integer` octave mis-track P2 flagged as a P4/P5 target).

**Symptom:** P2's landing report recorded that Beat This locks onto ~115.4 BPM on `liveshow_integer` against a ~132 BPM ground truth (≈7:8 ratio, 57% over-detection) and named "BPM range hint 60–200" as a possible P4/P5 fix (Peter's directive). P3 checked whether the `beat_this` package's inference API (`beat_this/inference.py`: `File2Beats` → `Audio2Beats` → `Spect2Frames`) actually accepts any such parameter. It does not — `Audio2Beats.__init__` takes only `checkpoint_path`, `device`, `float16`, `dbn`; `dbn=False` (the "minimal" postprocessing this codebase uses and must keep, per `manifold_audio/beat_tracking.py`'s own comment) is pure peak-picking on framewise beat/downbeat logits with zero tempo awareness. The ONLY place a `min_bpm`/`max_bpm` parameter exists anywhere in the package is inside `Postprocessor.__init__`'s `dbn=True` branch (`beat_this/model/postprocessor.py:27-33`, hardcoded `min_bpm=55.0, max_bpm=215.0`, not even exposed as a constructor argument to the caller) — which lazily imports madmom's `DBNDownBeatTrackingProcessor`, exactly the dependency P2 removed (D1/D2) and `beat_tracking.py` explicitly forbids re-enabling. No diagnostic run with a hint was performed, since doing so would require `dbn=True`.

**Root cause:** Beat This's "minimal" (non-madmom) postprocessing path was designed as a stateless framewise peak-picker with no global tempo model at all — a tempo-range constraint is architecturally a DBN-only concept in this package, not a general inference option.

**Fix shape:** the octave/ratio confusion needs a POST-HOC heuristic applied to Beat This's own beat-time output, not a detector-side parameter: e.g. detect that the median-IBI-derived BPM sits near a small-integer ratio (2:1, 3:2, 4:3, 7:8, etc.) of a target-genre-plausible range (60–200 BPM per Peter's directive) and re-fold/re-interval-select accordingly — analogous to `manifold_audio.bpm._normalize_bpm`'s existing octave-folding, but that function only folds by powers of 2 and would NOT catch a 7:8 ratio (confirmed: 115.4 * 8/7 ≈ 131.9, matching truth almost exactly, but `_normalize_bpm` never tries non-power-of-2 ratios). A future P4/P5 phase implementing this should start from `_normalize_bpm` in `manifold_audio/bpm.py` and extend its ratio set, not invent a new grid-folding mechanism.
notes: Backlog review 2026-10-09 — decision. Remaining: Decide whether production-safe Beat This should expose a tempo range/prior for octave correction, then document the chosen API or alternative. Evidence in record: source-only (not runtime-revalidated by this review). Ownership: unassigned. Pre-review activity: 2026-07-25T06:09:36Z; this metadata cleanup is not engineering progress. Original scope and acceptance remain authoritative.
